facts.text: In the Spirit Temple First Floor in the past, Skulltula #96 is on a fence across a pit.

evidence.quote: #96...Location: First Floor...Items: Requiem of Spirit...One of the rooms in the temple has a pit and a fence on the other side of it...The Skulltula is on that...fence.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #97
facts.text: In the Spirit Temple, Skulltula #97 is found by turning around at the top of the climbable wall leading to the Second Floor in the Lizalfos area.

evidence.quote: #97...Location: Second Floor...Items: Requiem of Spirit...There's an area with Lizalfos and a climbable wall that leads to the second...At the top of this wall, turn around to find a Skulltula.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #98
facts.text: In the Spirit Temple Second Floor in the past, Skulltula #98 is located above and behind Link in the room leading to the Iron Knuckle battle.

evidence.quote: #98...Location: Second Floor...Items: Requiem of Spirit...Just before your battle, as a kid, with the Iron Knuckle, you can find a...Skulltula above and behind you in the room leading to it.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #99
facts.text: In the Spirit Temple First Floor in the future, playing the Song of Time moves a blue block in front of an alcove in the trench room with rolling rocks to claim Skulltula #99.

evidence.quote: #99...Location: First Floor...Items: Silver Gauntlets...There's a room that has rocks that roll back and forth in a trench, and...there's a blue block in front of one of the alcoves.  Play the Song of Time...to move that block and claim the Skulltula.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #100
facts.text: In the Spirit Temple Second Floor big statue room in the future, playing the Scarecrow Song at the top of the left staircase summons Pierre to the opposite ledge, allowing Link to Longshot across and claim Skulltula #100.

evidence.quote: #100...Location: Second Floor...Items: Silver Gauntlets, Scarecrow Song...In the big statue room, climb up the left staircase (left facing the statue)...play the Scarecrow Song and Pierre will appear at a ledge...opposite.  Longshot to him and claim the final Skulltula.

facts.subject: dirt hole
facts.text: The dirt hole in the Zora's Domain area is the only hole without a Skulltula, so dumping bugs into it is unnecessary.

evidence.quote: NOTE: The dirt hole in this area is the only hole without a Skulltula, so...don't go nuts trying to dump bugs in it.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: At the entrance to Zora's River, rolling into the nearby tree knocks a Skulltula loose.

evidence.quote: Although you can't go very far in Zora's River without Bombs, you can still...reach the nearby tree at the entrance.  Roll into it to knock a Skulltula...loose.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: At night at the waterfall in Zora's River, a Skulltula crawls on the ladder in the water and can be shot with the Slingshot.

evidence.quote: Once you reach the waterfall, hop down into the water and you should see a...ladder.  At night, there's a Skulltula crawling on it.  Slingshot it and...climb up to claim it.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: About a third of the way up Zora's River at night, a Skulltula is high on the wall on the right side and can be reached with the Hookshot from the big platform.

evidence.quote: About a third of the way up the river is a Skulltula high on the wall on...the right side.  You can reach it by climbing up to the big platform...nearby, and Hookshot from there.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: About two-thirds of the way up Zora's River near a wooden bridge at night, a Skulltula is high up to the left and can be targeted with the Hookshot or Longshot.

evidence.quote: About two-thirds of the way up the river, about when you reach a wooden...bridge, look up and to the left to see a Skulltula rather high up.  It's an...easier mark with the Longshot, but you can use the Hookshot if you hop onto...the platform's guardrail.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: In Zora's Domain at night, a Skulltula is located on the wall to the left of where the Diving Game proprietor used to be and can be retrieved with the Longshot.

evidence.quote: Head to the location where the Diving Game's proprietor used to be.  Look...out and to the left to see a Skulltula on the wall.  Longshot it.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: At the back of Zora's Fountain on the piece of dry land, rolling into the tree knocks a Skulltula down from its branches.

evidence.quote: Make your way to the back of the area, with the piece of dry land.  Roll...into the tree there and knock a Skulltula from its branches.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: At Zora's Fountain at night, a Skulltula on the log sticking out of the water can be shot with the Slingshot and retrieved with the Boomerang.

evidence.quote: There's a log sticking out of the water.  Climb up to the highest point on...it and you should be able to see the Skulltula.  Slingshot it and use the...Boomerang to retrieve the token.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: At the back of Zora's Fountain, lifting the gray rock with Silver Gauntlets and bombing the hole leads to an underground passage with a Skulltula.

evidence.quote: Make your way to the back of the area, with the piece of dry land.  Use the...Gauntlets to pick up the gray rock lying here.  Set a Bomb to blow open the...small hole and drop down.  Make your way up this passage to find the...Skulltula.  Beware, because the passage is occupied by big Skulltulas that...you can only see with the Lens of Truth.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: At Lake Hylia at night, a Skulltula is found on one of the posts of the lonely platform to the left of the dead tree platform.

evidence.quote: Swim out a lonely platform to the left of a platform with a big dead tree.  ...There's a Skulltula on one of the posts at night.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Next to the Lakeside Laboratory, dumping a Bottle of Bugs into the soft earth hole forces out a Skulltula.

evidence.quote: Next to the Lakeside Laboratory is a patch of soft earth.  Dump a Bottle of...Bugs into the hole on that patch to force out a Skulltula.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: On the back of the Lakeside Laboratory at night, a Skulltula can be retrieved with the Boomerang.

evidence.quote: On the back of the Lakeside Laboratory is a Skulltula.  Use the Boomerang to...retrieve it.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: On the Lake Hylia island with the dead tree, using the Longshot to reach its branches leads to a Skulltula.

evidence.quote: On the island with the dead tree, Longshot up to its branches and you'll find...a Skulltula up here.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.object: crate at bottom of Lakeside Laboratory
facts.text: Inside the Lakeside Laboratory, rolling into the crate at the bottom reveals a Skulltula that can be killed and retrieved with the Hookshot.

evidence.quote: Inside the laboratory, drop down to the bottom.  Roll into the crate down...there to find a Skulltula.  Use the Hookshot to kill and retrieve it.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: In Basement 1 of Jabu-Jabu's Belly, a Skulltula is on the vine wall in the room with the water trench and switch.

evidence.quote: The room this Skulltula's in is a room with a trench of water in the middle,...and you step on a switch to raise the water to a level at which you can...climb out.  The Skulltula's on the nearby vine wall.  You can climb up to...him.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: After destroying the green tentacle in Jabu-Jabu's Belly, dropping through its hole from the first floor leads to a nearby Skulltula in Basement 1.

evidence.quote: After destroying the green tentacle, go the room on the first floor with...several holes leading to the basement.  Drop down the hole that the green...tentacle used to occupy and you should be able to reach a nearby Skulltula.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: A second Skulltula in Basement 1 of Jabu-Jabu's Belly is located in the same general room accessed by dropping down the hole where the green tentacle was.

evidence.quote: After destroying the green tentacle, go the room on the first floor with...several holes leading to the basement.  Drop down the hole that the green...tentacle used to occupy and you should be able to reach a nearby Skulltula.  ...Yes, this is exactly what I wrote for #54.  They're in the same general...place.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: On the first floor of Jabu-Jabu's Belly, a Skulltula is on the vine wall in the final room before the boss.

evidence.quote: This room is the very last room before the boss of this area, in which you...have to Boomerang a switch to move on.  The Skulltula is on the vine wall...heading up there.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: At the bottom of Gerudo Valley canyon, dumping a Bottle of Bugs into the dirt hole forces out a Skulltula.

evidence.quote: Grab the chicken near the bridge and leap off the canyon, floating down and...to the right towards the stretch of land at the bottom.  Down here, there is...a small dirt hole.  Dump a Bottle of Bugs onto the hole to force out a...Skulltula.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Walking up the plank leading to the big bridge in Gerudo Valley at night reveals a Skulltula to the right that can be retrieved with the Boomerang.

evidence.quote: As you walk up the plank leading to the big bridge, turn right.  If it's...night, you should see a Skulltula.  Use the Boomerang to retrieve the token.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Across the broken bridge in Gerudo Valley at night, a Skulltula is located on the wall behind the tents and can be hooked with the Hookshot.

evidence.quote: Either use Epona or the Longshot to cross the broken bridge.  Look behind...the tents and you'll see a Skulltula on the wall.  Hookshot it.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Across the broken bridge in Gerudo Valley at night, a Skulltula is on the back of the stone pillar to the left and can be Hookshot.

evidence.quote: Either use Epona or the Longshot to cross the broken bridge.  Look behind...the stone pillar off to your left to find a Skulltula on it.  Hookshot it.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: In the entrance room of the Forest Temple, looking up and to the right reveals a Skulltula.

evidence.quote: In the very entrance of the temple, look up and to your right to find the...first Skulltula of this dungeon.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: In the Forest Temple room with four torches, a Skulltula is high up on the wall near the door opposite the entrance.

evidence.quote: In the room with four torches, head to the door opposite from the door you...first enter.  You'll find the Skulltula on the nearby wall rather high up.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: In the northeast room of the Forest Temple with big Deku Babas, a Skulltula is on the wall and can be reached using the Hookshot on the island chest.

evidence.quote: In the northeast room (with big Deku Babas), you can find this Skulltula on...the wall.  To get to it, you can just make it by using the Hookshot on the...chest on the island, although it's easier to come in from the nearby room,...which you fall into from the second "twisted room".

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: In the northwest room of the Forest Temple, entering from the second floor and crossing the thin columns leads to a Skulltula.

evidence.quote: In the northwest room (with big Deku Babas), enter from the second floor and...cross the thin columns to reach this Skulltula.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: After descending the elevator to Basement 1 of the Forest Temple, pushing the rotating room walls reveals a Skulltula in one of the alcoves.

evidence.quote: After descending the elevator to the room you can rotate, push the walls and...examine all the alcoves.  One has a Skulltula.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.object: room past Song of Time block
facts.text: In the Fire Temple, climbing the entrance stairs, taking the right door, and playing the Song of Time to move the blue block leads to a room with a Skulltula on the wall.

evidence.quote: After entering, climb the stairs and take the door on the right.  Play the...Song of Time to move the blue block, then proceed and enter the next room.  ...You'll find Mr. Skulltula on a wall in that room.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: On the third floor of the Fire Temple, bombing a wall on the far north side of the rolling rock room reveals a Skulltula.

evidence.quote: On the eastern side of the third floor is a room with rocks rolling around.  ...Make your way to the far north side and bomb a wall there to find a...Skulltula.  You should be able to hear it skritching around.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: In the fifth floor room of the Fire Temple where the Megaton Hammer is found, a Skulltula is near the entrance.

evidence.quote: In the very room you get the Megaton Hammer, look for this Skulltula near the...entrance.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: In the Fire Temple, knocking the entrance pillar aside leads past the first room to a room with spinning tiles where a Skulltula is on the wall.

evidence.quote: In the entrance room, knock the pillar out of the way and proceed through.  ...Once you pass the first room, you'll come to a room with spinning tiles.  The...Skulltula is on the wall.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: In the Fire Temple, playing the Scarecrow Song near the northwestern exit summons Pierre, allowing Link to Longshot to him and reach a fifth floor area with a Skulltula.

evidence.quote: Go the same room as #67, and make your way to the upper part of the room.  ...Near the northwestern exit, play the Scarecrow Song to make Pierre appear.  ...Longshot to him, and then to the nearby target.  Ride up and make your way...to the fifth floor area.  You'll find the Skulltula close by.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: In the Ice Cavern room with the Heart Piece and Compass, a Skulltula is inside a small niche on the wall.

evidence.quote: In the room with the Heart Piece and the Compass, you'll find this Skulltula...in a little niche on the wall.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: In the Ice Cavern room with the spinning ice blade and silver gems, a Skulltula is located behind a cluster of icicles.

evidence.quote: In the room with the spinning ice blade and silver gems, you'll find a...Skulltula behind a bunch of icicles.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: In the Ice Cavern room with the pushable ice blocks, a Skulltula is on a nearby wall.

evidence.quote: In the room with the ice blocks you push around, you can find this...Skulltula on a nearby wall.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: In the Water Temple after draining the water, heading south into the corridor and using the Whirling Blade Technique on the crystal switch reveals a Skulltula.

evidence.quote: Drain all the water and head south into a corridor.  Once you reach the end...of the corridor, use the Whirling Blade Technique to hit the crystal...switch.  Take out the Skulltula on the other side.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: In the Water Temple underground river, dropping into the water wearing the Iron Boots reveals a Skulltula on the left wall.

evidence.quote: After dropping down into the underground river, hop into the water (with...the Iron Boots on), and keep an eye on the left wall.  You'll eventually...see the Skulltula.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Inside the central pillar of the Water Temple, a Skulltula can be reached from the second floor.

evidence.quote: Inside the pillar in the middle of the temple, you can find this Skulltula...reachable from the second floor.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: At the top of the pillar area in the Water Temple, heading west to the moving platforms room allows the Longshot to retrieve a Skulltula on the far right wall.

evidence.quote: At the top of the pillar area, head west to a room with moving platforms.  ...Use the Longshot to hit a Skulltula on the far right wall.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: On the way to the Boss Key in the Water Temple, a Skulltula is on the wall at the source of rolling rocks and can be grabbed with the Longshot.

evidence.quote: While going for the Boss Key, you'll find a corridor with rolling rocks.  ...When you reach the source of one of those series of rolling rocks, you'll...see a Skulltula on the wall.  Longshot it.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: In the Bottom of the Well, taking the northeast door from the central room leads to a room with a Like-Like and a Skulltula.

evidence.quote: From the large room in the center of the dungeon, take the northeast door.  ...Avoid holes and bad guys and make your way to a room with a Like-Like.  The...Skulltula is in this room.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: In the Bottom of the Well, unlocking the left locked room in the center area reveals a Skulltula that can be grabbed with the Boomerang.

evidence.quote: Find a key and unlock the left of the two rooms in the center room.  Use the...Boomerang to grab the Skulltula.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: In the Bottom of the Well, unlocking the right locked room in the center area and using the Lens of Truth around the pit allows the Skulltula to be retrieved with the Boomerang.

evidence.quote: Find a key and unlock the right of the two rooms in the center room.  Use...the Lens of Truth to find the safe path around the outside of the pit and...grab the Skulltula with the Boomerang.

facts.subject: Kokiri Forest
facts.text: The Kokiri live together in a small, protected section of the Lost Woods known as The Kokiri Forest, ruled by the Deku Tree.

evidence.quote: The Kokiri live together in a small, protected section of the Lost Woods known as "The Kokiri Forest."  Ruled by their benevolent demigod, The Deku Tree, the Kokiri live together in peaceful harmony.

facts.subject: Sacred Forest Meadow
facts.text: The Sacred Forest Meadow is located in the midst of the Lost Woods.

evidence.quote: In the midst of the Lost Woods there is a meadow, the Sacred Forest Meadow, which some Kokiri are known to visit periodically.

facts.subject: Forest Temple
facts.text: The Forest Temple is located in the midst of the Sacred Forest Meadow.

evidence.quote: In the midst of this meadow is the Forest Temple.

facts.subject: Zora's River
facts.text: The land of the Zoras is north of the Lost Woods, and they call Zora's River in the east and Lake Hylia in the south their home.

evidence.quote: North of the Lost Woods is the land of the Zoras...In addition to their mystic fountain and the aquatic caverns that make their home, the Zora call Zora's River in the east and Lake Hylia in the south their home.

facts.subject: Water Temple
facts.text: The Water Temple lies deep beneath Lake Hylia.

evidence.quote: Deep beneath Lake Hylia lies the Water Temple.

facts.subject: Desert Colossus
facts.text: The Desert Colossus is hidden in the midst of the Haunted Wasteland and is revealed to be the Spirit Temple.

evidence.quote: Hidden in the midst of the Haunted Wasteland is the Desert Colossus, an ancient oasis and home of the Gerudos.  The Desert Colossus is actually revealed to be the Spirit Temple.

facts.subject: Kakariko Village
facts.text: Kakariko Village is in the northeast corner of Hyrule, nestled at the foot of Death Mountain.

evidence.quote: In the northeast corner of Hyrule is the village of Kakariko...Kakariko Village is nestled at the foot of Death Mountain, Hyrule's resident active volcano.

facts.subject: Fire Temple
facts.text: The Fire Temple is located in the middle of Death Mountain's active crater.

evidence.quote: The Fire Temple is found in the middle of Death Mountain's active crater.

facts.subject: Hyrule Castle
facts.text: Hyrule Castle lies to the west of Death Mountain and contains a Market and housing for citizens and the Royal Family.

evidence.quote: To the west of Death Mountain lies Hyrule Castle.  Home to the Hylians, and Hyrule's namesake, Hyrule Castle contains a Market, and housing for the citizens of Hyrule and it's Royal Family.

facts.subject: Lon Lon Ranch
facts.text: Lon Lon Ranch is in the middle of Hyrule Field and is home to Talon, Malon, and Ingo.

evidence.quote: All of Hyrule is connected by a vast, sparsely forested field, and in the middle of this field is Lon Lon Ranch.  Home to Talon, his daughter Malon and their assistant, Ingo, Lon Lon Ranch provides the horses that the Hylians use to cross the field.

facts.subject: Gerudos
facts.text: The Gerudos are mostly female with only a single male born every one hundred years, and their fortress borders the Haunted Wasteland.

evidence.quote: The Gerudos are an earthy, secretive race whose people are mostly female.  Only a single male Gerudo is born every one hundred years...The Fortress borders along a desert, known only as the Haunted Wasteland.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula Token
facts.text: Rolling into the tree on the island in the southeast of Zora's Fountain reveals a Gold Skulltula that yields a token when killed.

evidence.quote: swim to the island in the very southeast part of the Fountain.  Roll into the tree to find a Gold Skulltula.  Kill it and take it's token.

facts.subject: Great Fairy's Fountain
facts.text: Dropping a bomb between two boulders against the wall reveals a cave leading to the Great Fairy's Fountain.

evidence.quote: Drop a bomb between the two boulders against the wall, and the wall will explode open revealing a massive cave opening.  Go through the cave to find your third Great Fairy's Fountain.

facts.subject: Farore's Wind
facts.text: Playing Zelda's Lullaby on the Triforce emblem summons the Great Fairy, who grants Farore's Wind.

evidence.quote: Run forward to the fountain, stand on the Triforce emblem and play Zelda's Lullaby to make the Dominatrix appear.  This time, you'll get Farore's Wind, a spell which lets you set checkpoints in Dungeons.

facts.subject: Jabu-Jabu's Belly
facts.text: Offering a bottled fish while standing in front of Jabu Jabu's mouth causes him to inhale Link into Jabu-Jabu's Belly.

evidence.quote: Go to the west side of the area, and climb up onto the altar in front of Jabu Jabu.  Stand directly in front of his mouth, and use the Fish you captured in the Bottle.  Jabu Jabu will inhale you right along with the Fish.

facts.subject: Parasitic Tentacles
facts.text: Parasitic tentacles blocking various areas of Jabu-Jabu's Belly must be destroyed to reach the elevator to the boss chamber.

evidence.quote: In the dungeon, players must try to activate an elevator in Jabu-Jabu's throat, which leads to the boss' chamber.  This is easier said then done, however, as several areas of Jabu-Jabu's Belly are blocked by parasitic tentacles, which must be destroyed first.

facts.subject: Octorok
facts.text: In the entrance room, Octoroks can be defeated using the Slingshot, and Shaboms can be defeated with Deku Nuts.

evidence.quote: Run forward a few feet, and a pair of Octoroks will appear on the left and right.  Kill them with your Slingshot, then use Deku Nuts to kill the Shaboms (the floating bubble enemies).

facts.subject: Entrance Ceiling Switch
facts.text: Shooting the yellow bump on the ceiling of the entrance room with the Slingshot unseals the door at the end of the hall.

evidence.quote: Run to the north end of the room and shoot the large yellow bump on the ceiling with your Slingshot.  The "door" at the end of the hall will unseal.  Go through it.

facts.subject: Biri
facts.text: A Biri can be stunned with a Deku Nut and then finished off with a sword strike.

evidence.quote: If a Biri gets too close, use a Deku Nut to stun it.  You actually can then kill it with your sword once it's stunned, but it's far easier to just avoid them.

facts.subject: Pit Room East Door
facts.text: Carrying Ruto through the east door on the lower level leads out of the Pit Room.

evidence.quote: Pick Ruto up, then leave through the east door, which should be behind you as you land from the upper level.

facts.subject: Water Room Switch
facts.text: Stepping on the switch in the center of the Water Room causes the water level to rise and sends Ruto back to the Pit Room if she is in the pit.

evidence.quote: Jump down into the pit, but be very careful that you don't step on the switch in the middle of the room.  The water level will rise, and Ruto (who doesn't like water... go figure) will return to the Pit Room.

facts.subject: Stinger
facts.text: Submerged Stingers can be forced to jump out using Deku Nuts and then killed with the Slingshot.

evidence.quote: Use Deku Nuts to make the Stingers (the submerged enemies whose fins you can see) jump up, and kill them with the Slingshot.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula Token
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula hangs on the west ivy wall of the Water Room, and raising the water level allows Link to climb up and collect its token.

evidence.quote: Once you have killed all of the Stingers, turn to the "ivy" covered wall to the west.  Kill the Gold Skulltula on the wall with the Slingshot.  Next, jump onto the switch, and the water level will rise.  Climb onto the "ivy" on the west wall, and up into the alcove, grabbing the Token on the way.

facts.subject: Fairy
facts.text: Destroying the pots in the west alcove of the Water Room reveals a Fairy and Slingshot Seeds.

evidence.quote: Destroy the pots in the alcove to find a Fairy and some Seeds.

facts.subject: Water Room Ceiling Switch
facts.text: Shooting the switch on the ceiling of the northern hallway with the Slingshot unlocks the door at the end of the hall.

evidence.quote: shoot the switch on the ceiling with your Slingshot (or you can even use Ruto to nail the switch if you're feeling sadistic.  The door at the end of the hall will unlock.  Go through it.

facts.subject: Elevator
facts.text: Riding the elevator while carrying Ruto brings Link to the upper level of the Pit Room.

evidence.quote: Get on the elevator, and ride it to the top of the Pit Room while carrying Ruto.

facts.subject: Business Scrub
facts.text: A submerged tunnel in the Elevator Room leads to a Business Scrub selling Deku Nuts.

evidence.quote: the submerged tunnel leads to a Business Scrub who sells overpriced Deku Nuts.

facts.subject: Pit Room Upper Level
facts.text: Crossing the upper floor of the Pit Room while avoiding Biri and floor holes leads to the opposite door.

evidence.quote: Run straight across the room to the opposite door, avoiding Biri and the pits in the floor.

facts.subject: Yellow Switch
facts.text: Stepping onto the yellow switch in the Crawling Hallway requires Link to be carrying Ruto to activate and unlock the door.

evidence.quote: Run to the right, and step onto the yellow switch while carrying Ruto.  Normally, your weight alone wouldn't be enough, but with Ruto's help then the switch will activate.  Go through the unlocked door in front of the switch.

facts.subject: Boomerang
facts.text: Defeating all the Stingers in the Stinger Room spawns a chest containing the Boomerang.

evidence.quote: this room is crawling with Stingers.  Use Deku Nuts or run in front of their paths to reveal them.  Kill them with your Slingshot.  Once they are all dead, a chest will appear.  Open it to find the Boomerang, an important weapon for Young Link.

facts.subject: Boomerang
facts.text: The Boomerang can be used to retrieve Gold Skulltula tokens from high and distant places.

evidence.quote: Most importantly, however, it lets you claim Skulltula Tokens from a range, finally giving you access to those troublesome Gold Skulltulas you may have seen lurking in high places.

facts.subject: Blue Switch
facts.text: The blue switch in the Crawling Hallway must be held down by leaving Princess Ruto on top of it to keep the door unlocked.

evidence.quote: Jump onto the switch while carrying Ruto, and it will press down.  However, if you step off the switch then it will rise again.  You'll have to leave Ruto behind on the switch, by stepping down on it, then pressing A to leave Ruto on it.  Go through the door once you've jammed the button, leaving Ruto behind.

facts.subject: Orange Tentacle
facts.text: Striking the narrow segment near the base of the Orange Tentacle four times with the Boomerang destroys it and removes other orange tentacles in the dungeon.

evidence.quote: Z-Target it, and use your Boomerang to attack the narrow segment near the base of the tentacle.  It will then retract into the wall.  You need to strike that segment three more times with the boomerang...Killing the Orange Tentacle will remove all of the other orange tentacles blocking passage to other areas of the dungeon.

facts.subject: Dungeon Map
facts.text: A chest containing the Dungeon Map appears in the room once the Orange Tentacle is defeated.

evidence.quote: A chest will appear once the Tentacle dies, open it to find the Dungeon Map.

facts.subject: Princess Ruto
facts.text: Speak with her when you land, and speak with her again, and she'll agree to come with you if you help her find her sacred stone in Jabu-Jabu's belly, and you now get the privilege of carrying Ruto around with you everywhere you go.

evidence.quote: Speak with her when you land, and she'll accidentally let slip that she lost a sacred stone in Jabu-Jabu's belly.  Speak with her again, and she'll agree to come with you, but only if you help her find her stone first.  You now get the privilege of carrying Ruto around with you everywhere you go.

facts.subject: Princess Ruto
facts.text: Ruto waits on the other side of the door in the Crawling Hallway to be picked up.

evidence.quote: Ruto will be waiting for you on the other side of the door.

facts.subject: Crawling Hallway
facts.text: From the blue switch, head to the left through the unblocked door to reach the Shabom Room.

evidence.quote: Pick the royal pain up, then go to the left from the blue switch.  This door is now unblocked.  Go through it.

facts.subject: Shabom Room
facts.text: Defeating all the Shaboms within forty seconds reveals a chest containing the Compass.

evidence.quote: This room requires you to kill a pack of Shaboms in forty seconds...Use both to defeat all of the Shaboms.  A chest will appear upon their demise.  Open it to find the Compass.

facts.subject: Crawling Hallway
facts.text: In the Crawling Hallway, proceed down the hall, take a left, go straight, and take another left to reach the door to the Blue Tentacle Room.

evidence.quote: Go down the hall, take a left, go straight, then left again.  Go through the door.

facts.subject: Blue Tentacle
facts.text: Hitting the Blue Tentacle with the Boomerang four times while dodging its strikes defeats it and removes all Blue Tentacles in the dungeon.

evidence.quote: Hit it with the boomerang, run forward to make it strike at you, then hit it with the boomerang again while dodging the attack.  Hit it four times to kill it.  All of the Blue Tentacles around the dungeon will now disappear.

facts.subject: Crawling Hallway
facts.text: In the Crawling Hallway, go right down the hall and take another right to reach the door to the Green Tentacle Room.

evidence.quote: Go right down the hall, then take another right.  Go through the door at the end of the hall.

facts.subject: Green Tentacle
facts.text: Eliminating the Biri and striking the Green Tentacle four times with the Boomerang defeats it and makes all Green Tentacles disappear.

evidence.quote: Eliminate the Biri first, then turn your attention to the Tentacle.  Hit it with the boomerang, run forward to make it strike at you, then hit it with the boomerang again while dodging the attack.  Hit it four times to kill it.  All of the Green Tentacles around the dungeon will now disappear.

facts.subject: Crawling Hallway
facts.text: Running straight across the Crawling Hallway leads back to the Pit Room.

evidence.quote: Run straight across the hallway back to the Pit Room.

facts.subject: Pit Room
facts.text: Dropping down the pit closest to the west wall, to the right when entering from the Crawling Hallway, accesses the lower area with Gold Skulltulas.

evidence.quote: If you weren't paying attention the last time you were here, the pit is the one closest to the west wall, to the right as you come in from the Crawling Hallway.  Drop down this pit.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula Token
facts.text: Facing north after dropping down the west pit reveals two Gold Skulltulas on the wall that can be defeated and collected with the Boomerang.

evidence.quote: When you land, set down Ruto and face the north.  You will see not one, but two Gold Skulltulas on the wall.  Kill them both with the Boomerang, then use the Boomerang again to claim their Tokens.

facts.subject: Bigocto
facts.text: Bigocto's weakpoint is a large green eye on his backside, which can be damaged with Jump Attacks after stunning him with the Boomerang.

evidence.quote: His weakpoint is a large green "eye" on his backside.  The Bigocto is vulnerable to the Boomerang - it stuns him and locks him in place...Once you have reached his backside, stun him with the Boomerang, and use a Jump Attack to damage his green eye.

facts.subject: Bigocto
facts.text: Two Jump Attacks to Bigocto's green eye will defeat him.

evidence.quote: Two Jump Attacks will defeat the Bigocto.

facts.subject: Bigocto Room
facts.text: Stepping onto the middle platform after defeating Bigocto raises the elevator to a hallway leading south.

evidence.quote: After the Bigocto is dead, step onto the middle platform and the elevator will rise...Run south down the hall and through the door, killing any Biri who get in your way.

facts.subject: Pink Things
facts.text: Stunning the Pink Things with the Boomerang allows Link to jump across them to reach the next door.

evidence.quote: Unfortunately, the only way to get across them is to stun them with the Boomerang.  Stun the first one with the Boomerang, then jump out onto it.  Then stun the second one, then jump to the door.

facts.subject: Blue Switch
facts.text: In the Elevator Room, a box from near the Pit Room door must be placed on the blue switch to keep it depressed.

evidence.quote: Run around to the door by the Pit Room and grab one of the boxes, then step onto the blue button.  The button will depress.  Drop the box so that it sits on the button, forcing it to stay activated.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula Token
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is located on the ivy wall in the southeast side of the Biri Room.

evidence.quote: Kill all of the Biri around the room, then go around to the southeast side of the room.  Kill the Gold Skulltula on the ivy wall, and climb up to take it's token.

facts.subject: North Door
facts.text: Hitting the switch to the right from the top of the ivy wall with the Boomerang unlocks the door in the north end of the room.

evidence.quote: At the top, look to the right to see a switch.  Z-Target it and use the Boomerang to hit it.  The door in the north end of the room will unlock.

facts.subject: Barinade
facts.text: In Barinade's first phase, circle the boss to avoid lightning bolts and sever the tentacles attached to the ceiling using the Boomerang.

evidence.quote: His main attack in this form is to shoot bolts of lightning at you with the "satellite dishes" on his head.  Z-Target the tentacles attached to the ceiling, and begin circling the boss...Destroy the tentacles attached to the ceiling with the Boomerang.

facts.subject: Barinade
facts.text: Stunning Barinade's base with the Boomerang detaches the circling Baris, allowing them to be destroyed with the Boomerang.

evidence.quote: Dodge through the circling Biris, and stun the boss by striking it's base with the Boomerang.  The Baris will release from their bonding to Barinade, and become vulnerable.  Destroy them with your Boomerang.

facts.subject: Barinade
facts.text: After all Baris are destroyed, stun Barinade with the Boomerang and strike its base with five Jump Attacks to defeat it.

evidence.quote: Once all of the Baris are dead, then you enter the boss' final phase, in which you are finally able to damage him.  Stun him with your Boomerang, then run into strike it's base with Jump Attacks...After five Jump Attacks, Barinade will be defeated.

facts.subject: Barinade
facts.text: Defeating Barinade leaves behind a Heart Container.

evidence.quote: Take the Heart Container that Barinade leaves behind, then enter the ring of shimmering blue light.

facts.subject: Princess Ruto
facts.text: Entering the blue teleport ring takes Link outside where Princess Ruto gives him the Zora Sapphire upon agreeing to marry her.

evidence.quote: The ring will teleport you and Ruto outside.  Ruto will give you the Zora Sapphire, but only if you agree to marry her.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula Token
facts.text: At nighttime, a Gold Skulltula is located on the wall on the west side of the tree trunk that arches over the water in Zora's Fountain.

evidence.quote: Climb up onto the large tree trunk which arches over the body of water in the south of the zone.  Go to the west side of the tree trunk and look on the wall to see a Gold Skulltula.  Kill it and take it's token with your Boomerang.

facts.subject: Zora's Fountain
facts.text: The cave entrance on the west side of Zora's Fountain leads back to Zora's Domain.

evidence.quote: Head back through the cave entrance in the west side of the zone to return to Zora's Domain.

facts.subject: Zora's Domain
facts.text: Diving off the waterfall to the right of King Zora's Throne Room leads to an underwater tunnel to Lake Hylia.

evidence.quote: From King Zora's Throne Room, go to the right and dive off of the waterfall.  Swim down into the water and into the tunnel to Lake Hylia.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula Token
facts.text: At nighttime in Lake Hylia, a Gold Skulltula is found on the rear side of the observatory when viewed from the wooden drawbridge.

evidence.quote: Look on the rear side of the observatory from the wooden drawbridge to find a Gold Skulltula.  Use the Boomerang to kill it and claim it's token.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula Token
facts.text: Bombing the center of a stone circle at the north edge of the quarry in Hyrule Field reveals a pit with a Gold Skulltula in the cow alcove behind webbing.

evidence.quote: Head into the quarry-like area, and go the north edge of it to find a circle of stones.  Drop a bomb in the middle of this circle of stones to find a hidden pit...Head for the alcove with the cow, and look on the wall in the rear of the alcove to find a Gold Skulltula.  Kill it and take it's token with the Boomerang.

facts.subject: Hyrule Field
facts.text: Traveling west from the quarry area of Hyrule Field enters Gerudo Valley.

evidence.quote: Go west to enter Gerudo Valley.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula Token
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is located just above the small waterfall near the log bridge in Gerudo Valley at night and its token can be retrieved with the Boomerang.

evidence.quote: Look just above the small waterfall to find a Gold Skulltula.  Kill it and take it's token with the Boomerang.

facts.subject: Gerudo Valley River
facts.text: Diving into the river from the drawbridge west of the log bridge carries Link downstream to Lake Hylia, which connects back to Zora's Domain via an underwater passage.

evidence.quote: Head out to the drawbridge west of the log bridge and dive into the river.  Ride it down stream back to Lake Hylia and use the underwater passage to return to Zora's Domain.

facts.subject: Zora's Domain Entrance Path
facts.text: Climbing to the path leading to the front entrance allows Link to return to Zora's River and ride it downstream to Hyrule Field.

evidence.quote: Climb up to the path that leads to the front entrance, return to Zora's River, and ride it downstream back to Hyrule Field.

facts.subject: Lone Tree Secret Pit
facts.text: Placing a bomb on the north side of the lone tree in the northeast corner of Hyrule Field reveals a hidden pit.

evidence.quote: Before you enter the Village, go north from the stairs to find a lone tree in the very northeast corner of the field.  Place a bomb on the north side of the tree to blast open a pit.  Drop down.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula Token
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula rests on webbing high on the wall at the end of the secret pit near Kakariko Village and can be killed to collect its token with the Boomerang.

evidence.quote: Run to the end of the pit and kill the Big Skulltula.  Look high on the wall, where a Gold Skulltula rests on a bit of webbing.  Kill the Gold Skulltula and take it's token with your Boomerang.

facts.subject: Giant's Wallet
facts.text: Speaking with the man in the rear of the House of Skulltula after defeating 30 Gold Skulltulas rewards Link with the Giant's Wallet, which holds up to 500 rupees.

evidence.quote: Speak with the man in the rear of the room, and he'll award you for killing 30 Gold Skulltulas with the Giant's Wallet.  This is the largest wallet in the game, which can hold up to 500 rupees.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula Token
facts.text: At night, a Gold Skulltula appears high on the wall at the far south end of the second row of gravestones in the southeast corner of Kakariko Graveyard.

evidence.quote: Head for the southeast corner of the graveyard, to the far south end of the second row of gravestones.  Look high on the wall to see another Gold Skulltula.  Kill it and take it's token with the Boomerang.

facts.subject: Magic Bean Soft Earth Patch
facts.text: A soft patch of earth where a Magic Bean can be planted is located in the northwest corner of Kakariko Graveyard.

evidence.quote: Now, head for the northwest corner of the graveyard where there is a soft patch of earth.  Plant one of your Magic Beans there.

facts.subject: Kakariko Windmill Door
facts.text: From the graveyard stairs in Kakariko Village, taking a right leads up a long staircase to the entrance of the Windmill behind a crate.

evidence.quote: From Kakariko Graveyard, take a right up the long staircase.  Enter the door on the right at the top of the stairs, behind the crate to enter the Windmill.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: A Piece of Heart sits high on a ledge to the left upon entering the Kakariko Windmill and can be grabbed using the Boomerang.

evidence.quote: Look to the left as you enter to see a Piece of Heart high on a ledge.  Get closer to it and use the Boomerang to snag it.

facts.subject: Dodongo's Cavern Soft Earth Patch
facts.text: A soft patch of earth suitable for planting a Magic Bean is located outside the mouth of Dodongo's Cavern on Death Mountain Trail.

evidence.quote: Start heading up the trail and enter the mouth of Dodongo's Cavern.  Plant one of your Magic Beans in the soft patch of earth, then enter the Cavern.

facts.subject: Antechamber Moving Platform
facts.text: Riding the moving platform on the right in front of the giant Dodongo's head takes Link to the second floor tunnel opposite the plaque.

evidence.quote: Head into the main chamber, out to in front of the giant Dodongo's head.  Board the moving platform on the right and ride it to the top.  Get off on the second floor, and enter the tunnel opposite the plaque.

facts.subject: Blade Trap Room Tunnel
facts.text: Dropping to the bottom level of the Blade Trap Room and climbing the southwest ladder leads through a tunnel back to the Antechamber.

evidence.quote: Jump off the cliff to the right as you enter the room to drop down to the bottom level.  Dodge the blade trap and climb the ladder near the southwest corner of the room.  Go through the tunnel back to the Antechamber.

facts.subject: Antechamber Wooden Bridge
facts.text: Crossing the wooden bridge on the second floor of the Antechamber leads to the door on the opposite side while avoiding Fire Keese.

evidence.quote: Cross the wooden bridge and enter the door on the opposite side.  Kill any Fire Keese who bother you.

facts.subject: Pillar Room Switch
facts.text: Pulling the Armos Statue away from the ladder on the south side of the Pillar Room allows Link to climb up and step on the pillar switch to unlock the doors.

evidence.quote: Kill the Fire Keese, then pull aside the Armos Statue blocking the ladder on the south side of the room.  Step on the switch on top of the pillar to unlock the doors, then leave through the north door.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula Token
facts.text: In the Bomb Flower Room, climbing the ivy walls to the iron platform allows Link to reach an alcove on the north side and retrieve a Gold Skulltula token with the Boomerang.

evidence.quote: Climb up the ivy walls to the top of the iron platform.  Look into the alcove on the north side of the room, and use the Boomerang to kill the Gold Skulltula and take it's token.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula Token
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is perched on the second story window of the left building by the entrance arch of Lon Lon Ranch at night.

evidence.quote: Head towards the arch leading into the field, and stop to look at the second story window on the left building.  Kill the Gold Skulltula on the window, and take it's token with the Boomerang.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula Token
facts.text: At Lon Lon Ranch at night, a Gold Skulltula is found on the southwest wall to the right of the mill.

evidence.quote: Head out into the field, towards the southwest wall, to the right of the mill.  Kill the Gold Skulltula and take it's token with the Boomerang, then return to Hyrule Field.

facts.subject: Running Man
facts.text: Speaking to the Running Man in Hyrule Field while wearing the Bunny Hood after he pauses running rewards Link with 500 rupees.

evidence.quote: Once he has stopped, speak to him while wearing the Bunny Hood, and he will give you 500 rupees for it.

facts.subject: Zelda's Escape
facts.text: Approaching the closed gates of Hyrule Castle triggers a cutscene where Zelda and Impa flee and Zelda throws the Ocarina of Time into the moat.

evidence.quote: When you get close enough, a cut scene will take place.  Zelda and Impa will race out of the gates, and Zelda will do a really fantastic John Elway impression by throwing you the Ocarina of Time, which will land in the moat.

facts.subject: Ocarina of Time
facts.text: Diving into the moat water outside Hyrule Castle recovers the Ocarina of Time, triggering a telepathic message from Zelda teaching the Song of Time.

evidence.quote: After the cutscene is over, dive into the water of the moat to get the Ocarina of Time, at which point Zelda will contact you telepathically and teach you the Song of Time.

facts.subject: Zora's Domain Waterfall Pool
facts.text: Swimming to the bottom of the deep pool to the right of the waterfall at the entrance to Zora's Domain leads to a warp tunnel connecting to the Lost Woods.

evidence.quote: Once you reach the entrance to Zora's Domain, look to the right of the waterfall, where there is a deep pool of water.  Swim to it's bottom, and enter the tunnel at the bottom to warp to Lost Woods.

facts.subject: Lost Woods Soft Earth Patch
facts.text: Dropping a Bottled Bug into the soft earth patch past the Business Scrub reveals a Gold Skulltula, and a Magic Bean can be planted in the soil.

evidence.quote: Drop a Bottled Bug into the patch of soft earth to reveal a Gold Skulltula (if you didn't get it last time you were here), and remember to recapture one of the three bugs that appears.  Plant one of the Magic Beans, then head for the large tree in the back of the clearing.

facts.subject: Forest Stage Invisible Hole
facts.text: Dropping into the hidden hole marked by hovering butterflies near the large tree leads to the Forest Stage.

evidence.quote: In the grass, there is a cluster of butterflies.  The butterflies are actually hovering over an invisible hole.  Drop down into this hole to enter the Forest Stage.

facts.subject: Lost Woods Path
facts.text: From the Forest Stage exit, heading through the log tunnel, right at the crossroads, right at the pool, left at the stone arch, right at the crossroads, and straight leads to the southwest tunnel.

evidence.quote: Run forward through the log tunnel, and go right at the crossroads on the other side.  Go right again at the pool of water, and left at the stone arch.  Turn right again at the next crossroads, and go straight at the next.  Enter the tunnel in the southwest corner of the next area.

facts.subject: Lost Woods Clearing Soft Earth Patch
facts.text: Dropping a Bottled Bug into the soft patch of earth in the southwest clearing uncovers a Gold Skulltula and allows planting a Magic Bean.

evidence.quote: Drop a Bottled Bug into the patch of soft earth to get the Gold Skulltula (if you didn't get it last time), and remember to recapture one of the bugs who comes out.  Plant one of your Magic Beans in the patch.

facts.subject: Deku Stick Upgrade
facts.text: A Deku Stick upgrade can be bought from the Business Scrub located in the rear of the valley.

evidence.quote: If you still haven't bought the Deku Stick Upgrade from the Business Scrub in the rear of this valley, then do so now.

facts.subject: Lost Woods Tunnel Path
facts.text: Turning around and passing back through the log tunnel, hanging right through the following log tunnel, and taking a right leads into Kokiri Forest.

evidence.quote: Turn around, and go back through the log tunnel.  Hang a right and go through the next log tunnel, then go to the right to enter Kokiri Forest.

facts.subject: Mask of Truth
facts.text: Paying the mask trader fifty rupees for the Bunny Hood completes the Happy Mask Trading sequence, unlocking the Mask of Truth which allows Link to read Gossip Stones.

evidence.quote: Speak with the mask trader, and pay him fifty rupees for the Bunny Hood.  You have now finished the entire Happy Mask Trading sequence, and can borrow any Mask that you want from the store.  For now, take the Mask of Truth, which lets you get hints from the Gossip Stones around the world, and also gets you a Deku Nut upgrade.

facts.subject: Musical Frogs
facts.text: Playing the Song of Time for the Musical Frogs at Zora's River awards Link fifty rupees.

evidence.quote: On the way, stop off at the Musical Frogs and play them the Song of Time to make back fifty rupees.

facts.subject: Deku Nuts Upgrade
facts.text: Wearing the Mask of Truth and speaking to the Deku Scrub Chief in the Forest Stage increases the number of Deku Nuts Link can carry.

evidence.quote: Put on the Mask of Truth, then step forward.  The Deku Scrubs down here will stare at you.  Go and speak to their Chief (the Scrub with the "mustache") on the right side of the  room, and he will increase the number of Deku Nuts you can carry.

facts.subject: Kokiri Forest
facts.text: Dropping a bug into the soft earth patch behind the shop on the east end of Kokiri Forest reveals a Gold Skulltula carrying a token.

evidence.quote: Jump down to the bottom level of Kokiri Forest and head for the shop on the east end.  Look for patch of soft earth behind the shop.  Drop a bug in it (remember to recapture one), and kill the Gold Skulltula that appears.  Take it's token, then plant the Magic Beans.

facts.subject: Magic Beans
facts.text: Plant Magic Beans in the soft earth patch behind the shop in Kokiri Forest.

evidence.quote: Look for patch of soft earth behind the shop.  Drop a bug in it (remember to recapture one), and kill the Gold Skulltula that appears.  Take it's token, then plant the Magic Beans.

facts.subject: Farore's Wind
facts.text: Farore's Wind can be cast at the start of the Deku Tree dungeon to warp back immediately after obtaining the Gold Skulltula.

evidence.quote: If you like, use Farore's Wind at the start of the dungeon so that you can warp right back to the start as soon as you have claimed the Gold Skulltula.

facts.subject: The Trunk
facts.text: Dropping down the hole in the middle of the first floor leads to the sub-basement of the Deku Tree.

evidence.quote: Drop down the hole in the middle of the first floor to reach the sub-basement.

facts.subject: sub-basement
facts.text: Climb onto the stone block on the north side of the sub-basement, jump to the upper ledge, and crawl through the west tunnel.

evidence.quote: Climb up onto the stone block on the north side of the room, jump onto the upper ledge, and crawl through the tunnel on the west side.

facts.subject: Small Nest
facts.text: In the Small Nest, light a Deku Stick on the torch to burn through the webbing in the northwest part of the room.

evidence.quote: Kill the Larva, then light a Deku Stick on the torch and use it to burn through the webbing in the northwest part of the room.

facts.subject: Small Nest
facts.text: Bomb the sealed wall past the webbing and open the door to enter the hidden room.

evidence.quote: Kill the Deku Baba on the other side, then bomb the sealed wall.  Open the door on the other side.

facts.subject: Hidden Room
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is located to the right of the door in the hidden room, and its token can be retrieved using the Boomerang.

evidence.quote: On the right of the door is a Gold Skulltula.  Kill it and take it's token using the Boomerang, then leave the dungeon and return to the Hyrule Castle Market.

facts.subject: Hyrule Castle Market
facts.text: The Temple of Time is located to the right of the Happy Mask Shop in the Hyrule Castle Market.

evidence.quote: Go to the Temple of Time.  It's to the right of the Happy Mask Shop.

facts.subject: Door of Time
facts.text: Playing the Song of Time on the red carpeting before the Door of Time with all three Spiritual Stones and the Ocarina of Time opens the Door of Time.

evidence.quote:
Stand on the red carpeting, take out the Ocarina of Time and play the Song of Time.

The three Spiritual Stones, together with the Ocarina of Time and the Song of Time, will open the Door of Time.

facts.subject: Master Sword
facts.text: Drawing the Master Sword from its pedestal beyond the Door of Time awakens Link as an adult seven years in the future.

evidence.quote: Run through the door, where you will find a pedestal which contains a Sword in a Stone.  This is, of course, the Master Sword.  Draw the Master Sword from it's pedestal.

When you pulled the Master Sword from it's pedestal, you were not yet ready for it's power.  The Sword placed you in a magical form of sleep for seven years, and in that time Ganondorf took the Triforce of Power (one of the fragments of the Triforce) for his own, and took control of Hyrule.

facts.subject: Rauru
facts.text: Upon waking, Rauru grants Link the Light Medallion and sends him back to the Temple of Time.

evidence.quote: When you awake, you will meet Rauru, the only awakened Sage.  To defeat Ganondorf, the other five Sages must be found and awakened in their respective Temples.  Rauru will give you the Light Medallion, a symbol of his power, and transport you back to the Temple of Time.

facts.subject: Sheik
facts.text: Sheik meets Link at the Temple of Time and advises him to visit Kakariko Village before heading to the Forest Temple.

evidence.quote: Once back at the Temple of Time, you will meet Sheik, the last of Impa's tribe of warriors....Sheik also advises you that, before you run off to the Forest Temple, you head for Kakariko Village, where you will find an item of great value.

facts.subject: Redead
facts.text: As an adult, Hyrule Castle Market is overrun with Redeads, which drop Magic Pots when killed.

evidence.quote: Hyrule Castle Market is now filled with Redeads.  This is actually a good thing - Redeads drop lots of Magic Pots, and this square is so full of them that refilling your Magic Pots is three easy kills away.

facts.subject: Poe Shop
facts.text: The former Gatehouse at the Hyrule Castle Drawbridge contains a Poe Shop where the shopkeeper buys captured Poes and Big Poes and offers the fourth bottle.

evidence.quote: If you want, you can enter the former Gatehouse to find a new Poe Shop, where the shopkeeper will buy your captured Poes and Big Poes.  The most important function of the Poe Shop is it is the place where you acquire the game's fourth and final bottle.

facts.subject: Hyrule Castle Drawbridge
facts.text: The shattered drawbridge remains open day and night leading out to Hyrule Field.

evidence.quote: Head northeast and through the drawbridge, which is now shattered and remains open day or night.

facts.subject: Epona
facts.text: Pay Ingo 10 rupees to enter the paddock, then play Epona's Song to summon the grown Epona.

evidence.quote: Pay him 10 rupees, and when you enter the paddock, ignore the horse that Ingo offers you.  Play Epona's Song, and the now fully-grown Epona will run towards you.

facts.subject: Ingo
facts.text: Speaking with Ingo while riding Epona prompts him to challenge Link to a horse race for 50 rupees.

evidence.quote: Now, speak with Ingo WHILE you are riding Epona (z-target him to make it easier), and Ingo will challenge you to a race for 50 rupees.  Accept the challenge.

facts.subject: Epona
facts.text: Defeat Ingo in two consecutive horse races, then sprint with carrots straight at the closed ranch gate to jump over it into Hyrule Field and claim Epona.

evidence.quote: Defeat Ingo, and he'll challenge you to another race.  And this time, if you win, he'll let you keep Epona....Once you defeat Ingo for the second time, he'll honor his bet, but he'll also prevent you from leaving the Ranch by closing the gate.  To make it over the gate, you must run around the path around the paddock in a counter-clockwise pattern.  Once you come around the corner and see the gate, burn all of your carrots at once and charge straight at the gate....Once you make it over the gate, then you will return to Hyrule Field and Epona will become yours.

facts.subject: Cucco
facts.text: Trampling Cuccos in the northeast corner of the pasture while riding Epona triggers an attacking flock that cannot harm Link while mounted.

evidence.quote: If you want to have some fun, you can also trample on the Cuccos in the northeast corner of the pasture, and a flock of Cuccos will appear and begin to attack you.  But because you're on Epona, they can't hurt you.

facts.subject: Big Poe
facts.text: Big Poes appear across Hyrule Field when riding Epona, but killing them requires the Fairy Bow from the Forest Temple.

evidence.quote: Now that you have Epona, you can spot the Big Poes that appear around Hyrule Field.  You can't actually kill them until you get the Fairy Bow from the Forest Temple, however.

facts.subject: Shooting Gallery
facts.text: The previously unfinished building in Kakariko Village is now completed as the adult Shooting Gallery.

evidence.quote: Notice that the unfinished building is now finished; it contains the new Shooting Gallery.  We'll return here once we get the Fairy Bow for the first Bow Upgrade.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: Riding the grown Magic Leaf on the left side of Kakariko Graveyard to the high cliff leads to a crate containing a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: Remember where we planted one of the Magic Beans as Young Link?  A Magic Leaf has now appeared there.  Step onto the Leaf to ride up to a high cliff, which contains a crate.  Roll into the crate to find a Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: flowered gravestone
facts.text: Pulling back the gravestone with flowers next to the Magic Leaf reveals a pit.

evidence.quote: Right next to the Magic Leaf, there is a gravestone with flowers on it.  Grab this gravestone from behind and pull it away to reveal a pit.  Drop down into the pit.

facts.subject: fence jumping
facts.text: Jumping over both fences in the Lon Lon Ranch paddock course earns back the 10 rupees paid to ride.

evidence.quote: Pay him 10 rupees, and when you enter the paddock, ignore the horse that Ingo offers you....Jump over both of the fences in the course to make back your ten rupees, then speak with Ingo.

facts.subject: Dampe
facts.text: Stepping forward in the cave causes Dampe's ghost to challenge Link to a race and start without notice.

evidence.quote:
Step forward a few feet to find the ghost of Dampe.  He will challenge you to a
race, and will start without notice.

facts.subject: Dampe's Race Route
facts.text: To navigate the race, run forward dodging flames, turn right at the hall end, turn left at the next corner, run along the left side between two flames, turn left and immediate right, turn right, left, and left tight, take another tight turn and enter the door; then turn right, right, wide left, enter the wide room, go through the right door, turn left, wide right, through another door, run to the wall, turn right, tight left, jump to the ledge on the left, take a wide left, and tight left into the room with a large pit.

evidence.quote:
Turn right at the halls end, taking the corner tight to dodge a flame.
Turn left at the next corner, taking the turn wide to dodge another flame....Run forward between the pair of flames, running along the left side of the gap.
Turn left and then right immediately on the other side, taking the turn wide to
dodge another flame.  Turn right, then left, then left again, taking the turn
tight.  Take another tight turn on the other side, and go through the door....Take a right on the other side, and another right, and then a wide left.  Run
along the left or right side of the tunnel, then enter the wide room.  Go
through the door on the right.  Take a left, then a wide right, then through
another door.  Run to the wall on the other side, then a right, then a tight
left....Jump onto the ledge to your left, and hug the left wall as you run forward to
dodge more flames.  Take a wide left, then a tight left to enter a tall room
with a large pit in the middle.  Run along the path around the perimeter of the
room and through the door at the top.

facts.subject: Dampe
facts.text: Speaking with Dampe in the room at the top of the race path rewards Link with the Hookshot.

evidence.quote: Speak with Dampe in this room, and he will give you the Hookshot.

facts.subject: Song of Time Blocks
facts.text: Playing the Song of Time makes the two blue blocks disappear, allowing Link to climb the staircase back into the Windmill.

evidence.quote:
Play the Song of Time to make them disappear, then climb up
the staircase on the other side to find yourself back in the Windmill.

facts.subject: Windmill Staircase
facts.text: If not collected as Young Link, a Piece of Heart is located at the top of the Windmill staircase.

evidence.quote:
If you didn't get the Piece of Heart from the Windmill as Young Link, then
you'll get it now at the top of the staircase.

facts.subject: Organ Grinder
facts.text: Standing in front of the Organ Grinder in the Windmill and taking out the Ocarina teaches Link the Song of Storms.

evidence.quote:
Drop down onto the main floor,
and then stand in front of the Organ Grinder in the Windmill.  Take out your
Ocarina of Time, and he'll teach you the Song of Storms.

facts.subject: Man on the Blue Roof
facts.text: Using the Hookshot from the fence outside the Windmill to latch onto the blue roof allows Link to speak to the man gazing at Death Mountain for a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote:
Jump onto the fence in front of the Windmill door, and look to the right to see
a tall building with a blue roof.  Use the Hookshot to latch onto the blue roof
(you should see a red targeting reticule on the roof)....Once you are on
the roof, speak with the man gazing up at Death Mountain to get another Piece
of Heart.

facts.subject: Impa's House
facts.text: At night, Hookshotting onto the roof of the House of Skulltula and then onto the roof of Impa's House leads to a Gold Skulltula on the southern wall.

evidence.quote:
Play the Sun's Song to make it nighttime....Climb up to the
entrance to Impa's House (the large house at the southern edge of town), and
use the Hookshot to get onto the roof of House of Skulltula.  Once there, use
the Hookshot again to reach the roof of Impa's House.  Head to the southern
wall of Impa's House, and kill the Gold Skulltula on the wall.  Take it's
token.

facts.subject: Ganon's Castle Stone Archway
facts.text: At nighttime, a Gold Skulltula is suspended over the lava on the right side of the stone archway outside Ganon's Castle.

evidence.quote:
Make sure it's nighttime, then head forward and around the corner.  Run under
the stone archway, and turn around on the other side.  On the right side of the
archway, suspended over the lava, there is a Gold Skulltula.  Kill it and take
it's token with the Hookshot.

facts.subject: Kokiri Twin's House
facts.text: At nighttime, a Gold Skulltula is located on the back of the tree of the Kokiri Twin's house, on the south side of the pond.

evidence.quote:
Change it to nighttime if you need to, then head for the east side of
the forest to the Kokiri Twin's house.  It's the house on the south side of the
pond with the twin branches coming out of it's top.  Kill the Gold Skulltula on
the back of the tree and take it's token with the Hookshot.

facts.subject: Magic Leaf Behind Shop
facts.text: Riding the Magic Leaf planted behind the Shop carries Link around Kokiri Forest to a hidden alcove containing Rupees.

evidence.quote:
If you planted the Magic Bean behind the Shop as Young Link, then you can now
ride the Magic Leaf on a scenic tour around the forest, finally ending near a
hidden alcove full of Rupees.

facts.subject: Mido
facts.text: Playing Saria's Song for Mido at the pond makes him let Link pass toward the forest stage.

evidence.quote:
At the stone arch, go right to find yourself at the
Pond.  A still-childlike Mido will block your path to the left.  Play him
Saria's Song, and he'll let you pass.

facts.subject: Forest Stage Cliff
facts.text: In the Forest Stage clearing, riding the Magic Leaf up to the cliff above leads to a Gold Skulltula.

evidence.quote:
At the crossroads after Mido, go left to find yourself back in the Forest Stage
clearing.  If you planted the Magic Beans here as a Child, then there will be a
Magic Leaf on the right side of the clearing.  Ride the Magic Leaf up to the
cliff above the clearing, where you will find a Gold Skulltula.  Kill it and
take it's token, then return to the previous crossroads.

facts.subject: Lost Woods Path
facts.text: From the entrance to Kokiri Forest, go right, left, right at the stone arch to Mido, left after Mido, left, left again, and right at the next crossroads to reach the Sacred Forest Meadow.

evidence.quote:
Go right from the entrance to Kokiri Forest,
and then left on the other side...At the stone arch, go right to find yourself at the
Pond.  A still-childlike Mido will block your path to the left.  Play him
Saria's Song, and he'll let you pass....Go left (straight if you're coming from the Pool), and left again on the other
side.  Take a right at the next crossroads to reach the Sacred Forest Meadow.

facts.subject: Moriblin
facts.text: Moriblins patrol the Sacred Forest Meadow maze and can be defeated by waiting for them to face away and shooting their backs with the Hookshot.

evidence.quote:
Moriblins are huge
goblin-like creatures who patrol the passages in the Sacred Forest Meadow....To defeat the Moriblins, wait
for them to face away from you and shoot them in the back with the Hookshot.

facts.subject: Meadow Maze Ladder
facts.text: At the top of the ladder in the Sacred Forest Meadow maze, go left a short distance to find a Gold Skulltula.

evidence.quote:
Climb up out of the pool, and climb up the
ladder on the left (if you see a Moriblin here, then wait for him to turn away
before climbing out of the pool).  At the top of the ladder, go to the left a
short ways to find a Gold Skulltula.

facts.subject: Meadow Maze Pit
facts.text: A pit in the center of the Sacred Forest Meadow maze contains a Fairy Fountain.

evidence.quote:
In the center of the maze, there is a pit
which contains a handy Fairy Fountain.

facts.subject: Monblin
facts.text: The Monblin at the top of the staircase attacks with shockwaves and is defeated by dodging left and right, getting behind him, and hitting his back with two Jump Attacks.

evidence.quote:
Go up the
stairset opposite the ladder, and at the top you'll see a Monblin.  The Monblin
will attack you by sending shockwaves down the long passage.  Dodge the
shockwaves by running to the left and right between each shockwave, and running
around behind the Monblin when you reach him.  Kill the Monblin by performing
two Jump Attacks against his backside, whereupon he will drop a large number of
Rupees.

facts.subject: Sheik
facts.text: Stepping onto the Triforce pedestal past the Monblin triggers Sheik to appear and teach the Minuet of Forest.

evidence.quote:
Once the Monblin is dead, go up the stairset behind him and step onto the large
pedestal inscribed with the Triforce, where a cutscene will introduce you to
Sheik once more.  Sheik will teach you the Minuet of Forest, which will
transport you to this location every time you play the song.

facts.subject: Shattered Stairset Tree Branch
facts.text: Hookshotting the large tree branch above the shattered staircase leads up to the entrance doorway of the Forest Temple.

evidence.quote:
After Sheik departs, use the Hookshot on the large tree branch which hangs
above the shattered stairset.  Once you're at the top of the stairs, go through
the doorway to enter Adult Link's first dungeon.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltulas
facts.text: There are one hundred Gold Skulltulas hidden throughout Hyrule in both time periods of the game in roughly equal portions.

evidence.quote:
Ocarina of Time continues that
tradition with one hundred Gold Skulltulas hidden throughout Hyrule.

Hidden in both time periods of the game in roughly equal portions, the Gold
Skulltulas are the symbols of a curse that affects a wealthy family in Kakariko
Village.

facts.subject: House of Skulltula
facts.text: Finding, destroying, and taking magic tokens from Gold Skulltulas frees members of the cursed family in Kakariko Village, and visiting the House of Skulltula rewards Link with a special item.

evidence.quote:
There are six members in the family total, and finding, destroying,
and taking the magic token from enough Gold Skulltulas will free one of the
family members from his curse.  Visiting the House of Skulltula at that point
will get Link some kind of special item, usually beneficial, sometimes
laughably useless.

facts.subject: Hookshot
facts.text: When Link first reaches adulthood, he must obtain the Hookshot before he can do anything else.

evidence.quote:
The game's beginning, and first three dungeons, are always the same, and when
you first reach adulthood, you MUST obtain the Hookshot before you can do
anything else.

facts.subject: Biggoron Sword Trading Sidequest
facts.text: Once Link has Epona, the Biggoron Sword sidequest can be completed at any time.

evidence.quote:
Once you have Epona, you can complete the Biggoron Sword
Sidequest at ANY time.

facts.subject: Fire Temple
facts.text: The Fire Temple and Ice Cavern can both be completed without the Fairy Bow from the Forest Temple.

evidence.quote:
The Fire Temple and Ice Cavern
can both be completed without the Fairy Bow from the Forest Temple, just as the
Ice Cavern and Forest Temple can be completed without the Megaton Hammer from
the Fire Temple, and the Fire Temple and Forest Temple can be completed without
the Iron Boots from the Ice Cavern.

facts.subject: Water Temple
facts.text: Completing the Ice Cavern and the Forest Temple allows progression to the Water Temple before finishing the Fire Temple.

evidence.quote:
And if you're done with the Ice Cavern and
the Forest Temple, then you can proceed to the Water Temple before finishing
the Fire Temple.

facts.subject: Gerudo Fortress
facts.text: The Gerudo Fortress can be completed at any time once the Forest Temple is finished and Link has both the Fairy Bow and Epona.

evidence.quote:
Additionally, once you finish the Forest Temple and have the
Fairy Bow, and once you have Epona, then the Gerudo Fortress CAN be completed
at ANY time (though this guide will wait until you HAVE to do it).

facts.subject: Bottom of the Well
facts.text: After completing the Forest Temple, Link can return to childhood at any time, making the Bottom of the Well available.

evidence.quote:
Also, once
you have completed the Forest Temple, you can return to your childhood at any
time, at which point The Bottom of the Well also becomes available.

facts.subject: Big Poe Hunting Sidequest
facts.text: The Big Poe hunting sidequest can be completed at any time after obtaining Epona and getting the Fairy Bow.

evidence.quote:
Lastly,
the Big Poe Hunting sidequest can be completed at any time after obtaining
Epona and getting the Fairy Bow.

facts.subject: Shadow Temple
facts.text: The Bottom of the Well mini-dungeon must be completed before the Shadow Temple can be completed.

evidence.quote:
Before the Shadow Temple can be
completed, however, then the Bottom of the Well Mini-Dungeon MUST be completed.

facts.subject: Spirit Temple
facts.object: Bottom of the Well and Gerudo Fortress
facts.text: Both the Bottom of the Well and the Gerudo Fortress must be completed before the Spirit Temple can be attempted.

evidence.quote:
And before the Spirit Temple can even be attempted, BOTH the Bottom of the Well
and the Gerudo Fortress must be completed.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: There are thirty-six hidden Pieces of Heart around Hyrule, and gathering four Pieces of Heart rewards an additional Heart Container, amounting to nine of the game's twenty available Heart Containers from Pieces of Heart.

evidence.quote:
Ocarina also honors it's predecessors with the inclusion of thirty-six hidden
Pieces of Heart.  Each Piece of Heart represents one-quarter of a Heart
Container, and gathering four Pieces of Heart rewards the player with an
additional Heart Container.  With thirty-six total Pieces of Heart hidden
around Hyrule, that amounts to nine of the game's twenty available Heart
Containers from Pieces of Heart.

facts.subject: Forest Temple
facts.text: The main goal in the Forest Temple is to defeat the four Poe Sisters and recover their stolen flames to reactivate the central elevator.

evidence.quote: Near the beginning of the dungeon, four Poe Sisters steal flames from a large altar, which causes an elevator in the middle of the altar to retract.  The main goal in the dungeon is tracking down and killing the Poe Sisters, and reclaiming their flames to reactivate the elevator.

facts.subject: Gray Wolfos
facts.text: Gray Wolfos can be defeated by backflipping out of their attack range and immediately performing a Jump Attack while their back is turned.

evidence.quote: Defeat them the same way you defeated the Gray Wolfos you encountered as a child: wait for them to attack, then backflip out of range, and immediately execute a Jump Attack while their back is turned.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is located at the top-right of the ivy wall near the trees at the Forest Temple entrance.

evidence.quote: Once you are at the top of the tree, look to the top-right of the ivy wall to find a Gold Skulltula.

facts.subject: Forest Temple Entrance
facts.text: A Small Key is inside a chest at the end of the adjacent tree branch above the entrance courtyard.

evidence.quote: Edge along to the edge of the tree branch, then jump to the tree branch adjacent to it.  Edge along this tree branch to the end, and open the chest to find a Small Key.

facts.subject: Big Skulltula
facts.text: A single shot from the Hookshot instantly kills a Big Skulltula.

evidence.quote: Now, a single shot from the Hookshot to any part of the Big Skulltula will kill it instantly.

facts.subject: The Torch Room
facts.text: In the Torch Room, the four Poe Sisters appear and steal the four torch flames, lowering the central elevator.

evidence.quote: Run forward into the rooms a short ways, and the four Poe Sisters will appear and steal the four flames from the torches in the center of the room.  This will cause the elevator in the center of the room to lower.

facts.subject: The Torch Room
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is located to the right at the top of the stairs in the Torch Room.

evidence.quote: At the top of the stairs, look to the right to spot a Gold Skulltula.  Kill it and take it's token with the Hookshot, then go through the door at the top of the stairs.

facts.subject: Stalfos
facts.text: Stalfos will not attack if one is Z-Targeted, and they become vulnerable to attacks from behind or the side immediately following their attacks, especially jump attacks.

evidence.quote: The Stalfos are slightly chivalrous, and will not attack you if you have one of them Z-Targeted.  So Z-Target one of them as quick as you can... Stalfos can block most of your attacks, but just like Wolfos they are briefly vulnerable immediately after they attack.  This is especially true after they perform their Jump Attack.  Attack them from the side or from behind immediately after they attack to dispatch them easily.

facts.subject: Lower Stalfos Chamber
facts.text: Defeating both Stalfos in the Lower Stalfos Chamber causes a chest containing a Small Key to appear.

evidence.quote: Once both of the Stalfos are dead, a chest will appear in the center of the room.  Open it to get a Small Key.

facts.subject: Blue Block
facts.text: Playing the Song of Time with the Ocarina of Time removes the blue block in the Torch Room hallway, uncovering a door.

evidence.quote: Stand near the block and play the Song of Time with the Ocarina of Time to remove the block, revealing a door.

facts.subject: West Courtyard
facts.text: Climbing the ivy wall on the right side of the West Courtyard leads to an alcove with a door.

evidence.quote: Go to the right side of the courtyard, where you will find an ivy wall... Climb the Ivy Wall, sticking as far to the right as possible to avoid the Skullwalltula.  Enter the alcove at the top of the ivy wall and go through the door inside.

facts.subject: Balcony Hallway
facts.text: Defeating the Blue Bubble in the Balcony Hallway unlocks the exit door and spawns a chest containing the Dungeon Map.

evidence.quote: Kill the Blue Bubble, and the door on the other end of the hall will open, and a chest will appear.  Open the chest to get the Dungeon Map.

facts.subject: East Courtyard Balcony
facts.text: Hookshotting to the target above the opposite balcony and pressing the floor switch drains the well in the corner of the East Courtyard.

evidence.quote: Look to the left to see another balcony with a small white circle above it.  Shoot this circle with the Hookshot to pull yourself over to that balcony.  Step on the switch on this balcony, and the well in the corner of the Courtyard will drain.

facts.subject: East Courtyard
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is clinging to the wall around the corner from the chest on the cliff in the East Courtyard.

evidence.quote: If you stand on the right side of the dirt path where it dead-ends at the pool, you can use your Hookshot to latch onto the chest... The real prize is the Gold Skulltula, which is found clinging to the wall around the corner from the chest.

facts.subject: The Well
facts.text: A chest at the end of the well passage contains a Small Key.

evidence.quote: Open the chest at the end of the passage to find a Small Key.

facts.subject: The Well
