facts.text: Climbing the ivy wall at the end of the well passage leads back to the West Courtyard.

evidence.quote: Climb up the Ivy Wall to it's top to find yourself back in the West Courtyard.

facts.subject: The Torch Room
facts.text: The locked door at the top of the stairs in the Torch Room requires a Small Key and leads toward the West Passage.

evidence.quote: Go up the stairs and use one of your Small Keys to open the door.

facts.subject: Blue Bubble
facts.text: A Blue Bubble can be made vulnerable by letting it touch your raised shield while Z-Targeting it, or stunned using the Hookshot.

evidence.quote: Defeat it by holding up your Shield while Z- Targeting it, and let it touch you.  This will cause the blue flame around it to vanish, at which point it will become vulnerable.  Alternatively, you can also stun it with the Hookshot, but the Blue Bubble's speed and the Hookshot's slowness can make this strategy problematic.

facts.subject: Blue Bubble
facts.text: A Blue Bubble is found at the bottom of the Stone Block Room in the Forest Temple.

evidence.quote: Defeat the Blue Bubble, then run forward and climb up the ladder.

facts.subject: Stone block puzzle
facts.text: In the Stone Block Room, the giant stone block must be pushed along the arrows painted on the floor.

evidence.quote: If you look to the left as you enter this room, you'll see a massive stone block, with arrows painted on the floor.  You must push the stone block along these arrows.

facts.subject: Stone block puzzle
facts.text: Push the giant stone block forward until a passage opens on the left, then slip through behind it and push it back until the gap closes.

evidence.quote: Push it forward, and you will see a ladder appear on the right.  Ignore it for now.  Keep pushing the block forward, until a passage appears on the left which is large enough for you to slip through.  Run around behind the stone block, and push it back until the gap you just passed through is closed again.

facts.subject: Stone block puzzle
facts.text: Push the stone block forward until it stops, circle around the ledge taking three rights, and push it into a small alcove to create a climbable step to the third level.

evidence.quote: Move around to the side of the stone block, and push the block forward until it stops.  Turn around, and go back down the passage you just pushed the block down.  Go back around the ledge, taking three rights, to find yourself back on the other side of the stone block.  Push it forward once more until it falls into a small alcove.  You can now jump up to the third level by climbing onto the stone block.

facts.subject: Stone block puzzle
facts.text: Climb the ladder to the third level, turn right through the doorway, and push the upper stone block forward until it stops before returning to the second level.

evidence.quote: Climb up the ladder, turn to the right at the top of the ladder, and right again through the doorway.  Push the stone block directly in front of you forward until it stops, then drop back down to the second level via the ladder.

facts.subject: Stone block puzzle
facts.text: Climb onto the lower stone block to reach the second level, head down the passage to the third-level stone block, and push it into a pit in the floor to access the top level.

evidence.quote: Back on the second level, run to the stone block that you pushed into place earlier, and climb on top of it to reach the second level.  Run down the passage at the top to reach the stone block on the third level, and push it forward until it falls into another small pit in the floor, letting you reach the top level of this room.  Climb up to the top level.

facts.subject: Blue Bubble
facts.text: Two Blue Bubbles inhabit the upper room past the ladder at the top level of the Stone Block Room.

evidence.quote: Go right after climbing up two ledges, and then up the ladder around the next corner.  Go right around the next corner, and either kill or dodge the two Blue Bubbles before going through the door at the other end of the room.

facts.subject: Wallmaster
facts.text: Wallmasters hang from the ceiling and will drag Link back to the entrance of the dungeon if they land on him.

evidence.quote: This is actually a warning about Wallmasters, enemies who appear periodically throughout the game.  If they manage to land on you, then they will drag you back to the entrance of the Dungeon.

facts.subject: Wallmaster
facts.text: To avoid a falling Wallmaster, run in large circles and slash it with a sword when it lands, or switch to First Person Mode to cause it to temporarily vanish.

evidence.quote: If you see the shadow of a Wall Master coming down on you, then quickly begin running in very large circles to avoid it, and then kill it with your Sword when it lands.  Alternatively, if you don't or can't kill the Wall Master, you can also enter First Person Mode, and the creature will temporarily disappear.

facts.subject: Stone pillar
facts.text: Jump out to the stone pillar directly ahead and then jump to the right to reach the exit door.

evidence.quote: Kill or ignore the Wallmaster, and then jump out to the stone pillar directly in front of you, then jump to the right from there.  Enter the door.

facts.subject: West Stairwell
facts.text: The West Stairwell features walls decorated with three portraits depicting a Poe Sister.

evidence.quote: This room is a large series of stairs, with walls that are dotted with three portraits.  Images of one of the Poe Sisters appears in each of these portraits.

facts.subject: Stalfos
facts.text: A Stalfos in the Upper Stalfos Room has the magical ability to walk freely across the large central pit.

evidence.quote: Run into the room, watching out for the large pit in the center which drops back down to the Lower Stalfos Room.  A Stalfos will appear, one who has the magical ability to walk over the pit as though it weren't there.

facts.subject: Stalfos
facts.text: Defeating the first Stalfos lowers an elevator containing two more Stalfos that must both be eliminated quickly to prevent them from regenerating.

evidence.quote: Defeat the Stalfos, and an elevator will drop down from above, covering the pit.  This elevator carries two more Stalfos.  You must defeat both of them quickly; if you take too long on the second one after defeating the first one, then they will both regenerate.

facts.subject: Chest
facts.text: Defeating all three Stalfos in the Upper Stalfos Room causes a chest containing the Bow and Arrows to appear.

evidence.quote: Defeat both of them, and a Chest will appear which contains the Bow and Arrows.

facts.subject: West Stairwell
facts.text: The West Stairwell is identified by stairs positioned on the left side and a red-colored Poe Sister.

evidence.quote: You'll know if this is the West Stairwell, since the stairs will be on the left side and the Poe Sister will be colored red.  If the stairs are on the right and the Poe Sister is colored blue, then you're in the wrong stairwell.

facts.subject: Poe Sister portraits
facts.text: Shooting the portrait containing the Poe Sister with the Bow and Arrow from a distance burns it to ashes, and destroying all three portraits makes the Poe Sister appear at the bottom of the stairwell.

evidence.quote: You must now shoot the portrait which contains the Poe Sister using the Bow and Arrow.  If you get too close, then the Poe Sister will vanish, and move to another painting.  So you want to shoot the portrait from as far away as possible. ... Once you shoot out the picture containing the Poe, then the portrait will burn into ashes, and the Poe will move to another picture.  Destroy all three pictures in the stairwell, and the Poe Sister will appear at the bottom of the stairwell.

facts.subject: Poe Sister
facts.text: The Poe Sister disappears when hit with an arrow, vanishes if targeted with Z-Targeting, and performs a spinning torch attack if approached too closely.

evidence.quote: Go down the stairs and shoot her with an Arrow, whereupon she will disappear.  Wait for her to appear again, then shoot her with another Arrow.  Repeat until she dies.  If you attempt to Z-Target her, then she will vanish.  So don't even attempt to Z-Target her.  If you draw too close to her, visible or invisible, then she will perform a spinning attack with her torch.

facts.subject: Chest
facts.text: Defeating the red Poe Sister in the West Stairwell relights the torches and causes a chest with a Small Key to appear.

evidence.quote: Once she is dead, then her Flame will return to the torch in this room, as well as to the torch back in the Torch Room, and a chest will appear.  Open it to get a Small Key.

facts.subject: Silver eye switch
facts.text: Shooting the silver eye above the door in the Stone Block Room with the Bow and Arrow straightens the Twisted Hallway on the other side.

evidence.quote: Turn around as you come into the room, and look above the door to see a silver eye.  Shoot the eye with your Bow and Arrow.  The Twisted Hallway on the other side of the door will straighten itself out.

facts.subject: Blue chest
facts.text: Opening the blue chest in the straightened West Twisted Hallway yields the Boss Key.

evidence.quote: Open the blue chest to get the Boss Key, which will let you open the door to the Boss' chamber.

facts.subject: Blue Bubbles
facts.text: Killing both Blue Bubbles in the room beneath the pit opens the locked door to the south.

evidence.quote: Kill both of the Blue Bubbles in this room to open the door in the south of the area.  Go through the door.

facts.subject: Big Deku Baba
facts.text: A Big Deku Baba guards the upper ledge in the West Courtyard.

evidence.quote: Run along the ledge, killing the Big Deku Baba on the way.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula hangs above the broken column platform with two Recovery Hearts in the West Courtyard and its token can be retrieved with the Hookshot.

evidence.quote: Look to the right from the Deku Baba, where you will see a broken column which makes a makeshift platform.  It also has two Recovery Hearts.  Jump out to these Recovery Hearts and walk slowly to the far edge of the broken columns, and look up to find a Gold Skulltula.  Kill it and take it's token with the Hookshot, then jump back to the ledge with the (dead) Deku Baba.

facts.subject: West Courtyard upper ledge
facts.text: An alcove at the far end of the upper ledge in the West Courtyard houses an exit door.

evidence.quote: There are a number of alcoves on the right as you go along the ledge.  Go into the alcove on the far end of the ledge to find a door.  Go through it.

facts.subject: Floormaster
facts.text: A Floormaster uses a charging attack and becomes invulnerable when it glows green.

evidence.quote: This room contains a Floormaster, which is similar to the Wallmaster, except it cannot grab you and drag you back to the dungeon's entrance.  It instead employs a charging attack, which is a more traditional attack then the Wallmaster.  If the Floormaster glows green, it becomes invulnerable and is about to attack.

facts.subject: Floormaster
facts.text: Attacking the Floormaster when not glowing splits it into three smaller hands that must be quickly killed using the Bow and Arrow before they grow back.

evidence.quote: Attack the Floormaster when it is not glowing, and when it dies it will split into three smaller Floormasters.  Kill these midgets quickly using the Bow and Arrow, otherwise they will quickly grow into full-sized Floormasters.

facts.subject: Chest
facts.text: Defeating the Floormaster causes a chest containing a Small Key to appear.

evidence.quote: After the Floormaster is dead, a chest will appear in the room.  Open it to get a Small Key.

facts.subject: West Courtyard upper ledge
facts.text: Turning right on the West Courtyard upper ledge leads through a door back into the Stone Block Room.

evidence.quote: Back on the ledge, turn to the right and go through the door.

facts.subject: Chest
facts.text: Shooting the golden eye on the third level of the Stone Block Room spawns a chest containing a bundle of arrows.

evidence.quote: If you like, you can stop on the third level to shoot a golden eye with an arrow, which will give you a chest with a bundle of arrows.

facts.subject: Silver eye switch
facts.text: Shooting the silver eye above the doorway re-twists the hallway to allow access back to the West Stairwell and Upper Stalfos Room.

evidence.quote: Otherwise, shoot the silver eye above the doorway to re-twist the hallway.  Once the hallway is properly screwed up again, go through the door and return to the West Stairwell, and back to the Upper Stalfos Room.

facts.subject: Upper Stalfos Room
facts.text: Go through the opposite door in the Upper Stalfos Room to proceed.

evidence.quote:
The Forest Temple - Upper Stalfos Room

Go through the opposite door.

facts.subject: East Stairwell
facts.text: Destroy all three portraits in the East Stairwell to make the Poe Sister appear at the bottom, then defeat her to reveal a chest containing the Compass.

evidence.quote:
Once all three
portraits are destroyed, then the Poe Sister will appear at the bottom of the
stairwell.  Defeat her the same way you defeated the previous one.  Once she is
dead, a chest will appear.  Open it to get the Compass.

facts.subject: East Stairwell
facts.text: Climb to the top of the East Stairwell and go through the locked door.

evidence.quote:
Climb back to the top
of the stairwell, and go through the locked door.

facts.subject: Wallmaster
facts.text: Drop down to the floor in the East Twisted Hallway and wait for the Wallmaster to appear, then dodge and kill it.

evidence.quote:
Drop down to the floor and wait for the Wallmaster to appear.  Dodge it and
kill it.

facts.subject: Green Bubbles
facts.text: Two Green Bubbles are found in the hallway at the top of the tall ladder to the right of the entrance door.

evidence.quote:
To the right from the door where you entered the room is a tall
ladder with a doorway at the top.  Go down the hallway inside, where you will
encounter two Green Bubbles.

facts.subject: Green Bubbles
facts.text: Green Bubbles randomly toggle their flame shield on and off, can have their shield disabled by walking into them with a raised shield, and can be shot with arrows when their flame turns off.

evidence.quote:
Green Bubbles are identical to Blue Bubbles, only they do not aggressively
attack and their flame shield randomly toggles on and off.  You can also
disable their shield by walking into them with your shield up.  Shoot the Green
Bubbles with Arrows when their Green Flame turns off, or ignore them.

facts.subject: The Flaming Arrow Room
facts.text: Ride the rotating platforms and shoot an arrow through the center torch flame onto the frozen eyeball switch to melt the ice, activate the switch, and twist the previous hallway.

evidence.quote:
To shoot the switch, you must
ride on the rotating platforms, and shoot an arrow through the flame, and onto
the eyeball switch.  The flaming arrow will melt the ice and activate the
switch.  Once the eyeball switch is activated, then the previous room will
twist itself up.

facts.subject: East Twisted Hallway
facts.text: Drop down the pit in the corner to the right of the twisted hallway after killing the Wallmaster.

evidence.quote:
Run around waiting for the Wallmaster, and kill it
when it lands.  Drop down the pit in the corner, to the right as you jump down
from the hallway.

facts.subject: Crushing Ceiling Room
facts.text: Run south between safe gaps as the crushing ceiling falls, and step on the switch halfway down the hall on the right to open the exit door.

evidence.quote:
Keep running
south down the room, stopping at each gap to spy the next gap and kill any Big
Skulltulas with arrows as needed.  Halfway down the hall on the right is a
switch.  Step on this switch to open the door at the end of the hall.

facts.subject: Yellow Poe Sister
facts.text: Shoot the Poe Sister portrait with an arrow to drop puzzle blocks, push the non-matching fifth block aside, and assemble the other four blocks to reveal and defeat the yellow Poe Sister.

evidence.quote:
Shoot the portrait of the Poe Sister on the wall with an arrow, and the puzzle
blocks hanging above will come down.  Four of the blocks can be pushed together
to form a picture of the yellow Poe Sister.  The fifth is superfluous.  Find
the block which doesn't match (the color should be fairly easy to distinguish),
and push it out of the way before pushing the other blocks together to make the
Poe Sister appear.  Kill her the same way you defeated the other two.

facts.subject: Puzzle Block Room
facts.text: Once the Green Flame is back in place, climb up the ledge near the torch and exit through the door.

evidence.quote:
Once the Green Flame is back in place, climb up the ledge near the torch and go
through the door.

facts.subject: Big Skulltula
facts.text: Kill the Big Skulltula on the ceiling in the East Hallway and exit through the door at the end.

evidence.quote:
Kill the Big Skulltula on the ceiling, and go through the door at the other end
of the hall.

facts.subject: Amy Poe
facts.text: When Amy splits into four versions, identify the real Amy by the little spin she performs upon splitting and shoot her with an arrow.

evidence.quote:
Amy is very different from her sisters.  She will split into four
different versions.  One is the real Amy, the other three are fakes....The real Amy does a little spin when she first splits up.  Shoot
this Amy with an arrow, and she will split into four new Amys.

facts.subject: The Torch Room
facts.text: Defeating Amy brings the final flame into place and raises an elevator in the floor, which leads down.

evidence.quote:
Once Amy dies, then the last flame will come into place, and the elevator in
the floor will rise up.  Go down this elevator.

facts.subject: Spinner Room
facts.text: Push the north side of the left wall handle south, then step on the switch in the northwest room to open a door.

evidence.quote:
As soon as you enter the room, go to the left and grab hold of the north side
of the handle.  Push it towards the south.  Head for the northwest corner of
the room, where there is a small room with a switch inside it.  Step onto the
switch, and a door will open elsewhere in the room.

facts.subject: Spinner Room
facts.text: Push the north side of the right wall handle south, then step on the switch in the eastern alcove to open a gate.

evidence.quote:
As you come out of the room, go to the handle on the right.  Stand on the north
side of the handle, and push it to the south.  Go to the east side of the room,
and enter the small alcove to step onto another switch.  Another gate will open
elsewhere in the room.

facts.subject: Spinner Room
facts.text: Push the eastern side of the wall handle west and enter the southwest room to defeat a Big Skulltula and open a chest containing arrows.

evidence.quote:
Go to the right and to the eastern side of the handle, and push it to the west.
Go to the southwest and into the small room.  Kill the Big Skulltula and open
the chest to find a bundle of arrows.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula Token
facts.text: In the southwest alcove of the Spinner Room, kill the Gold Skulltula on the wall to the left and retrieve its token with the Hookshot.

evidence.quote:
The Forest Temple - Spinner Room
New Quest Item: Gold Skulltula Token x1 [GS054]...Turn around, and look on the wall to the
left.  Kill the Gold Skulltula and take it's token with the Hookshot.

facts.subject: Spinner Room
facts.text: Push the south side of the handle north, then step on the south switch to open the grating over the northern doorway.

evidence.quote:
Go to the right as you come out of the small alcove, and go to the south side
of the handle.  Push it north.  Go to the south of the room, and step on the
switch.  The grating covering the doorway on the north side of the room will
now open.  Go to the north side of the room and through the doorway.  Enter the
door on the other side.

facts.subject: Phantom Ganon
facts.text: In the first phase, shoot Phantom Ganon with an arrow as he emerges from the brighter painting scattering electricity.

evidence.quote:
To damage Phantom Ganon in this phase, you must shoot
him with an arrow as he emerges from the painting.  The real Phantom Ganon will
make the painting slightly brighter.

facts.subject: Phantom Ganon
facts.text: In the second phase, reflect Phantom Ganon's lightning balls back at him using sword strikes or Bottles to stun him.

evidence.quote:
Phantom Ganon will now begin throwing balls of lightning at you.  To damage him
now, you must stun him by reflecting these lightning balls back at him using
sword strikes (if you're feeling silly, you can also use Bottles).

facts.subject: Phantom Ganon
facts.text: Once Phantom Ganon is stunned on the ground, attack him with the Biggoron Sword or Master Sword, performing only one jump attack before using regular strikes.

evidence.quote:
Once the ball strikes Phantom Ganon, then he will be stunned briefly and fall
to the ground.  At this point, you should run in and begin pummeling him to
death with the Biggoron Sword (or Master Sword if you don't have the Biggoron
Sword yet).  Only do one Jump Attack, then proceed to regular strikes.

facts.subject: Heart Container
facts.text: Defeating Phantom Ganon causes a Heart Container to appear.

evidence.quote:
After he dies, take the Heart Container that appears and enter the beam of
light.

facts.subject: Saria
facts.text: Entering the beam of light transports Link to the Chamber of the Sages, where Saria gives him the Forest Medallion.

evidence.quote:
You will be transported to the Chamber of the Sages, where you will
meet the Sage of the Forest... Saria.  After Saria gives you her power in the
form of the Forest Medallion, you will be transported back outside to the
Kokiri Forest, where a new Deku Tree will sprout.
You will also acquire the FOREST MEDALLION.

facts.subject: Pierre the Scarecrow
facts.text: Playing the song invented as Young Link back to the Scarecrow on the northeastern shore of Lake Hylia establishes the Scarecrow's Song to summon Pierre.

evidence.quote:
Return to this Scarecrow now, and play the song for him again.  This song will
now become the Scarecrow's Song, which will summon Pierre the Scarecrow to
various points throughout the game.

facts.subject: Scarecrow's Song
facts.text: If you forgot or never played a song for the scarecrow, Sheik at the Temple of Time teaches how to return to childhood to teach Pierre a new song.

evidence.quote:
If you've forgotten the song that you played for the Scarecrow (or never played
a song for him in the first place), then return to the Temple of Time, where
Sheik will teach you how to return to Link's childhood, letting you teach
Pierre a new song.

facts.subject: Malon's obstacle course
facts.text: Waking Talon as part of the Biggoron Sword sequence allows Link to race Epona around Malon's course.

evidence.quote: If you've awoken Talon as part of the Biggoron Sword Trading Sequence, then he will have returned to the Ranch, and Malon will now let you participate in a time trial run around the course on Epona.

facts.subject: Cow
facts.text: Beating Malon's best time around the course rewards Link with a personal Cow delivered to Link's House in Kokiri Forest.

evidence.quote: Complete the course and beat Malon's best time, and Malon will reward you with your own personal Cow back at Link's House in Kokiri Forest.
Talk to Malon and she'll let you run an obstacle course...with Eponia to win a cow for your house.

facts.subject: Malon's obstacle course
facts.text: To clear the course, hug the inside wall, use a carrot before each hurdle, use only one carrot for the pair of low hurdles, recover carrots before the final hurdle, and burn all carrots on the final leg.

evidence.quote: To complete the course, hug the inside wall and use a Carrot just before each hurdle in the fence (for the pair of extremely low hurdles one-third of the way through the course, only use one carrot to clear them both.  Use the long, empty stretch before the last hurdle to recover your carrots.  On the last leg of the second lap, burn all of your carrots in one go.

facts.subject: Prelude of Light
facts.text: Sheik teaches the Prelude of Light inside the Master Sword chamber.

evidence.quote: Run back into the Master Sword chamber, and Sheik will teach you the Prelude of Light.

facts.subject: Prelude of Light
facts.text: Playing the Prelude of Light warps Link straight to the Temple of Time.

evidence.quote: This song will warp you straight to the Temple of Time, much in the same way that the Minuet of Forest takes you straight to the Forest Temple.

facts.subject: House of Skulltula
facts.text: The reward for collecting 40 Gold Skulltula tokens in the House of Skulltula is Bombchus.

evidence.quote: Also, if you skipped the 40 Skulltula reward, get it now.  Which is Bombchus.

facts.subject: Shooting Gallery
facts.text: Hitting all targets in one run at the adult Shooting Gallery across from the windmill rewards the first Quiver upgrade.

evidence.quote: Head for the building across from the Windmill, which was the unfinished structure in Link's childhood.  Enter it....Keep playing the game until you nail all of the targets in one go, and the clerk will reward you with the first Quiver upgrade.

facts.subject: Shooting Gallery
facts.text: Targets in the adult Shooting Gallery appear in the following pattern: middle, left then right, jumping from middle, left and right simultaneously, two rupees from right moving left, and two rupees from left moving right.

evidence.quote:
The order is as follows:
1.)  In the middle
2.)  From the left, then from the right
3.)  Jumps from the middle
4.)  From the left AND right
5.)  Two rupees coming from the right, going left
6.)  Two rupees coming from the left, going right

facts.subject: Shooting Gallery
facts.text: If a single blue rupee appears from the left, the next target will always come from the right.

evidence.quote: Note number 2: if a single blue rupee comes from the left, then the next one will ALWAYS come from the right, despite the randomness of the rest of it.

facts.subject: Death Mountain Trail
facts.text: Ascending Death Mountain Trail requires dodging crashing boulders along the path from the foot of the trail.

evidence.quote: Go up the path from the foot of Death Mountain Trail, dodging the boulders that come crashing down along the way.

facts.subject: Antechamber
facts.text: From the Dodongo Skull platform in the Antechamber, take the right elevator, jump onto the lower ledge, and follow the southern darkened tunnel on the left.

evidence.quote: Run forward, out to the elevator and to the middle platform in front of the giant Dodongo Skull.  Go to the right onto the next elevator, and jump out to the lower ledge (do not ride the elevator up).  Once on the ledge, head back towards the southern edge of the room and go through the darkened tunnel on the left at the south edge of the ledge.

facts.subject: Baby Dodongo
facts.text: A trio of Baby Dodongos emerge from the ground in the Lower Southeast Hall and explode upon defeat.

evidence.quote: Run forward into the hall, and kill the trio of Baby Dodongo's who come out of the ground.  Remember to watch out; they explode.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula Token
facts.text: Playing the Scarecrow's Song summons Pierre the Scarecrow to a high cliff, allowing Link to Hookshot up and kill the Gold Skulltula behind him.

evidence.quote: Stop and play the Scarecrow's Song.  Pierre the Scarecrow will magically appear on the cliff above.  Use the Hookshot on Pierre to pull yourself up onto the cliff, and kill the Gold Skulltula behind Pierre.  Take it's token, then return to the start of the dungeon by walking or using Farore's Wind.

facts.subject: Magic Leaf
facts.text: Riding the grown Magic Leaf outside Dodongo's Cavern transports Link directly up to Goron City.

evidence.quote: Go back out to Death Mountain Trail and use the Magic Leaf out front of Dodongo's Cavern to ride up to Goron City (the Leaf won't be there if you didn't plant the Magic Bean as Young Link, in which case you'll have to walk).

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula Token
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula clings to the back of the platform suspended over Goron City, reachable by climbing out onto the ropes and using the Hookshot at night.

evidence.quote: Play the Sun's Song to make it nighttime if you need to, then run down the rope bridges to the platform suspended over the middle of Goron City.  There is a Gold Skulltula clinging to the back of this platform.  Go to one of the ropes on the left or right sides of the platform, and climb out far enough so that you can see the Skulltula on the back of the platform.  Kill it and take it's token with the Hookshot.

facts.subject: Link, Darunia's Son
facts.text: Stopping the Goron rolling around the third floor using Bombs or Bombchus reveals him to be Link, Darunia's Son.

evidence.quote: Look down to the third floor (the level immediately beneath Goron City's top floor), and you'll see a tiny little Goron rolling around there, much like the Biggoron used to do as Young Link.  Jump down, and try to blow up the Goron using Bombs to make him stop....Speak with the Goron, and he'll reveal himself to be Link, Darunia's Son.

facts.subject: Goron Tunic
facts.text: Talking to Link, Darunia's Son about the Dragon and the Gorons rewards Link with the Goron Tunic and opens Darunia's Chamber.

evidence.quote: Ask him about the Dragon when prompted, and he'll stop crying long enough to explain.  He'll then start crying again.  Ask him about the Gorons, and he'll stop crying again, and ask you to save them.  He'll then give you the Goron Tunic, and the door to Darunia's Chamber will open.

facts.subject: Goron Tunic
facts.text: Equipping the Goron Tunic eliminates the environmental heat timer in Death Mountain Crater and the Fire Temple.

evidence.quote: Put on the Goron Tunic, which removes the time limit in Death Mountain Crater and the Fire Temple.

facts.subject: Darunia's Chamber
facts.text: Pulling back the large carved stone Goron block at the back of Darunia's Chamber opens a passage to Death Mountain Crater.

evidence.quote: In the back of Darunia's Chamber, there is a large stone block with a crude carving of a Goron on it.  Grab onto the block and pull back to reveal a doorway.  Go through it.

facts.subject: broken bridge
facts.text: Hookshotting the wooden beam above the far side of the broken bridge pulls Link across the chasm in Death Mountain Crater.

evidence.quote: Go to the left as you enter the Crater, and you will find a broken bridge.  Stand on the edge of the bridge, and use the Hookshot to pull yourself across using the wooden beam hanging above the other side of the bridge as an anchor.

facts.subject: Bolero of Fire
facts.text: Sheik appears across the bridge in Death Mountain Crater to teach Link the Bolero of Fire.

evidence.quote: Run down the bridge a short ways, and Sheik will appear to teach your the Bolero of Fire, the song that warps you to the Fire Temple at any time.

facts.subject: Master Sword pedestal
facts.text: Placing the Master Sword back into its pedestal reverts Link back to childhood.

evidence.quote: Run back into the Master Sword chamber, and replace the Master Sword on it's pedestal to return to Link's childhood.

facts.subject: ivy wall and marble arch
facts.text: Climbing the ivy wall and jumping down from the large marble arch allows Link to land past the locked gate and sneak past two guards.

evidence.quote: Climb up the ivy wall to the top (it has some rough spots where if you don't climb up in just the right place, you'll fall off).  At the top, run forward a bit, past the gossip stone, to the top of the large marble arch.  Drop down to the ground on the other side of the arch, where you will land on the other side of the gate which formerly blocked your path.  You probably don't realize it, but you've already snuck past two of the guards.

facts.subject: garden hill and moat
facts.text: Running up the third break in the hill toward the flowers leads to a brick wall that links to the moat and the stone platform beyond.

evidence.quote: The place you need to run up is the third break in the hill, approximately near it's center.  Go straight up the hill, and at the top there is a cluster of flowers.  Run straight at these flowers, then begin running forward and slightly to the left until you reach a wall.  Part of the wall is tiled with some bricks; climb up these bricks....Jump straight off the cliff, and go right into the moat.  Swim down to the end of the moat until it breaks left, then climb up onto the small patch of dirt, and from there climb up to the stone platform.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula Token
facts.text: Playing the Song of Storms under the tree by the moat opens a secret pit where bombing the left wall reveals a Gold Skulltula.

evidence.quote: As you climb out of the moat, there is a tree to your right sitting at the corner of the fence.  Stand beneath this tree and play the Song of Storms to make a pit appear.  Drop down into this pit.  There are three bombable walls in this pit, one in front of you as you enter, one to the left and one to the right.  Bomb the wall on the left (it's slightly behind you from where you land), to reveal a Gold Skulltula.  Kill it and take it's token, then return to the Garden.

facts.subject: Castle Guard
facts.text: Allowing a guard in the garden to spot Link causes the guard to throw him outside the gate.

evidence.quote: Run back in the opposite direction you came from while riding the moat and allow one of the Guards to spot you.  The guard will throw you back outside the gate.

facts.subject: House of Skulltula
facts.text: The reward for Fifty Skulltulas in the House of Skulltula is a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: Get the reward for Fifty Skulltulas, which is a Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Musical Frogs
facts.text: Playing the Song of Storms to the Musical Frogs upstream in Zora's River rewards a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: Go upstream to the Musical Frogs, and play them the Song of Storms, plus any other songs which you haven't played for them yet.  When you play the Song of Storms, then they will give you a Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Musical Frogs
facts.text: Playing Zelda's Lullaby, Epona's Song, Sun's Song, Saria's Song, Song of Storms, and Song of Time to the Musical Frogs unlocks another minigame.

evidence.quote: Play the rest of the basic songs (Zelda's Lullaby, Epona's Song, Sun's Song, Saria's Song, Song of Storms and Song of Time), and the Musical Frogs will challenge you with another minigame.  Stand on the log and whip out the Ocarina to play the game.

facts.subject: Musical Frogs minigame
facts.text: In the Musical Frogs minigame, the lowest frog corresponds to the A Button while the remaining four correspond to the directions on the C-Pad.

evidence.quote: Flies will appear above the Frog's heads, and you must press the button associated with that frog to make him eat it.  The lowest frog is matched with the A Button, and the remaining four frogs in the cross-shape are matched to each direction on the C-Pad.

facts.subject: Musical Frogs minigame
facts.text: Completing the button sequence A Button, C-Left, C-Right, C-Down, C-Left, C-Right, C-Down, A Button, C-Down, A Button, C-Down, C-Right, C-Left, A Button in the Musical Frogs minigame awards a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote:
You can also play a minigame with the Frogs to win ANOTHER Piece of Heart....The order is as follows:
A Button, C-Left, C-Right, C-Down, C-Left, C-Right, C-Down, A Button, C-Down, A
Button, C-Down, C-Right, C-Left, A Button

facts.subject: Bolero of Fire
facts.text: Playing the Bolero of Fire warps Link to Death Mountain Crater.

evidence.quote: Once you have both Pieces of Heart from the Musical Frogs, play the Bolero of Fire to warp to Death Mountain Crater.

facts.subject: Death Mountain Crater
facts.text: Without the Goron Tunic, time spent in Death Mountain Crater is limited before dying from the heat.

evidence.quote: Without the protection of the Goron Tunic, your time here is limited before you die from the heat, so let's be quick.

facts.subject: soft earth
facts.text: Dropping a Bottled Bug into the soft earth patch to the left of the warp-in point produces a Gold Skulltula whose token can be collected.

evidence.quote: Begin by looking to the left from where you warp in, where you will find one of those elusive patches of soft earth.  Drop a Bottled Bug into it (you haven't thrown it away, have you!?), but remember to recapture one of the three who comes out.  Kill the Gold Skulltula and take it's token, then plant one of your two remaining Magic Beans in the patch.

facts.subject: Prelude of Light
facts.text: Playing the Prelude of Light returns Link to the Temple of Time.

evidence.quote: Play the Prelude of Light to return to the Temple of Time.

facts.subject: Master Sword
facts.text: Drawing the Master Sword returns Link to adulthood.

evidence.quote: Take the Master Sword once more to return to Adulthood, and play the Bolero of Fire to head back to Death Mountain Crater.

facts.subject: pile of rubble
facts.text: Riding the sprouted Magic Leaf and jumping onto the tall pile of rubble awards a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: Board the Magic Leaf and ride it up.  Near the start of it's path, it will pass by a tall pile of rubble with a Piece of Heart on top and loop around it several times.  Jump off the leaf onto the pile of rubble to get the Heart Piece.

facts.subject: cliff alcove
facts.text: Riding the Magic Leaf near the south entrance allows jumping to a rock by the cliff face and climbing down to an alcove containing a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: The Leaf will pass briefly by a large rock right near the cliff face; this is your opportunity to jump out to the cliff....Walk slowly off the cliff to grab hold of the rock face, and climb down a short distance to an alcove halfway down the cliff face.  Climb below the alcove, then climb up into it (if you try to drop down from above, you'll just fall right into the lava).  Take the Piece of Heart, then play the Bolero of Fire to warp back down to the pedestal (it's faster then climbing back up).

facts.subject: stone structure
facts.text: Crossing the bridge north of the pedestal and climbing down the ladder into the pit inside the stone structure leads to the Fire Temple entrance.

evidence.quote: From the pedestal, head north across the bridge and into the large stone structure.  Climb down the ladder into the pit, and enter the doorway adjacent to the ladder to enter the Fire Temple.

facts.subject: Fire Temple
facts.text: Reaching the Fire Temple boss chamber next to the entrance requires activating a bridge accessible from the dungeon's top floor.

evidence.quote: The boss' chamber is literally next door to the entrance.  The challenge in reaching it is in activating the bridge which leads to his door, which can only be accessed at the dungeon's top-most floor.

facts.subject: trapped Gorons
facts.text: Rescuing trapped Gorons throughout the Fire Temple provides Small Keys and the Boss Key.

evidence.quote: The dungeon is also unique in that Keys aren't really hidden, but are instead sort-of rewards for rescuing the Gorons trapped in the dungeon.  Even the Boss Key is held by one of the Gorons.  Rescuing all of them is a necessary, if tedious, part of the dungeon.

facts.subject: Fire Keese
facts.text: Fire Keese flap around above the stairs in the Entrance Hall.

evidence.quote: Run up the stairs as you enter, watching out for the Fire Keese who flap around above.  Kill them with arrows if you like, then head through the door on the left at the top of the stairs.

facts.subject: Darunia
facts.text: Darunia appears in the Pillar Room and heads off to fight Volvagia after asking Link to rescue the imprisoned Gorons.

evidence.quote: In this room you'll meet with Darunia.  He'll run off to fight Volvagia, and begs Link to rescue the Gorons who are being held prisoner in the Fire Temple.

facts.subject: Pillar Room cell chest
facts.text: Stepping on the switch across the lava pillars in the Pillar Room opens a cell containing a Goron and a chest with a Small Key.

evidence.quote: Look to the left after the cutscene, and you'll see a number of pillars rising out of the lava.  Jump out to these pillars, and along them to the platform in the left corner of the room.  Step onto the switch to open the cell directly in front of you.  Speak with the Goron inside to free him, then open the chest in his cell to find a Small Key.

facts.subject: Entrance Hall
facts.text: Running straight across the Entrance Hall leads to the Lava Cavern.

evidence.quote: Run straight across the room and enter the door on the other side....Run to the left side of this large room.  You can work your way along the series of platforms in the middle of the room, or you can go along the border of the room, or you can just march right through the lava.

facts.subject: Prison Corridor #1 cell chest
facts.text: Stepping on the switch in Prison Corridor #1 opens a cell containing a Goron and a chest with a Small Key.

evidence.quote: Run down to the end of the hall and step on the switch to open the cell door.  Speak with the Goron and open the chest inside to get another Small Key.

facts.subject: Block of Time
facts.text: Playing the Song of Time moves the Block of Time in the Lava Cavern to allow access to the upper door leading to the Killer Tile Room.

evidence.quote: Play the Song of Time to make the block change positions, blocking the door you just came through.  Climb up onto the Block of Time, and go through the door on top of the sandstone platform.

facts.subject: Like-Like
facts.text: A Like-Like in the Killer Tile Room can swallow Link and eat his clothes and Hylian Shield, which can be reclaimed once it is killed.

evidence.quote: Near the back of the room is a strange, pulsating creature.  This is a Like-Like, a relatively weak enemy who does possess the rather annoying ability to eat your Clothes and Hylian Shield.  Slash him to death (use the Biggoron Sword if you have it), and if he manages to swallow you, reclaim your stolen items after he dies.

facts.subject: Killer Tile Room wall
facts.text: Killing the Gold Skulltula on the wall of the Killer Tile Room yields a Gold Skulltula token.

evidence.quote: Kill the Gold Skulltula on the wall and take it's token, then return to the previous room.

facts.subject: oddly-colored wall
facts.text: Bombing the oddly-colored wall on the sandstone platform across the Lava Cavern reveals a door.

evidence.quote: Jump up onto it and use a Bomb on the oddly-colored wall to reveal a door.  Go through it.

facts.subject: switch
facts.text: Stepping on the switch in Prison Corridor #2 opens the prison cell directly in front.

evidence.quote: Run forward and step on the switch to open the prison cell directly in front of you.

facts.subject: Lava Cavern
facts.text: The north door of the Lava Cavern is to the right when exiting Prison Corridor #2.

evidence.quote: Head to the door on the north side of the room and go through it.  It's the door to the right as you come out of the Prison Corridor #2.

facts.subject: log bridge
facts.text: Sliding down the steep log bridge leads inside the cage, which can be climbed to reach platforms above and below.

evidence.quote: Run forward, and you will slide down a steep log bridge to the inside of the cage that takes up the predominant portion of the room.  Grab onto the wall of this cage and climb to it's top level.

facts.subject: massive block
facts.text: Pushing the massive block off the east sandstone pillar onto the erupting lava column allows it to serve as an elevator to the upper level door.

evidence.quote: On the east sandstone pillar, there is a massive block.  Get behind this block and push it off the ledge, onto the huge column of lava that periodically bursts in the middle of the room.  Jump down and stand on the block, and use it as an elevator to reach the upper level the next time the lava column erupts.

facts.subject: Fire Slug
facts.text: Defeat Fire Slugs by aggressive attacking, raising your Shield if the slug expands into a column-shape.

evidence.quote: Defeat the Fire Slug by attacking it aggressively (put up your Shield if it expands into a large column-shape; it's about to attack if it does).

facts.subject: stone block
facts.text: Push the stone block into the track below and pull it into position on the floor's carved stone face.

evidence.quote: Push the stone block off the ledge (it can only be pushed one way) so that it lands in the stone track below.  Jump down and get in front of the block, and pull it backwards into position on the stone face carved into the floor.

facts.subject: Diamond Switch
facts.text: Dropping a bomb off the cliff near the Diamond Switch activates it and temporarily removes the flame pillar around the wire wall.

evidence.quote: Drop a bomb off the cliff so that it lands near the Diamond Switch, and quickly climb onto the ledge behind you.  The bomb's explosion will activate the switch, temporarily removing the pillar of flames that surrounds the wire wall.  Climb up this new wire wall to the top level, and go through the door at the top.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Bombing the hollow wall in the Boulder Maze alcove reveals a Gold Skulltula that yields a token.

evidence.quote: Use a Bomb to destroy the left side of the wall (it isn't discolored, but if you strike it with your sword it sounds hollow).  Kill the Gold Skulltula on the other side and take it's token.

facts.subject: Boulder Maze perimeter
facts.text: Following the perimeter of the Boulder Maze keeping your right side to the wall leads to an alcove with a door.

evidence.quote: Again keeping your right side to the wall, follow the perimeter of the room.  You'll reach another small alcove with a door inside it.  Go through it.

facts.subject: chest
facts.text: Stepping on the switch in Prison Corridor #3 frees a Goron whose chest contains a Small Key.

evidence.quote: Run down the hall and step on the switch to free the Goron.  Speak with the Goron, then open his chest to get another Small Key.

facts.subject: Goron
facts.text: Stepping on the switch at the dead end of the Boulder Maze opens a cell where a Goron gives Link a Small Key.

evidence.quote: Once you make it around to the far left side of the room, you will happen across a Goron's prison cell which is at the end of a dead end in the maze.  Step on the switch in front of the cell to open it, and speak with the Goron inside.  Take his key.

facts.subject: Boulder Maze locked door
facts.text: Return along the Boulder Maze perimeter to unlock and pass through the locked door.

evidence.quote: Return to the locked door we passed earlier and go through it.

facts.subject: Silver Eye
facts.text: Shooting the Silver Eye on the wall with an arrow unlocks the sealed right door in the Narrow Span Room.

evidence.quote: Shoot the Silver Eye on the wall with an arrow to unlock the sealed door on the right from where you enter.

facts.subject: chest
facts.text: A chest to the right inside the Lava Curtain Room contains the Dungeon Map.

evidence.quote: Look to the right as you enter to find a chest which contains the Dungeon Map.

facts.subject: Narrow Span Room
facts.text: Enter the locked door on your right upon returning to the Narrow Span Room from the Lava Curtain Room.

evidence.quote: Enter the locked door on your right as you come out from the Lava Curtain room.

facts.subject: wire platforms
facts.text: Crossing the three wire platforms while dodging the rising lava curtain leads to sandstone steps and the upper left door.

evidence.quote: Run all the way along the wire platform (the curtain moves slowly and is easy to dodge), and jump across to the next wire platform at the gap.  Keep running along the new wire platform, jump onto a third wire platform, and jump again onto the large sandstones steps on the other side of the platform.  Climb to the top of the stairs and go through the door on the left.

facts.subject: switch
facts.text: Stepping on the small platform switch on top of the Boulder Maze opens a cell door on the far side of the room.

evidence.quote: Look to the left once more to see a small platform with a switch.  Jump out to the switch and step on it.  A cell door on the far side of the room will open, revealing another Goron.

facts.subject: chest
facts.text: Opening the chest inside the Goron's cell on top of the Boulder Maze yields a Small Key.

evidence.quote: Speak with the Goron and open his chest to get another Small Key.

facts.subject: huge gash
facts.text: Dropping a bomb onto the huge gash in the floor reveals a massive pit that Link can drop down.

evidence.quote: Drop a bomb onto this gash, and the explosion will reveal a massive pit.  Drop down to the bottom of this pit.

facts.subject: chest
facts.text: Opening the chest in the Goron's cell yields another Small Key.

evidence.quote: Speak with the Goron and open the chest in his cell to get another Small Key.

facts.subject: Goron Cell Switch
facts.text: Stepping on the switch in the hall opens the Goron's double-sided cell doors.

evidence.quote: Step on it, and the Goron's double-sided cell doors will open.

facts.subject: Goron Cell Chest
facts.text: Opening the chest inside the Goron's cell yields a Small Key.

evidence.quote: Speak with the Goron and open his chest to get another Small Key.

facts.subject: Three-Tiered Room Wire Wall
facts.text: Climbing the wire wall leads back up to the Boulder Maze.

evidence.quote: Turn around and go back down the hall, and use the wire wall to climb back up to the Boulder Maze.

facts.subject: Pierre the Scarecrow
facts.text: Playing the Scarecrow's Song summons Pierre the Scarecrow onto the wall platform in the Boulder Maze.

evidence.quote: Play the Scarecrow's Song, and Pierre the Scarecrow will appear up on the platform.

facts.subject: Pierre's Platform
facts.text: Using the Hookshot on the circular target allows Link to pull himself to a rising elevator platform.

evidence.quote: Pull yourself over to this platform, and the platform will begin to rise. Ride the elevator to the top of the shaft, and go through the door adjacent to the elevator.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula token is obtained by killing the skulltula on the corner wire mesh in the Two-Tiered Room.

evidence.quote: Climb the wire mesh to the next level, and look to the wire mesh in the corner to spy a Gold Skulltula.  Kill it and take it's token

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula hangs on the cliff wall above the pit in the Time Trial Room.

evidence.quote: As soon as you enter the room, walk forward to the edge of the cliff and look to the left to spy another Gold Skulltula hanging on the cliff wall above the pit.  Kill it and take it's token with the Hookshot.

facts.subject: Time Trial Chest
facts.text: Stepping on the switch temporarily removes the flames around the chest containing 200 rupees.

evidence.quote: The pillar of flames surrounding the chest at the top of the room will now disappear, and you have a limited to time to open the chest before the flames return...Once you have the 200 rupees, then drop down to the Narrow Span room through the pit in the center of the room.

facts.subject: Narrow Span Room South Door
facts.text: Heading through the south door leads back to the Lava Curtain Room.

evidence.quote: Head through the south door (to the right of the sealed door, closest to the silver eye target) to return to the Lava Curtain Room.

facts.subject: Lava Curtain Room Sandstone Ledge
facts.text: Jumping from the jutting platform to the west-center sandstone ledge leads to a locked door.

evidence.quote: Jump from this piece of the platform up to the sandstone ledge (it looks like a jump you can't make, but you can).  Go through the locked door.

facts.subject: Fire Trap Room Maze
facts.text: Navigating the maze requires keeping the wall on the right, turning left at flame walls, and turning right after posts.

evidence.quote: Keeping the wall on your right side, move slowly forward until a wall of flames appears in your path.  Go to the left (watch out for a roving boulder), and take a right immediately after passing the first post on your right.  Go right again and head back towards the wall to find a door.

facts.subject: Compass Corridor Chest
facts.text: Opening the chest at the end of the hall reveals the Compass.

evidence.quote: Run to the end of the hall and open the chest to find the Compass.

facts.subject: Fire Trap Room Totem Path
facts.text: The path past the fire-spitting totem pole requires hugging the left wall and passing between two poles to reach the exit door.

evidence.quote: Watch out for the giant totem pole here; the faces spit fire.  Hug the wall and go around, keeping your left side facing the wall...When another wall of flames appears in your path, go right and pass between the pair of poles directly in front of you.  Take a left immediately on the other side, and you'll reach the door.

facts.subject: Fire Curtain Switch
facts.text: Pressing the switch behind the fire wall temporarily drops the giant curtain of flames on the north side of the room.

evidence.quote: Go to the left and pass between the pair of posts just to the left of the fire wall, and you can reach the switch.  The giant curtain of flames on the north side of the room will now disappear.

facts.subject: Dummy Door
facts.text: Blowing up the crushing dummy door with a bomb reveals another door behind it.

evidence.quote: Blow up the door with a bomb.  The dummy door will disappear, revealing another door.

facts.subject: Flare Dancer
facts.text: Using the Hookshot pulls the Flare Dancer's heart free from its flaming body.

evidence.quote: To damage the Flare Dancer, the first thing you must do is separate it's heart from it's flaming body using the Hookshot.

facts.subject: Flare Dancer
facts.text: Circling the room in the opposite direction lets Link intercept the running heart with a jump attack.

evidence.quote: Begin circling the room in the opposite direction so that you intercept it halfway around the room, and use a jump attack to deal damage to it

facts.subject: Upper Flare Dancer Room Center Platform
facts.text: Defeating the Flare Dancer removes the central flames and allows the center platform to rise as an elevator.

evidence.quote: Once the Flare Dancer is dead, then the pillar of flames in the middle of the room will disappear.  Climb up onto the platform in the middle of the room, and it will begin to rise.  Go through the door at the top of the shaft.

facts.subject: Diamond Switch
facts.text: Dropping a bomb from the second floor onto the diamond switch removes the flame pillar surrounding the mesh ladder.

evidence.quote: Once up here, drop a bomb down to the bottom floor, right next to the diamond switch.  The explosion will remove the pillar of flames that surround the mesh ladder leading to the next level.

facts.subject: The Tippy-Top Room Chest
facts.text: The chest at the top of the narrow staircase contains the Megaton Hammer.

evidence.quote: The Fire Temple - The Tippy-Top Room...New Item: Megaton Hammer...step on the switch to make a pillar of flames surrounding a chest near the top of the room disappear.  To reach the chest before time runs out, then you have to run up the narrow staircase on the inside of the giant ring that the room creates.

facts.subject: Stone Face Block
facts.text: Smashing the stone face on the floor with the Megaton Hammer drops the block into the room below.

evidence.quote: Stand on the large stone face coming out of the floor, and smash the face with the Megaton Hammer.  The block will fall down to the room below.

facts.subject: Corner Totem Pole
facts.text: Smashing both pieces of the corner totem pole with the Megaton Hammer reveals a door.

evidence.quote: Smash it with the Megaton Hammer from the left or right until both pieces are gone to reveal a door.

facts.subject: Hidden Staircase Room
facts.text: Smashing the stone block that rises out of the pit with the Megaton Hammer causes a stairwell to appear inside the pit.

evidence.quote: Smash the face with the Megaton Hammer, and a stairwell will appear inside the pit.

facts.subject: Hidden Staircase Room door
facts.text: Dropping a wooden box onto the blue switch at the bottom of the stairs unseals the door.

evidence.quote: Drop the wooden box onto the blue switch at the bottom of the stairs to unseal the door.  Go through the door.

facts.subject: Fire Trap Room
facts.text: Smashing the stone block in the corner of the chamber above the Fire Trap Room with the Megaton Hammer drops Link to the floor below and creates a booster to higher doors.

evidence.quote: Stand on the stone block in the corner and smash it with the Megaton Hammer to fall to the floor below.  The stone block has created a booster that lets you access doors in this room that were previously out of your reach.

facts.subject: Fire Trap Room high ledge door
facts.text: Smashing the rusted switch beside the sealed door on the higher ledge with the Megaton Hammer unseals the door.

evidence.quote: Smash the rusted switch with your Megaton Hammer to unseal the door.  Go through it.

facts.subject: Block of Time
facts.text: Playing the Song of Time transports the Block of Time across the room down to the floor.

evidence.quote: Play the Song of Time to transport it down to the floor.

facts.subject: Goron cell
facts.text: Smashing the rusty switch on the opposite ledge with the Megaton Hammer opens the Goron cell below.

evidence.quote: Jump across to the opposite ledge, and smash the rusty switch with the Megaton Hammer to open the cell below.

facts.subject: Goron cell chest
facts.text: A chest inside the Goron cell contains a Small Key.

evidence.quote: Drop down and speak with the Goron in the cell, then take the Key from the chest in his cell.

facts.subject: Fire Trap Room stone block
facts.text: Smashing the large stone block held by scaffolding with the Megaton Hammer allows Link to ride it all the way down.

evidence.quote: Jump out to the block, stand on top of it and smash the block with the Megaton Hammer.  Ride the block all the way down to it's destination far below.

facts.subject: Entrance Hall east door
facts.text: Smashing the pieces of the totem pole away with the Megaton Hammer on the east side of the Entrance Hall reveals a door.

evidence.quote: Use the Megaton Hammer to smash the pieces of the totem pole away (make sure to stand on the left or right side of the totem) to reveal a door.  Go through it.

facts.subject: Room of Fiery Enemies door
facts.text: Defeating all the Fire Keese and Fire Slugs in the room opens the sealed door on the other end.

evidence.quote: Kill any leftovers, and the sealed door on the other end of the room will open. Go through it.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Defeating the Gold Skulltula in the Deja Vu Room yields a Gold Skulltula Token.

evidence.quote: Kill the Like-Like, then kill the Gold Skulltula and take it's token.

facts.subject: Flare Dancer
facts.text: A Flare Dancer mini-boss is fought in the Lower Flare Dancer Room, where the Biggoron Sword is effective and the Megaton Hammer attacks too slowly.

evidence.quote: Defeat another Flare Dancer here.  This one is identical to the last one. Remember to use the Biggoron Sword if you have it.  Don't bother with the Megaton Hammer; it attacks too slowly.

facts.subject: Lower Flare Dancer Room chest
facts.text: Defeating the Flare Dancer makes its flame pillar disappear and reveals a chest containing bombs.

evidence.quote: Once the Flare Dancer is dead, then his pillar of flames disappears, revealing a chest.  Open the chest to get some... bombs.

facts.subject: Boss Key Prison Room chest
facts.text: Smashing the rusted switch opens the cell containing a Goron and an ornate chest with the Boss Key.

evidence.quote: Use the Megaton Hammer to smash the rusted switch, opening the double-sided cell.  Speak with the Goron, then open the ornate chest to find the Boss Key.

facts.subject: Pillar Room Boss Key door
facts.text: Using the knocked-down pillar allows Link to jump across to the Boss Key door in the Pillar Room.

evidence.quote: With the pillar from the Fire Trap room knocked down to this point, you can now jump across to the Boss Key door that you couldn't reach the last time you were here (not that it mattered, since you didn't have the key anyway).  Jump across to the door, and go through it.

facts.subject: Volvagia
facts.text: In phase 1, Volvagia emerges from one of nine pits marked by smoke and cinders and can be stunned with a Megaton Hammer jump attack before being damaged.

evidence.quote: In Volvagia's first phase, he appears randomly in one of the nine pits that dot the battlefield.  You'll know which pit he'll appear in, as a large amount of smoke and cinders will appear around the pit... Smash his head with the Megaton Hammer (use a Jump Attack with the Megaton Hammer for best results), and it will briefly stun Volvagia.

facts.subject: Volvagia
facts.text: When Volvagia flies around breathing fire in phase 2, Link can avoid damage by continuously running in a small circle near the center of the arena.

evidence.quote: In his second phase, Volvagia will emerge from one of the pits (again, you can tell which ones by the smoke and cinders that appear around the pit) and fly around the room, chasing you and trying to breath fire on you.  The easiest way to avoid damage in this phase is to just run continuously to the left or right in a small circle, preferably near the center of the battlefield.

facts.subject: Volvagia
facts.text: When Volvagia flies to the ceiling causing boulders to rain down, the attack can be avoided by running to the arena's edge and hanging off.

evidence.quote: The roof will begin to fall, raining the battlefield with boulders.  Easily the best way to avoid this form of attack is to just run to the edge of the battlefield and hang off the edge.

facts.subject: Volvagia
facts.text: Defeating Volvagia causes a Heart Container to appear.

evidence.quote: After Volvagia dies, then take the Heart Container that appears and enter the ring of light to meet the Sage of Fire, Darunia.

facts.subject: Darunia
facts.text: Entering the ring of light after defeating Volvagia allows Link to meet Darunia, the Sage of Fire, and obtain the Fire Medallion.

evidence.quote: After Volvagia dies, then take the Heart Container that appears and enter the ring of light to meet the Sage of Fire, Darunia.

facts.subject: Shattered plank bridge
facts.text: Link can cross the shattered plank bridge in Death Mountain Crater by using the Hookshot on the planks hanging off the cliff.

evidence.quote: Use the Hookshot to pull yourself over to the other side of the bridge (target the planks hanging off the cliff and climb up them like a ladder).

facts.subject: Great Fairy Fountain entrance
facts.text: Smashing the two rocks across the drawbridge with the Megaton Hammer opens the doorway to a Great Fairy Fountain.

evidence.quote: On the other side of the drawbridge, there are two rocks which can be seen covering the entrance to a doorway, which is only partially visible.  Use the Megaton Hammer to smash the rocks and enter the doorway (you may have to smash the rocks multiple times), which turns out to be a Great Fairy Fountain.

facts.subject: Great Fairy of Bondage
facts.text: Playing Zelda's Lullaby while standing on the Triforce symbol inside the fountain summons the Great Fairy of Bondage to double Link's magic meter.

evidence.quote: Play Zelda's Lullaby while standing on the symbol, and the Great Fairy of Bondage will appear and double the size of your magic meter.

facts.subject: Upper Death Mountain Crater path
facts.text: Smashing the gray rock outside the Great Fairy's Fountain with the Megaton Hammer opens a path with a ladder leading to upper Death Mountain Crater.

evidence.quote: As you come out of the Great Fairy's Fountain, you'll find yourself practically thrown right into another gray rock.  Smash it with the Megaton Hammer, and you'll open a path leading up to upper Death Mountain Crater.  Jump over to the ladder and climb to it's top.

facts.subject: Link's Tree House
facts.text: The door in the northwest corner of Link's Tree House leads outside to Kokiri Forest.

evidence.quote: Head out the door in the northwest corner.

facts.subject: Saria
facts.text: Saria approaches Link on his porch outside his tree house.

evidence.quote: On Link's porch, you will be approached by Saria, one of the game's more important sub characters.

facts.subject: Mido
facts.text: Mido blocks the archway leading to the Great Deku Tree and refuses to let Link pass until he finds both a sword and a shield.

evidence.quote: Jump across the small pool of water to the large arch that leads to the Great Deku Tree. Speak with Mido, the Kokiri who blocks your path. He'll refuse to let you pass until you find both a Sword and Shield (a task which he thinks is impossible, but we'll soon prove otherwise).

facts.subject: Kokiri Sword
facts.text: The Kokiri Sword is found inside a treasure chest on a tree trunk past the rolling boulder tunnel in the Kokiri Training Ground.

evidence.quote: Enter the small tunnel by standing in front of it and pressing A. Crawl to the tunnel's other side... Open the treasure chest sitting on the tree trunk to find the Kokiri Sword.

facts.subject: Deku Shield
facts.text: A shield must be bought from the shop for 40 rupees.

evidence.quote: Next item on your list is a Shield, which you'll have to buy from the shop for 40 rupees.

facts.subject: Kokiri Training Ground
facts.text: Navigating the alcoves along the boulder path yields two blue rupees and bushes that may drop rupees.

evidence.quote: Run left and into the small alcove. Take the blue rupee and slash the bush, and take the rupee that it may or may not drop... Run left around the corner, then another left. Take the blue rupee in the far alcove, then slash the bush which should (hopefully) yield another Rupee.

facts.subject: Kokiri Training Ground
facts.text: Targeting a rock outside the tunnel and performing repeated backflips awards a blue rupee and a green rupee.

evidence.quote: On the outside of the tunnel, Z-Target one of the rocks to the left. Begin performing backflips (hold back and press A) over and over until you reach the edge of the training ground. Run back towards the rock and repeat the backflips until you are awarded a blue rupee and a green rupee.

facts.subject: Mido's House
facts.text: The chests inside Mido's House contain 11 rupees and a Recovery Heart.

evidence.quote: Open all of his chests for 11 rupees and a Recovery Heart.

facts.subject: Mido's House
facts.text: A blue rupee is located on the ledge behind Mido's House.

evidence.quote: Jump up to the ledge behind Mido's House, and look behind his house to find another Blue Rupee.

facts.subject: Kokiri Forest Pond
facts.text: Jumping across the platforms in the water awards a blue rupee upon reaching the opposite shore, and another blue rupee when repeated in the opposite direction.

evidence.quote: Run directly at these platforms, and run across them. Link will automatically jump from each one as you run along them. If you do it properly, after you have reached the opposite shore of the water you will receive a blue rupee. Repeat this in the opposite direction to receive another blue rupee.

facts.subject: Kokiri Forest
facts.text: The house in the southeast corner contains six rupees in pots, which respawn upon exiting and re-entering.

evidence.quote: The house in the southeast corner has the most rupees (six, look in the pots), and leaving then entering the house repeatedly will respawn the pots.

facts.subject: Kokiri Shop
facts.text: The Deku Shield can be purchased from the clerk at the Kokiri Shop.

evidence.quote: Purchase a Deku Shield from the clerk.

facts.subject: Kokiri Forest
facts.text: Climbing the vine-covered wall behind Mido's House and entering the large hollow log leads to the Lost Woods.

evidence.quote: Head back to Mido's House in the northwest corner of the Kokiri Forest, then climb up on the ledge behind his house. Look for the wall covered in vines, then climb the vines to the top. Work your way around along the ledge and enter the large hollow log to enter the Lost Woods.

facts.subject: Business Scrub
facts.text: A Business Scrub can be defeated by reflecting its Deku Nut back with the Deku Shield or by striking it with a Jump Attack.

evidence.quote: To beat this Business Scrub and make him sell you his wares, either reflect his Deku Nut back into his face with the Deku Shield, or do a Jump Attack.

facts.subject: Deku Stick Capacity Upgrade
facts.text: The Business Scrub in the Lost Woods upgrades Link's Deku Stick carrying capacity to 20 for 40 rupees and fills his sticks.

evidence.quote: Speak with him, and he will upgrade the total amount of Deku Sticks you can carry to 20 for 40 rupees (and he'll maximize your Deku Sticks for free).

facts.subject: Lost Woods
facts.text: From the Business Scrub area, climbing the ladder and navigating through a series of hollow logs returns Link to Kokiri Forest.

evidence.quote: Return to the opposite side of the valley and climb the ladder back to the top. Go through the hollowed log, then hang a right into another hollowed log. Go left or right (it doesn't matter which) through another hollowed log to return to the Kokiri Forest.

facts.subject: Mido
facts.text: Once Link has obtained both a sword and a shield, Mido permits him to pass through the passage toward the Great Deku Tree.

evidence.quote: Head to the east side of the area, back across the pond, and speak with Mido again. Now that you've lived up to his challenge to find a Sword and Shield, he'll let you pass.

facts.subject: Deku Baba
facts.text: Deku Babas in the passage die in one sword hit and leave behind Deku Sticks.

evidence.quote: Halfway through it, you'll encounter a bunch of Deku Babas. These guys die in one hit from your sword, and leave behind Deku Sticks.

facts.subject: Great Deku Tree
facts.text: Entering the mouth of the Great Deku Tree begins the first dungeon.

evidence.quote: The Deku Tree will test Link and Navi, by having them enter his uh... mouth, and defeat the parasite that has been placed at his roots. Enter his mouth to begin the first dungeon.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Smashing the first red rock on the left on the path to the cliff face of Death Mountain with the Megaton Hammer at night reveals a Gold Skulltula.

evidence.quote: Drop down from the peak of Death Mountain to the long path leading up to the cliff face, where you are normally pelted with burning rocks while trying to make your way up.  Smash the first red rock on the left with the Megaton Hammer, and you'll find a Gold Skulltula (if it isn't there, then make sure it's nighttime).

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Smashing the red rock on the cliff above Dodongo's Cavern with the Megaton Hammer at night reveals another Gold Skulltula.

evidence.quote: Head for the cliff above Dodongo's Cavern (where you threw the Bomb Flower down as Young Link to unseal Dodongo's Cavern).  There's another red rock here. Smash it with the Megaton Hammer to find another Gold Skulltula (again, it must be nighttime).

facts.subject: Death Mountain
facts.text: Playing the Prelude of Light on Death Mountain returns you to the Temple of Time.

evidence.quote: You're done on Death Mountain now, so play the Prelude of Light to return to the Temple of Time.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is located high on the south wall of Zora's River, reachable by jumping to a cliff ledge with a pit in it and using the Hookshot at night.

evidence.quote: If it isn't nighttime, then play the Sun's Song now, face the south wall and look up.  You'll see a Gold Skulltula high on the wall.  Unfortunately, you can't reach it from here....At the top, face south again where you will see a cliff with a pit in it.  Jump out to this ledge, but avoid the pit.  You're now in range of that Gold Skulltula that we passed earlier.  Make it nighttime if you need to, then nail the Gold Skulltula and take it's token with the Hookshot.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is found on the northwestern wall near the end of the wooden drawbridge before the Zora's Domain waterfall, obtainable with the Hookshot.

evidence.quote: Near the end of the wooden drawbridge just before the waterfall, if you look on the northwestern wall you will find another Gold Skulltula.  You may need to stand on the fence to reach it with the Hookshot.

facts.subject: Zora's Domain waterfall
facts.text: Playing Zelda's Lullaby at the Zora's Domain waterfall opens the waterfall and grants entry to Zora's Domain.

evidence.quote: Once you have both of the Skulltulas in this zone, head to the Zora's Domain waterfall, play Zelda's Lullaby to open the waterfall and enter Zora's Domain.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: At night, a Gold Skulltula is located to the left of the very edge of the waterfall near King Zora's throne room and can be killed and collected with the Hookshot.

evidence.quote: Head to the left towards the top of the waterfall, and edge to the very edge of the waterfall.  Look to the left to see a Gold Skulltula.  Kill it and take it's token with the Hookshot, then return to King Zora's throne room.

facts.subject: King Zora's throne room
facts.text: The passage behind King Zora's throne leads into Zora's Fountain.

evidence.quote: Climb up to the passage behind King Zora's throne and enter Zora's Fountain.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: A Piece of Heart is located across a second set of steadily rotating ice platforms reached by heading north-east across the frozen platforms from Jabu-Jabu's vacated altar.

evidence.quote: Climb up the small bit of frozen hill, and jump out onto the first of many frozen platforms.  Jump carefully along the ice platforms, and when you reach the second one, you can choose to go north or north-east.  Go north-east first to get a Piece of Heart.  The second set of ice platforms on the way to the Piece of Heart steadily rotates.

facts.subject: Zora's Fountain
facts.text: Navigating north across the ice platforms to the northern edge of the pond leads to a massive cave mouth that enters the Ice Cavern.

evidence.quote: Once you have the Piece of Heart, head back to the giant platform and go north along the ice platforms.  Jump along them to the northern edge of the pond and into the massive cave mouth that has appeared here.  Enter the cave mouth to reach the Ice Cavern.

facts.subject: Freezzard
facts.text: Freezzard enemies can freeze Link with an ice breath attack, but can be pulled toward Link with the Hookshot and defeated with sword strikes or Din's Fire.

evidence.quote: When the room widens out into a large room with a frozen floor, you'll meet three Freezzard enemies. Defeat them with sword strikes or Din's Fire.  Don't try to struggle towards them on the frozen ice.  Just use the Hookshot on them to pull yourself right to them.  The Freezzards can freeze you solid using an ice breath attack, and can move slowly around on the frozen floors, but are otherwise relatively harmless.

facts.subject: Silver Rupees
facts.text: Collecting all the Silver Rupees in the room with the spinning Giant Frozen Scythe Thing of Incredibly Painful Death unlocks the door at the top of the cliff.

evidence.quote: This room contains a number of Silver Rupees, which must be gathered to unlock the door in the north end of the room so that you can progress onwards....The door at the top of the cliff will now unlock.  Climb up and go through it.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is located on the ceiling above the silver rupee behind three blue stalagmites in the scythe room.

evidence.quote: There is another silver rupee behind three blue stalagmites in the corner (to the left as you first enter the room).  Kill the Gold Skulltula on the ceiling above while you grab this rupee.

facts.subject: Ice Keese
facts.text: Ice Keese freeze Link on contact without losing their ice effect, and should be defeated from afar using arrows.

evidence.quote: This room contains a new kind of Keese, the Ice Keese.  These guys are annoying.  Really freaking annoying.  If they touch you, then they will freeze you solid.  However, unlike the Fire Keese, they do not lose their Ice effect after they touch you.  Try and kill them from afar with arrows.

facts.subject: Blue Fire
facts.text: A pillar of Blue Fire in the Ice Keese room can be stored in empty Bottles and used to melt Red Ice.

evidence.quote: This platform contains a pillar which houses a pillar of Blue Fire.  Blue fire can be used to melt the Red Ice that you've seen around Zora's Domain.  Empty two of your Bottles (you'd better have at least two by this point in the game), and fill them with Blue Fire.

facts.subject: Freezzard
facts.text: A Freezzard can be defeated in one hit by using a Jump Attack with the Biggoron Sword or the Megaton Hammer.

evidence.quote: Kill the Freezzard at the other end (he tends to hog up this part of the path, so use a Jump Attack with the Biggoron Sword or a Megaton Hammer for a 1HKO).

facts.subject: Dungeon Map
facts.text: The Dungeon Map is inside a large chest that must be melted with Blue Fire.

evidence.quote: Use the Blue Fire on the large chest to the right of the (dead) Freezzard, and open it to get the Dungeon Map (the pot frozen with Red Ice contains a fairy).

facts.subject: Compass
facts.text: Melting the Red Ice covering the chest on the right side of the room with Blue Fire yields the Compass.

evidence.quote: Refill your empty bottle with Blue Flame, then use both of your bottles of Blue Flame to melt the Red Ice covering the chest on the right side of the room, and the Piece of Heart on the left side of the room. Open the chest to get the Compass.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: A Piece of Heart is encased in Red Ice on the left side of the room and requires Blue Flame to melt.

evidence.quote: Refill your empty bottle with Blue Flame, then use both of your bottles of Blue Flame to melt the Red Ice covering the chest on the right side of the room, and the Piece of Heart on the left side of the room.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula hangs on the wall to the right of the Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: When you get the Piece of Heart, look on the wall to the right to see a Gold Skulltula. Kill it and take it's token.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is located in the corner to the right upon entering the block pushing room and can be retrieved using the Hookshot.

evidence.quote: While you're getting rid of the Keese, get the Gold Skulltula in the corner (to your right as you come in from the GFSTIPD room) and take it's token with the Hookshot.

facts.subject: Ice Block Puzzle
