evidence.quote: Get the first Silver Rupee from the middle of the room, directly behind the set of invisible spikes closest to the door...Next pull yourself up to the Longshot target on the east side of the room, and you'll fall onto a Silver Rupee on your way down...Now go to the west side of the room, where there is another Longshot target, and a Silver Rupee suspended above the floor...If you look above the high ledge on the north wall with the Lens, then you'll see an invisible Longshot target on the ceiling.  You have to pull yourself up to this target, and pass through the Silver Rupee on the way to get it...The last Silver Rupee is on an invisible ledge in the northeast corner...Now that you have all five Silver Rupees, the door on the west side of the room will open.  Go through it.

facts.subject: Skull
facts.text: Kill the four Keese and toss a bomb into the hollow top of the large skull to explode it and reveal a Small Key in the rubble.

evidence.quote: When you get to the top, kill the four Keese (two of them are in the other corners of the room, but will attack you if they see you).  Once the Keese are out of the way, then toss a bomb into the hollowed-out top of the Skull.  The Skull will explode, revealing a key in the rubble.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula GS084
facts.text: Kill the Gold Skulltula in the Skull Room to collect its token.

evidence.quote: Take the Key, and kill the Gold Skulltula for it's token, then return to the previous room.

facts.subject: The Shadow Temple - Silver Rupee Room
facts.text: Climb up to the platform on the north end of the Silver Rupee Room by using the Longshot on the invisible ceiling target, then proceed through the locked door.

evidence.quote: Climb up to the platform on the north end of the room by using the Longshot on the invisible target on the ceiling.  Go through the locked door.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula GS082
facts.text: Kill the Gold Skulltula on the other side and take the Gold Skulltula Token.

evidence.quote: Go through it and kill the Gold Skulltula on the other side, as well as two chests which contain a Blue Rupee and Arrows (use the Lens to see the second chest).  Take the Gold Skulltula Token, then return to the Guillotine Chamber.

facts.subject: Blade Traps and fan hallway
facts.text: In the hallway with Blade Traps and a fan, wait for the fan to stop blowing before running past the Blade Traps in Kokiri Boots.

evidence.quote:
If the fan starts blowing, then it
will push you backwards (you can fight it by running into the wind), so wait
for it to stop blowing, then run past the Blade Traps.  If you equip the Iron
Boots, then the fan can't affect you (but you'll also move too slowly to get
past the Blade Traps, so stick with the Kokiri Boots).

facts.subject: Big Skulltula
facts.text: A Big Skulltula hangs from the ceiling around the corner in the hallway.

evidence.quote: Go around the corner and kill the Big Skulltula that hangs from the ceiling.

facts.subject: Powerful fan hallway
facts.text: Equipping the Iron Boots stabilizes Link against the hallway's powerful fan while walking toward the pit.

evidence.quote:
The fan in this hallway is more powerful, and DOES have the ability to push you
backwards, even if you fight it.  So use the Iron Boots to stabilize yourself,
and walk slowly around the corner, where you will find another fan and a large
pit.

facts.subject: Pit across ledge
facts.text: Link can pull himself across the large pit to the opposite ledge by using the Longshot while keeping the Iron Boots equipped.

evidence.quote:
Keeping the Iron Boots equipped, use the Longshot on the opposite ledge
above the pit to pull yourself across.

facts.subject: Silver Eye
facts.text: Holding down the Z Button and keeping the shield up while walking forward blocks flames spit by the Silver Eye above the door.

evidence.quote:
The Silver Eye above the door on the
other end of the hall will spit fire at you, so hold down the Z Button and
keep your shield up while walking forward to block the flames.

facts.subject: Fake wall ledge
facts.text: Switching to the Hover Boots by the last fan on the right wall allows the wind to blow Link through a fake wall on the left onto a ledge.

evidence.quote:
When you reach
the last fan on the right wall, change from the Iron Boots to the Hover Boots.
With the help of the Hover Boots, the fan will blow you through a fake wall on
the left and onto a ledge.  Go through the door on the other side of the wall.

facts.subject: Gibdos chest
facts.text: Defeating the Gibdos in the room while dodging Blade Traps causes a chest containing a Blue Rupee to appear.

evidence.quote:
Change back to the Kokiri Boots, then kill the Gibdos in this room while
dodging the Blade Traps on the floor, and a chest will appear.  Open it for a
Blue Rupee

facts.subject: Rubble chest
facts.text: Bombing the rubble pile in the southeast corner and using the Lens of Truth reveals a hidden chest containing a Small Key.

evidence.quote:
bomb the pile of rubble in the southeast corner of the room.
Use the Lens of Truth to see the chest beneath the rubble, and open it to get a
Small Key.

facts.subject: Stone block
facts.text: In the room with the fog river, push or pull the large stone block along the floor track into the small trench near the ladder.

evidence.quote:
Look to the left as you enter the room to see a large stone block.  Grab it and
push/pull it along the track in the floor to the small trench near the ladder,
to the right of the door you came through.

facts.subject: Southwest alcove
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula token is in a southwest alcove visible from the front of the boat, reachable with the Longshot or Scarecrow's Song.

evidence.quote:
go to the front of the boat, and look to the southwest.
You'll see an alcove with a Gold Skulltula in it.  You can use the Scarecrow's
Song to make Pierre appear up in that alcove, or you can just shoot the
Skulltula from the boat with the Longshot.

facts.subject: Cursed Boat
facts.text: Standing on the Triforce symbol on the boat and playing Zelda's Lullaby causes the boat to begin moving west.

evidence.quote:
return to the Boat and stand on the Triforce symbol.  Play Zelda's
Lullaby, and the boat will begin to move.

facts.subject: Stalfos
facts.text: Several waves of Stalfos attack as the boat travels west across the fog river.

evidence.quote: As the boat moves west, you'll have to fight off several waves of Stalfos.

facts.subject: Cursed Boat
facts.text: When the boat reaches the west side of the room, Link must immediately jump off the south side onto shore before the boat sinks.

evidence.quote:
Once the boat reaches the west side of the room, immediately jump
off the south side of the boat onto the shore.  Because the boat is going to
sink.

facts.subject: Floor Master Room
facts.text: Using the Lens of Truth reveals the invisible maze walls in the Floor Master Room.

evidence.quote:
In
actuality, this room is a simple rudimentary maze.  The catch is, the walls are
invisible.  Use the Lens of Truth to see the invisible walls.

facts.subject: Crushing walls
facts.text: Using Din's Fire burns both of the spike-covered wooden walls crushing toward Link.

evidence.quote:
This room contains two walls, each covered with spikes, both of which are
crushing towards you.  This would be a problem, except for the fact that both
of the walls are made of wood.  Use Din's Fire to burn them both.

facts.subject: Ornate chest
facts.text: Killing the Redead on the east side of the Crushing Walls Room allows Link to open an ornate chest containing the Boss Key.

evidence.quote:
Go to the
east side of the room, and kill the Redead.  Open the ornate chest to get the
Boss Key.

facts.subject: West chest
facts.text: The chest on the west side of the Crushing Walls Room contains a Blue Rupee.

evidence.quote: The chest on the west side of the room contains a Blue Rupee.

facts.subject: Floor Master Room south door
facts.text: Navigating around the invisible walls to the south side of the Floor Master Room leads to the door of the Invisible Floor Master Room.

evidence.quote:
Make your way around the invisible walls to the south side of the room, and go
through the door there.

facts.subject: Invisible Floor Master
facts.text: Using the Lens of Truth reveals the invisible Floor Master, and Din's Fire quickly kills the three invisible midget Floor Masters it splits into.

evidence.quote:
This room contains an invisible Floor Master.  Use the Lens of Truth to see it.
Once you defeat it, it will split into three midget Floor Masters (who are also
invisible), which will grow full size if you don't kill them quickly.  Use
Din's Fire to quickly kill all three.

facts.subject: Invisible Floor Master chest
facts.text: Defeating the invisible Floor Master and its spawn causes a chest containing a Small Key to appear in the rear of the room.

evidence.quote:
Once the Floor Master and his spawn are
dead, a chest appears in the rear of the room.  Open it to get a Small Key,
then return to the previous room.

facts.subject: Floor Master Room west door
facts.text: Navigating around the invisible walls to the west side of the Floor Master Room leads through the door to the Triple Skull Room.

evidence.quote:
Make your way around the invisible walls to the west side of the room, and go
through the door there.

facts.subject: Triple Skull Room wall
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula token is located on the wall behind the three rotating skulls in the Triple Skull Room.

evidence.quote:
This room is similar to the Skull Room you passed previously, but has three
rotating Skulls in it.  You don't actually have to destroy any of them, unless
you want lots of rupees.  Nail the Gold Skulltula on the wall behind the
Skulls, take it's token, then return to the previous room.

facts.subject: Floor Master Room east door
facts.text: Navigating around the invisible walls to the east side of the Floor Master Room leads through the door on that side.

evidence.quote:
Make your way around the invisible walls to the east side of the room, and go
through the door there.

facts.subject: Bomb flower pillar
facts.text: Shooting a Fire Arrow at one of the bomb flowers surrounding the tall pillar across the pit causes the pillar to fall and form a bridge across the gap.

evidence.quote:
On the left side of the ledge opposite the pit, there is a
tall pillar which is surrounded by bomb flowers.  Nail one of the bomb flowers
with a Fire Arrow, and the pillar will fall down, making a bridge leading
across the gap.

facts.subject: Geometric Shape Room
facts.text: Equipping the Hover Boots and using the Lens of Truth allows Link to cross invisible platforms to reach the ledge with the Boss Door.

evidence.quote:
Equip the Hover Boots and use the Lens of Truth to see the platforms in this
room.  Run out to the T-Shaped platform directly in front of the door, then go
to the left to the straight platform.  From there, go right to the next
platform, and then to the ledge with the Boss Door.

facts.subject: Bongo Bongo
facts.text: Dropping into the pit in the middle of the room begins the boss fight against Bongo Bongo on a giant bongo drum.

evidence.quote:
-------------B-O-S-S-------------
Phantom Shadow Beast BONGO BONGO...Drop down the pit in the
middle of the room to begin the fight.

The entire boss fight is fought on a giant drum.

facts.subject: Bongo Bongo
facts.text: Equipping the Kokiri Boots avoids making the boss fight against Bongo Bongo unnecessarily difficult.

evidence.quote:
Just make sure you're using the
Kokiri Boots, otherwise this fight will be unnecessarily difficult.

facts.subject: Bongo Bongo
facts.text: Quickly shooting both of Bongo Bongo's hands with arrows using Z-Targeting stuns them and makes his eye appear.

evidence.quote:
To damage Bongo Bongo, you must make his eye appear.  To do this, shoot both of
his hands with arrows to stun them.  They recover quickly, so shoot fast.  Use
Z-Targeting; the hands move much too fast, and the constant movement of the
drum makes manual aiming pretty much impossible.

facts.subject: Bongo Bongo
facts.text: Looking between Bongo Bongo's stunned hands with the Lens of Truth reveals his eye, which can be shot with an arrow before attacking his fallen torso with a Biggoron Sword Jump Attack.

evidence.quote:
Once you stun both hands, use
the Lens of Truth to look at the space between the hands, and you'll see Bongo
Bongo's eye.  Shoot it with an Arrow as well, and Bongo Bongo's torso will fall
to the floor, letting you attack it.  As always, that attack should be a Jump
Attack from the Biggoron Sword

facts.subject: Bongo Bongo
facts.text: Stunning Bongo Bongo's hands causes them to drop more magic or arrows if Link runs low.

evidence.quote:
If you run low on
magic or arrows, Bongo Bongo's hands drop more when you stun them.

facts.subject: Heart Container
facts.text: Bongo Bongo leaves behind a Heart Container upon defeat.

evidence.quote: Take the Heart Container that Bongo Bongo leaves behind

facts.subject: Impa
facts.text: Entering the beam of light after defeating Bongo Bongo awakens Impa as the Sage of Shadow and awards Link the Shadow Medallion.

evidence.quote:
New Quest Item: Shadow Medallion...enter the beam of
light to meet the Sage of Shadow: Impa
After completing the Shadow Temple then...and Impa will entrust this to Link.

facts.subject: Gerudo Fortress gate
facts.text: The gate in the northwest corner of the Gerudo Fortress leads to the Haunted Wasteland once Link has obtained the Bow and Epona.

evidence.quote:
This part of the guide can be finished immediately after obtaining the Bow and
Epona, so you may have finished it already.  If you have, then head for the
Haunted Wasteland through the gate in the northwest corner of the Gerudo
Fortress immediately.

facts.subject: Kakariko Graveyard
facts.text: After warping back to Kakariko Graveyard from the Chamber of the Sages, head to Hyrule Field and travel west to Gerudo Valley.

evidence.quote:
After you warp back here from the Chamber of the Sages, then head for Hyrule
Field and go to Gerudo Valley, in the west side of the Field.

facts.subject: Gerudo Valley Canyon
facts.text: Link can cross the fallen bridge over the canyon in Gerudo Valley by jumping with Epona or pulling himself over with the Longshot.

evidence.quote: Go up the log bridge near the entrance of the Valley, and when you reach the fallen bridge spanning the canyon, either use Epona to jump over the gap or the Longshot to pull yourself over.

facts.subject: Carpenter
facts.text: The Master Carpenter waits on the far side of the canyon and explains that his assistants were captured after running off to join the Gerudo Thieves.

evidence.quote: If you speak with the Carpenter on the other side of the canyon, he'll report that he came to the Valley to repair the bridge.  But, his assistants ran off to join the Gerudo Thieves, and were captured.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula Token
facts.text: At night, a Gold Skulltula is found on the wall behind the Carpenter's Tent, reachable with the Longshot.

evidence.quote: There is a Gold Skulltula on the wall behind the Tent.  Kill it and take it's token with the Longshot.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula Token
facts.text: At night, another Gold Skulltula is located on the back of the natural stone arch opposite the Carpenter's Tent.

evidence.quote: Head south to the wall opposite the tent, where there is an arch formed from the natural stone.  Look on the back of the arch to see another Gold Skulltula (it has to be nighttime).  Kill the Skulltula and take it's token with the Longshot.

facts.subject: Gerudo Guards
facts.text: If Link is spotted by patrolling Gerudo guards, he is captured and thrown into a prison cell.

evidence.quote: Climb up the stairs, where you will find purple-suited Gerudos patrolling the area.  Allow one of them to see you, and you will be thrown into a prison.

facts.subject: Prison Cell
facts.text: Link can escape the prison cell by hooking the wooden awning high above the south window with the Longshot.

evidence.quote: Look south in the prison cell, and look high on the wall to find a window.  Pull yourself up to the window by shooting the wooden awning with the Longshot.

facts.subject: Gerudo Guard
facts.text: Patrolling Gerudos can be stunned with arrows, or temporarily with the Longshot.

evidence.quote: Stun the Gerudo closest to this door with an arrow (you can use the Longshot if you run out of arrows, but it doesn't stun the guards for nearly as long), then quickly jump down from the window sill and into the door before the Gerudo recovers.

facts.subject: Gerudo Thief
facts.text: When a Gerudo Thief crouches and spreads her swords apart, she is preparing a stun attack that will send Link back to the prison cell if it hits.

evidence.quote: You'll know that the Gerudo is going to do this when she crouches slightly and holds her swords far apart.  If you get hit by this attack, you will instantly lose the fight and return to the prison cell back in the Fortress.

facts.subject: Gerudo Thief
facts.text: Defeating the Gerudo Thief guarding Ichiro's cell yields a Small Key.

evidence.quote: Once the Gerudo Thief is defeated, take the Small Key she leaves behind and open Ichiro's cell.

facts.subject: Ichiro
facts.text: Link frees the carpenter Ichiro by unlocking his cell with the Small Key dropped by the Gerudo Thief.

evidence.quote: Once the Gerudo Thief is defeated, take the Small Key she leaves behind and open Ichiro's cell.  Run inside and speak with him to free him.

facts.subject: Gerudo Guard
facts.text: Using Z-Focus to peek around corners allows Link to spot a rooftop Gerudo guard and shoot her in the back with an arrow.

evidence.quote: Peek around the corner using the Z-Focus maneuver you learned back in Sacred Forest Meadow, and you'll see a patrolling Gerudo Guard.  Wait for her to face away from you, then nail her in the back with an arrow.

facts.subject: Gerudo Thief
facts.text: Defeating the Gerudo Thief near Sabooro's cell provides a Small Key used to unlock the cell.

evidence.quote: Defeat the Gerudo Thief that appears, and then open Sabooro's Cell.

facts.subject: The Kitchen
facts.text: In the Kitchen, Link can stun both guards with arrows and cross the room using Hover Boots.

evidence.quote: Shoot both of the guards in the room with arrow to stun them, then equip the Hover Boots.  Use them to run out to the ledge directly in front of you from the doorway.  From the ledge, run across to the ramp on the other side of the kitchen.

facts.subject: Fortress Roof
facts.text: Climbing the ivy around the corner of the adjacent rooftop leads to the top level of the Fortress.

evidence.quote: Jump over the gap here to the adjacent roof, then around the corner to find a wall covered with ivy.  Climb the ivy to the top level of the Fortress.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula Token
facts.text: At night, a Gold Skulltula clings to the east wall of the northern roof and can be killed and collected using the Longshot.

evidence.quote: When you reach the north end of the roof, you will see an adjacent roof with a chest sitting on it.  If it's nighttime, then you will also see a Gold Skulltula clinging to the wall on the east side.  Use the Longshot to kill it and take it's token.

facts.subject: Rooftop Chest
facts.text: A chest containing a Piece of Heart sits on an isolated roof that Link can reach by targeting it with the Longshot or summoning Pierre with the Scarecrow's Song.

evidence.quote: The gap between the roofs is too far to jump, so use the Longshot on the chest to pull yourself over to it (the Longshot's range is just barely far enough to reach it).  Alternatively, you can also use the Scarecrow's Song to make Pierre appear, presenting a closer target....Open the chest to get a Piece of Heart, then play the Sun's Song to warp back to the doorway from the Kitchen.

facts.subject: Gerudo Thief
facts.text: Defeating the Gerudo Thief by Jiro's cell yields a Small Key to unlock his cell.

evidence.quote: Take the Small Key that the Gerudo Thief leaves behind, then open the Jiro's Cell.

facts.subject: Jiro
facts.text: Link opens Jiro's cell with the Small Key and speaks with him so he can escape.

evidence.quote: Take the Small Key that the Gerudo Thief leaves behind, then open the Jiro's Cell.  Speak with him, and he'll escape.

facts.subject: Gerudo Thief
facts.text: Defeating the Gerudo Thief near Shiro's cell awards a Small Key used to open the cell.

evidence.quote: Use the Small Key that the Thief drops to open Shiro's cell, then run inside and speak with him to free him.

facts.subject: Gerudo Lieutenant
facts.text: After Shiro is freed, a Gerudo Lieutenant appears and presents Link with the Gerudo Membership Card.

evidence.quote: After Shiro is freed, a Gerudo Lieutenant will appear and speak with you.  She is so impressed by your abilities to sneak around the Fortress, that she'll make you an Honorary Gerudo Thief, and present you with a Gerudo Membership Card.

facts.subject: Gerudo's Membership Card
facts.text: The Gerudo Membership Card allows Link to roam Gerudo's Fortress freely without harassment, opens access to the Gerudo Training Ground, Horseback Archery Range, Haunted Wasteland gate, and sees the Gerudo Valley bridge repaired.

evidence.quote: This Card does many things.  For one, it lets you move around Gerudo Fortress freely without the guards harassing you.  It also lets you access the Gerudo Training Ground and the Horseback Archery Range, letting you win the Ice Arrows (Gerudo Training Ground), the Biggest Quiver, and a Piece of Heart (both from the Horseback Archery Range).  The Card's most important function, however, is that it lets Link open the gate in the northwest end of the Fortress, letting him access the Haunted Wasteland, the Desert Colossus and the Spirit Temple.  Also, the bridge back in Gerudo Valley is now repaired.

facts.subject: Sabooro
facts.text: Defeat the Gerudo Thief that appears, open Sabooro's Cell, and speak with him again to free him.

evidence.quote: Defeat the Gerudo Thief that appears, and then open Sabooro's Cell.  Speak with him again to free him, then head back out of the cell.

facts.subject: Gerudo's Training Ground
facts.text: The Gerudo's Training Ground is located in the southeast corner of the Fortress behind a door blocked by a metal grating.

evidence.quote: From this point on, you can complete the Gerudo's Training Ground at any time.  It's in the southeast corner of the Fortress.  Speak with the guard out front of the door blocked by a metal grating, pay the entrance fee and she'll let you inside.

facts.subject: Gerudo's Training Ground
facts.text: The Ice Arrows can be obtained in the Training Ground, though finishing every room requires the Silver Gauntlets from the Spirit Temple.

evidence.quote: You can complete the Training Ground and get the Ice Arrows now, but you won't be able to finish every room in the Training Ground without the Silver Gauntlets from the Spirit Temple.

facts.subject: Horseback Archery Range
facts.text: Riding up the eastern passage on Epona leads to the Horseback Archery Range.

evidence.quote: On Epona, ride up the passage that leads east to reach the massive Horseback Archery Range.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula Token
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula hangs high on the target on the north side of the Horseback Archery Range and can be killed with the Longshot.

evidence.quote: If you're after the Gold Skulltula here, then it's high on the target on the north side of the area.  Use the Longshot to kill it and take it's token, then return to the awning near the south side of the gallery.

facts.subject: Gerudo in White
facts.text: A Gerudo dressed in white stands beneath the awning on the south side of the gallery during the daytime to host the horseback archery game.

evidence.quote: Speak with the Gerudo dressed in white beneath the awning (she only appears during the daytime, so use the Sun's Song if you need to), and pay her the fee to play the game.  You must be riding Epona before you speak to her (unless you don't have Epona, in which case you just speak to her on foot).

facts.subject: Horseback Archery Range
facts.text: If you do not have Epona, the Gerudos will lend you one of their horses for the shooting range.

evidence.quote: If you don't have Epona, then don't fret; the Gerudo's will sportingly let you borrow one of their horses for the Shooting Range.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: Scoring at least 1,000 points with twenty arrows in the Horseback Archery Range awards a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: You get twenty arrows to use, and in order to win the Piece of Heart from this game you must score at least 1,000 points....Once you score 1,000 points, you'll win the Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Arrow Quiver x50
facts.text: Scoring at least 1,500 points in the Horseback Archery Range awards the Biggest Quiver upgrade.

evidence.quote: Play the game again and score at least 1,500 to earn the Quiver.  If you score 1,500 or more on your first attempt, then you have to play again to earn the Quiver and repeat the feat.

facts.subject: Haunted Wasteland Gate
facts.text: Speaking to the Gerudo atop the northwest tower opens the gate leading into the Haunted Wasteland.

evidence.quote: Once you have the Biggest Quiver, the Piece of Heart, and the Ice Arrows (if you choose), then head for the northwest corner of the Fortress and climb to the top of the tower there.  Speak with the Gerudo at the top, and she'll open the gate for you.  Run through the gate and into the desert to enter the Haunted Wasteland.

facts.subject: Haunted Wasteland Entrance
facts.text: Crossing the sinking sand gap at the entrance requires using the Longshot on the crate situated across the gap.

evidence.quote: To begin with, you will appear between a pair of flags.  Run forward through the flags, and past the crate until you reach a large gap filled with sinking sand.  Use the Longshot on the crate on the other side of the gap to pull yourself over.

facts.subject: Flag Trail
facts.text: Straying too far from the trail of flags warps Link back to the beginning of the Haunted Wasteland.

evidence.quote: Start running to the next flag you can see to the northwest, and continue in a similar fashion from flag to flag.  If you stray too far from a flag, then you will be warped back to the start of the Wasteland.

facts.subject: Song of Storms
facts.text: Playing the Song of Storms causes lightning to briefly illuminate the horizon, revealing the position of the next flag.

evidence.quote: If you can't see where the next flag is, then you can play the Song of Storms.  The lightning caused by the storm will briefly light up the horizon, revealing the next flag.

facts.subject: Carpet Merchant
facts.text: Following the sign after the second flag leads to the Carpet Merchant, who sells Bombchus.

evidence.quote: After the second flag in the series, you will reach a sign which points you to the Carpet Merchant.  Follow the sign to the Merchant if you like, but all he sells is Bombchus.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula Token
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is located at the bottom of the pit inside the stone structure surrounded by red flags.

evidence.quote: At the end of the path of flags, you will reach a large stone structure surrounded by a circle of red flags.  Near the south side of the structure is an opening.  Go through it, and drop down the cliff to it's bottom.  Kill the Gold Skulltula at the bottom of the pit, and take it's token with the Longshot.

facts.subject: Purple Rupee Chest
facts.text: Lighting both torches inside the pit with Din's Fire or Fire Arrows makes a chest containing a Purple Rupee appear.

evidence.quote: If you light both of the torches with Din's Fire or Fire Arrows, then a chest containing a Purple Rupee will appear.

facts.subject: Lens of Truth
facts.text: Activating the Lens of Truth atop the stone structure reveals a guiding ghost that leads the way across the desert to the Desert Colossus.

evidence.quote: Standing on top of the structure and facing north, turn on the Lens of Truth to see a ghost....Follow the ghost on it's winding path through the desert, and you will eventually see a pair of flags....From the pair of double flags, you'll see another flag to the west.  Run towards it to enter the Desert Colossus.

facts.subject: Leevers
facts.text: Leevers only surface in the sand, so moving onto solid ground protects Link from their attacks.

evidence.quote: The Leevers are weak and can only appear in the sand, so if you run quickly to any part of the ground that isn't sand then you're safe from them.

facts.subject: Great Fairy's Fountain
facts.text: Bombing the cracked wall between the two trees to the right of the Wasteland entrance reveals the Great Fairy's Fountain.

evidence.quote: Head for the pair of trees to your right as you enter from the Haunted Wasteland.  There is a crack in the wall between the two trees.  Use a bomb to blow it open, then enter the doorway you created.

facts.subject: Nayru's Love
facts.text: Playing Zelda's Lullaby on the Triforce symbol inside the Great Fairy's Fountain grants the magic spell Nayru's Love.

evidence.quote: Run into the fountain and stand on the Triforce symbol.  Play Zelda's Lullaby, and the Great Fairy of Sexual Dominance will appear to give you Nayru's Love, the final magic spell in the game.

facts.subject: Nayru's Love
facts.text: Nayru's Love renders Link invulnerable to damage, consuming one-quarter of a full magic meter per cast.

evidence.quote: By far the most useful of the three, Nayru's Love makes you invulnerable to all damage....The only downside to Nayru's Love is it uses one-quarter of your magic bar to cast (half of it if you haven't gotten the Magic Bar Upgrade).

facts.subject: Oasis Fairy Fountain
facts.text: Playing the Song of Storms while standing on the flat rocks near the dried oasis refills it with water to create a Fairy Fountain.

evidence.quote: Head for the dried up oasis in the south of the area.  If you stand on the pile of flat rocks near the oasis and play the Song of Storms, then the oasis will be refilled with water and becomes a Fairy Fountain.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula Token
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is perched near the fronds of a palm tree near the oasis and can be gathered using the Longshot.

evidence.quote: On one of the palm trees near the Oasis is a Gold Skulltula.  It's near the top, near the fronds.  Kill it and take it's token with the Longshot.

facts.subject: Spirit Temple Entrance
facts.text: The entrance to the Spirit Temple is located at the base of the massive Colossus statue in the west of the area.

evidence.quote: Now head for the Colossus itself, the huge stone statue in the west corner of the area.  Enter the small door at it's base.

facts.subject: Requiem of Spirit
facts.text: Exiting the Spirit Temple triggers an encounter with Sheik, who teaches the Requiem of Spirit to warp to the desert as a child.

evidence.quote: Sheik will appear in front of you, and make some cryptic remark about using the Master Sword as a boat to sail on the rivers of time, and using the song to reach the Desert as a Child.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula Token
facts.text: Dropping a bottled bug into the soft soil patch to the left of the Spirit Temple entrance unearths a Gold Skulltula.

evidence.quote: Head for the entrance to the Spirit Temple.  To the left of the door there is the game's final patch of soft earth.  Drop a Bottled Bug in the patch to make a Skulltula appear, and don't bother recapturing one of the bugs - you won't need them anymore.  Kill the Skulltula and take it's token.

facts.subject: Bugs
facts.text: Bugs can be captured under a rock located north of the oasis.

evidence.quote: If you need a new Bug, then they can be found underneath a rock north of the Oasis.

facts.subject: Magic Bean
facts.text: Link can plant his final Magic Bean into the soft soil patch to the left of the Spirit Temple entrance.

evidence.quote: Plant your final Magic Bean in the patch of soft earth, then head into the temple.

facts.subject: Spirit Temple
facts.text: The Spirit Temple is the only dungeon requiring both Young Link and Adult Link to finish, divided into the smaller West Wing for Young Link and the larger East Wing for Adult Link.

evidence.quote: The Spirit Temple is unique in that it is the only dungeon which requires both Young Link and Adult Link to finish (with the possible exception of Dodongo's Cavern, which contains a Skulltula only obtainable with Adult Link).  The Temple is divided into two wings: The West Wing, and the East Wing.  The West Wing is smaller, and is largely Young Link's territory.  The East Wing is much larger, and is Adult Link's stomping grounds.

facts.subject: Spirit Temple
facts.text: The Spirit Temple contains two dungeon items—one each for Young Link and Adult Link—though only Adult Link can use either of them.

evidence.quote: The Spirit Temple also contains two Dungeon Items, one each for Young Link and Adult Link (though Adult Link is the only person who can use either of them).

facts.subject: Hylian Shield
facts.text: Young Link should switch back to the Hylian Shield in the Spirit Temple due to fire-based enemies.

evidence.quote: Young Link is going to face a lot more fire-based enemies here, so change back to the Hylian Shield if you're use the Deku Shield.

facts.subject: Nabooru
facts.text: At the top of the entrance stairs in the Spirit Temple, Nabooru is found attempting to crawl into a small hole.

evidence.quote: At the top of the stairs, go to the left to find a Gerudo Thief trying to crawl into a hole that is far too small for her.  This is Nabooru, the second-in-command to Ganondorf that heard so many unpleasant things about as an adult.

facts.subject: Nabooru
facts.text: When speaking with Nabooru, telling her 'Nothing, really.' when she asks what you are up to leads her to ask for help fighting Ganondorf.

evidence.quote: Tell her "Nothing, really." when she asks what you're up to.  Past that, she'll ask you more questions, but it doesn't matter what your answers are.  Nabooru will ask  you to help her to - of all things - fight Ganondorf.

facts.subject: crawlspace
facts.text: After Nabooru moves aside, crawl through the crawlspace to proceed.

evidence.quote: Once Nabooru moves aside, crawl through the crawlspace yourself.

facts.subject: Armos Knight
facts.text: An Armos Knight can be defeated by dropping a bomb next to it and hitting it with a sword right before the bomb detonates, or by using Bombchus.

evidence.quote: Drop a bomb next to the Knight, and attack him with the sword just before the bomb explodes.  The explosion will then defeat the Knight.  If you screw up, use Bombchus to defeat him.

facts.subject: Keese
facts.text: In the Armos Knight Room, use the Boomerang to defeat the Keese on the wall above the crawlspace.

evidence.quote: Next, use a Boomerang to kill the Keese on the wall behind the Armos, just above another crawlspace.

facts.subject: door left of crawlspace
facts.text: Defeating all enemies in the Armos Knight Room unseals the doors, allowing passage through the door to the left of the crawlspace.

evidence.quote: Once you have killed all of the enemies in the room, the doors in the room will unseal themselves.  Go through the door to the left of the crawlspace.

facts.subject: Stalfos
facts.text: Defeat the Stalfos in the Stalfos Room by dodging its attacks and striking immediately afterwards.

evidence.quote: Run forward, and ten-year-old Link will have to fight a Stalfos. ... Dodge the Stalfos' attacks, and attack immediately after he does.

facts.subject: Green Bubble
facts.text: Stun the Green Bubble floating in the pit with the Boomerang and kill it with the Slingshot.

evidence.quote: Once you have beaten the Stalfos, face the pit with the Green Bubble floating around in it.  Stun the Bubble with the Boomerang, and defeat it with a Slingshot attack.

facts.subject: Crystal Switch
facts.text: Aiming the Boomerang to the left of the bridge allows it to hit the Crystal Switch behind the grating, causing the bridge to fall.

evidence.quote: You must now use the Boomerang to hit the Crystal Switch behind the grating.  Aim the Boomerang just to the left of the bridge, and it will hit the switch on it's way around, causing the bridge to fall.

facts.subject: Anubis
facts.text: Anubis enemies can only be defeated with Fire, such as using Din's Fire or triggering the room's fire trap.

evidence.quote: As you enter the room, you'll encounter a new, flying enemy: an Anubis.  These enemies can only be defeated with Fire. ... Use Din's Fire to kill it (you can also use the fire trap activated by the crystal switch in the room, but this takes far too long in my opinion).

facts.subject: Anubis Pit Room door
facts.text: Defeating the Anubis unseals the door on the right side of the room.

evidence.quote: Once the Anubis is defeated, the door on the right side of the room will unseal itself.  Go through it.

facts.subject: Silver Rupees
facts.text: Collecting all five Silver Rupees from the grating creates a bridge in the middle of the room.

evidence.quote: Once all of the Silver Rupees are gathered, then a bridge will appear in the middle of the room, breaking the grating wall.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Across the bridge in the Lower Silver Rupee Chamber, kill the Gold Skulltula on the right side of the grating with the Boomerang to claim its token.

evidence.quote: Once on the other side of the bridge, turn around to face the grating.  There is a Gold Skulltula on the right side of the grating.  Kill it and take it's token with the Boomerang

facts.subject: chest
facts.text: Lighting the two torches near the wall with Din's Fire spawns a chest containing a Small Key on the other side of the bridge.

evidence.quote: then light both of the torches near the wall with Din's Fire.  The lit torches will make a chest appear back on the other side of the room.  Run back across the bridge and open the chest to get a Small Key.

facts.subject: crawlspace
facts.text: In the Armos Knight Room, enter the crawlspace to the right of the door to reach the Small Hall.

evidence.quote:
You'll come out of the door on the right side of the Armos Knight Room.  To the right of the door as you come out is a crawlspace.  Go through it to it's other side.

-------------------------------
The Spirit Temple - Small Hall

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: At the top of the tiled wall in the Sun Cavern, turn around to find a Gold Skulltula and retrieve its token with the Boomerang.

evidence.quote: At the top of the tiled wall, turn around to find another Gold Skulltula.  Use the Boomerang to kill it and take it's token.

facts.subject: sun panel
facts.text: Blowing up the rock on the wall with a Bombchu reveals sunlight that hits the sun panel on the floor, unsealing the opposite door.

evidence.quote: Use a Bombchu to blow open the rock (if you don't have any Bombchus, then activate the Crystal Switch on the wall to make a chest of them appear).  The rock will be blown to pieces, revealing a patch of sunlight that will shine on the sun panel on the floor.  The sun will light up, unsealing the door on the opposite wall.

facts.subject: statue
facts.text: Pushing the statue off the cliff makes it land on a button, unsealing a door on an upper level.

evidence.quote: As you come out of the door, there is a statue near you.  Grab hold of it, and push it off the cliff on the other side of the statue.  It will fall, landing on a button.  The button will unseal a door on an upper level.

facts.subject: chest
facts.text: Lighting the pair of torches in front of the Colossus statue with Din's Fire reveals a chest containing the Dungeon Map.

evidence.quote: Run towards the center of the room, near the front of the Colossus statue, where you will find a pair of torches.  Light them with Din's Fire to make a chest appear.  Open it to get the Dungeon Map.

facts.subject: West Stairwell
facts.text: Running up the stairs in the West Stairwell leads through the door at their top.

evidence.quote: Run up the stairs and through the door at their top.

facts.subject: stone block
facts.text: Pushing the stone block with a sun panel into the beam of light on the northwest side of the room lights up the panel and opens the south door.

evidence.quote: Pull out this block, and push it into the beam of light on the northwest side of the room...The sun panel will light up, opening the door on the south side of the room.

facts.subject: Beamos
facts.text: A Beamos near the stone blocks can attack Link while he pushes stone blocks.

evidence.quote: Kill the Beamos near the stone blocks if you need to; it can attack you while you are pushing the stone blocks around.

facts.subject: Silver Rupees
facts.text: Collecting all of the Silver Rupees in the room causes the gold torch on the east side of the room to light up.

evidence.quote: Once you have all of the Silver Rupees, then the gold torch in the east side of the room will light up.

facts.subject: chest
facts.text: Lighting all three unlit torches with a Deku Stick before any go out causes a chest containing a Small Key to appear on the low wall in the south side of the room.

evidence.quote: Use this torch to light a Deku Stick, and in turn light all of the unlit torches throughout the room. If you can light all of them without one of them going out, then a chest containing a Small Key will appear...There are three unlit torches in the room; one near the east door, one in the northeast section of the room, and one near the south door.  The chest appears on the low wall in the south side of the room.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is located above the entrance door in the Upper West Stairwell.

evidence.quote: Look above the door you come through to find a Gold Skulltula.  Kill it and take it's token with the Boomerang, then go through the door at the top of the stairs.

facts.subject: Iron Knuckle
facts.text: Striking the suit of armor sitting on a throne initiates a miniboss fight against an Iron Knuckle.

evidence.quote: Run left as you enter the room to find a suit of armor sitting on a throne.  Strike the suit of armor to begin a miniboss fight.

facts.subject: Iron Knuckle
facts.text: Nayru's Love provides temporary invulnerability to attack the Iron Knuckle directly.

evidence.quote: Or the easier, faster method is to just use Nayru's Love and go kamikaze while you are invulnerable.

facts.subject: Iron Knuckle
facts.text: Once an Iron Knuckle reaches half health, part of its armor breaks off and its movement and attack speed increase.

evidence.quote: Once you whittle it down to half health, then part of it's armor will break off and his movement and attack speed will increase.

facts.subject: West Iron Knuckle Room
facts.text: Defeating the Iron Knuckle opens the door behind its throne leading to a tunnel back out to an arm of the Desert Colossus.

evidence.quote: Once the Iron Knuckle is dead, then the door behind it's throne will open.  Go through the door, and through the tunnel on the other side to find yourself back in the Desert Colossus, high up in one of it's arms.

facts.subject: chest
facts.text: Opening the chest on the left arm of the Desert Colossus awards the Silver Gauntlets.

evidence.quote: After Kaepora Gaebora's speech, open the chest in front of you to get the Silver Gauntlets.

facts.subject: Prelude of Light
facts.text: Playing the Prelude of Light teleports Link back to the Temple of Time.

evidence.quote: Play the Prelude of Light to return to the Temple of Time.

facts.subject: Master Sword
facts.text: Drawing the Master Sword again turns Link back into Adult Link.

evidence.quote: Retake the Master Sword to become Adult Link once again.

facts.subject: King Zora's throne room
facts.text: The opening behind King Zora's throne leads into Zora's Fountain.

evidence.quote: Climb up to King Zora's throne room, and go through the opening behind his throne to Zora's Fountain.

facts.subject: large gray rock
facts.text: The Silver Gauntlets allow Link to lift the large gray rock blocking the cave mouth in the southeast area of Zora's Fountain.

evidence.quote: Now that you have the Silver Gauntlets, you can lift the large gray rock in the middle of the cave mouth (it was formerly invulnerable to bombs).

facts.subject: rock
facts.text: Bombing the rock beneath the large gray rock exposes a pit that drops Link to a ramp winding through the outer walls of Zora's Fountain.

evidence.quote: Underneath, you'll find another rock.  Bomb this rock to destroy it and find a pit (sometimes this rock is already destroyed).  Drop down the pit...You'll land at the bottom of a ramp, winding up through the outer walls of Zora's Fountain to an alcove high above.

facts.subject: invisible Big Skulltulas
facts.text: Equipping the Lens of Truth reveals invisible Big Skulltulas along the winding ramp that can be killed with the Longshot.

evidence.quote: Use the Lens of Truth as you climb up the ramp to see several invisible Big Skulltulas.  Kill them with the Longshot.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is located on the wall to the left of the ladder's top in the high alcove of Zora's Fountain.

evidence.quote: Kill the (not invisible) Big Skulltula at the top, and then look on the wall left of the top of the ladder to find the final Overworld Gold Skulltula.  Kill it and take it's token.

facts.subject: Requiem of Spirit
facts.text: Playing the Requiem of Spirit teleports Link back to the Desert Colossus.

evidence.quote: Otherwise, play the Requiem of Spirit to return to the Desert Colossus.

facts.subject: Magic Leaf
facts.text: Planting Magic Beans as a child creates a Magic Leaf to the left of the Spirit Temple entrance.

evidence.quote: If you planted the Magic Beans as a child, then there will now be a Magic Leaf to the left of the door.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Riding the Magic Leaf and jumping off after the second rock at nighttime reveals an Overworld Gold Skulltula.

evidence.quote: Jump off after the second rock, and if it's nighttime you'll find the game's last OVERWORLD Gold Skulltula (the final two are found in the Spirit Temple).

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: Riding the Magic Leaf until it passes the arch east of the Spirit Temple entrance allows Link to jump onto the arch and obtain a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: Run back to the Magic Leaf, and this time ride it around until it flies by the arch to the east of the entrance to the Temple.  Jump off the leaf onto this arch to get the Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: The Spirit Temple
facts.text: The Spirit Temple is divided into the West Wing and the East Wing, and requires both Young Link and Adult Link to finish.

evidence.quote:
The Spirit Temple is unique in that it is the only dungeon which requires both
Young Link and Adult Link to finish (with the possible exception of Dodongo's
Cavern, which contains a Skulltula only obtainable with Adult Link).  The
Temple is divided into two wings: The West Wing, and the East Wing.

facts.subject: Giant blue block
facts.text: At the top of the entrance stairs, pushing the giant blue block into the pit requires the Silver Gauntlets.

evidence.quote:
At the top of the stairs, go to the right to find a doorway blocked
by a giant blue block.  Run up to the block and grab hold of it, and now that
you have the Silver Gauntlets, you can push it forward.  Keep pushing it
forward until the block falls into a pit in the ground.

facts.subject: Crystal Switch
facts.text: Hitting the Crystal Switch on the ceiling in the entrance opens the doors on the left and right sides of the room.

evidence.quote:
Bomb the Beamos, and then nail the Crystal
Switch on the ceiling above to open the doors on the left and right sides of
the room.

facts.subject: Silver Rupee
facts.text: Reaching the Silver Rupee suspended above the floor in the Rolling Boulder Room requires running out to it using the Hover Boots.

evidence.quote:
None of the Silver Rupees are particularly hard to
find, but to reach the one suspended slightly above the floor you'll need to
run out to it using the Hover Boots.

facts.subject: Rolling Boulder Room door
facts.text: Collecting all five Silver Rupees in the Rolling Boulder Room unseals the door on the far side of the room.

evidence.quote:
All five of the Silver Rupees in the room will unseal the door on the
far side of the room.

facts.subject: Rolling Boulder Room
facts.text: Playing the Song of Time moves the Block of Time to reveal a Gold Skulltula behind its original position.

evidence.quote:
To get the Gold Skulltula in this room, play the Song of Time near the Block of
Time to transport the Block of Time into an adjacent alcove.  The Gold
Skulltula is behind the Block of Time's original position.

facts.subject: Small Chest Room
facts.text: Defeating the Like-Like that drops from the ceiling allows Link to open the chest containing a Small Key.

evidence.quote:
Step forward, and a
Like-Like will fall from the ceiling.  Kill the Like-Like, then open the chest
to get a Small Key.

facts.subject: Spirit Temple Entrance
facts.text: The unlocked door on the west side of the entrance leads into the Triforce/Compass Room.

evidence.quote:
Go through the door on the west side of the room, the one we didn't go through
last time we were here.  If that isn't specific enough for you, then it's the
door that's not locked and the door that we didn't just come through.

facts.subject: Triforce/Compass Room
facts.text: Playing Zelda's Lullaby on the Triforce symbol spawns a chest on the opposite ledge containing the Compass, reached with the Longshot.

evidence.quote:
step onto the Triforce symbol and play Zelda's
Lullaby.  A chest will appear on the opposite ledge.  Pull yourself over to it
with the Longshot, and open the chest to get the Compass.

facts.subject: Spirit Temple Entrance
facts.text: The locked door on the north side of the entrance leads toward the Lower Mirror Chamber.

evidence.quote:
Go through the locked door on the north side of the room, to your left as you
come out of the Triforce/Compass Room.

facts.subject: Floor Master
facts.text: In the mirror room, an invisible Floor Master can be killed with a Jump Attack, and its offspring defeated with Din's Fire.

evidence.quote:
Run around to the other side of the
mirror, where there is an invisible Floor Master.  Z-Target him (the lens is
optional) and use a Jump Attack to kill it one hit, then use Din's Fire to kill
it's offspring.

facts.subject: Sun panels
facts.text: Shining sunlight onto the third sun panel using the mirror unseals the western door.

evidence.quote:
Push it forward until the mirror shines
the light of the sun onto each of the sun panels in the room.  The first two
sun panels will make chests appear (the first contains a recovery heart, the
second a frost trap).  The third panel will unseal the door in the west of the
room.  The last panel will make a Wall Master appear and attempt to capture
you.

facts.subject: The Colossus Chamber
facts.text: Playing Zelda's Lullaby on the Colossus statue's left hand causes a chest with a Small Key to appear on the right hand.

evidence.quote:
Stand on the symbol on the left hand and play Zelda's Lullaby, and a chest will
appear on the opposite hand (the statue's right).  Re-equip the Kokiri Boots,
and use the Longshot to pull yourself over to the opposite hand.  Open the
chest to get a Small Key.

facts.subject: Pierre
facts.text: Playing the Scarecrow's Song where Navi flutters summons Pierre, allowing Link to Longshot across the pit.

evidence.quote:
At the top, look north, and Navi will flutter over to the other
side of the pit.  Play the Scarecrow's Song, and Pierre will appear on the
other side.  Pull yourself over to him with the Longshot.

facts.subject: The Colossus Chamber
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is located behind Pierre across the pit in the Colossus Chamber, providing the one hundredth token.

evidence.quote:
Go around behind
Pierre to find another Gold Skulltula.  Kill it and take it's token.  Congratulations, that makes one hundred Skulltula Tokens.

facts.subject: The Colossus Chamber
facts.text: The locked door in the southeast corner of the Colossus Chamber leads to the next level of the temple.

evidence.quote:
Climb back up both flights of
stairs, and go through the locked door in the southeast corner.

facts.subject: Anubis
facts.text: Fire Arrows can be used to defeat the three Anubis easily in the Treble Anubis Room.

evidence.quote:
Young Link had to face one Anubis.  Adult Link gets to face three.  Use your
Fire Arrows to defeat them easily.

facts.subject: Beamos statue
facts.text: Bombing the Beamos statue on the north side of the Treble Anubis Room opens the door in the southeast.

evidence.quote:
Bomb the Beamos statue on the north side of
the room, and the door in the southeast of the room will open.  Go through it.

facts.subject: Blue switch
facts.text: Shooting an Armos with an arrow coaxes it into hopping onto the blue switch to open the sealed door on the south side of the room.

evidence.quote:
Directly in front of you as you enter is a blue switch, which opens the
sealed door on the south side of the room.  To open it, you have to coax one of
the Armos Knights surrounding the switch into stepping on it, and staying on it
long enough for you to go through the door before it seals itself again...Stand near
the sealed door, and shoot the Armos with an arrow.  It will come to life and
hop towards you.  When it steps on the switch, go through the door.

facts.subject: Upper East Stairwell
facts.text: The Upper East Stairwell contains two chests visible with the Lens of Truth that hold recovery hearts.

evidence.quote:
This room contains two chests, which contain lousy recovery hearts.  You can
use the Lens of Truth to see the chests, if you really need two recovery hearts
that badly.

facts.subject: Iron Knuckle
facts.text: Repeatedly performing a Jump Attack followed by a backflip is an effective tactic against the Iron Knuckle as Adult Link.

evidence.quote:
A tactic that seems to work particularly well, but only works with Adult Link,
is to repeatedly perform a Jump Attack followed by a backflip, followed by a
Jump Attack, followed by a backflip, etc.

facts.subject: East Iron Knuckle Room
facts.text: Defeating the Iron Knuckle opens the door behind its throne leading into a tunnel.

evidence.quote:
Once the Iron Knuckle is dead, then the door behind it's throne will open.  Go
through it and through the tunnel on the other side.

facts.subject: Colossus statue's outstretched hand
facts.text: Opening the chest that appears on the Colossus statue's outstretched hand yields the Mirror Shield.

evidence.quote: As you come out onto the Colossus statue's outstretched hand, a chest will appear.  Open it to get the Mirror Shield.

facts.subject: Mirror Shield
facts.text: The Mirror Shield can reflect light, absorb certain kinds of magic, and cannot be stolen by Like-Likes.

evidence.quote: Two, it can reflect light.  Three, it can absorb certain kinds of magic (this actually only works in one boss fight, but it's worth mentioning).  Lastly, it can't be stolen by Like-Likes.

facts.subject: East Iron Knuckle Room
facts.text: Running through the door in front and then through the northeast door leads to the Upper East Stairwell.

evidence.quote: Run through the door in front of you, then through the door in the northeast corner of the room.

facts.subject: Upper East Stairwell
facts.text: Running down the stairs in the Upper East Stairwell and through the north door leads to the Quad Armos Room.

evidence.quote: Run down the stairs and through the door on the north side of the room.

facts.subject: Quad Armos Room north door
facts.text: Standing in the beam of light and aiming the Mirror Shield at the wall's sun panel unseals the north door.

evidence.quote: Stand in the beam of light, and aim the Mirror Shield (hold R) at the sun panel on the wall.  The door in the north of the room will unseal itself.

facts.subject: Small Key Room
facts.text: Opening the chest inside the Small Key Room yields a Small Key.

evidence.quote: Run into the room and open the chest to get a Small Key.

facts.subject: Quad Armos Room
facts.text: The door on the west side of the Quad Armos Room leads into the Treble Anubis Room.

evidence.quote: Go through the door on the west side of the room, to your right as you come out of the Small Key Room.

facts.subject: Treble Anubis Room
facts.text: Unlocking and passing through the locked door in the southwest corner of the Treble Anubis Room leads to the Sliding Panels Room.

evidence.quote: Head to the southwest corner of the room and go through the locked door.

facts.subject: Sliding Panels Room
facts.text: Beamos on pillars can be killed with thrown bombs, and the wall of sliding panels can be scaled by climbing aligned platforms or using the Longshot.

evidence.quote: As you come into the room, kill the pair of Beamos on the pillars by throwing bombs at them.  Look at the wall to the right after you do.  It's covered with sliding panels, each of which contains a platform that can be climbed on.  Now, you can either wait for the panels to align and climb up... or you can just aim for the top panel and use the Longshot.

facts.subject: Sliding Panels Room
facts.text: Destroying both Beamos enemies atop the panel ladder lets you proceed through the north door.

evidence.quote: At the top of the ladder of panels, destroy both of the Beamos enemies and go through the north door.

facts.subject: Triforce Door Room door
facts.text: Standing on the Triforce symbol atop the stairs and playing Zelda's Lullaby unseals the door in front of it.

evidence.quote: Go up the stairs, and stand on the Triforce symbol at the top.  Stand on it and play Zelda's Lullaby, and the door before the triforce symbol will unseal itself.

facts.subject: Boss Key Room
facts.text: Shooting the golden eye behind the false door reveals a high platform, allowing you to Longshot up, step on a switch, and open the ornate chest holding the Boss Key.

evidence.quote: The false door to the left of the pillar of flames hides a golden eye.  Shoot the eye with an arrow, and a second platform will appear high above the room.  Aim for the Longshot target above this platform, and then jump from that platform to the one above the pillar of flames.  Step on the switch, and the pillar will disappear, letting you access the ornate chest that holds the Boss Key.

facts.subject: Triforce Door Room
facts.text: Heading through the door on the west side of the Triforce Door Room leads into the Upper Sun Chamber.

evidence.quote: Go right as you come out of the Boss Key Room, through the door on the west side of the area.

facts.subject: Upper Sun Chamber crystal switch
facts.text: Activating the crystal switch behind the bars with a vertical sword slash or spin attack opens the sealed door.

evidence.quote: activate the crystal switch behind the bars to the left with a vertical sword slash or a spin attack.  The sealed door in front of you will open.

facts.subject: Upper Sun Chamber mirror puzzle
facts.text: Bombing the odd rock formation opens a passage, allowing mirrors to be rotated east and north to channel sunlight into the ceiling mirror and activate the elevator sun panel.

evidence.quote: Go to the east side of the room, and drop a bomb on the odd formation of rock there to blast open an opening to the next room.  Staying in the current room, move around to the back of the mirror, grab hold of the left handle, and push it until the mirror faces east, through the doorway you just opened...Grab hold of the left handle, and push it until the mirror faces north...Back in the first area of this odd room, notice that the beam of sunlight from the two mirrors in the other half of the room are shining on the large mirror on the ceiling.  Jump down into the pit, and stand in this beam of sunlight.  Use it to activate the sun panel on the west wall using the Mirror Shield, and the floor will begin to lower - it's really an elevator.

facts.subject: The Colossus Room
facts.text: Reflecting the sunlight beam onto the Colossus statue's face disintegrates it into a grating, which can be Longshotted to reveal the Boss Door.

evidence.quote: Use the Mirror Shield to reflect the beam onto the statue's face, where it will begin to disintegrate, revealing a grating.  Target the grating with the Longshot, and pull yourself over to it.  When you land, the grating will rise, revealing the Boss Door.  Go through it.

facts.subject: Iron Knuckle
facts.text: Using the Biggoron Sword, Nayru's Love, and the Backflip Jump Attack trick is effective against the Iron Knuckle mini-boss in Nabooru's Throne Room.

evidence.quote: Remember to use the Biggoron Sword if you have it (which you can, should, by now), since the shield is basically worthless against the Iron Knuckle's attacks.  Again, if the battle gets too hot, then use Nayru's Love.  The Backflip/Jump Attack trick works really well on this Iron Knuckle as well.

facts.subject: Iron Knuckle
facts.text: Defeating the Iron Knuckle breaks its armor to reveal Nabooru, whom Koume and Kotake then capture with a spell before teleporting away.

evidence.quote: After a relatively quick battle, the Knuckle's armor will fall off, revealing Nabooru.  Koume and Kotake had brainwashed her, which was how she ended up as Ganondorf's loyal servant.  The twins will appear again and capture Nabooru use some kind of spell on Nabooru, whereupon she disappears, then teleport away themselves.

facts.subject: Twinrova
facts.text: In phase one of the boss fight, the Mirror Shield must be used without Z-Targeting to reflect one sister's elemental beam into the opposing sister.

evidence.quote: The Sisters each have their own element which opposes the other.  Kotake is Ice, and Koume is Fire...You have to now use the Mirror Shield to reflect this beam into the other sister, much as you reflected the beams of light earlier in the dungeon...Don't even TRY to Z-Target to aim the beam; if you do, the beam will just fire off in some random direction and won't even get near the other sister.

facts.subject: Twinrova
facts.text: In phase two, the Mirror Shield must absorb three consecutive spells of the same alignment to unleash a massive beam that stuns Twinrova.

evidence.quote: In order to stun Twinrova and make her vulnerable to attack, you have to absorb three spells of the same alignment IN A ROW.  This means that, if you absorb two fire spells, then an ice spell, then the two fires will be negated and you have to absorb two more ice spells.

After you absorb three beams of the same alignment in a row, then the Mirror Shield will unleash a massive beam back at Twinrova (keep the shield drawn to make sure the beam connects).  This will stun her momentarily, causing her to fall to the platform below her.

facts.subject: Twinrova
facts.text: Once Twinrova is stunned on the lower platform, equipping Hover Boots and landing a Jump Attack followed by sword strikes damages her.

evidence.quote: At this point, quickly equip the Hover Boots and draw your sword.  Run out to Twinrova.  When you're halfway across the gap, use a Jump Attack to go the rest of the way and damage Twinrova at the same time.  Then switch to basic sword strikes.

facts.subject: Twinrova chamber
facts.text: Defeating Twinrova leaves a Heart Container on one of the outer platforms in the chamber.

evidence.quote: Take the Heart Container that they leave behind, which is on one of the outer platforms in the chamber.  This should also be your twentieth Heart Container - congratulations.

facts.subject: Nabooru
facts.text: Entering the beam of light opposite the Heart Container awakens Nabooru as the Sage of Spirit and grants the Spirit Medallion.

evidence.quote: Enter the beam of light opposite the Heart Container to meet the Sage of Spirit: Nabooru...Once all six of the sages are assembled (Rauru, Saria, Darunia, Ruto, Impa and Nabooru), then a cutscene will take place immediately after you get the final medallion.  Rauru will tell you to return to the Temple of Time.
After completing the Spirit Temple then...and the Gerudo gives this to you.

facts.subject: Prelude of Light
facts.text: Playing the Prelude of Light warps Link back to the Temple of Time.

evidence.quote: Play the Prelude of Light to warp back to the Temple of Time.

facts.subject: Princess Zelda
facts.text: Entering the Temple of Time triggers a cutscene revealing Princess Zelda as the Seventh Sage before she is captured by Ganondorf.

evidence.quote:
As soon as you enter the Temple of Time, a cutscene will take place.  Zelda's
whereabouts are finally revealed - but she is captured by Ganondorf seconds
later....The last big
revelation in this cutscene is that there is a Seventh Sage - the Sage of Time,
Princess Zelda.

facts.subject: Princess Zelda
facts.text: Princess Zelda gives Link the Light Arrows right before she is captured.

evidence.quote:
Zelda manages to give you the Light Arrows (the only weapon,
apart from the Master Sword, which can truly hurt him) just before she is
captured.

facts.subject: Ganon's Castle
facts.text: Heading for Ganon's Castle from the upper entrance of Hyrule Castle Market triggers the Sages to automatically form a bridge of light.

evidence.quote:
Once you're done deciding if you care about any of the above things, then head
for Ganon's Castle using the upper entrance in Hyrule Castle Market.  The Sages
will automatically create a bridge of light into the castle for you when you
near it's front entrance.

facts.subject: Keep
facts.text: The Keep has six branching hallways representing the six Sages, each containing a seal that must be destroyed to lower the shield around Ganon's Tower.

evidence.quote:
The Keep is a large central hub, with six hallways branching off from it.
Each hallway represents one of the six Sages and their alignments - Forest,
Fire, Water, Shadow, Spirit, and Light.  In each hallway, there is a seal which
must be destroyed, which will lower the shield surrounding the entrance to
Ganon's Tower in the center of the Keep.

facts.subject: Entrance
facts.text: Running down the stairs at the entrance and between the pair of Beamos statues leads through a door into the Keep.

evidence.quote:
Run down the stairs as you enter the dungeon.  At the bottom of the flight of
stairs, run right between the pair of Beamos statues and through the door.

facts.subject: Keep
facts.text: Going right upon entering the Keep leads to a door with the Forest Medallion emblazoned above it.

evidence.quote:
Go right as you enter the Keep, and you will reach a door with the Forest
Medallion emblazoned above it.  Go through this door.

facts.subject: Gray Wolfos
facts.text: In Forest Seal Room One, stepping into the middle of the room spawns a Gray Wolfos, which can be defeated by backflipping away from its attack and jump attacking its back.

evidence.quote:
Step into the middle of the room, and a Gray Wolfos will appear.  Defeat it in
the usual fashion (wait for it to attack, backflip out of the way, then Jump
Attack when it's back is turned).

facts.subject: Chest
facts.text: Defeating the Gray Wolfos in Forest Seal Room One spawns a chest containing a Blue Rupee.

evidence.quote: A chest will appear, which contains a Blue Rupee.

facts.subject: Sealed door
facts.text: In Forest Seal Room One, using Din's Fire on the carpet lights four surrounding torches, and shooting a Fire Arrow at the torch above the sealed door unseals it.

evidence.quote:
Stand on the carpeting in the middle of the room, and use Din's Fire to
light the four torches surrounding the carpet.  Next, use a Fire Arrow to light
the torch above the sealed door.  The door will unseal itself.

facts.subject: Block of Time
facts.text: Playing the Song of Time when Navi flutters beneath the Silver Rupee above the pit causes a Block of Time to appear.

evidence.quote:
As you enter, look to the left to see a Silver Rupee
hanging above a pit.  Navi will flutter down underneath the Silver Rupee; play
the Song of Time when she does this, and a Block of Time will appear.

facts.subject: Block of Time
facts.text: Equipping the Iron Boots stops the fan from blowing Link around while walking out onto the Block of Time to grab the Silver Rupee.

evidence.quote:
Equip the Iron Boots to keep the fan from blowing you around, and then walk out
onto the Block of Time to take the rupee.

facts.subject: Hover Boots
facts.text: Running toward the left ledge with Hover Boots while the fan blows carries Link across the room on the wind.

evidence.quote:
Wait for the fan to stop blowing,
then switch to the Hover Boots.  Stand still and wait for the fan to start
blowing again.  Run towards the ledge on the left side of the room when this
happens, and the fan's wind will blow you to the ledge.

facts.subject: Beamos
facts.text: Tossing a bomb over to the Beamos statue destroys it.

evidence.quote:
Switch back to the Kokiri Boots, and toss a bomb over to the Beamos statue to
destroy it.

facts.subject: Beamos platform
facts.text: Jumping to the vacated Beamos platform allows Link to reach the right side of the room to collect another Silver Rupee.

evidence.quote:
Jump out to the Beamos statue's vacated platform, then go to the right side of
the room to gather another Silver Rupee.

facts.subject: Fan platform
facts.text: Climbing to the sealed door and waiting for the right fan to stop blowing allows Link to jump out and grab a Silver Rupee.

evidence.quote:
Climb up to the front of the sealed door, and look to the right to see another
Silver Rupee in front of a fan.  Wait for the fan to stop blowing, then jump out
to grab the Silver Rupee.

facts.subject: Switch
facts.text: Jumping down to the platform beneath the fan on the left of the sealed door and stepping on the switch makes a Longshot statue appear beneath the high Silver Rupee.

evidence.quote:
Look to the left of the sealed door, and there is another fan.  Beneath the fan
is another platform, with a switch on it.  Wait for the fan to stop blowing,
then jump down to the switch.  Stand on it, and a Longshot statue will appear
beneath that single Silver Rupee we couldn't reach before.

facts.subject: Sealed door
facts.text: Longshooting up to the statue and grabbing the Silver Rupee unseals the door on the opposite side of the room.

evidence.quote:
Longshot yourself
up to the statue, and then grab the Silver Rupee.  The sealed door on the other
side of the room will unseal itself.

facts.subject: Mido
facts.text: Speaking to Mido near the entrance of Kokiri Forest causes him to blame Link for the Deku Tree's death and leave.

evidence.quote: Mido is once again blocking your path, so speak to him.  Mido will blame you for the Deku Tree's death, the take off, presumably to sulk somewhere.

facts.subject: Kokiri Forest
facts.text: Crossing the lake and heading to the western edge of Kokiri Forest allows Link to exit through a hollowed log.

evidence.quote: Jump across the lake and follow the path to the western edge of Kokiri Forest.  The Kokiri who originally blocked your path here is now gone, so you can exit through the hollowed log.  Go through to leave the Kokiri Forest.

facts.subject: Saria
facts.text: Saria gives Link the Fairy Ocarina as a parting gift on the bridge leading to Hyrule Field.

evidence.quote: As you pass over the bridge leading to Hyrule Field, you will come across Saria.  She accepts that Link is leaving, and gives him the Fairy Ocarina as a parting gift.

facts.subject: Kaepora Gaebora
facts.text: Kaepora Gaebora stops Link upon entering Hyrule Field to explain how to get to Hyrule Castle and how the map works.

evidence.quote: Take a few steps forward, and simultaneously the best and most annoying character in the game will stop you: Kaepora Gaebora.  He'll explain how to get to Hyrule Castle, and also how your map works.

facts.subject: Hyrule Castle Gates
facts.text: Rolling continually along the road to Hyrule Castle ensures Link reaches it before night falls and the gates close.

evidence.quote: Follow the road to it's end to reach Hyrule Castle.  Make sure you roll all the way (by continually pressing the A button as you run), otherwise it will be night time by the time you reach Hyrule Castle, and the gates will be closed.

facts.subject: Crate
facts.text: Rolling into the crates in the rear of the Gatehouse reveals a Gold Skulltula that yields a token.

evidence.quote: Smash all of the pots in this room with your sword, then destroy the crates in the rear of the room by rolling into them.  One of them contains a Gold Skulltula.  Kill it, and take the token it leaves behind.

facts.subject: Malon
facts.text: Malon is found near the opposite side of the fountain in the Hyrule Castle Market.

evidence.quote: Head around to the opposite side of the fountain, and speak with the little girl in the white dress.  This is Malon, another important bit character.

facts.subject: Shooting Gallery
facts.text: To win the Big Bullet Bag in the Shooting Gallery, you must shoot every rupee that appears without missing any.

evidence.quote: To win the Big Bullet Bag, you have to shoot every rupee that appears without missing a single one.

facts.subject: Shooting Gallery
facts.text: In the initial Shooting Gallery round, rupees appear in a preset sequence: in the middle; from the left, then from the right; jumping from the middle; from left and right simultaneously; two from the right going left; and two from the left going right.

evidence.quote:
For this first run through the Shooting Gallery, the rupees appear in a preset order.  The order is:

1.)  In the middle
2.)  From the left, then from the right
3.)  Jumps from the middle
4.)  From the left AND right
5.)  Two rupees coming from the right, going left
6.)  Two rupees coming from the left, going right

facts.subject: Shooting Gallery Clerk
facts.text: Successfully shooting all targets in the Shooting Gallery rewards the Bullet Bag x40, increasing Slingshot capacity by 10.

evidence.quote: Keep playing the minigame until you successfully shoot all of the targets, and the clerk will award you with the Bullet Bag x40, which increases the ammo capacity of your Slingshot by 10.

facts.subject: Hyrule Castle Gatehouse Pots
facts.text: If you run out of rupees for the Shooting Gallery, smash the pots in the Gatehouse to replenish supplies.

evidence.quote: If you run out of rupees trying to complete the game, then return to the Hyrule Castle Gatehouse and smash the pots to replenish your supplies.

facts.subject: Tree
facts.text: Rolling into Kaepora Gaebora's tree in the Hyrule Castle Garden after he flies away reveals a Gold Skulltula.

evidence.quote: Listen to his rant about guards, then when he flies away roll into his tree to make a Gold Skulltula appear.

facts.subject: White Dog
facts.text: At night, a small white dog behind the stall to the left of the Market entrance from the Drawbridge will follow Link.

evidence.quote: Run behind the little stall to the left, and you should coax a small white dog into following you.

facts.subject: Little Richard's Owner
facts.text: Returning the lost dog Little Richard to the lady in the second house on the left in the Back Alley rewards a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: Speak with the big fat lady in this house, and she will recognize the lost dog as her own.  She'll reward you with a Piece of Heart for finding Little Richard (good golly, miss molly!).

facts.subject: Malon
facts.text: Malon stands near a vine on the wall in the Garden and gives Link an egg to hatch into a chicken to wake her father Talon.

evidence.quote: Malon should now be standing near a long vine on the wall to your right....Malon also gives you an Egg, for no apparent reason.  You'll need the Chicken inside the egg to wake Talon, however, so accept it with gratitude.

facts.subject: Ivy Wall
facts.text: Climbing the ivy wall and dropping down on the other side of the marble arch sneaks Link past the first two guards.

evidence.quote: Climb up the ivy wall to the top (it has some rough spots where if you don't climb up in just the right place, you'll fall off).  At the top, run forward a bit, past the gossip stone, to the top of the large marble arch.  Drop down to the ground on the other side of the arch, where you will land on the other side of the gate which formerly blocked your path.

facts.subject: Garden Hill Path
facts.text: Run up the hill at the third graphical break near its center toward the flowers at the top, then proceed forward and slightly left to find and climb a brick wall.

evidence.quote: The place you need to run up is the third break in the hill, approximately near it's center.  Go straight up the hill, and at the top there is a cluster of flowers.  Run straight at these flowers, then begin running forward and slightly to the left until you reach a wall.  Part of the wall is tiled with some bricks; climb up these bricks.

facts.subject: Castle Moat
facts.text: Jumping off the cliff past the gossip stone into the moat and swimming to its left end leads to a dirt patch and a stone platform where Talon is sleeping.

evidence.quote: Jump straight off the cliff, and go right into the moat.  Swim down to the end of the moat until it breaks left, then climb up onto the small patch of dirt, and from there climb up to the stone platform.  Run to the left from the stone platform, where you will find Talon fast asleep.

facts.subject: Talon
facts.text: Using the hatched Chicken near Talon wakes him up, causing him to run off and clear the path.

evidence.quote: Stand near Talon so that Navi flutters near him, then use the Chicken to wake him up.  Speak with Talon, and he will suddenly remember that he left Malon behind.  He'll run off, clearing the path for you to push the milk crates near Talon into position so that you can sneak in through the castle moat.

facts.subject: Drainage Pipe
facts.text: Pushing the milk crates into Talon's vacated spot lets Link jump to the drainage pipe, which must be entered during the daytime.

evidence.quote: Push both of the milk crates through the gap which was recently vacated by Talon.  You can then climb onto the crates, and then jump over to the draining pipe which feeds the moat.  If it's nighttime, then loiter around until it becomes daytime.  You won't be able to sneak through the next area at night, as the guard is increased at night.  Once it's daytime, climb through the drainage pipe to enter the next area.

facts.subject: Forest Seal
facts.text: Destroying all six spheres in the Keep removes the barrier in the middle of the Keep, granting access to Ganon's Tower.

evidence.quote: Destroying all six spheres in the Keep will remove the barrier in the middle of the Keep, letting you enter Ganon's Tower.

facts.subject: Forest Seal
facts.text: Shooting the Forest Seal barrier with a Light Arrow causes Saria to appear and send you back to the Keep.

evidence.quote: Shoot the barrier with a Light Arrow, and Saria will appear.  She will send you back to the Keep.

facts.subject: Water Seal Door
facts.text: Heading right down the stairs from the Forest Seal hallway leads to a door inscribed with the Water Medallion.
