evidence.quote: Head to the right as you come out of the Forest Seal hallway, and go right down the stairs.  At the bottom is a door inscribed with the Water Medallion.

facts.subject: Freezzard
facts.text: Fire Arrows work quite well to defeat the two Freezzards in Water Seal Room One.

evidence.quote: Two Freezzards will also appear.  Kill both of the Freezzards (Fire Arrows work quite well), and the door behind the wall of ice will unseal itself.

facts.subject: Blue Fire
facts.text: Blue Fire in the center of Water Seal Room One can be captured in an empty bottle and used to melt the sheet of ice blocking the door.

evidence.quote: Capture some of the Blue Fire in the center of the room in an empty bottle, and then use it to melt the sheet of ice blocking the door.

facts.subject: Water Seal Room Two Block Puzzle
facts.text: In Water Seal Room Two, there is a two-minute time limit to complete the ice block puzzle.

evidence.quote: In this room, you have two minutes to finish a block-pushing puzzle similar to the one you solved previously in the Ice Cavern.

facts.subject: Water Seal Room Two Block Puzzle
facts.text: To solve the puzzle, push the rear ice block right against a rock, then forward into a pit; next, push the remaining ice block forward across the pit, forward again from the door side, and forward to the opposite wall.

evidence.quote: There are two ice blocks in the room; run to the left side of the rear block, and push it to the right so that it collides with a rock in the ground.  Then go to the left side of the block, and push it forward so it lands in a pit in the front of the room.  Now, go to the remaining Ice Block, go to it's right side and push it forward, so that it slides across the pit you just filled in with the other block.  Go to the block's right side again (the side closest to the door you came through), and push the block forward.  Now go around to the side of the block closest to the right wall, and push it forward to the opposite wall.

facts.subject: Rusted Switch
facts.text: Melt the ice on the ledge with Blue Fire and hit the rusted switch with the Megaton Hammer to unseal the rear door in Water Seal Room Two.

evidence.quote: Use your bottle of Blue Fire to melt the ice.  Press down the rusted switching using the Megaton Hammer to unseal the door in the rear of the room.

facts.subject: Water Seal
facts.text: Dispelling the Water Seal orb with Light Arrows causes Princess Ruto to appear and transport you back to the Keep.

evidence.quote: Shoot the orb with the Light Arrows to dispel it.  Ruto will appear, and transport you back to the Keep.

facts.subject: Shadow Seal Door
facts.text: Going right up the stairs in the Keep leads to the door emblazoned with the Shadow Medallion.

evidence.quote: Go right up the stairs, and through the door emblazoned with the Shadow Medallion.

facts.subject: Shadow Seal Room One Chest
facts.text: The chest to the left in Shadow Seal Room One contains a Blue Rupee and can be reached using the Longshot or by playing the Song of Time to make three Blocks of Time appear and using the Hover Boots.

evidence.quote: Look to the left as you enter the room, and you'll see a chest.  Use the Longshot to pull yourself over to the chest.  Alternatively, you can also use the Song of Time to make three Blocks of Time appear, where you can then reach the chest with the Hover Boots.  The chest contains a Blue Rupee.

facts.subject: Unlit Torch
facts.text: Lighting the unlit torch with a Fire Arrow causes a series of temporary platforms to appear towards the back of the room.

evidence.quote: Turn around from the chest to see an unlit torch.  Light it with a Fire Arrow, and a series of platforms will temporarily appear.

facts.subject: Shadow Seal Room One Chest
facts.text: Stepping onto the switch on the opaque platforms before time runs out makes a chest containing the Gold Gauntlets appear on the previous ledge.

evidence.quote: Quickly run down them and step onto the switch before time runs out and the platforms disappear again... A chest will appear back on the previous ledge; go to it and open it to get the Gold Gauntlets.

facts.subject: Gold Gauntlets
facts.text: The Gold Gauntlets allow you to pick up and hurl aside various Black Obelisks found inside and outside Ganon's Castle.

evidence.quote: With these, you can hurl aside the various Black Obelisks that appear both inside and outside Ganon's Castle

facts.subject: Rusty Switch
facts.text: Following an invisible path with the Lens of Truth and smashing the rusty switch with the Megaton Hammer unseals the back door in Shadow Seal Room One.

evidence.quote: Look to the left side of the room from this platform, and use the Lens of Truth to see an invisible path.  Follow it to the rusty switch.  Smash it with the Megaton Hammer to activate it.  The door in the back of the room will unseal it.

facts.subject: Shadow Seal
facts.text: Destroying the Shadow Seal with a Light Arrow makes Impa appear to return you to the Keep.

evidence.quote: Destroy the seal with a Light Arrow, and Impa will appear to return you to the Keep.

facts.subject: Fairy Fountain
facts.text: Across the bridge of light outside Ganon's Castle, lifting and hurling aside the black obelisk with the Gold Gauntlets at the end of the small canyon reveals a Fairy Fountain.

evidence.quote: Head back across the bridge of light, and go left under the arch on the other side.  Climb over the rubble here and go to the end of the small canyon.  With the Gold Gauntlets, you can pick up the black obelisk here and hurl it aside, revealing a Fairy Fountain

facts.subject: Great Fairy
facts.text: Playing Zelda's Lullaby on the Triforce Symbol summons the Great Fairy, who enhances your defenses, doubling your health and giving heart containers a white border.

evidence.quote: Run forward and stand on the Triforce Symbol, and play Zelda's Lullaby to make the Great Fairy appear... She'll enhance your defenses - in essence, doubling your health.  Notice how your heart containers now have a white border.

facts.subject: Fire Seal Door
facts.text: The door emblazoned with the Fire Medallion is located in the Keep past the Shadow Seal.

evidence.quote: Enter the door emblazoned with the Fire Medallion past the Shadow Seal.

facts.subject: Fire Seal Room One
facts.text: Completing Fire Seal Room One requires the Gold Gauntlets and wearing the Goron Tunic to survive the room's heat.

evidence.quote: You can't complete this Seal without the Gold Gauntlets... Equip your Goron Tunic as you enter to survive the heat of the room.

facts.subject: Fire Seal Room One Silver Rupees
facts.text: Collecting all five Silver Rupees across the sinking platforms, rotating flames ledge, under the black obelisk, on the Fire Slug platform, and across the makeshift pillar bridge unseals the rear door.

evidence.quote: Jump out to the platform and grab the Silver Rupee... Follow the path of the flames around to the rear of the platform, and take the second Silver Rupee... Climb up to the black obelisk, and with the Gold Gauntlets you can throw it aside, where it will land across the room.  Take the Silver Rupee that was underneath the pillar... Kill the Fire Slug, and take the Silver Rupee.  The pillar you tossed aside earlier is now forming a makeshift bridge to the last Silver Rupee.  Jump out to the pillar, and then to the last Silver Rupee.  The door in the rear of the room will now unseal itself.

facts.subject: Fire Seal Room One Rear Door
facts.text: Using the Longshot on the target to the right of the unsealed door pulls you over to reach the exit.

evidence.quote: Look towards the back of the room, and use the Longshot on the target to the right of the now-unsealed door to pull yourself over to it.  Go through the door.

facts.subject: Fire Seal
facts.text: Destroying the Fire Seal with a Light Arrow summons Darunia, who returns you to the Keep.

evidence.quote: Destroy the Seal with a Light Arrow, and Darunia will appear to send you back to the Keep.

facts.subject: Light Seal Door
facts.text: At the bottom of the stairs to the right of the Fire Seal door, throwing aside a black obelisk reveals the door inscribed with the Light Medallion.

evidence.quote: At the bottom of the stairs, there is another black obelisk.  Throw it aside, where it will shatter against the shield guarding Ganon's Tower.  The door behind the black obelisk is inscribed with the Light Medallion.  Go through it.

facts.subject: Light Seal Room One Chest
facts.text: Defeating the invisible Big Skulltula and four invisible Keese using the Lens of Truth makes a chest containing a Small Key appear in the middle of Light Seal Room One.

evidence.quote: This room is full of invisible enemies; namely, a Big Skulltula and four invisible Keese.  Use the Lens of Truth to find and kill them all, then open the chest that appears in the middle of the room to get a Small Key.

facts.subject: Light Seal Room Two Chest
facts.text: Playing Zelda's Lullaby on the Triforce symbol makes a chest appear with a Small Key.

evidence.quote: Stand on the triforce symbol and play Zelda's Lullaby.  Open the chest that appears to get a Small Key.

facts.subject: Light Seal Room Three Silver Rupees
facts.text: Within a one-minute time limit, Longshot to the ceiling target above the central pillar and collect all five Silver Rupees from the alcoves and pillar area to unseal the exit door.

evidence.quote: Time Limit: 1:00... Look on the ceiling above the pillar to see a Longshot target.  Pull yourself up to it using the Longshot.  When you land, you will get the first Silver Rupee... Look to the left of the sealed door on the other side of the room, where you will find a small alcove with the second Silver Rupee... From this alcove, run back towards the pillar in the center of the room and into the alcove beside it to get another Silver Rupee.  Head around to the opposite side of the pillar, where you will find two more identically placed Silver Rupees; one in alcove, another near the pillar.  Once you get all five of the rupees, then the sealed door will unseal itself.

facts.subject: Light Seal Room Three
facts.text: Using the Lens of Truth in Light Seal Room Three reveals that the wall on the opposite side of the room is fake.

evidence.quote: Use the Lens of Truth, and you'll see the wall on the other side of the room is fake.

facts.subject: Light Seal Orb
facts.text: Walking through the fake wall reveals the orb, which must be shot with a Light Arrow so Rauru can appear and send Link back to the Keep.

evidence.quote: Walk through it, to find the orb.  Shoot it with a Light Arrow, and Rauru (remember Rauru?) will appear to send you back to the Keep.

facts.subject: Spirit Seal Door
facts.text: Going right from the Light Seal door and up the stairs leads to a door emblazoned with the Spirit Medallion.

evidence.quote: Go to the right from the Light Seal door, and up the flight of stairs.  At the top there is a door emblazoned with the Spirit Medallion.  Go through it.

facts.subject: Silver Rupee
facts.text: In Spirit Seal Room One, destroying the Beamos statue allows Link to Longshot to the ceiling target and claim the Silver Rupee above it, followed by a second Silver Rupee behind the Beamos.

evidence.quote: Destroy the Beamos statue directly in front of you with a Bomb or a Bombchu, then use the Longshot target on the ceiling to pull yourself up to the rupee above the (former) Beamos.  Take the second Silver Rupee from behind the Beamos.

facts.subject: Silver Rupee
facts.text: The three remaining Silver Rupees in Spirit Seal Room One are gathered near Blade Traps located in the corners of the room.

evidence.quote: Gather the three remaining Silver Rupees from near the Blade Traps in the corners of the room.

facts.subject: Spirit Seal Room One Door
facts.text: Collecting all five Silver Rupees in Spirit Seal Room One unseals the rear door.

evidence.quote: Once you have all five of the Silver Rupees, the door in the rear of the room will unseal itself.

facts.subject: Fire Slug
facts.text: Spirit Seal Room Two contains a pair of Fire Slugs that must be destroyed.

evidence.quote: Destroy the pair of Fire Slugs in this room, then look towards the steel bars on the left.

facts.subject: Treasure Chest
facts.text: Hitting the Crystal Switch on the other side of the steel bars with a Spin Attack spawns a chest containing Bombchus.

evidence.quote: There is a Crystal Switch just on the other side.  Use the Spin Attack to activate the switch, making a chest appear.  Open the chest to get some Bombchus - the clue to solving this puzzle.

facts.subject: Crystal Switch
facts.text: Sending a Bombchu forward through the gap near the top of the bars activates the Crystal Switch between two torches on the other side of the room, unsealing the door.

evidence.quote: Stand back a bit, line yourself up with the crystal switch, and let loose a Bombchu.  It will go forward, through a gap near the top of the bars, and to the other side of the room, activating the switch....Go through the door after it unseals itself

facts.subject: Spider Web
facts.text: Burning the spider web on the ceiling with a Fire Arrow allows a beam of sunlight to shine into the room.

evidence.quote: Destroy the spider web with a Fire Arrow, and a beam of sunlight will shine into the room.

facts.subject: Sun Panel
facts.text: Reflecting sunlight with the Mirror Shield onto the sun panel to the right of the tunnel unseals the door, while other sun panels summon Wall Masters.

evidence.quote: Use the Mirror Shield to activate the sun panels in the room.  The sun panel you want is the one to the right of the tunnel you came through (if you face the sealed door, it's directly behind you and to the right).  The other sun panels will just make Wall Masters appear, who you must then defeat.

facts.subject: Spirit Seal Orb
facts.text: Shooting the Spirit Seal Orb with a Light Arrow causes Nabooru to appear, returning Link to the Keep and dispelling the barrier around Ganon's Tower.

evidence.quote: Destroy the Orb here with a Light Arrow, and Nabooru will appear and send you back to the Keep.  This should be the last of the six seals, so the barrier surrounding Ganon's Tower will disappear.

facts.subject: Bridge to Ganon's Tower
facts.text: Crossing the bridge to the left inside the Keep leads through the entrance door into Ganon's Tower.

evidence.quote: With the barrier around Ganon's Tower gone, head to the right until you see a bridge to the left.  Go across this bridge and through the door to enter Ganon's Tower.

facts.subject: Fire Keese
facts.text: Tower Floor One contains four Fire Keese that must be killed before proceeding up the spiral staircase.

evidence.quote: Kill the quad of Fire Keese in this room, then head up the spiral staircase to the left.  Watch out for the Fire Keese on your way up the stairwell.

facts.subject: Tower Floor One Staircase
facts.text: Climbing the spiral staircase in Tower Floor One leads to a door on the right at the top.

evidence.quote: head up the spiral staircase to the left.  Watch out for the Fire Keese on your way up the stairwell.  At the top, go through the door on the right.

facts.subject: Dinolfos
facts.text: Defeating both Dinolfos in Tower Floor Two unseals both doors in the room.

evidence.quote: You'll have to defeat both of the Dinolfos in the room before it will open....Once both of the Dinolfos are defeated, then the doors will unseal.

facts.subject: Tower Floor Two Staircase
facts.text: Climbing the Tower Floor Two stairs leads to a door on the left at the landing.

evidence.quote: Climb up the stairs, and at landing on top, go through the door on the left.

facts.subject: Stalfos
facts.text: Entering Tower Floor Three spawns two Stalfos around a large central pillar of flames.

evidence.quote: Step into the room, and two Stalfos will appear.  The large pillar of flames in the middle of the room makes fighting this pair of Stalfos a delicate matter.

facts.subject: Ornate Chest
facts.text: Defeating both Stalfos causes the central flame pillar to extinguish, revealing an ornate chest containing the Boss Key.

evidence.quote: Once both of the Stalfos are dead, then the pillar of flames in the middle of the room will die away, revealing an ornate chest.  Open it to get the Boss Key.

facts.subject: Tower Floor Three Staircase
facts.text: Passing through the door behind the Boss Key chest and climbing the stairs leads to a door on the left.

evidence.quote: Go through the door behind the chest....Climb up the stairs, and at the landing on top, go through the door on the left.

facts.subject: Iron Knuckle
facts.text: Shooting one of the two Iron Knuckles in Tower Floor Four with an arrow awakens it individually, enabling the Backflip-Jump Attack pattern.

evidence.quote: If you shoot one of them with an arrow, then it will come to life and come towards you without disturbing the other.  If you wake them up one at a time in this fashion, then you can do the Backflip-Jump Attack trick, which they still haven't learned to defend against.

facts.subject: Iron Knuckle
facts.text: If both Iron Knuckles on Tower Floor Four are accidentally awakened simultaneously, activating Nayru's Love is recommended.

evidence.quote: If you accidentally awaken both of the Iron Knuckles, then using Nayru's Love is an excellent idea.

facts.subject: Tower Floor Four Staircase
facts.text: Defeating both Iron Knuckles unseals the doors, leading up a staircase to a boss door on the left.

evidence.quote: Once both of the Iron Knuckles are defeated, then the doors will unseal themselves.  Go through the door that the camera focuses on.
Climb up the stairs, and at the landing on top, go through the boss door on the left.

facts.subject: Pots
facts.text: Tower Floor Five contains numerous pots that provide Magic Power and Recovery Hearts when broken.

evidence.quote: This room contains a ton of pots.  Smash them to find Magic Power and Recovery Hearts, if you need them.

facts.subject: Tower Floor Five Staircase
facts.text: Exiting the right door in Tower Floor Five and ascending the stairs leads through a boss door to the fight with King of Thieves Ganondorf.

evidence.quote: Go through the door to the right of where you came in to head further up the tower....Climb up the stairs, and at the landing on top, go through the boss door on the left.

facts.subject: Ganondorf
facts.text: During the fight against Ganondorf, Navi cannot Z-Target or offer advice until Ganondorf is stunned with a Light Arrow.

evidence.quote: Navi is unavailable during this fight, meaning you can't Z-Target and she can't give you advice with C-Up.  Once Ganondorf is stunned with a Light Arrow, then Navi can Z-Target again, but Navi becomes unavailable once more when Ganondorf recovers.

facts.subject: Ganondorf
facts.text: Ganondorf's lightning balls must be reflected back at him with sword strikes or Empty Bottles until he is struck and stunned, allowing Link to hit him with a Light Arrow.

evidence.quote: Ganondorf will throw balls of lightning at you, which you must reflect back at him with sword strikes (or you can use Empty Bottles if you're feeling creative)....Ganondorf will reflect the balls back at you as well, so keeping reflecting them until one strikes and stuns Ganondorf.  There is a new wrinkle to the fight at this point; you must now shoot Ganondorf with a Light Arrow, whereupon he will become stunned.

facts.subject: Ganondorf
facts.text: Equipping the Hover Boots allows Link to float across the collapsed floor pit to damage the stunned Ganondorf with a Jump Attack.

evidence.quote: Quickly equip the Hover Boots and use them to cross the pit in the middle of the floor.  Just like in the Twinrova fight, use a Jump Attack when you're halfway across the pit to deal extra damage to him, then switch to normal attacks.

facts.subject: Ganondorf
facts.text: Shooting Ganondorf with a Light Arrow when he raises both arms to charge a large spell will immediately cancel the attack and stun him.

evidence.quote: Ganondorf will occasionally use a new attack where he will charge up a lot of power (you'll know when he's doing it, as he will hold up both arms to create the spell instead of just one arm for the Lightning Ball).  To stop him from using this attack, shoot him with a Light Arrow.  This will instantly stun him, letting you get in more attacks.

facts.subject: Tower Escape
facts.text: Following Ganondorf's defeat, Link and Zelda have three minutes to escape the crumbling tower.

evidence.quote: You've got three minutes to escape the tower before it is destroyed... with you inside.

facts.subject: Tower Escape Route
facts.text: Link must stay close to Princess Zelda as she navigates Tower Floor Five and the Tower Exterior ledges, because only Zelda can unseal the exit doors.

evidence.quote: Follow Zelda down the tower.  Only she can open the sealed doors on the way down, so there's no point getting too far ahead of her....Go to the left, keeping near Zelda to ensure that she keeps moving.  When she gets to the other side of the room, she'll open the door....Jump over to the ledge that Zelda stands on, and keep following her down the tower.  At the bottom, she'll unseal another door.

facts.subject: Tower Floor Four
facts.text: In Tower Floor Four, follow Zelda around the burning rubble in the middle of the room and proceed through the door after she opens it.

evidence.quote:
Follow Zelda to the right, around the burning rubble in the middle of the room.
Go through the door after Zelda opens it.

facts.subject: Tower Exterior
facts.text: Follow Zelda down Tower Exterior and go through the door at the bottom after she opens it.

evidence.quote:
Keep following Zelda down the tower.  When she opens the door at the bottom, go
through it.

facts.subject: Tower Floor Three Stalfos
facts.text: In Tower Floor Three, Zelda is trapped behind a pillar of flame in the middle of the room and two Stalfos appear that must be defeated to progress.

evidence.quote:
Keep near Zelda in this room, and when she reaches the middle of the room
she'll be trapped behind a pillar of flame.  Two Stalfos will appear, and
you've got to defeat them to progress.

facts.subject: Tower Floor Three Stalfos
facts.text: Casting Nayru's Love and attacking with the Biggoron Sword allows you to quickly defeat the two Stalfos in Tower Floor Three to free Zelda.

evidence.quote:
You don't have time to play it
carefully, so use Nayru's Love and the Biggoron Sword and just go kamikaze on
the Stalfos.  Once they are both dead, Zelda will be freed.

facts.subject: Tower Floor Two
facts.text: In Tower Floor Two, follow Zelda through the burning rubble and through the door she opens, down the stairs, and through the door on the left at the bottom.

evidence.quote:
Follow Zelda through the burning rubble, and when she reaches the door she'll
open it.  Go through the door here, and keep following Zelda down the stairs.
At the bottom, Zelda will open the door on the left.  Go through it.

facts.subject: Keep Bridge Redead
facts.text: A Redead is positioned on the bridge in the Keep of Ganon's Castle, which can be run past or killed with the Biggoron Sword.

evidence.quote:
Run along to the end of the bridge.  Run past the Redead (whose sole purpose
seems to be to waste whatever precious seconds you may have remaining), or kill
it with the Biggoron Sword.

facts.subject: Keep Bridge
facts.text: At the other end of the bridge in the Keep, Zelda opens the door leading up the stairs to the final door to escape the tower.

evidence.quote:
At the other end of the bridge, Zelda will open
the door.  Go through it and up the stairs on the other side, and wait for
Zelda to open the final door to escape the tower.

facts.subject: Ganon
facts.text: After Ganondorf transforms into Ganon among the tower ruins, Link lacks access to the Master Sword at first, but Navi is available to Z-Target Ganon.

evidence.quote:
After a cutscene, run forward towards the ruins of the tower, where Ganondorf
will emerge.  Except now he has been transformed into the evil demon Ganon....At the start of the fight you won't have access to the Master Sword....For this
ultimate showdown, Navi will be available for you to Z-Target Ganon, unlike in
the previous fight against him.

facts.subject: Ganon
facts.text: Ganon's weakspot is his tail, which can be struck with a Jump Attack using the Biggoron Sword or Megaton Hammer after performing side dodges to get behind him.

evidence.quote:
Like all evil demons of the underworld, Ganon's weakspot is his tail.  In his
first phase, you'll have to Z-Target Ganon and then begin performing side
dodges (hold right or left and press A) to speed around behind Ganon.  When you
get behind him, do a Jump Attack with the Biggoron Sword or Megaton Hammer to
deal a hefty amount of damage to Ganon.

facts.subject: Master Sword
facts.text: Damaging Ganon's tail repeatedly lowers the perimeter flames around the arena, allowing Link to run to Zelda and reclaim the Master Sword.

evidence.quote:
Repeat this method until a cutscene shows the flames around the perimeter of
the arena lowering.  Run over to Zelda and retake the Master Sword when this
happens.

facts.subject: Ganon
facts.text: In the final phase, get behind Ganon by shooting his face with a Light Arrow or rolling between his legs, attack his tail, and strike the final blow with the Master Sword.

evidence.quote:
You have two options: shoot him in the face with a Light Arrow, or
release your Z-Target and roll between his legs.  Whichever path you choose,
once you are on his backside, Z-Target him and perform a Jump Attack on his
tail....Only the Master Sword can defeat Ganon.  After a cutscene, you will be
prompted to attack Ganondorf while he is being held in place by Zelda's magic.
Do this, and the game is over.

facts.subject: Main Adventure Progression
facts.text: The game's standard progression chart outlines 35 main steps from obtaining the Kokiri Sword and Deku Shield to defeating Ganon.

evidence.quote:
This is the Walkthrough for people who don't want to be told exactly what
to do and where to go, but is instead a general outline of the game's standard
and preferred progression chart...35. Defeat Ganon.

facts.subject: Happy Mask Salesman Sidequest
facts.text: The Happy Mask Salesman sidequest is available to Young Link at the Happy Mask Shop in Hyrule Castle Market after opening the gate to Death Mountain Trail.

evidence.quote:
The Happy Mask Salesman Sidequest is the only Sidequest available to Young
Link.  The sidequest begins at the Happy Mask Shop in Hyrule Castle Market, at
any time after the opening the gate to Death Mountain Trail.

facts.subject: Mask of Truth
facts.text: Completing the Happy Mask Salesman sidequest awards the Mask of Truth, which allows reading hints from Gossip Stones across Hyrule.

evidence.quote:
The Happy Mask Salesman Sidequest ultimately nets you the Mask of Truth, which
lets you get hints from the Gossip Stones that dot Hyrule.

facts.subject: Deku Stick and Deku Nut upgrades
facts.text: Capacity upgrades for Deku Sticks and Deku Nuts are obtained in the Forest Stage in connection with the Happy Mask Salesman sidequest.

evidence.quote:
The only thing you really get out of this sidequest which
is worth mentioning is a Deku Stick and Deku Nut capacity upgrade, both of
which are obtained in the Forest Stage

facts.subject: Keaton Mask
facts.text: The Keaton Mask is borrowed for 10 Rupees and sold for 15 Rupees to the guard near the gate to Death Mountain Trail in Kakariko Village.

evidence.quote:
Sold To: Guard near the gate to Death Mountain Trail in Kakariko Village.
Borrow Price: 10 Rupees
Sell Price: 15 Rupees

facts.subject: Skull Mask
facts.text: The Skull Mask is borrowed for 15 Rupees and sold for 10 Rupees to the lone Skullkid in southwest Lost Woods.

evidence.quote:
Sold To: The Lone Skullkid in southwest Lost Woods.
Borrow Price: 15 Rupees
Sell Price: 10 Rupees

facts.subject: Skull Mask
facts.text: The Skull Mask allows access to the Deku Stick capacity upgrade in the Forest Stage.

evidence.quote:
The
Skull Mask also lets you access the Deku Stick capacity upgrade in the Forest
Stage.

facts.subject: Spooky Mask
facts.text: The Spooky Mask is borrowed for 30 Rupees and sold for 30 Rupees to Dampe's Fanboy in Kakariko Graveyard during the day.

evidence.quote:
Sold To: Dampe's Fanboy in the Kakariko Graveyard (daytime only)
Borrow Price: 30 Rupees
Sell Price: 30 Rupees

facts.subject: Bunny Hood
facts.text: The Bunny Hood is borrowed for 50 Rupees and sold for 500 Rupees to the Running Man in Hyrule Field after Jabu-Jabu's Belly is finished.

evidence.quote:
Sold To: The Running Man in Hyrule Field (only after Jabu-Jabu's Belly is
finished)
Borrow Price: 50 Rupees
Sell Price: 500 Rupees

facts.subject: Bunny Hood Sale
facts.text: Without the Giant's Wallet, Link will only receive 99 or 200 Rupees from the 500 Rupees the Running Man pays for the Bunny Hood.

evidence.quote:
Sell Price: 500 Rupees...if you don't have the Giant's Wallet then you'll only get 99 or 200 out of that
five hundred.

facts.subject: Mask of Truth
facts.text: The Mask of Truth can only be worn by Young Link to get hints from Gossip Stones, and can be used in the Forest Stage to earn a Deku Nut capacity upgrade.

evidence.quote:
The Mask of Truth, the best of the available masks, lets you use the Gossip
Stones around Hyrule to receive hints.  Which would be cool, except only Young
Link can wear the Mask of Truth...The Mask of Truth can also be used in the
Forest Stage to earn a Deku Nut capacity upgrade.

facts.subject: Goron Mask
facts.text: Wearing the Goron Mask causes Gorons to mistake Link for an actual Goron, deplore how small and weak he is, and insist he eat something.

evidence.quote:
When worn, this Masks makes those lovably foolish Gorons mistake you for an
actual Goron, who will deplore about what a small, weak Goron you are, and
insist you eat something.

facts.subject: Zora Mask
facts.text: Speaking to Zoras while wearing the Zora Mask causes them to treat Link sarcastically.

evidence.quote:
If you speak to Zoras while wearing this mask, they will sarcastically treat
you the way you'd expect a little kid running around in a mask to be treated.

facts.subject: Gerudo Mask
facts.text: The Gerudo Mask does not fool any of the Gerudos.

evidence.quote:
If you thought this mask would actually fool any of the Gerudos, then go jump
off a cliff.

facts.subject: Epona's Song
facts.text: Speaking with Malon in the pasture of Lon Lon Ranch as Young Link until she mentions her mother and playing the Ocarina teaches Epona's Song, which tames Epona and yields free milk from any cow.

evidence.quote:
Head for
Lon Lon Ranch during the daytime, and head for the middle of the pasture.
Speak with Malon until she mentions her mother, then pull out your Ocarina
(Fairy Ocarina, Ocarina of Time, it doesn't matter which).  Malon will then
teach you Epona's Song, which tames Epona and also makes any Cow in the game
give you a free bottle of Lon Lon Milk.

facts.subject: Ingo Horse Rental
facts.text: Speaking with Ingo at the rear pasture as Adult Link allows you to ride a horse for ten rupees.

evidence.quote:
Run to the pasture in the rear of the ranch, and speak with Ingo.
After a lengthy speech about how great Ganondorf is, Ingo will offer to let you
ride a horse for ten rupees.

facts.subject: Epona
facts.text: Playing Epona's Song inside the pasture causes Epona to appear and run toward Link.

evidence.quote:
Ignore the horse that Ingo offers you, and play Epona's Song.  Epona will
appear and run towards you.

facts.subject: Ingo's First Race
facts.text: Speaking to Ingo while riding Epona prompts a horse race for fifty rupees, which can be won by using two or three carrots to pass him on the inside rail of a corner and blocking him.

evidence.quote:
speak to Ingo while riding Epona and he will
challenge you to a race for fifty rupees....In the first race against Ingo, he goes fairly slowly, and
takes the corners very wide.  Stay close behind him until he gets near a
corner, then quickly hug the inside rail and burn two or three carrots to shoot
in front of him.  At this point, just carefully steer yourself to stay directly
in front Ingo, preventing him from getting in front of you.

facts.subject: Ingo's Second Race
facts.text: Winning the first race causes Ingo to bet Epona on a rematch where Link can burn two or three carrots on the first turn to pass and block him.

evidence.quote:
After you win the first race, Ingo will have a meltdown and frantically bet
Epona on a rematch.  Agree.  This time, Ingo will cheat and leave the starting
gate a second before the clock goes off.  Even though he now goes slightly
faster and cheats at the start, the race is still identical, and he still takes
turns incredibly wide.  Wait for the first turn in the track, and burn two or
three carrots to shoot in front of him while he takes the wide corner.

facts.subject: Lon Lon Ranch
facts.text: Link can escape Lon Lon Ranch by running counter-clockwise around the pasture track on Epona and burning all six carrots to jump over the closed gate.

evidence.quote: Return to the track going around the pasture, and run around it in a counter-clockwise direction (the opposite direction you go in the race)...When you reach the last turn in the course and can see the gate directly in front of you, burn all six of your carrots at once and run straight at the gate.  If you aim yourself properly you'll soar right over the gate and Epona will now be yours to use in Hyrule Field, Lake Hylia, Gerudo Valley and Lon Lon Ranch.

facts.subject: Epona
facts.text: Playing Epona's Song makes Epona appear.

evidence.quote: Simply play Epona's Song to make her appear.

facts.subject: Transportation Songs
facts.text: Playing any Transportation Song automatically sets the timer on any timed trading items to 0:01.

evidence.quote: Using any of the Transportation Songs (Prelude of Light, Minuet of Forest, etc.) will automatically set the timer on any Timed Items to 0:01.

facts.subject: Cucco Lady
facts.text: The Cucco Lady standing near the pasture by the entrance to Kakariko Graveyard gives Link the Pocket Egg.

evidence.quote: In order to obtain the Pocket Egg, head for Kakariko Village and speak with the Cucco Lady.  She is standing near the pasture in the rear of town, near the entrance to the Kakariko Graveyard.

facts.subject: Pocket Egg
facts.text: Playing the Sun's Song hatches the Pocket Egg into the Pocket Cucco.

evidence.quote: Once you have the Pocket Egg, play the Sun's Song until the Pocket Egg hatches into the Pocket Cucco.

facts.subject: Talon
facts.text: Using the Pocket Cucco near Talon while he is sleeping inside the building at the bottom of the stairs wakes him up.

evidence.quote: Make sure that it is daytime, then enter the building at the bottom of the stairs near the middle of town.  Talon is sleeping on the bed.  Use the Pocket Cucco while standing near Talon, and he will awaken.

facts.subject: Cucco Lady
facts.text: Showing the hatched Pocket Cucco to the Cucco Lady in Kakariko Village earns Cojiro.

evidence.quote: Return to the Cucco Lady and show her the Pocket Cucco, and she'll give you Cojiro, the Blue Cucco.

facts.subject: Carpenter's Son
facts.text: Showing Cojiro to the Carpenter's Son in the Lost Woods rewards Link with the Odd Mushroom.

evidence.quote: Show him Cojiro, and the Carpenter's Son will admit that he has been cursed, and the only cure is a Potion which must be made from an Odd Mushroom.  He'll give you the Odd Mushroom.

facts.subject: Hag
facts.text: Showing the Odd Mushroom to the Hag behind the Kakariko Potion Shop turns it into the Odd Potion within a 3:00 time limit.

evidence.quote: Time Limit: 3:00 ... The Odd Mushroom is on a three minute time limit, so you have to high tail it back to Kakariko Village.

facts.subject: Kokiri Girl
facts.text: Giving the Odd Potion to the Kokiri Girl in the Lost Woods rewards Link with the Poacher's Saw.

evidence.quote: Give the Kokiri Girl the Odd Potion, and she'll give you the Poacher's Saw.

facts.subject: Carpenter
facts.text: Showing the Poacher's Saw to the Carpenter outside the tent in Gerudo Valley yields the Broken Goron's Sword.

evidence.quote: Speak with the Carpenter on the other side of the bridge, standing outside of the tent, and then show him the Poacher's Saw.  He'll recognize it as his own, and give you the Broken Goron's Sword.

facts.subject: Biggoron
facts.text: Showing the Broken Goron's Sword to Biggoron at the peak of Death Mountain prompts him to ask for medicinal eyedrops from King Zora.

evidence.quote: Once you're at the peak, arouse Biggoron's attention by standing on the right side of the cliff, and then show him the Broken Goron's Sword.  He'll admit that he'd love to  repair the Sword, but he can't because the last eruption blinded him.  You'll have to get some medicinal eyedrops from the King Zora first.

facts.subject: Potion Shop
facts.text: A Blue Flame can be purchased from the Potion Shop in Kakariko Village for 300 rupees.

evidence.quote: You have two options to unfreeze King Zora: you can either go to Kakariko Village and purchase a Blue Flame from the Potion Shop there (for a hefty 300 rupee price tag), or you can head for the Ice Cavern ahead of schedule and get a Blue Flame for free.

facts.subject: Freezzard
facts.text: Defeating three Freezzards in the first room of the Ice Cavern with sword strikes or Din's Fire opens the locked door.

evidence.quote: Enter the Ice Cavern, and run down the passage to the first room.  Kill the three Freezzard's in the room using sword strikes or Din's Fire while dodging the Blade Trap.  Enter the door that opens.

facts.subject: Silver Rupees
facts.text: Collecting all Silver Rupees in the rotating ice blade room of the Ice Cavern unlocks the next door.

evidence.quote: Run down the hall to the next room, which contains a large blade made of ice that rotates steadily.  Gather all of the Silver Rupees in the room, and enter the door that opens.

facts.subject: Blue Fire
facts.text: A pillar of Blue Fire can be captured in an empty bottle on the second level of the Ice Cavern.

evidence.quote: Run to the end of this passage, and in the next room run along the different platforms to the pillar of Blue Fire on the second level...Capture the Blue Fire in a bottle, and return to the King Zora.

facts.subject: King Zora
facts.text: Unfreezing King Zora with Blue Fire and presenting the Prescription gives Link the Eyeball Frog.

evidence.quote: Use the bottle of Blue Fire while standing next to the King to unfreeze him.  Show him the Prescription, and he'll give you the ingredients needed.
The Eyeball Frog must be delivered to the scientist in the Observatory at Lake Hylia in less then three minutes.

facts.subject: Scientist
facts.text: Delivering the Eyeball Frog to the scientist in the Lake Hylia Observatory within 3:00 yields the Eyedrops.

evidence.quote: Part VIII: The Eyeball Frog...Time Limit: 3:00...Step inside and show the Scientist the Eyeball Frog, and after mistaking them for his dinner, he'll make you the Eyedrops.

facts.subject: Biggoron's Eyedrops
facts.text: Delivering Biggoron's Eyedrops to Biggoron on Death Mountain has a four minute time limit.

evidence.quote:
Time Limit: 4:00

You've now got to run clear across Hyrule and climb Death Mountain in less then
four minutes.

facts.subject: Biggoron
facts.text: Ride Epona to Kakariko Village and travel up Death Mountain Trail to deliver the Eyedrops to Biggoron.

evidence.quote:
Step outside the Observatory and get back on Epona.  Ride her back to Hyrule
Field, and jump back over the fences.  Go to Kakariko Village in the northeast
corner of the zone.  Get off Epona and enter the Village, then go to Death
Mountain Trail in the north of the Village...Give Biggoron the Eyedrops.

facts.subject: Sun's Song
facts.text: Playing the Sun's Song six times forces three days to pass while waiting for Biggoron to repair the sword.

evidence.quote:
Play the Sun's Song six times to force three days to pass, then
show Biggoron your Claim Check.

facts.subject: Biggoron
facts.text: Showing the Claim Check to Biggoron rewards Link with the Biggoron Sword.

evidence.quote:
show Biggoron your Claim Check.  He'll give you the Biggoron Sword for all your
trouble.

facts.subject: Biggoron Sword
facts.text: The Biggoron Sword deals twice the damage of the Master Sword, but prevents Link from using a shield while wielding it.

evidence.quote:
The Biggoron Sword deals twice the damage that the Master Sword does,
but is so large that you can't handle a Shield while using it.

facts.subject: Treasure Room
facts.text: The central Treasure Room of the Gerudo Training Ground contains the Ice Arrows.

evidence.quote:
The Gerudo Training Ground is a series of obstacle courses and timed
challenges, built in a rough square around a central "Treasure Room."  This
Treasure Room contains, among other useless trinkets, the Ice Arrows.

facts.subject: Ice Arrows
facts.text: Reaching the Ice Arrows requires a minimum of seven Small Keys.

evidence.quote:
You need a minimum of seven keys to reach the Ice Arrows, and once you have acquired this number of keys the
dungeon is essentially "finished" and you can go about your business elsewhere.

facts.subject: Gerudo Training Ground
facts.text: The Gerudo Training Ground cannot be fully completed without the Silver Gauntlets from the Spirit Temple.

evidence.quote:
The dungeon cannot be completed "fully" without the Silver Gauntlets from the
Young Link portion of the Spirit Temple.

facts.subject: Gerudo Training Ground Entrance
facts.text: The entrance to the Gerudo Training Ground is situated on the southeastern edge of Gerudo Fortress after Link rescues the Carpenters.

evidence.quote:
The Gerudo Training Ground is only available after Adult Link rescues the
captured Carpenters in Gerudo Fortress and becomes an honorary Gerudo Thief...The entrance to the Training Ground is on the
southeastern edge of the Gerudo Fortress.  Speak with the Gerudo Lieutenant
standing near the steel grating, pay the entrance fee, and she will let you in.

facts.subject: Entrance Room
facts.text: Shooting the golden eye switch above the entrance door spawns a chest containing arrows.

evidence.quote:
At the top of the
stairs, turn around and look up above the door frame to see a golden eye
switch.  Shoot the eye switch with an arrow, and a chest will appear in between
two of the pillars in the room.  Open it to get a bundle of arrows.

facts.subject: Entrance Room
facts.text: A chest between the opposite pillars in the entrance room contains a Blue Rupee.

evidence.quote:
Another
chest in between the pillars opposite contains a Blue Rupee.

facts.subject: Entrance Room
facts.text: The door directly opposite the entrance leads to the Treasure Chamber, while doors to the left and right lead into the Training Ground.

evidence.quote:
There are three doors in this room.  The one directly opposite the entrance
leads to the Treasure Chamber, which should be your last destination.  The
doors to the left and right of the Treasure Chamber go to the Gerudo Training
Ground.

facts.subject: Sand Stalfos Room
facts.text: Defeating the two Stalfos in the Sand Stalfos Room within one minute makes a chest containing a Small Key appear.

evidence.quote:
Run past the Blade Trap and
into the room, and a pair of Stalfos will appear.  Defeat them in the usual
fashion, and in under 1:00, and a chest containing this room's Small Key will
appear.

facts.subject: Silver Rupee/Rolling Boulder Room
facts.text: Collecting all the Silver Rupees in the Rolling Boulder Room within the 1:30 time limit unseals the exit door.

evidence.quote:
Time Limit: 1:30...This Silver Rupee will unseal the door at
the back of the room.

facts.subject: Large Block Room
facts.text: Defeating all four Wolfos in the Large Block Room spawns a chest containing arrows.

evidence.quote:
Once
all four Wolfos are dead, a chest will appear which contains a bundle of
arrows.

facts.subject: Like-Like Room
facts.text: Defeating the three Like-Likes behind the blue block reveals an invisible chest in a small pit containing a Small Key.

evidence.quote:
Enter this door to find a small room
which houses three Like-Likes.  Kill them all, and two chests will appear.  Use
the Lens of Truth and look in one of the small pits in the room to find an
invisible chest, which contains a Small Key.

facts.subject: Large Block Room
facts.text: Destroying the false door and looking above it with the Lens of Truth reveals an invisible passage with a target.

evidence.quote:
Destroy the False Door against the wall using Bombs or the Megaton Hammer, then
look on the wall above it with the Lens of Truth to see an invisible passage.  Pull yourself up to the Longshot Target with the Hookshot/Longshot.

facts.subject: Totem Room
facts.text: Entering the door on the high right ledge of the Totem Room leads to a chest containing a Small Key.

evidence.quote:
When you enter the room, you will be on a high ledge.  Run along the ledge to
the right, where there is a door.  Go through it and open the chest inside to
get a Small Key, then return to the Totem Room.

facts.subject: Totem Room
facts.text: Shooting all the statue's eyes with arrows in one pass from the rotating platform drops a chest with a Small Key and unlocks the lower door.

evidence.quote:
After all of the eyes are pierced with arrows, then a chest will fall down in
front of the statue, and the door on the lower level will unlock.  Pull
yourself over to the chest with the Longshot (just jump if you don't have the
Longshot), and then open the chest to get a Small Key.

facts.subject: Flaming Enemy Room
facts.text: Defeating all the Fire Slugs and Fire Keese spawns a chest containing arrows and unseals a door.

evidence.quote:
Run into the room and start massacring all of the numerous Fire Slugs and Fire
Keese who run around here.  Once all of them are dead, a door will unseal
itself and a chest will appear.  Open the chest to get another bundle of
arrows.

facts.subject: Flaming Enemy Room
facts.text: Smashing the statues with the Megaton Hammer reveals a switch that extinguishes the flame pillar guarding a Small Key chest.

evidence.quote:
Using the Megaton Hammer, smash all of the statues around the perimeter of the
room.  The two statues to the right of the chest of arrows hide a switch and a
golden eye...Step onto the switch, and the pillar of flames guarding the
chest in the center of the room will deactivate.  Open it to get a Small Key.

facts.subject: The Sea of Fire
facts.text: Falling into the lava in the Sea of Fire requires collecting all five Silver Rupees over again.

evidence.quote: If you fall in this room at any time, you will have to get all of the Silver Rupees over again.

facts.subject: Silver Rupee
facts.text: The first Silver Rupee in the Sea of Fire is reached by pulling Link to the Longshot target above the entrance doorway.

evidence.quote: Pull yourself up to the Longshot target here with the Hookshot/Longshot to get the first Silver Rupee.

facts.subject: Silver Rupee
facts.text: A second Silver Rupee is located on a platform to the left of the cliff edge in the Sea of Fire.

evidence.quote: Walk to the edge of the cliff, and on the left you will see a platform with another Silver Rupee on it.  Jump down to it.

facts.subject: Blocks of Time
facts.text: Playing the Song of Time where Navi flutters in the Sea of Fire causes two Blocks of Time to appear.

evidence.quote: Navi will flutter out into an empty space in the middle of the room; play the Song of Time here to make two Blocks of Time appear (if only one appears, you didn't get close enough - but one is enough).

facts.subject: Small Key
facts.text: A Small Key lies on the high ledge against the right wall, reached by jumping from the Blocks of Time.

evidence.quote: Climb up onto the Blocks of Time, and from there jump to the high ledge against the right wall.  Take the Small Key that lies up here.

facts.subject: Silver Rupee
facts.text: Jumping left from the lower Block of Time leads to a third Silver Rupee, and jumping from the block to another platform leads to a fourth.

evidence.quote: Jump back out to the lower Block of Time, and from there jump to the left to get another Silver Rupee.  Jump back to the Block of Time, and then jump out to the next platform with a Silver Rupee on it.

facts.subject: switch
facts.text: Hitting the switch on the platform to the right temporarily shuts off the pillar of flames on the other side of the room to allow access to the last Silver Rupee.

evidence.quote: Look to the right here to see another platform, which has a switch on it.  This switch deactivates the pillar of flames on the other side of the room, letting you get the last Silver Rupee.

facts.subject: door
facts.text: Gathering all five Silver Rupees in the Sea of Fire unseals the exit door on the left side of the room.

evidence.quote: Once you have all five Silver Rupees, the door on the left side of the room will unseal.

facts.subject: Blocks of Time
facts.text: Playing the Song of Time in the center of the Underwater Rupee Room makes the floor Blocks of Time vanish, revealing a pool of water.

evidence.quote: Run into the middle of the room, and play the Song of Time to make the Blocks of Time in the floor vanish.  Equip the Iron Boots and the Zora Tunic, and then sink into the pool of water beneath the Blocks of Time.

facts.subject: Shell Blade
facts.text: Shell Blades at the bottom of the pool in the Underwater Rupee Room can be defeated with the Hookshot.

evidence.quote: Defeat all of the Shell Blades at the bottom of the pool with the Hookshot, and watch out for the Blade Trap.

facts.subject: Small Key
facts.text: Collecting all five Silver Rupees in the Underwater Rupee Room spawns a chest above the pool containing a Small Key.

evidence.quote: Once you have all five Silver Rupees, a chest will appear back above the pool of water.  Climb out of the pool and open the chest to get a Small Key.

facts.subject: The Sea of Fire
facts.text: The door on the left side of the Sea of Fire leads into the Dinolfos Room.

evidence.quote: From the door to the Underwater Rupee Room, head to the left side of the Sea of Fire and go through the door there.

facts.subject: Dinolfos Room
facts.text: The Dinolfos Room requires defeating all enemies within a 1:30 time limit.

evidence.quote:
Hint: Defeat all the enemies in a LIMITED TIME!
Time Limit: 1:30

facts.subject: Beamos
facts.text: The Beamos in the Dinolfos Room can be blown up using a Bomb or Bombchus.

evidence.quote: Blow up the Beamos statue with a Bomb or Bombchus, and then kill the Dinofols in the room.

facts.subject: Small Key
facts.text: Defeating both Dinolfos and the Beamos in the Dinolfos Room spawns a chest containing a Small Key.

evidence.quote: Once both of the Dinolfos and the Beamos are dead, then a chest containing a Small Key will appear.  Take the Small Key, and then go through the door to the left of the Dinolfos Room to return to the entrance.

facts.subject: Treasure Room
facts.text: The Treasure Room is entered through the door across from the dungeon entrance.

evidence.quote: Go through the door across from the entrance and into the Treasure Room.

facts.subject: Treasure Room
facts.text: The Treasure Room has nine locked doors, with the final key hidden inside the room itself.

evidence.quote: This room contains nine locked doors - which might seem problematic, since you only have eight keys (seven if you tried this dungeon before you got the Silver Gauntlets).  Luckily, the ninth key is hidden in the room itself.

facts.subject: Small Key
facts.text: Climbing the wire wall through the ceiling passage revealed by the Lens of Truth in the first room on the left leads to a chest with a Small Key.

evidence.quote: In the first room on the left, use the Lens of Truth and look on the ceiling above to find a hidden passage.  Use the wire wall to the left of the door to climb up into it...At the top, you'll find a chest which contains Key #8/#9.

facts.subject: Treasure Room
facts.text: Chests on the right side of the Treasure Room contain Bombchus and a Bundle of Arrows.

evidence.quote:
Right from the entrance -
Bombchus, Bundle of Arrows

facts.subject: Treasure Room
facts.text: Chests on the left side of the Treasure Room contain a Purple Rupee, a Red Rupee, a Bundle of Arrows, and the Ice Arrows.

evidence.quote:
Left from the entrance -
Purple Rupee, Red Rupee, Bundle of Arrows, Ice Arrows

facts.subject: Treasure Room
facts.text: Warp songs cannot be played inside the Gerudo Training Ground, requiring Link to walk out.

evidence.quote: Once you have the Ice Arrows, then you can just leave (you'll have to walk out - warp songs don't work in here).

facts.subject: Big Poe Hunting Sidequest
facts.text: Big Poes can only be captured as Adult Link while riding Epona and using the Fairy Bow.

evidence.quote: Big Poes can only be obtained with Epona and the Bow and Arrows, as Adult Link.  If you don't have either Epona or the Bow and Arrows, then you can't capture them.

facts.subject: Big Poe
facts.text: Shooting a Big Poe with two arrows turns it into a Wisp that can be captured in an Empty Bottle.

evidence.quote: After killing a Big Poe with two arrows, then it will become a Wisp which can be captured like a normal Poe in an Empty Bottle.

facts.subject: Bottle
facts.text: Delivering all ten captured Big Poes to the Poe Shop in Hyrule Castle rewards the final Bottle.

evidence.quote: Deliver captured Big Poes to the Poe Shop in Hyrule Castle (the building on the left as you first enter Hyrule Castle).  Once you capture all ten and take them to the Poe Man, he'll give you the game's final bottle.

facts.subject: Big Poe
facts.text: Regular Poes appear while on foot, whereas Big Poes only appear while riding horseback on Epona.

evidence.quote: Regular Poes appear in the same places that Big Poes do while on foot.  These can be killed while on foot, but don't be fooled; they don't count as Big Poes.  Big Poes only appear while on horseback

facts.subject: Big Poe #01
facts.text: Big Poe #01 appears by the signpost immediately south of Hyrule Castle when riding west from the stone bridge near Kakariko Village.

evidence.quote:
Big Poe #01
Location: The signpost immediately south of Hyrule Castle.

The best way to get this Poe is to ride west from the stone bridge near Kakariko Village straight at the signpost south of Hyrule Castle.

facts.subject: Big Poe #02
facts.text: Big Poe #02 appears on the cliff overlooking the entrance to Kakariko Village when Link rides right up to the cliff's edge.

evidence.quote:
Big Poe #02
Location:  The cliff overlooking the entrance to Kakariko Village.

This is hands-down the hardest Big Poe in the game to kill.  Pretty much the only way to make it appear is to ride right up to the edge of the cliff, at which point the Poe will appear and begin to fly away.

facts.subject: Big Poe #03
facts.text: Big Poe #03 appears at the point where the stone wall east of Lon Lon Ranch breaks to the left when riding south along its eastern edge.

evidence.quote:
Big Poe #03
Location:  The stone wall east of Lon Lon Ranch.

This one is much easier then Big Poe #02.  Simply ride south along the wall's eastern edge, and the Big Poe will appear at the point where the wall breaks to the left.

facts.subject: Big Poe #04
facts.text: Big Poe #04 appears at the intersection of the Y-Shaped Road southeast of Lon Lon Ranch when riding west past the gray stone toward the fence gap.

evidence.quote:
Big Poe #04
Location:  The intersection of the Y-Shaped Road southeast of Lon Lon Ranch.

This Big Poe is quite easy.  The best way to get it is to ride west from the entrance to Kokiri Forest, straight for the gray stone near the crossroads of the Y-Shaped road...Keep heading west past the stone, and the Big Poe will appear.

facts.subject: Big Poe #06
facts.text: Big Poe #06 appears south of the tall tree at the bottom tip of the Y-Shaped Road when riding from east to west.

evidence.quote:
Big Poe #06
Location:  South of the tree at the bottom tip of the Y-Shaped Road.

Head for the bottom tip of the Y-Shaped Road, and you will find a tall tree standing by itself.  Riding from the east to the west, pass by the south side of this tree to make the Big Poe appear.

facts.subject: Big Poe #05
facts.text: Big Poe #05 appears in the center of the grove of golden-leafed trees in southeast Hyrule Field when riding at the gap to the right of the tan stone.

evidence.quote:
Big Poe #05
Location:  The center of the grove of golden-leafed trees in Southeast Hyrule
Field....Look for the tan-
colored stone in the middle of the grove of trees, and start riding at the gap
to the right of the stone.  The Poe will appear in this gap

facts.subject: Big Poe #07
facts.text: Big Poe #07 appears at the intersection of the three-way road near Gerudo Valley when approached from the south while facing towards the gap.

evidence.quote: ------------ Big Poe #07 Location: The intersection of the three-way road near Gerudo Valley.

facts.subject: Big Poe #08
facts.text: Big Poe #08 appears when riding north from the road near Gerudo Valley and passing by the west side of the lone tree west of Lon Lon Ranch.

evidence.quote: ------------ Big Poe #08 Location: The lone tree west of Lon Lon Ranch.

facts.subject: Big Poe #08
facts.text: Follow Big Poe #08 to the top of the hill and shoot it when the hill levels out rather than trying to shoot it uphill.

evidence.quote: Big Poe #08 ... The only disadvantage to this one is the Poe will be going uphill, making this an extremely difficult shot.  Your best bet is to not even try to shoot it when it first appears, but just follow it to the top of the hill, and then shoot it when the hill levels out further up.

facts.subject: Big Poe #09
facts.text: Big Poe #09 appears near bushes south of the river in northwest Hyrule Field when riding southeast from the corner where the wall and river meet towards the Lon Lon Ranch tree.

evidence.quote: ------------ Big Poe #09 Location: South of the river in northwest Hyrule Field.

facts.subject: Big Poe #10
facts.text: Big Poe #10 appears near the lone tree outside Lon Lon Ranch when brushing along the southern edge of the tree while riding west.

evidence.quote: ------------ Big Poe #10 Location: The lone tree near the entrance to Lon Lon Ranch.

facts.subject: Empty Bottle
facts.text: Killing Big Poe #10 and returning all ten Big Poes to the Poe Shop earns an Empty Bottle.

evidence.quote: Big Poe #10 ... Kill it and take it back to the Poe Shop, and you'll have earned your Bottle.

facts.subject: Deku Stick
facts.text: Young Link can use Deku Sticks to transfer fire from a lit torch to adjacent unlit torches around a room, though the stick expires if lit for too long.

evidence.quote: Deku Sticks are tools commonly used by Young Link.  With them, Young Link can light the Sticks on a lit torch, and transfer that flame to adjacent torches around the room.  The Stick expires if lit for too long.

facts.subject: Deku Baba
facts.text: Deku Babas drop Deku Sticks if Link stuns them and kills them while their stem extends straight into the air.

evidence.quote: Deku Sticks are commonly found on Deku Babas; to obtain them from the enemies, stun them and then kill them while their stem extends straight in the air.

facts.subject: Deku Nut
facts.text: Deku Nuts explode in a bright flash upon striking the ground to stun vulnerable enemies and destroy Shabom bubbles in Jabu-Jabu's Belly, but have no effect on minibosses and bosses.

evidence.quote: An item used exclusively in combat, Deku Nuts explode in a bright flash when they strike the ground.  The flash temporarily stuns all enemies in the area who are vulnerable to the stun.  Deku Nuts are particularly effective against the bubble-like Shabom enemies in Jabu-Jabu's Belly, as the bubbles are destroyed by the Nut's flash.  Deku Nuts have absolutely no effect on more powerful enemies, i.e. Minibosses and Bosses.

facts.subject: Fairy Slingshot
facts.text: The Fairy Slingshot is the first ranged weapon found in Inside the Deku Tree for Young Link and is effectively replaced by the Boomerang.

evidence.quote: First Found: Inside the Deku Tree...The first ranged weapon in the game, the Fairy Slingshot is also the weakest ranged weapon in the game.  It is one of the items used most regularly by Young Link, but it is effectively replaced by the more powerful Boomerang, which also has the bonus of having infinite ammo.

facts.subject: Fairy Ocarina
facts.text: Saria gives Young Link the Fairy Ocarina in Kokiri Forest, which is used most frequently to open doorways with Zelda's Lullaby until obtaining the Ocarina of Time.

evidence.quote: First Found: Kokiri Forest...A gift from Link's Kokiri friend, Saria, the Fairy Ocarina is essentially a placeholder for Young Link until he obtains the Ocarina of Time after the third dungeon.  The Fairy Ocarina is used most frequently to open doorways using Zelda's Lullaby, but can be used to play other songs.

facts.subject: Bottles
facts.text: Bottles can store restorative items like Fairies and Lon Lon Milk, as well as capture Bugs and Blue Fire.

evidence.quote: Bottles, long a staple of the Zelda series, are used to store helpful restorative items like Fairies and Lon Lon Milk.  Bottles can also be used to capture Bugs and Blue Fire, which have their own uses in the game.

facts.subject: Empty Bottle
facts.text: Young Link obtains the first of four Empty Bottles from Talon at Lon Lon Ranch after finding all three Special Cuccos among the flock of Normal Cuccos.

evidence.quote: The first bottle in the game is obtained with Young Link, and is won from Talon in Lon Lon Ranch after you have awoken him in the Hyrule Castle Garden.  Find all three of his "Special Cuccos" in the flock of Normal Cuccos, and he'll award you with an Empty Bottle, the first of four.

facts.subject: Empty Bottle
facts.text: Young Link obtains the second bottle in Kakariko Village by gathering all the Cuccos in town and returning them to the Cucco Pasture near the graveyard entrance.

evidence.quote: The second bottle in the game is also obtained by Young Link.  In Kakariko Village, gather all of the Cuccos in town and return them to the Cucco Pasture near the entrance to Kakariko Graveyard.  Three of the Cuccos can only be reached by gliding off of cliffs and over fences using other Cuccos.

facts.subject: Empty Bottle
facts.text: Young Link retrieves the third bottle from the bottom of Lake Hylia by diving down after obtaining the Silver Scale.

evidence.quote: The third bottle in the game is, again, obtained by Young Link, and is also the only Bottle that you HAVE to get.  Once you have earned the Silver Scale, head for Lake Hylia and dive down to retrieve the Bottle from the Lake's bottom.

facts.subject: Empty Bottle
facts.text: Adult Link receives the fourth bottle from the Poe Man in Hyrule Castle after capturing all ten Big Poes in Hyrule Field using Epona and the Fairy Bow.

evidence.quote: The last bottle in the game is the only one found by Adult Link.  Once you have Epona and the Fairy Bow, hunt down and capture all ten of the Big Poes in Hyrule Field and deliver them to the Poe Shop in Hyrule Castle.  The Poe Man will give you the fourth bottle when you do.

facts.subject: Bombs
facts.text: Bombs are stored in a pouch made from a Dodongo's Stomach, are first found as the dungeon item in Dodongo's Cavern, and are used to blow open weakened walls and defeat King Dodongo.

evidence.quote: First Found: Dodongo's Cavern...The "Goron's Special Crop" is stored in a special pouch made from a Dodongo's Stomach.  Bombs can be used to blow open weakened walls, and are required to defeat certain armored enemies and solve a number of other minor puzzles.  They are also instrumental in defeating the King Dodongo.  The Bombs are first found as the dungeon item in Dodongo's Cavern.

facts.subject: Bombchus
facts.text: Bombchus are mobile bombs that climb walls and explode on contact, and they can be bought from the shop in the Back Alley or won from the Bombchu Bowling Alley after Dodongo's Cavern.

evidence.quote: Bombchus are mobile bombs which follow a straight line and then explode when they contact something.  They have the ability to climb along walls, and to a lesser extent ceilings.  The earliest time that you can obtain them is in the Hyrule Castle Market, immediately after finishing Dodongo's Cavern.  You can either buy them from the shop in the Back Alley, or win them from the Bombchu Bowling Alley.

facts.subject: Din's Fire
facts.text: Din's Fire creates an expanding ring of fire that burns enemies and lights torches, and it is obtained at the dead end in Hyrule Castle Garden immediately after getting Bombs from Dodongo's Cavern.

evidence.quote: First Found: Hyrule Castle Garden...When used, this spell creates a ring of fire that expands out and encompasses everything in the room.  It will burn any enemies it makes contact with, and also lights any unlit torches it makes contact with.  Din's Fire is used primarily to solve several torch-lighting puzzles throughout the game, but is also useful against several smaller, weakened enemies, such as the Mini-Floor Masters.  Din's Fire can be obtained from the dead end in Hyrule Castle Garden immediately after obtaining the Bombs from Dodongo's Cavern.

facts.subject: Magic Beans
facts.text: Magic Beans planted in soft earth as Young Link grow into flying Magic Leaves that Adult Link can ride to reach out-of-reach areas.

evidence.quote: The Magic Beans can be planted in the plots of soft earth that dot the Hyrule countryside as Young Link.  Once planted, these beans begin to grow, and when you return to these areas with Adult Link, you will find a flying Magic Leaf that can be used to access out-of-reach areas.

facts.subject: Magic Beans
facts.text: The Bean Man upstream in Zora's River sells 10 Magic Beans starting at 10 Rupees, with each successive bean increasing by 10 Rupees up to 100 Rupees, for a grand total of 550 Rupees.

evidence.quote: The Magic Beans are purchased from the Bean Man upstream from the entrance to Zora's River.  He has ten total to sell.  The Magic Beans cost 10 Rupees initially, but raise in price by 10 rupees for each successive purchased Bean, until the final Bean reaches 100 rupees.  All 10 Beans cost a grand total of 550 rupees.

facts.subject: Farore's Wind
facts.text: Farore's Wind is obtained from a Great Fairy in Zora's Fountain by bombing the wall in the southeast area.

evidence.quote: Farore's Wind is obtained from a Great Fairy in Zora's Fountain.  Use a bomb to open the wall in the southeast area of the fountain, which leads to the Fountain.

facts.subject: Farore's Wind
facts.text: Farore's Wind allows the player to set a waypoint in a dungeon and return to it when casting the spell again elsewhere in the dungeon.

evidence.quote: With it, you can set a Waypoint somewhere in a Dungeon, and using the spell again elsewhere in the dungeon will let you return to the original waypoint.

facts.subject: Boomerang
facts.text: The Boomerang is the dungeon item found in Jabu-Jabu's Belly.

evidence.quote: The Boomerang is the dungeon item in Jabu-Jabu's Belly.

facts.subject: Boomerang
facts.text: The Boomerang can retrieve distant items such as Gold Skulltulas, defeat certain enemies, and stun others.

evidence.quote: An important item for Young Link, as it is the first item in the game which has the ability to grab items and return them to you from a distance.  Namely, Gold Skulltulas.  The Boomerang also has the ability to defeat certain enemies, and stun others.

facts.subject: Boomerang
facts.text: When aiming the Boomerang, lining up the target with the back of Link's head acts as a targeting reticule.

evidence.quote: When aiming the Boomerang, you can use Link's head as a targeting reticule.  Just line up your target with the back of Link's head, and let go.

facts.subject: Ocarina of Time
facts.text: The Ocarina of Time is obtained from the moat outside Hyrule Castle after obtaining all three Spiritual Stones.

evidence.quote: The Ocarina of Time is obtained from the moat outside Hyrule Castle, but only appears there once you have obtained all three of the Spiritual Stones.

facts.subject: Ocarina of Time
facts.text: The Ocarina of Time replaces the Fairy Ocarina and possesses magical qualities that allow the player to open the Door of Time and access the Sacred Realm.

evidence.quote: The Ocarina of Time replaces the Fairy Ocarina that Young Link gets from Saria, and it's magical qualities allows you to open the Door of Time and access the Sacred Realm.

facts.subject: Hookshot
facts.text: The Hookshot is won from Dampe's Ghost underneath his gravestone in Kakariko Graveyard shortly after Link becomes an adult.

evidence.quote: The Hookshot is found almost immediately after Link enters adulthood, and is won from Dampe's Ghost underneath his gravestone in Kakariko Graveyard.

facts.subject: Hookshot
facts.text: The Hookshot allows Adult Link to latch onto wooden objects or special targets, pierce hard armor like that of Big Skulltulas, and retrieve distant Skulltula tokens.

evidence.quote: With it, you can latch onto certain objects in the environment (mostly things made of wood, but also special targets) and pull yourself up to it.  The Hookshot is also a powerful ranged tool, and is able to penetrate certain hard armors (such as the armor of the Big Skulltula).  It can also retrieve distant Skulltula Tokens in the same fashion as the Boomerang.

facts.subject: Fairy Bow
facts.text: The Fairy Bow is the dungeon item obtained from the Forest Temple.

evidence.quote: The Fairy Bow is the dungeon item from The Forest Temple.

facts.subject: Fairy Bow
facts.text: Fairy Bow arrows can be infused with Fire, Ice, and Light powers to deal extra damage to enemies and solve puzzles.

evidence.quote: The arrows that the Fairy Bow fires can be enhanced with the powers of Fire, Ice and Light, to deal additional damage to enemies or solve other puzzles.

facts.subject: Megaton Hammer
facts.text: The Megaton Hammer is the dungeon item found in the Fire Temple.

evidence.quote: The Megaton Hammer is the dungeon item from the Fire Temple.

facts.subject: Volvagia
facts.text: The Megaton Hammer is used to solve puzzles and defeat Volvagia, the boss of the Fire Temple.

evidence.quote: The Megaton Hammer is used to solve numerous puzzles and defeat the Fire Temple's boss, Volvagia, but otherwise it's existence is easily forgotten.

facts.subject: Longshot
facts.text: The Longshot is an upgraded Hookshot with double the range and serves as the dungeon item from the Water Temple.

evidence.quote: An upgraded version of the Hookshot, the Longshot is functionally the same but has double the range.  The Longshot is the dungeon item from the Water Temple.

facts.subject: Fire Arrow
facts.text: After completing the Water Temple, shooting an arrow into the morning sun from the south island in Lake Hylia spawns the Fire Arrows on the smaller island.

evidence.quote: To obtain them, complete the Water Temple, then stand on the large island in south of Lake Hylia.  Wait for the sun to rise (the Sun's Song won't work, you'll just have to wait for time to pass normally), then fire an arrow into the sun.  The Fire Arrows will appear on the smaller island.

facts.subject: Fire Arrow
facts.text: Fire Arrows can light distant torches, burn objects such as spider webs, and defeat certain enemies.

evidence.quote: The Fire Arrow can be used to light far off torches, or to burn certain other objects (such as spider webs).  The Fire Arrow is also required to defeat certain enemies.

facts.subject: Lens of Truth
facts.text: The Lens of Truth is found by Young Link inside the Bottom of the Well.

evidence.quote: The Lens of Truth is found by Young Link in the Bottom of the Well, and though he has access to it, there is rarely cause for Young Link to use it.

facts.subject: Lens of Truth
facts.text: The Lens of Truth is required to access the Spirit Temple entrance and defeat the boss of the Shadow Temple.

evidence.quote: It is required to defeat the Shadow Temple's boss, as well as to access the entrance to the Spirit Temple.

facts.subject: Lens of Truth
facts.text: Rapidly toggling the Lens of Truth on and off prevents the magic meter from draining.

evidence.quote: The Lens constantly drains a small amount of your magic meter while using it, however rapidly turning the Lens on and off prevents the magic meter from being drained.

facts.subject: Ice Arrow
facts.text: The Ice Arrows are acquired in the Gerudo Training Ground by choosing the left door inside the Treasure Room.

evidence.quote: The Ice Arrows are obtained from the Gerudo Training Ground by taking the left door in the Treasure Room.

facts.subject: Nayru's Love
facts.text: Nayru's Love is found inside a cave at the Desert Colossus just before entering the Spirit Temple.

evidence.quote: You can get it from a cave in the Desert Colossus just before entering the Spirit Temple, which is good timing since the Iron Knuckles inside the Spirit Temple are vicious competitors.

facts.subject: Nayru's Love
facts.text: Nayru's Love grants invulnerability for a limited period of time.

evidence.quote: Nayru's Love makes you invulnerable for a period of time (around a minute, I believe, but I haven't timed it).

facts.subject: Light Arrow
facts.text: Princess Zelda bestows the Light Arrows upon Link in the Temple of Time after all six Medallions have been acquired.

evidence.quote: The Light Arrows are given to Link in the Temple of Time after he has obtained all six Medallions from the Spiritual Sages.

facts.subject: Ganondorf
facts.text: Light Arrows are the only weapons capable of making Ganondorf vulnerable to the Master Sword, and they are required to break the seals in Ganondorf's Keep.

evidence.quote: A gift from Princess Zelda when you finally find her near the end of the game, the Light Arrows are the only weapons in all of Hyrule that can make Ganondorf vulnerable to the power of the Master Sword.  The Light Arrows are also required to destroy the Seals in Ganondorf's Keep.

facts.subject: Zelda's Lullaby
facts.text: Zelda's Lullaby is taught to Link by Impa in Hyrule Castle Garden using the sequence C-Left, C-Up, C-Right, C-Left, C-Up, C-Right.

evidence.quote:
First Found: Hyrule Castle Garden
Sequence: C-Left, C-Up, C-Right, C-Left, C-Up, C-Right

Taught to you by Impa after you first meet Princess Zelda, Zelda's Lullaby is easily the song you will play most throughout the game.

facts.subject: Zelda's Lullaby
facts.text: Zelda's Lullaby is used to open Great Fairy Fountains, enter Darunia's Chamber, access Zora's Domain, and manipulate water levels inside the Water Temple.

evidence.quote: You need to use it to access the Great Fairy Fountains, you must use it to open the door to Darunia's Chamber, you must use it to enter Zora's Domain, you must use it to raise and lower the water levels in the Water Temple... the list goes on.

facts.subject: Epona's Song
facts.text: Epona's Song is taught by Malon at Lon Lon Ranch with the sequence C-Up, C-Left, C-Right, C-Up, C-Left, C-Right.

evidence.quote:
First Found: Lon Lon Ranch
Sequence: C-Up, C-Left, C-Right, C-Up, C-Left, C-Right

Taught to you by Malon in Lon Lon Ranch, Epona's Song has two primary functions: one, it lets you ride Epona as Adult Link, and two, gets you free milk from any cow in the game.

facts.subject: Saria's Song
facts.text: Saria's Song is learned from Saria in the Sacred Forest Meadow with the sequence C-Down, C-Right, C-Left, C-Down, C-Right, C-Left.

evidence.quote:
First Found: Sacred Forest Meadow
Sequence: C-Down, C-Right, C-Left, C-Down, C-Right, C-Left

Taught to you by Saria when you visit her in the Sacred Forest Meadow, Saria's Song is required to get Darunia to trust you, and is later needed to get past Mido in the Lost Woods as Adult Link.

facts.subject: Saria's Song
facts.text: Playing Saria's Song allows Link to communicate telepathically with Saria to receive hints about where to go next.

evidence.quote: It also lets you telepathically communicate with Saria at any time, who will generally give you vague hints about where you should go next.

facts.subject: Sun's Song
facts.text: The Sun's Song is learned in the Royal Family's Tomb in Kakariko Graveyard with the sequence C-Right, C-Down, C-Up, C-Right, C-Down, C-Up, alternating time between 12:00 and 0:00.

evidence.quote: Learned in the Royal Family's Tomb in Kakariko Graveyard, the Sun's Song alternates the time of day between 12:00 (noon) and 0:00 (midnight).

facts.subject: Sun's Song
facts.text: When playing the Sun's Song in a zone where the passage of time is fixed, Link is warped back to the zone entrance upon the time change.

evidence.quote: In a zone where the passage of time is normal, then it will work normally.  In a zone where the passage of time is fixed, then you will be warped back to where you first entered the zone when time changes.

facts.subject: Courtyard Guard
facts.text: Shooting the window on the left side of the courtyard with the Slingshot causes a guard to throw a bomb back at Link.

evidence.quote: Shoot the window on the left side of the courtyard with your Slingshot, and a guard will throw a bomb at you.

facts.subject: Courtyard Window
facts.text: Shooting the right courtyard window depicting Mario characters rewards a red rupee.

evidence.quote: Look at the window on the right, and you'll see images of Mario, Peach, Bowser and Yoshi.  Shoot this window for a red rupee.

facts.subject: Princess Zelda
facts.text: Speaking with Princess Zelda in the courtyard leads to Link meeting her.

evidence.quote: Once you reach the northern edge of the topiary, run through the arch to reach the center of the Courtyard, and the Princess of Destiny: Zelda...After you've done this, speak with Zelda.

facts.subject: Princess Zelda
facts.text: Agreeing to help Princess Zelda rewards Link with Zelda's Letter, which opens the gate to Death Mountain in Kakariko Village.

evidence.quote: Agree to help her, and she will give you Zelda's Letter.  This will let you pass through the gate in Kakariko Village to Death Mountain.

facts.subject: Impa
facts.text: Impa blocks the exit from the courtyard and teaches Link Zelda's Lullaby before guiding him out to Hyrule Field.

evidence.quote: Run towards the entrance to the courtyard, and you will find the way blocked by Impa, Zelda's attendant (basically, nurse/bodyguard).  Impa will teach you Zelda's Lullaby, easily the most important and overused song in the game.  Impa will then show you back outside to Hyrule Field, and point you in the direction of Kakariko Village.

facts.subject: Hyrule Field
facts.text: Heading south across Hyrule Field leads into the opening of Lon Lon Ranch during the daytime.

evidence.quote: Point yourself south, and head for the large structure whose opening is just visible.  Run straight through to the opening to enter Lon Lon Ranch.  Make sure it is daytime before you enter.

facts.subject: Talon's Cucco Minigame
facts.text: Finding all three special cuccos in Talon's minigame before time runs out rewards Link with a Bottle filled with Lon Lon Milk.
