evidence.quote: He will throw three "special" cuccos into the pack of regular cuccos, and if you can find all three of the special cuccos before the time runs out, then he'll reward you with a Bottle, filled with Lon Lon Milk.

facts.subject: Talon's Cucco Minigame
facts.text: Talon's minigame can be simplified by throwing all the cuccos behind the counter where Talon sits before selecting the special ones.

evidence.quote: Or you can cheat by throwing all of the cuccos into the corner, behind the long counter that Talon sits on.  "Select" the Cuccos by picking them up.

facts.subject: Malon
facts.text: Speaking to Malon in the pasture until she mentions her mother and presenting the Ocarina prompts her to teach Epona's Song.

evidence.quote: Speak with Malon again until she mentions her mother, then whip out your Ocarina.  Malon will then teach you Epona's Song.

facts.subject: Epona's Song
facts.text: Playing Epona's Song for any cow in the game yields free Lon Lon Milk.

evidence.quote: In addition to eventually letting you ride Epona later in the game, Epona's Song will also get you free Lon Lon Milk from ANY cow in the game.

facts.subject: Mill Crate Tunnel
facts.text: Pushing the milk crates in the corner of the Mill reveals a crawl tunnel leading to an empty nest containing a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: In the corner of the room, there are a large number of milk crates...The X marks where a new tunnel will have appeared.  Crawl through the tunnel to find an empty nest, which houses a Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Pasture Tree Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Rolling at night into the tree to the left of the pasture arch drops a Gold Skulltula holding a token.

evidence.quote: Run through the arch that leads to the pasture, and roll into the tree just to the left of the arch.  Kill the Gold Skulltula that falls down, and take it's token.

facts.subject: Pasture Awning Gold Skulltula
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is found at night on the outer wall of the small awning behind the pasture.

evidence.quote: Now, circle around to the back of the pasture, so that you are on the outer wall of the small awning.  Kill the Gold Skulltula and take it's token, but watch out for the Guay bird enemies.

facts.subject: Hyrule Field
facts.text: Traveling due east of Lon Lon Ranch across Hyrule Field leads to the Lost Woods Bridge entrance into Kokiri Forest.

evidence.quote: Head back to Kokiri Forest now, which is at the three o'clock position on your map.  It's pretty much due east of Lon Lon Ranch.  Make sure it's nighttime, then enter the hollowed out log, run across the Lost Woods Bridge and enter Kokiri Forest.

facts.subject: Know-It-All Brothers' House Gold Skulltula
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is found at night behind the Know-It-All Brother's House in Kokiri Forest, reachable by backflipping into its token.

evidence.quote: Climb the hill to your right as you enter, and go around to the rear of the Know-It-All Brother's House (the large, squat tree house with the giant leaf coming out of it's top).  Kill the Gold Skulltula back here, and grab the token by facing away from the token, holding down Z, and holding back and A to backflip into the token.

facts.subject: Kokiri Forest Cliff
facts.text: Climbing the ivy wall behind Mido's House leads to a hollowed log tunnel into the Lost Woods.

evidence.quote: Climb down to Mido's House, and climb up to the cliff behind his house.  Climb up the Ivy Wall, go around the corner of the cliff, and through the hollowed log to the Lost Woods.

facts.subject: Target Tree Drum
facts.text: Hitting the center of the hanging drum three consecutive times for 100 points with the Slingshot makes a Deku Scrub appear with the Bullet Bag x50.

evidence.quote: Shoot the drum hanging from the tree limb, and try to adjust your aim so that you hit the exact middle.  You'll know you've done it right, as it will give you 100 points...Three successive shots to the exact center of the drum will cause a Deku Scrub to appear, who will reward you with the Bullet Bag x50, the largest Slingshot ammunition bag in the game.

Shoot thee perfect bull's-eyes (score 100 points three  
times in a row) and collect the biggest seed bag.

facts.subject: Skull Kid Ocarina Minigame
facts.text: Completing three rounds of the Ocarina memory game with the two Skullkids on the low tree trunk earns a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: Stand on the low trunk, and two Skullkids will appear.  Take out your Ocarina, and play a lengthy memory game with them.  Complete the entire game (three rounds, each becoming increasingly longer and harder) to earn another Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Lost Woods
facts.text: The stone arch near Kaepora Gaebora in the Lost Woods connects to Goron City, but requires proper equipment to use.

evidence.quote: If you're wondering, the stone arch here goes to Goron City, one of our next destinations.  Unfortunately, as of yet, we can't use this shortcut as we aren't properly equipped.

facts.subject: Lost Woods Pool
facts.text: The underwater pool in the Lost Woods leads to Zora's Domain.

evidence.quote: On the other side, there is a pool.  This pool leads to Zora's Domain, but as with the Goron City shortcut we're not properly equipped to use it yet.

facts.subject: Lost Woods Path
facts.text: From the pool room in the Lost Woods, taking the left tunnel, then straight, then left, and right at the crossroads enters the Sacred Forest Meadow.

evidence.quote: Go left through another tunnel.  Go straight from here through another tunnel, then hang a left through another tunnel, then go right at the next crossroads to enter the Sacred Forest Meadow.

facts.subject: Song of Time
facts.text: The Song of Time is first taught by Zelda when Link obtains the Ocarina of Time, using the sequence C-Right, A Button, C-Down, C-Right, A Button, C-Down.

evidence.quote:
Song of Time
First Found: Hyrule Field
Sequence: C-Right, A Button, C-Down, C-Right, A Button, C-Down

First taught to you by Zelda when you first obtain the Ocarina of Time

facts.subject: Song of Time
facts.text: The Song of Time is used initially to open the Door of Time in the Temple of Time, and later as Adult Link to interact with Blocks of Time.

evidence.quote: the Song of Time is initially used to open the Door of Time in the Temple of Time. Later on, as Adult Link, the Song of Time is used to interact with Blocks of Time.

facts.subject: Song of Storms
facts.text: The Song of Storms is taught to Adult Link in the Windmill by the Organ Grinder with the sequence A Button, C-Down, C-Up, A Button, C-Down, C-Up.

evidence.quote:
Song of Storms
First Found: Kakariko Village - Windmill (Adult Link)
Sequence: A Button, C-Down, C-Up, A Button, C-Down, C-Up

Taught to Adult Link in the Windmill by the Organ Grinder

facts.subject: Song of Storms
facts.text: The Song of Storms is required to gain access to the Bottom of the Well dungeon as Young Link.

evidence.quote: The Song of Storms is required to gain access to the Bottom of the Well dungeon as Young Link, but this is it's only required used.

facts.subject: Song of Storms
facts.text: The Song of Storms can optionally fill the dried up oasis in Desert Colossus, and its storm eases crossing the Haunted Wasteland.

evidence.quote: It can optionally be used to fill the dried up oasis in Desert Colossus, and the storm it creates makes crossing the Haunted Wasteland easier.

facts.subject: Minuet of Forest
facts.text: The Minuet of Forest is taught to Link by Sheik at the back of the Sacred Forest Meadow using the sequence A Button, C-Up, C-Left, C-Right, C-Left, C-Right.

evidence.quote:
Minuet of Forest
First Found: Sacred Forest Meadow
Sequence: A Button, C-Up, C-Left, C-Right, C-Left, C-Right

The first of the magical transportation songs that Adult Link learns, the Minuet of Forest is taught to Link by Sheik when he reaches the back of the Sacred Forest Meadow.

facts.subject: Minuet of Forest
facts.text: The Minuet of Forest transports Link to the Sacred Forest Meadow at any time, providing access to the Forest Temple and a nearby Fairy Fountain.

evidence.quote: The Minuet transports Link (Young or Adult) to the Sacred Forest Meadow at any time, giving easy access to the Forest Temple and a nearby Fairy Fountain.

facts.subject: Bolero of Fire
facts.text: The Bolero of Fire is taught to Link by Sheik at the bottom level of Death Mountain Crater via the door in Darunia's Chamber, using the sequence C-Down, A Button, C-Down, A Button, C-Right, C-Down, C-Right, C-Down.

evidence.quote:
Bolero of Fire
First Found: Death Mountain Crater
Sequence: C-Down, A Button, C-Down, A Button, C-Right, C-Down, C-Right, C-Down

The third of the magical transportation songs that Adult Link can learn, the Bolero of Fire is taught to Link by Sheik when he reaches the bottom level of the Death Mountain Crater (use the door in Darunia's Chamber).

facts.subject: Bolero of Fire
facts.text: The Bolero of Fire transports Link to Death Mountain Crater, granting access to the Fire Temple and allowing Young Link to reach a hidden soft soil earth patch.

evidence.quote: The Bolero transports Link (Young or Adult) to Death Mountain Crater, giving easy access to the Fire Temple.  Young Link must use the transportation song to reach one of the most cunningly hidden earth patches in the game.

facts.subject: Serenade of Water
facts.text: The Serenade of Water is taught to Link by Sheik after obtaining the Iron Boots in the Ice Cavern, using the sequence A Button, C-Down, C-Right, C-Right, C-Left.

evidence.quote:
Serenade of Water
First Found: Ice Cavern
Sequence: A Button, C-Down, C-Right, C-Right, C-Left

The fourth of the magical transportation songs that Adult Link can learn, the Serenade of Fire is taught to Link by Sheik after he obtains the Iron Boots from the Ice Cavern.

facts.subject: Serenade of Water
facts.text: The Serenade of Water transports Link to Lake Hylia, providing easy access to the Water Temple.

evidence.quote: The Serenade transports Link (Young or Adult) to Lake Hylia, giving easy access to the Water Temple.

facts.subject: Requiem of Spirit
facts.text: The Requiem of Spirit is taught by Sheik after Link enters, leaves the Spirit Temple, and returns to the Desert Colossus, using the sequence A Button, C-Down, A Button, C-Right, C-Down, A Button.

evidence.quote:
Requiem of Spirit
First Found: Desert Colossus
Sequence: A Button, C-Down, A Button, C-Right, C-Down, A Button

The sixth of the magical transportation songs that Adult Link can learn, the Requiem of Spirit is taught to Link by Sheik after he enters, and then leaves the Spirit Temple and returns to the Desert Colossus.

facts.subject: Requiem of Spirit
facts.text: The Requiem of Spirit transports Link to Desert Colossus, which Young Link must use to access the Spirit Temple because the Gerudo Thieves block the bridge into the Fortress.

evidence.quote: The Requiem transports Link (Young or Adult) to the Desert Colossus, giving easy access to the Spirit Temple.  Young Link must use this song to access to the Spirit Temple, since the Gerudo Thieves won't let him cross the bridge into the Fortress.

facts.subject: Nocturne of Shadow
facts.text: The Nocturne of Shadow is taught by Sheik after Adult Link finishes the Forest, Fire, and Water Temples and enters Kakariko Village, using the sequence C-Left, C-Right, C-Right, A Button, C-Left, C-Right, C-Down.

evidence.quote:
Nocturne of Shadow
First Found: Kakariko Village
Sequence: C-Left, C-Right, C-Right, A Button, C-Left, C-Right, C-Down

The fifth of the magical transportation songs that Adult Link can learn, the Nocturne of Shadow is taught to Link by Sheik after he finishes the Forest, Fire and Water Temple and enters Kakariko Village.

facts.subject: Nocturne of Shadow
facts.text: The Nocturne of Shadow transports Link to the high ledge in Kakariko Graveyard, which is the only way to reach the Shadow Temple.

evidence.quote: The Nocturne transports Link (Young or Adult) to the high ledge in Kakariko Graveyard.  This is the ONLY way to reach the Shadow Temple.

facts.subject: Prelude of Light
facts.text: The Prelude of Light is taught by Sheik after completing the Forest Temple and returning to the Temple of Time, using the sequence C-Up, C-Right, C-Up, C-Right, C-Left, C-Up.

evidence.quote:
Prelude of Light
First Found: The Temple of Time
Sequence: C-Up, C-Right, C-Up, C-Right, C-Left, C-Up

The second of the magical transportation songs that Adult Link can learn, the Prelude of Light is taught to Link by Sheik after he finishes the Forest Temple and returns to the Temple of Time.

facts.subject: Prelude of Light
facts.text: The Prelude of Light transports Link to the Temple of Time, enabling quick travel between Adulthood and Childhood.

evidence.quote: The Prelude of Light transports Link (Young or Adult) to the Temple of Time, making travel between Adulthood and Childhood a quick and painless task.

facts.subject: The Scarecrow's Song
facts.text: The Scarecrow's Song is taught by the player as Young Link to a scarecrow in Lake Hylia using an custom eight-note melody containing at least two different notes.

evidence.quote: A hidden song, the Scarecrow's Song is taught by the player to one of the scarecrows in Lake Hylia by Young Link.  You can make up any song you like, with a few requirements: it can't be any of the other songs in the game, it must contain eight notes, and it must contain at least two different notes.

facts.subject: Pierre the Scarecrow
facts.text: Playing the same Scarecrow's Song to the scarecrow in Lake Hylia as Adult Link allows Link to summon Pierre the Scarecrow around Hyrule as a makeshift Hookshot target.

evidence.quote: Once you have become Adult Link, return to Lake Hylia and play the Scarecrow the same song you played as Young Link.  The Scarecrow will "remember" the Song, and the Scarecrow's Song can now be played at various places around Hyrule to make Pierre the Scarecrow appear.  Pierre can be used as a makeshift Hookshot target.

facts.subject: Kokiri Training Ground
facts.text: The Kokiri Sword is found in the back of the Kokiri Training Ground and is required by Mido before meeting the Deku Tree.

evidence.quote: Found in the back of the Kokiri Training Ground, the Kokiri Sword is one of the items that Mido requires you to find before you can meet the Deku Tree.

facts.subject: Master Sword
facts.text: The Master Sword is found in the Temple of Time and serves as the main weapon wielded by Adult Link, pairing with the Hylian or Mirror Shield.

evidence.quote:
Master Sword
First Found: The Temple of Time
Used By: Adult Link...The main weapon used by Adult Link, it is preferred for most of the basic fights thanks to the fact that you can pair it with the Hylian or Mirror Shield.

facts.subject: Giant's Knife
facts.text: The Giant's Knife is sold for two hundred rupees by Biggoron in the back of Goron City, but it is fragile and breaks upon use.

evidence.quote: Purchased for two hundred rupees from the Biggoron stashed away in the back of Goron City, the Giant's Knife is poorly crafted and will break when used.

facts.subject: Biggoron Sword
facts.text: The Biggoron Sword is obtained on Death Mountain Trail as the ultimate reward for completing the Biggoron Sword Trading Sidequest.

evidence.quote:
Biggoron Sword
First Found: Death Mountain Trail
Used By: Adult Link

The ultimate reward for finishing the Biggoron Sword Trading Sidequest, the Biggoron Sword is identical to the Giant's Knife.

facts.subject: Biggoron Sword
facts.text: The Biggoron Sword does not shatter when used, but it is so large that Link cannot wield a shield simultaneously.

evidence.quote: Only the Biggoron who crafts this one is actually a competent swordsmith, so it won't shatter when used...The Biggoron Sword is so large that a shield cannot be wielded while using it.

facts.subject: Deku Shield
facts.text: The Deku Shield can be purchased from the Kokiri Shop for forty rupees and is required by Mido to visit the Deku Tree.

evidence.quote: Purchased from the Kokiri Shop for forty rupees, this is the other item that Mido requires you to get before he'll let you visit the Deku Tree.

facts.subject: Hylian Shield
facts.text: The Hylian Shield can be found underneath a gravestone in Kakariko Graveyard, or bought later from the Bazaar in Hyrule Castle Market and Kakariko Village.

evidence.quote: One of your first opportunities to acquire the shield is underneath one of the gravestones in Kakariko Graveyard, though you can also purchase it from the Bazaar in Hyrule Castle Market and Kakariko Village later on.

facts.subject: Like-Likes
facts.text: Like-Likes can easily steal Hylian Shields from Link during combat.

evidence.quote: Hylian Shields are easily stolen by Like-Likes, so be careful when combating these foes.

facts.subject: Mirror Shield
facts.text: The Mirror Shield is first found in the East Wing of the Spirit Temple.

evidence.quote:
Mirror Shield
First Found: Spirit Temple, East Wing

facts.subject: Mirror Shield
facts.text: The Mirror Shield's surface reflects beams of light to solve certain puzzles and reflects Twinrova's magic beams.

evidence.quote:
It's surface can reflect beams of
light to other areas of the room, which is required to solve certain puzzles.
The Mirror Shield can also reflect Twinrova's magic beams, which is the only
way to defeat that boss.

facts.subject: Mirror Shield
facts.text: The Mirror Shield cannot be stolen by Like-Likes.

evidence.quote:
The best thing about the Mirror Shield is that it
cannot be stolen by Like-Likes.

facts.subject: Kokiri Tunic
facts.text: The Kokiri Tunic is green, worn at the start of the game, and cannot be lost.

evidence.quote:
The standard clothing worn by Link, the Kokiri Tunic is green in color and has
no enhancements.  You begin the game wearing this tunic, and it's the only
tunic in the game which cannot be lost.

facts.subject: Goron Tunic
facts.text: A free Goron Tunic is given after meeting Link the Goron in Goron City.

evidence.quote:
A free Goron Tunic is given to you after you meet Link
the Goron in Goron City.

facts.subject: Goron Shop
facts.text: Additional Goron Tunics can be purchased from the Goron Shop for 300 rupees with the Giant's Wallet.

evidence.quote:
Additional tunics can be purchased from the Goron
Shop for 300 rupees (which means you'll need the Giant's Wallet).

facts.subject: Goron Tunic
facts.text: Wearing the Goron Tunic makes Link invulnerable to the heat of Death Mountain Crater and the Fire Temple, canceling the time limit.

evidence.quote:
When
worn, Link becomes invulnerable to the overwhelming heat of Death Mountain
Crater and the Fire Temple.  In essence, it cancels the time limit you have to
remain in these areas.

facts.subject: Zora Tunic
facts.text: King Zora gives Link a free Zora Tunic after being unfrozen from Red Ice using a bottle of Blue Fire.

evidence.quote:
A free
Zora Tunic is given to you by King Zora after unfreezing him from the Red Ice
(use a bottle of Blue Fire).

facts.subject: Zora Shop
facts.text: Additional Zora Tunics can be purchased from the Zora Shop for 300 rupees once the shop door is unfrozen.

evidence.quote:
Additional tunics can be purchased from the Zora
Shop for 300 rupees (which means you'll need the Giant's Wallet).  You'll have
to unfreeze the door to the Zora Shop the same way you unfroze the King Zora.

facts.subject: Zora Tunic
facts.text: The Zora Tunic allows the wearer to breathe underwater, canceling the time limit while wearing Iron Boots.

evidence.quote:
The Zora Tunic is made from Zora Skin, and allows the wearer to breath
underwater in the same manner that the Zora do.  In essence, it cancels the
time limit you have to remain underwater while wearing the Iron Boots.

facts.subject: Kokiri Boots
facts.text: Kokiri Boots are default equipment at the start of the game and cannot be stolen by Like-Likes.

evidence.quote:
The default boots that you begin the game with, the Kokiri Boots have good
traction and react the way you would expect boots to act.  They cannot be
stolen by Like-Likes.

facts.subject: Iron Boots
facts.text: The Iron Boots are first found in the Ice Cavern and are required in the Water Temple.

evidence.quote:
Iron Boots
First Found: Ice Cavern
Used By: Adult Link

Found in the Ice Cavern, the Iron Boots are needed in the Water Temple.

facts.subject: Iron Boots
facts.text: Iron Boots sink Link to the bottom of pools of water, slow him on dry ground, and make him invulnerable to strong dungeon wind gusts.

evidence.quote:
While
worn, it forces Link to the sink to the bottom of pools of water.  While on dry
ground, the Iron Boots force Link to move very slowly, but he becomes
invulnerable to strong gusts of wind from the fans in certain dungeons.

facts.subject: Hover Boots
facts.text: The Hover Boots are first found in the Shadow Temple.

evidence.quote:
Hover Boots
First Found: Shadow Temple

facts.subject: Hover Boots
facts.text: Hover Boots allow Link to run over a pit as solid ground for one second, increase wind effects, and make running on solid ground feel like ice.

evidence.quote:
The Hover Boots can be used to run over a pit as though it were solid ground
for one second...Hover Boots increase the effects of gusts of wind in the
same way that Iron Boots decrease the effect.  While wearing the Hover Boots,
running around on solid ground is like running around on ice.

facts.subject: Fairy Slingshot Ammunition Capacity Upgrade #1
facts.text: The first slingshot ammunition pouch is found inside the Deku Tree and holds 30 Deku Seeds.

evidence.quote:
Fairy Slingshot Ammunition Capacity Upgrade #1
First Found: Inside the Deku Tree
Used By: Young Link

Found along with the Fairy Slingshot, this ammunition pouch holds 30 Deku Seeds
(the Slingshot's preferred ammunition).

facts.subject: Shooting Gallery
facts.text: Shooting all targets at the Hyrule Castle Market Shooting Gallery awards the first Bullet Bag upgrade, increasing Slingshot capacity by 10.

evidence.quote:
Keep playing the minigame until you successfully shoot all of the targets, and
the clerk will award you with the first Bullet Bag  upgrade, which increases
the ammo capacity of your Slingshot by 10.

facts.subject: Shooting Gallery
facts.text: In the Hyrule Castle Market Shooting Gallery, rupees appear in a preset order across 6 rounds.

evidence.quote:
For this first run through the Shooting Gallery, the rupees appear in a preset
order.  The order is:

1.)  In the middle
2.)  From the left, then from the right
3.)  Jumps from the middle
4.)  From the left AND right
5.)  Two rupees coming from the right, going left
6.)  Two rupees coming from the left, going right

facts.subject: Fairy Slingshot Ammunition Capacity Upgrade #3
facts.text: Shooting the center of the drum hanging from a tree three times in a row in the southeast corner of Lost Woods summons a Deku Scrub who gives the final Slingshot ammo upgrade.

evidence.quote:
The last Slingshot Ammunition upgrade is found in the southeast corner of Lost
Woods.  Hanging above the valley where the Twin Skullkids dance, there is a
drum hanging from a tree.  Shoot the center of this drum three times in a row
(a large "100" appears when you hit it in the correct place), and a Deku Scrub
will appear and give you the upgrade.

facts.subject: Fairy Bow Ammunition Capacity Upgrade #1
facts.text: The first arrow quiver is found with the Fairy Bow in the Forest Temple and holds 30 arrows.

evidence.quote:
Fairy Bow Ammunition Capacity Upgrade #1
First Found: The Forest Temple
Used By: Adult Link

Found along with the Fairy Bow, this arrow quiver holds 30 arrows.

facts.subject: Shooting Gallery
facts.text: Hitting all targets in one go at the adult Shooting Gallery in Kakariko Village rewards the first Quiver upgrade.

evidence.quote:
Keep playing the game until you nail
all of the targets in one go, and the clerk will reward you with the first
Quiver upgrade.

facts.subject: Shooting Gallery
facts.text: At the Kakariko Shooting Gallery, if a single blue rupee comes from the left, the next target will always come from the right.

evidence.quote:
Note number 2: if a single blue rupee comes from the left, then the next one
will ALWAYS come from the right, despite the randomness of the rest of it.

facts.subject: Horseback Archery Range
facts.text: Scoring at least 1,500 points in the Horseback Archery Range minigame earns the second Quiver upgrade.

evidence.quote: Once you score 1,000 points, you'll win the Piece of Heart. Play the game again and score at least 1,500 to earn the Quiver.

facts.subject: Bomb Bag x30
facts.text: Stopping the rolling Goron with a bomb inside the northern tunnel on the third floor of Goron City awards the Bomb Bag x30 upgrade.

evidence.quote:
Drop down to the third
level of the city (the level directly beneath the top floor), where there is a
Biggoron rolling around the level in a giant loop.  You can stop him by placing
a bomb in his path so that it explodes just as he passes over it.  If you do
this while he is passing through the tunnel in the northern part of the third
floor, then he will give you the Bomb Bag x30 as a reward for your daring.

facts.subject: Horseback Archery Range
facts.text: Scoring at least 1,000 points at the Horseback Archery Range in Gerudo Fortress awards a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote:
You get twenty arrows to use, and in order to win the Piece
of Heart from this game you must score at least 1,000 points...Once you score 1,000 points, you'll win the Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Bomb Ammunition Capacity Upgrade #1
facts.text: The default Bomb Bag is obtained along with the Bombs in Dodongo's Cavern and holds twenty bombs.

evidence.quote:
This is the default Bomb Bag that you get along with the Bombs in Dodongo's
Cavern.  It holds only twenty bombs, but can quickly be upgraded to the maximum
level as soon as you are finished with the dungeon.

facts.subject: Bomb Bag
facts.text: The final Bomb Bag upgrade can be won at the Bombchu Bowling Alley in Hyrule Castle Market, which opens after clearing Dodongo's Cavern.

evidence.quote: Head for Hyrule Castle Market, and go to the newly-opened Bombchu Bowling Alley (it opens after you finish Dodongo's Cavern).  In addition to the Bomb Bag, you can also win: Bombs, Bombchus, a Purple Rupee, and a Piece of Heart.  Just keep playing the game until the clerk offers you the Bomb Bag as a reward.

facts.subject: Bombchu Bowling
facts.text: Bombchu Bowling requires sending a Bombchu into the hole on the opposite end across three increasingly difficult course goals.

evidence.quote: The object of Bombchu Bowling is to send the Bombchu (a mobile bomb) into the hole on the opposite end of the course.  The course has three different goals to obtain, each one becoming progressively more difficult.

facts.subject: Bombchu Bowling
facts.text: For the first goal in Bombchu Bowling, stand slightly to the right of the center arrow and time the release so the Bombchu avoids the Blade Trap.

evidence.quote: For the first goal, the target is always in the center of the field.  Simply stand in the exact middle of the field (slightly to the right of the center arrow is the exact middle of the field) and time it so your Bombchu avoids the Blade Trap.

facts.subject: Bombchu Bowling
facts.text: In the second round the target may appear on the top, left, or right, requiring dodging a small Cucco.

evidence.quote: The next level of the field can be on the top, left, or right, and adds a small Cucco to dodge.

facts.subject: Bombchu Bowling
facts.text: The third goal of Bombchu Bowling is in the center and features a Fat Cucco standing roughly in the middle of the field.

evidence.quote: The last goal is always in the exact center, and adds a Fat Cucco who always stands roughly in the center of the field (but you can sneak a Bombchu by it if you're careful).

facts.subject: Bombchu Bowling
facts.text: Players should stand in the center unless the target is on the right in the second round, or angle along the wall if the hole is on the left.

evidence.quote: When you're playing Bombchu Bowling, always position yourself in the center of the field.  The one exception is when the target appears on the right in the second round; you have to minorly adjust your position to the left or right, otherwise it's impossible to angle yourself properly for the Bombchu to enter the target.  If the hole appears on the left side of the field, then adjust your angle so that the Bombchu goes along the floor, then the wall, then into the hole.

facts.subject: Goron Bracelet
facts.text: Darunia gifts the Goron Bracelet to Young Link after being cheered up with Saria's Song.

evidence.quote: The Goron Bracelet is a gift to Young Link from Darunia, after cheering him up with Saria's Song.

facts.subject: Goron Bracelet
facts.text: The Goron Bracelet increases Link's strength, enabling him to pluck Bomb Flowers from the ground and pick up weeds.

evidence.quote: The Goron Bracelet increases Young Link's strength, giving him the ability to pluck Bomb Flowers from the ground.  He can also pick up weeds... not that you will ever have to.

facts.subject: Silver Gauntlets
facts.text: The Silver Gauntlets are found in the west wing of the Spirit Temple by Young Link and enable Adult Link to push and pull huge blue blocks.

evidence.quote: Obtained late in the adventure, the Silver Gauntlets are found by Young Link, though only Adult Link can use them.  Once he has the Silver Gauntlets, then he can push and pull the huge blue blocks that appear in the Spirit Temple and Gerudo Training Ground.

facts.subject: Gold Gauntlets
facts.text: The Gold Gauntlets are found in Ganon's Castle and allow Adult Link to lift and throw large black obelisks.

evidence.quote: With the Gold Gauntlets, Link can lift up the black obelisks that appear in Ganon's Castle and throw them aside.  One of the black obelisks hides the game's last Fairy Fountain, another hides a door in the Keep, and the last is needed to finish the Fire Seal.

facts.subject: Silver Scale
facts.text: The Silver Scale is won from the diving minigame at the top of the waterfall in Zora's Domain, accessed through the tunnel in King Zora's throne room.

evidence.quote: The Silver Scale is won from the diving minigame at the top of the Zora's Domain waterfall.  Go left through the tunnel in King Zora's throne room to reach it.

facts.subject: Silver Scale
facts.text: The Silver Scale increases Link's diving depth from 3 meters to 6 meters and is required to get the third bottle and enter Zora's Fountain.

evidence.quote: The Silver Scale doubles Link's diving depth from 3 meters to 6 meters.  It is required to obtain the game's third bottle and access Zora's Fountain.

facts.subject: Diving Minigame
facts.text: To complete the diving minigame, hold A while diving to collect all the rupees thrown off the waterfall by the Zora.

evidence.quote: The Zora will throw a handful of rupees off the waterfall, which you need to dive down and grab.  Simply position yourself above the rupees, and hold down A as you dive down to grab them...Once you have grabbed all of the rupees from around the waterfall, the Zora will call down for you to return to him and he'll give you a reward.  He'll give you the Silver Scale, which doubles how deep you can go in a single dive.

facts.subject: Fishing Pond
facts.text: The largest fish in the pond are found near the submerged log on the left and the reeds on the right.

evidence.quote: The biggest fish are found near the submerged log on the left side of the pond and the reeds on the right.  Once a fish is on the line, hold down A and pull backwards on the control stick to reel the fish in.

facts.subject: Fishing Pond
facts.text: Fish that break free disappear permanently, but exiting and re-entering the Fishing Pond causes them to respawn.

evidence.quote: The unfortunate downside to this is that once a fish breaks free from the line, it disappears permanently.  If the pond starts running low on larger fish, then leave it and re-enter, and they will respawn.  I find it also helps to alternate between holding back and to the left, and back and to the right every few seconds while you reel the fish in.

facts.subject: Epona
facts.text: Obtaining Epona as Adult Link requires having learned Epona's Song as Young Link at Lon Lon Ranch.

evidence.quote: Epona is won from Lon Lon Ranch, and can be obtained immediately after becoming Adult Link (it can, and should, be your first task as Adult Link).  First, you're going to need Epona's Song, so if you didn't learn that as Young Link then you'll have to visit Lon Lon Ranch in the past and learn it.

facts.subject: Ingo
facts.text: Paying Ingo 10 rupees to enter the paddock, playing Epona's Song, jumping both fences, and talking to him while riding triggers a race for 50 rupees.

evidence.quote: Pay him 10 rupees, and when you enter the paddock, ignore the horse that Ingo offers you.  Play Epona's Song, and the now fully-grown Epona will run towards you...Jump over both of the fences in the course to make back your ten rupees, then speak with Ingo...speak with Ingo WHILE you are riding Epona (z-target him to make it easier), and Ingo will challenge you to a race for 50 rupees.  Accept the challenge.

facts.subject: Ingo
facts.text: Ingo can be defeated in the horse race by staying in front of his path or hugging the inside rail while pacing carrot usage.

evidence.quote: Defeat Ingo by getting in front of him, and carefully steering Epona so that you stay in front of his path.  Alternatively, you can also use a steady amount of carrots and hug the inside the rail.  Use your first four carrots quickly, then wait for one to regenerate, then use another carrot, then wait for it to regenerate, then use another, etc. etc.

facts.subject: Ingo
facts.text: Ingo cheats by starting 1 second early in the second race, but running inside and cutting in front when he takes corners wide defeats him.

evidence.quote: Defeat Ingo, and he'll challenge you to another race.  And this time, if you win, he'll let you keep Epona.  Agree.  On this race, Ingo will cheat, and start a second before the clock says Go...He tends to take the corners very wide, so that's your opportunity to move in front of him.

facts.subject: Epona
facts.text: After beating Ingo twice, run counter-clockwise around the paddock and burn all carrots to jump the locked gate into Hyrule Field to win Epona.

evidence.quote: Once you defeat Ingo for the second time, he'll honor his bet, but he'll also prevent you from leaving the Ranch by closing the gate.  To make it over the gate, you must run around the path around the paddock in a counter-clockwise pattern.  Once you come around the corner and see the gate, burn all of your carrots at once and charge straight at the gate...Once you make it over the gate, then you will return to Hyrule Field and Epona will become yours.

facts.subject: Super Spin Attack
facts.text: The Super Spin Attack adds two magic-consuming charge levels that double range at blue and triple range at red.

evidence.quote: This upgrade increases the range of Link's Spin Attack by a wide margin, and gives it two charge levels.  The first level, blue, doubles the range of the Spin Attack, and the second level, red, triples the range...Both levels of the Super Spin Attack use a small amount of the magic meter.

facts.subject: Spin Attack
facts.text: A blue Super Spin Attack can be executed quickly by rotating the joystick and attacking, while releasing B just as the sword glows blue costs no magic.

evidence.quote: You can quickly execute a blue level Super Spin Attack by rotating the joystick and pressing the attack button...If you like, you can still execute a standard Spin Attack by holding down the B-Button, and releasing it just as the sword glows blue.  The spin attack will execute, but will not use any Magic Power.

facts.subject: Super Spin Attack
facts.text: The Super Spin Attack is obtained from the Great Fairy of Power on Death Mountain peak by bombing the rock formation to the left of the Crater entrance.

evidence.quote: The Super Spin Attack is obtained from the Great Fairy of Power on the peak of Death Mountain.  Use a bomb to blow open the odd formation of rock to the left of the entrance to Death Mountain Crater to find the entrance to the fountain.
Inside the Great Fairy's Fountain...located above the Goron City on the...Death Mountain Trail, need Bomb Bag.

facts.subject: Magic Meter Upgrade
facts.text: The Magic Meter Upgrade doubles the Magic Meter and is received from the Great Fairy of Power behind silver rocks smashed with the Megaton Hammer.

evidence.quote: The Magic Meter Upgrade doubles the size of the Magic Meter.  It is obtained from the Great Fairy of Power, who resides behind a pair of silver rocks in the lower half of Death Mountain Crater.  Use the Megaton Hammer to smash the rocks blocking the entrance to the cave.

facts.subject: Defense Upgrade
facts.text: The Defense Upgrade is granted by the Great Fairy of Courage outside Ganon's Castle behind a black obelisk requiring the Gold Gauntlet to move.

evidence.quote: A gift from the Great Fairy of Courage, who lives near the bridge of light that leads into Ganon's Castle.  To access the fountain, you have to have the Gold Gauntlet.  Head down the path behind the shattered arch, where you will find one of the game's black obelisks.  Pick it up and toss it aside to gain access to the fountain.
You will find this Great Fairy Fountain...outside of Ganon's Castle after you...acquire the Golden Gauntlets.

facts.subject: Deku Stick Capacity Upgrade #1
facts.text: A Business Scrub in the southwest valley of the Lost Woods sells a Deku Stick capacity upgrade from 10 to 20 for forty rupees.

evidence.quote: A Business Scrub in the southwest valley of the Lost Woods sells he upgrade for forty rupees.  It raises your Deku Stick capacity from 10 to 20 (and also maxes your Deku Sticks).

facts.subject: Deku Stick Capacity Upgrade #2
facts.text: Wearing the Skull Mask on the platform before the Deku Scrubs at the Forest Stage in the Lost Woods increases Deku Stick capacity to 30.

evidence.quote: The second Deku Stick Upgrade can be obtained from the Forest Stage, but requires the Skull Mask.  The Forest Stage is located in the clearing near the center of the Lost Woods...Drop down into the Forest Stage, equip the Skull Mask, and stand on the platform before the Deku Scrubs.  They'll award you with the Deku Stick upgrade, which raises your capacity to 30.

facts.subject: Gold Scale
facts.text: The Gold Scale increases Link's diving depth to nine meters and is won at the Fishing Pond with Adult Link by catching a record breaking fish of fifteen pounds.

evidence.quote: The Gold Scale increases Link's diving depth to nine meters, it's maximum length...The Gold Scale is won from the Fishing Pond with Adult Link, though Young Link can benefit from it's effects as well...In order to win the Gold Scale, you have to capture a record breaking fish: fifteen pounds.

facts.subject: Deku Scrub Leader
facts.text: Wearing the Mask of Truth on the platform in the Forest Stage prompts the Deku Scrub leader to give Link the second Deku Nut upgrade, which becomes unobtainable after travelling to adulthood.

evidence.quote: The second Deku Nut Upgrade is can be gotten in the Forest Stage, but requires the Mask of Truth....Drop down into the Forest Stage, equip the Mask of Truth, and stand on the platform before the Deku Scrubs.  The Scrubs will stare at you.  Run over and speak with their leader (the tall one with the mustache), and he'll give you the Deku Nut upgrade....This upgrade is unobtainable if you travel to Adulthood before getting it.

facts.subject: Child's Wallet
facts.text: The Child's Wallet is the default wallet that Link begins the game with, and it can hold 99 rupees.

evidence.quote: This is the default wallet that you begin the game with.  It can hold only 99 rupees.

facts.subject: House of Skulltula
facts.text: The Adult's Wallet holds 200 rupees and is rewarded by the House of Skulltula after killing 10 Gold Skulltulas and collecting their tokens.

evidence.quote: It is a reward from the House of Skulltula, and is obtained after you have killed 10 Gold Skulltulas and taken their tokens.  The Adult's Wallet holds 200 rupees.

facts.subject: House of Skulltula
facts.text: The Giant's Wallet holds 500 rupees and is awarded by the House of Skulltula after collecting 30 Gold Skulltula tokens.

evidence.quote: The largest wallet in the game is also obtained from the House of Skulltula.  After you have killed 30 Gold Skulltulas, return to the House and get the reward.  The Giant's Wallet holds 500 rupees.

facts.subject: Gerudo Fortress
facts.text: The Gerudo's Card is obtained after freeing the four carpenters from Gerudo Fortress.

evidence.quote: The membership card for the Gerudo Thieves, the Gerudo's Card is obtained after you free the four carpenters from the Fortress (which can be done as early as when you first get the Hookshot, though it's easier with the Bow).

facts.subject: Gerudo's Card
facts.text: The Gerudo's Card prevents Gerudo Guards from throwing Link in jail and provides access to the Haunted Wasteland, Gerudo Training Ground, and Horseback Archery Range.

evidence.quote: The Gerudo's Card stops the Gerudo Guards from throwing you in jail, and also lets you access the Haunted Wasteland, the Gerudo Training Ground and the Horseback Archery Range.

facts.subject: Kokiri Emerald
facts.text: The Kokiri Emerald is the first of three Spiritual Stones and is given as a gift from the Great Deku Tree.

evidence.quote: The first of three Spiritual Stones, the Kokiri Emerald is a gift from the Great Deku Tree.

facts.subject: Goron Ruby
facts.text: The Goron Ruby is the second of three Spiritual Stones and symbolizes the pact of brotherhood between Link and the Gorons.

evidence.quote: The second of the three Spiritual Stones, the Goron Ruby is a symbol of the pact of brotherhood that Link shares with the Gorons.

facts.subject: Zora Sapphire
facts.text: The Zora Sapphire is the last of three Spiritual Stones and symbolizes the engagement between Link and Princess Ruto.

evidence.quote: The last of the three Spiritual Stones, the Zora Sapphire is a symbol of the engagement between Link and Ruto.

facts.subject: Light Medallion
facts.text: Rauru gives Link the Light Medallion in the Chamber of the Sages immediately after Link draws the Master Sword from its pedestal.

evidence.quote: A gift from Rauru, the Sage of Light, the Light Medallion is the symbol of Rauru's power.  You obtain it in the Chamber of the Sages, immediately after taking the Master Sword from it's pedestal.

facts.subject: Forest Medallion
facts.text: Saria bestows the Forest Medallion in the Chamber of the Sages after completing the Forest Temple.

evidence.quote: A gift from Saria, the Sage of Forest, the Forest Medallion is the symbol of Saria's power.  You obtain it in the Chamber of the Sages after finishing the Forest Temple.

facts.subject: Fire Medallion
facts.text: Darunia grants the Fire Medallion in the Chamber of the Sages after finishing the Fire Temple.

evidence.quote: A gift from Darunia, the Sage of Fire, the Fire Medallion is the symbol of Darunia's power.  You obtain it in the Chamber of the Sages after finishing the Fire Temple.

facts.subject: Water Medallion
facts.text: Ruto gives the Water Medallion in the Chamber of the Sages upon clearing the Water Temple.

evidence.quote: A gift from Ruto, the Sage of Water, the Water Medallion is the symbol of Ruto's power.  You obtain it in the Chamber of the Sages after finishing the Water Temple.

facts.subject: Shadow Temple
facts.text: Obtaining the Forest Medallion, Fire Medallion, and Water Medallion grants access to the Shadow Temple.

evidence.quote: Once the Forest Medallion, Fire Medallion and Water Medallion are obtained, then you can gain access to the Shadow Temple.

facts.subject: Shadow Medallion
facts.text: Impa grants the Shadow Medallion, the symbol of her power, upon finishing the Shadow Temple.

evidence.quote: A gift from Impa, the Sage of Shadow, the Shadow Medallion is the symbol of Impa's power.

facts.subject: Spirit Medallion
facts.text: Nabooru grants the Spirit Medallion, the symbol of her power, after finishing the Spirit Temple.

evidence.quote: A gift from Nabooru, the Sage of Spirit, the Spirit Medallion is the symbol of Nabooru's power.

facts.subject: Ganon's Castle
facts.text: Obtaining both the Shadow and Spirit Medallions creates the road to Ganon's Castle.

evidence.quote: Once you have obtained both the Shadow and Spirit Medallions, then the road to Ganon's Castle will be created.

facts.subject: Skullkid twins
facts.text: Completing three rounds of the Ocarina memory game with the twin Skullkids as Young Link awards a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: Stand on the tree trunk in front of the twin Skullkids and pull out your Ocarina.  The Skullkids will play a memory-style game with you.  Complete three rounds to earn the Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Lone Skullkid
facts.text: Playing Saria's Song on the tree trunk for the lone Skullkid in southwest Lost Woods as Young Link earns a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: Stand on the tree trunk in front of the lone Skullkid, and play him Saria's Song.  He'll give you a Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Business Scrub
facts.text: A Business Scrub in a pit below a rock near the entrance to the Sacred Forest Meadow sells the first Deku Nut Upgrade for forty rupees.

evidence.quote: The first Deku Nut Upgrade is found in the Lost Woods.  Use a bomb to blow up the rock near the entrance to the Sacred Forest Meadow, and in the pit below you'll find a pair of Business Scrubs.  One of them sells the upgrade for forty rupees.

facts.subject: House of Skulltula
facts.text: The Stone of Agony is rewarded by the House of Skulltula for killing twenty Gold Skulltulas, causing the rumble pak to rumble slightly over hidden pits.

evidence.quote: A reward from the House of Skulltula for killing twenty Gold Skulltulas and taking their tokens, the Stone of Agony works in conjunction with the rumble pak to reveal hidden pits.  When you pass over one of these pits, the pak will rumble slightly.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: Link can use a Bomb to open a hidden pit in the fenced-in square near the Lake Hylia entrance and buy a Piece of Heart from a Business Scrub for ten rupees.

evidence.quote: Head for the fenced-in square near the entrance to Lake Hylia.  Jump into the middle of the fences, and head for the approximate center.  Use a Bomb to blast open a hidden pit in the middle of the pasture (use the Stone of Agony to find it easier, if you have it.  Buy the Piece of Heart from a Business Scrub down here for a mere ten rupees.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: Link can place a bomb near a lone tree north of Lon Lon Ranch to reveal a hidden pit containing a pool with a Piece of Heart at the bottom, reachable with the Steels Boots or Gold Scale.

evidence.quote: Look for a lone tree north of Lon Lon Ranch.  Place a bomb near the tree to reveal a hidden pit (use the Stone of Agony to find it easier, if you have it). Jump into the pit, and kill the Tektite at the bottom.  Either use the Steels Boots or the Gold Scale to go to the bottom of the pool and get the Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: Returning the small white dog from behind a stall near the Gate in Hyrule Castle Market to the woman in the second door on the left in the back alley rewards a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: Look for a small white dog behind a stall near the entrance to the Gate.  Run near it so that it follows you, then enter the back alley near the entrance to the Treasure Chest Game.  Enter the second door on the left and speak with the fat lady inside.  She'll recognize the dog as her own, and reward you with a Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: A Piece of Heart can be won as a prize by successfully completing all three goals in the Bombchu Bowling Alley.

evidence.quote: Keep playing the Bombchu Bowling Alley game until the Piece of Heart is offered up as a prize...Completing all three goals successfully will win you whatever prize the clerk showed you at the start.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: Reaching the last room of the nighttime Treasure Chest Game in Hyrule Castle Market rewards a Piece of Heart from a lone chest.

evidence.quote: Enter the Treasure Chest Game near the entrance to the Back Alley in Hyrule Castle Market (it's only open at night)...When you reach the last room in the minigame, you will find a lone chest which contains a Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Treasure Chest Game
facts.text: In the Treasure Chest Game, each room contains two chests with either a Small Key or a Rupee booby prize, and the Lens of Truth can be used to see the contents of each chest.

evidence.quote: There are two chests in this room, one of which contains a Small Key, the other of which contains a Rupee.  The Key lets you progress, the rupee is a booby prize.  Normally, you'd have to guess which chest contains the Key.  But the Lens of Truth makes things easier.  Simply use the Lens of Truth to see the contents of each chest, and take the Small Key in each room.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: Pushing milk crates in the corner of the grain mill at Lon Lon Ranch reveals a crawl tunnel leading to an empty nest containing a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: In the corner of the mill, there are a large number of milk crates...The X marks where a new tunnel will have appeared.  Crawl through the tunnel to find an empty nest, which houses a Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: In Kakariko Village, the opening on the backside of Impa's House can be reached by floating with a Cucco from the unfinished house, riding Kaepora Gaebora from Death Mountain Trail, or using the Hookshot as Adult Link.

evidence.quote: One, as Young Link grab a Cucco and float out to the balcony from the top of the unfinished house.  Two, as Young Link hitch a ride from Kaepora Gaebora on top of Death Mountain Trail.  He'll drop you off on top of Impa's House.  From there, drop down to the opening...Lastly, with Adult Link simply use the Hookshot to get on top of Impa's House, then drop down to the doorway from there.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: The Piece of Heart on the high ledge in the Windmill can be grabbed with the Boomerang as Young Link or reached upon finishing Dampe's Cave Race as Adult Link.

evidence.quote: As Young Link, use the Boomerang to grab the Piece of Heart from the ledge.  Or, with Adult Link you can finish Dampe's Cave Race, which will spit you out right next to the Piece of Heart when you finish.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: As Adult Link, pulling onto the blue roof across from the Windmill and speaking with the man gazing up at Death Mountain rewards a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: As Adult Link, pull yourself up to the blue roof across from the Windmill.  Speak with the man gazing up at Death Mountain, and he'll give you a Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: Link receives a Piece of Heart as a reward from the House of Skulltula upon obtaining fifty Skulltula Tokens.

evidence.quote: Get fifty Skulltula Tokens, then get the Piece of Heart as a reward from the House of Skulltula.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: Pulling aside a gravestone in the rear of Kakariko Graveyard reveals a pit where defeating the Redead and playing the Sun's Song spawns a chest containing a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: Pull aside the Gravestones in the rear of Kakariko Graveyard.  One of them has a pit underneath it.  Drop into this pit, and kill the Redead inside.  Play the Sun's Song, and a chest appears which contains the Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: During the Grave Digging Minigame between nightfall and 10:00, paying Dampe 10 rupees to dig dirt patches in Kakariko Graveyard can uncover a Piece of Heart hidden in one of twelve patches.

evidence.quote: From nightfall to 10:00, Dampe will operate a Grave Digging Minigame in the Graveyard...In one of the twelve dirt patches dotted around the graveyard, there is hidden a Piece of Heart.  In order to find the Piece of Heart, stand directly on that dirt patch so that way Dampe will stop directly in front of it, then speak to Dampe and pay him 10 rupees to dig up that patch of dirt.  Most of the dirt patches contain at the very least some rupees.  Keep playing the game until you dig up the Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Heart-Pounding Grave Digging Tour
facts.text: The Grave Digging Minigame operates only from nightfall to 10:00 and cannot be accessed with the Sun's Song, requiring Link to wait for nightfall in Hyrule Field or Death Mountain Trail.

evidence.quote: The game only operates from nightfall to 10:00, so you can't use the Sun's Song to access it.  You'll have to return to Hyrule Field or Death Mountain Trail and wait for the wolf's howl that indicates nightfall, then return to Kakariko Graveyard.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: Planting a Magic Bean in the soft earth on the west side of Kakariko Graveyard allows Adult Link to ride the Magic Leaf up to a ledge crate containing a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: As Young Link, plant a Magic Bean in the patch of soft earth on the west side of the Graveyard.  Return to the Graveyard as Adult Link, and ride the Magic Leaf up to a high ledge.  Roll into the crate on the ledge to find a Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: Completing Dampe's Cave Race underneath the flower-covered gravestone in Kakariko Graveyard in under one minute rewards a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: Dampe's Cave Race Game can be found underneath a gravestone on the left side of Kakariko Graveyard.  It's the only gravestone with flowers growing on it.  Drop down the pit underneath the grave...If you make it under one minute, then Dampe will give you a Piece of Heart for your efforts.

facts.subject: Death Mountain Trail
facts.text: A Piece of Heart can be reached above Dodongo's Cavern by backflipping over the shortened fence from the Bomb Flower alcove as Young Link, or by riding the Magic Leaf as Adult Link after planting Magic Beans near the cavern entrance.

evidence.quote: Stand in the small alcove with the Bomb Flower, and do a backflip over the shortened bit of fence.  You'll land on the cliff below.  Alternatively, you can plant the Magic Beans near the entrance to Dodongo's Cavern as Young Link, then return as Adult Link and ride the Magic Leaf up to the Heart Piece.

facts.subject: Death Mountain Crater
facts.text: A Piece of Heart is located in an alcove halfway down the cliff on the north side of Death Mountain Crater, accessible by climbing down the cliff and approaching from below.

evidence.quote: The Heart Piece can be found in an alcove halfway down the cliff on the north side of Death Mountain Crater.  Climb down the cliff and approach the alcove from below to get the Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Death Mountain Crater
facts.text: Without the Goron Tunic, Young Link will die if time runs out in the extreme heat of Death Mountain Crater, and fairies will not help.

evidence.quote: Without the aid of the Goron Tunic, Young Link is susceptible to the extreme heat of Death Mountain Crater.  If you fail to reach the Piece of Heart before time runs out, then you will DIE.  Fairies don't help you.

facts.subject: Death Mountain Crater
facts.text: A Piece of Heart sits on top of a massive rock near the warp-in point in Death Mountain Crater, reached by riding the Magic Leaf grown from planting Magic Beans in the soft earth patch to the left of the warp.

evidence.quote: There is a patch of soft earth just to your left as you warp in.  Plant the Magic Beans, then either save and quit out or use the Prelude of Light to return to the Temple of Time.  Go forward in time to Adult Link, and return to Death Mountain Crater.  Use the Magic Leaf to ride around to the Piece of Heart, which is on top of one of the massive rocks near the warp-in point.

facts.subject: Goron City
facts.text: Lighting all torches on the bottom floor of Goron City causes the large pot to spin, and stopping it with an explosive bomb so that the happy face points forward reveals a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: Use a Deku Stick to transfer the flame from Darunia's Room to the torches around the bottom floor of Goron City.  Once all of the torches are lit, then the large pot will begin to spin.  Run up to the next level of Goron City so that you are level with the top of the pot.  Throw a bomb into the pot, and when it explodes the pot will stop spinning.  If the pot stops with the happy face pointing forward, then a Piece of Heart will appear.

facts.subject: Zora's River
facts.text: A Piece of Heart rests on top of a high pillar halfway up Zora's River, accessible with a Cucco, the Boomerang, or the Hover Boots.

evidence.quote: At the top of the ladder, grab another Cucco and use it to hover over to the top of the pillar, which holds a Heart Piece.  Alternatively, you can also use the Boomerang with Young Link or the Hover Boots with Adult Link.

facts.subject: Musical Frogs
facts.text: Playing the Song of Storms for the Musical Frogs in Zora's River rewards Link with a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: Go to the Musical Frogs, and play them the Song of Storms.  They will reward you with  a Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Musical Frogs
facts.text: Playing the basic songs initiates a minigame where eating the flies in sequence earns a Piece of Heart: A Button, C-Left, C-Right, C-Down, C-Left, C-Right, C-Down, A Button, C-Down, A Button, C-Down, C-Right, C-Left, A Button.

evidence.quote: Play all of the basic songs (Zelda's Lullaby, Epona's Song, Sun's Song, Saria's Song, Song of Storms and Song of Time), and the Musical Frogs will play a Musical Game with you.  Flies will appear above the Frog's heads, and you must press the button associated with that frog to make him eat it....The order is as follows: A Button, C-Left, C-Right, C-Down, C-Left, C-Right, C-Down, A Button, C-Down, A Button, C-Down, C-Right, C-Left, A Button

facts.subject: Zora's River
facts.text: Near the entrance to Zora's Domain, a platform back downstream holds a Piece of Heart that can be reached using a Cucco, the Boomerang, or the Hover Boots.

evidence.quote: From the high ledge near the entrance to Zora's Domain, turn around and look back downstream.  You'll see a platform with a Piece of Heart on it.  Use the Cucco to glide out to it.  Alternatively, you can also use the Boomerang or the Hover Boots.

facts.subject: Zora's Domain
facts.text: Lighting all braziers across Zora's Domain before any burn out reveals a chest behind the waterfall containing a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: If you did it fast enough so that you lit all the braziers without any of them burning out, then a chest will appear behind the Waterfall which contains a Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: As Adult Link, jump along the icebergs from the first iceberg in Zora's Fountain to the east branch to get a Piece of Heart at the end of the string.

evidence.quote:
Head for the first iceberg in Zora's Fountain, and jump out along the icebergs
until you reach the huge one.  The icebergs branch north and east from here.
Run to the east iceberg, and run out to the end of the string of icebergs to
get the Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: As Adult Link, equip the Iron Boots and sink to the very bottom of the pool in Zora's Fountain to obtain a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote:
Equip the Iron Boots and sink to the very bottom of the pool.  The Piece of
Heart lies at the bottom.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: In the Ice Cavern room with the large spinning ice scythe, melt the east wall with blue fire to find a small room and use a Bottle of Blue Fire to melt the red ice containing a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote:
Head for the room with the large spinning scythe made of ice.  On the east side
of the room, there is a wall which can be melted with blue fire.  Go through
this wall, and on the other side you'll find a small room.  In this room, there
is a chunk of red ice.  The Piece of Heart is inside it.  Use a Bottle of Blue
Fire to melt the red ice.

facts.subject: Fishing Minigame
facts.text: As Young Link, speak to the clerk at the Lake Hylia Fishing Pond and pay him 20 rupees to play the Fishing Minigame.

evidence.quote:
As Young Link, go to the Fishing Pond in Lake Hylia.  Speak with the Clerk to
the right, and pay him 20 rupees to play the Fishing Minigame.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: Catch a record-breaking fish of at least nine pounds in the Fishing Minigame and show it to the clerk to receive a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote:
In order to win the Piece of Heart, you have to capture a record breaking fish:
nine pounds...Once you have captured a nine-pound fish (minimum), return to the Clerk and
show him your fish.  He'll give you a Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: Plant a Magic Bean behind the Observatory as Young Link, then as Adult Link ride the Magic Leaf or use the Scarecrow's Song and Hookshot to reach the roof and climb the ladder to a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote:
As Young Link, plant a Magic Bean in the patch of soft earth near the backside
of the Observatory.  Back as Adult Link, ride the Magic Leaf to the roof of the
observatory, and from there climb the ladder to the top of the tower.  The
Heart Piece is on top.  Alternatively, you can also reach the roof using the
Scarecrow's Song and Hookshot.

facts.subject: Gold Scale
facts.text: Adult Link can win the Gold Scale from the Fishing Pond by catching a fifteen-pound or larger fish.

evidence.quote:
First, win the Gold Scale from the Fishing Pond by catching a fifteen-pound or
larger fish with Adult Link.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: Dive all the way down to the bottom of the observatory pool with the Gold Scale and speak with the scientist to receive a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote:
Then, go to the observatory and jump into the
pool of water.  Dive all the way down to the bottom of the pool, then speak
with the scientist.  He'll give you a Piece of Heart for your accomplishment.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: Glide down with a Cucco as Young Link or use the Longshot as Adult Link to reach a cliff ledge in Gerudo Valley, then roll into the crate to find a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote:
As Young Link, grab a Cucco and glide down to the ledge on the far wall of the
cliff.  It has a crate sitting on it.  Roll into the crate to find a Piece of
Heart.  Alternatively, you can also use the Longshot with Adult Link.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: In Gerudo Valley, glide with a Cucco behind the waterfall at the east end of the canyon and climb the ladder behind it to reach a Piece of Heart at the top.

evidence.quote:
Grab a Cucco, and use it to float down to the backside of the waterfall at the
east end of the canyon.  Land in the water behind the waterfall, where there is
no current, and climb up the ladder behind the waterfall.  The Piece of Heart
is at the top of the ladder.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: On the top floor of Gerudo Fortress, use the Longshot to reach the chest on the north side to obtain a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote:
Head to the top floor of Gerudo Fortress.  Look to the north side of the
fortress, where you will see the chest.  Use the Longshot to pull yourself over
to it.  Open the chest to get the Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: Score at least 1,000 points in the Horseback Archery Minigame using twenty arrows to win a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote:
You get twenty arrows to use, and in order to win the Piece
of Heart from this game you must score at least 1,000 points...Once you score 1,000 points, you'll win the Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: Plant a Magic Bean near the Spirit Temple entrance as Young Link, then return as Adult Link and ride the Magic Leaf to reach a Piece of Heart on top of an archway.

evidence.quote:
As Young Link, play the Requiem of Spirit to warp to the Desert Colossus.  Run
to the entrance to the Spirit Temple, where you will find a patch of soft earth
just to it's left.  Plant the Magic Bean here.  Become Adult Link, and return
to the Desert Colossus.  Use the Magic Leaf to float around the Desert
Colossus, and near the end of it's path you'll pass by an archway.  Jump on top
of it, and you'll find the Piece of Heart on top of the arch.

facts.subject: House of Skulltula
facts.text: Destroying the one hundred Gold Skulltulas around Hyrule frees the family in the House of Skulltula of its curse.

evidence.quote:
If you find and destroy the one hundred Gold
Skulltulas around Hyrule, then you will free the family of it's curse.

facts.subject: Adult's Wallet
facts.text: Collecting 10 Gold Skulltula tokens rewards the Adult's Wallet, which raises rupee capacity from 99 rupees to 200 rupees.

evidence.quote:
10 Tokens - Adult's Wallet

The Adult's Wallet raises your rupee capacity from 99 rupees to 200 rupees.

facts.subject: Stone of Agony
facts.text: Collecting 20 Gold Skulltula tokens rewards the Stone of Agony, which causes the Rumble Pak to rumble near a hidden pit.

evidence.quote:
20 Tokens - The Stone of Agony

The Stone of Agony causes your Rumble Pak to Rumble when you near a hidden pit.

facts.subject: Giant's Wallet
facts.text: Collecting 30 Gold Skulltula tokens rewards the Giant's Wallet, which raises rupee capacity from 200 to 500 rupees.

evidence.quote:
30 Tokens - Giant's Wallet

The Giant's Wallet raises your rupee capacity from 200 to 500 rupees.

facts.subject: Bombchus
facts.text: Collecting 40 Gold Skulltula tokens rewards Bombchus.

evidence.quote:
40 Tokens - Bombchus

Yep.  Lousy Bombchus.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: Collecting 50 Gold Skulltula tokens rewards a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote:
50 Tokens - Piece of Heart

At 50, you get the best reward, a Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Huge Rupee
facts.text: Collecting all 100 Gold Skulltulas rewards 200 rupees, which can be claimed repeatedly by speaking with the Patriarch again after leaving and re-entering the house.

evidence.quote:
100 Tokens - Huge Rupee

Yep.  The ultimate reward for getting all 100 Gold Skulltulas is... 200 rupees.
Sort of.  You can keep leaving and re-entering the house, speaking with the
Patriarch again to get another 200 rupees.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: During nighttime, a Gold Skulltula is found behind the Know-It-All Brothers House in Kokiri Forest.

evidence.quote:
This Gold Skulltula is found behind the Know-It-All Brothers House during
nighttime.  The Know-It-All Brothers House is the building to the right as you
enter Kokiri Forest from Hyrule Field.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Dropping a Bottled Bug into the patch of soft earth behind the Kokiri Shop causes a Gold Skulltula to emerge.

evidence.quote:
Drop a Bottled Bug into the Patch of Soft Earth behind the Kokiri Shop.  A Gold
Skulltula will emerge.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: At the back of the Twin's House near the entrance to the Deku Tree, the Hookshot is used to find and kill a Gold Skulltula.

evidence.quote:
Head for the back of the Twin's House.  This is the house with the two branches
coming out of the top.  It's next door to Saria's House, and closest to the
entrance to the Deku Tree.  Use the Hookshot to find and kill the Gold
Skulltula.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Dropping a Bottled Bug into the patch of soft earth in the southwest corner valley of the Lost Woods causes a Gold Skulltula to appear.

evidence.quote:
Head for the valley in the southwest corner of the Lost Woods.  Drop a Bottled
Bug into the patch of soft earth, where a Gold Skulltula will appear.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Dropping a Bottled Bug into the patch of soft earth in the clearing near the Forest Stage entrance in the central Lost Woods causes a Gold Skulltula to appear.

evidence.quote:
Head for the clearing in the center of the Lost Woods, near where you enter the
Forest Stage.  Drop a Bottled Bug into the patch of soft earth, where a Gold
Skulltula will appear.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Planting a Magic Bean in the central Lost Woods clearing as Young Link allows Adult Link to ride the Magic Leaf to reach a Gold Skulltula on the ledge.

evidence.quote:
As Young Link, plant a Magic Bean in the patch of soft earth in the clearing
near the center of the Lost Woods.  Return here as Adult Link, and you will
find a Gold Skulltula on the ledge that the Magic Leaf leads to.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Climbing the ladder near the stairs in Sacred Forest Meadow and jumping along the cliff reveals a Gold Skulltula high on the east wall that can be killed with the Hookshot.

evidence.quote:
Climb up the ladder near the stairs in the back of the Sacred Forest Meadow.
Jump along the cliff of the maze, and look high on the east wall to see the
Gold Skulltula.  Kill it and take it's token with the Hookshot.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Using a bomb near the roots of the lone tree north of Kakariko Village reveals a pit containing a Gold Skulltula high on the opposite wall.

evidence.quote:
Head for the lone tree in the corner of Hyrule Field, north of Kakariko
Village.  Use a bomb near the roots of the tree to reveal a pit.  Drop down it,
and you will find a pit which contains a Gold Skulltula high on the opposite
wall.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Placing a bomb in the circle of stones east of Gerudo Valley opens a pit where Din's Fire burns webbing to reveal a Gold Skulltula on the wall behind the cow.

evidence.quote:
Look for a circle of stones east of Gerudo Valley.  Place a bomb in the middle
of the stones to reveal a pit.  Drop down it.  Use Din's Fire to burn away the
webbing covering the walls in the room, then look in the alcove which contains
the Cow.  On the wall behind the Cow is a Gold Skulltula.

facts.subject: Gatehouse crate
facts.text: Inside the Gatehouse near the drawbridge into Hyrule Castle, rolling into the two crates near the guard in the back of the room reveals a Gold Skulltula.

evidence.quote:
The Gatehouse is the small building near the drawbridge into Hyrule Castle.
Roll into the two crates near the guard in the back of the room.  In one of
them is a Gold Skulltula.  Kill it and take it's token.

facts.subject: Garden entrance tree
facts.text: Rolling into the large tree near the entrance to the Garden causes a Gold Skulltula to fall from the branches.

evidence.quote:
Roll into the large tree near the entrance to the Garden.  This is the same
tree that Kaepora Gaebora sits in when you first arrive in the garden.  A Gold
Skulltula will fall from the branches.

facts.subject: Ganon's Castle marble arch
facts.text: At Ganon's Castle in the future, a Gold Skulltula hangs above the lava on the back right side of the shattered marble arch and can be taken with the Hookshot.

evidence.quote:
Head for Ganon's Castle in the future, and look to the back of the shattered
marble arch to see a Gold Skulltula.  It hangs above the lava on the right side
of the arch, facing it from the back.  Kill it and take it's token with the
Hookshot.

facts.subject: Hyrule Castle Garden tree pit
facts.text: Playing the Song of Storms beneath the tree at the corner of the moat reveals a pit where bombing one of three walls reveals a Gold Skulltula.

evidence.quote:
At the corner of the
moat, there is a tree.  Stand beneath the tree and play the Song of Storms to
reveal a pit.  Drop down the pit, and bomb the three walls in the room.  Behind
one of the walls is the Gold Skulltula.  Kill it and take it's token with the
Boomerang.

facts.subject: Lon Lon Ranch second story window
facts.text: On the tall second story building to the left of the entrance to Lon Lon Ranch, a Gold Skulltula crawls on one of the second story windows.

evidence.quote:
Look on the tall second story building to the left of the entrance to Lon Lon
Ranch.  The Gold Skulltula crawls around on one of the second story windows.
Kill it and take it's token with the Boomerang.

facts.subject: Lon Lon Ranch paddock tree
facts.text: Rolling into the tree southwest of the paddock in Lon Lon Ranch causes a Gold Skulltula to fall from the branches.

evidence.quote:
Roll into the tree southwest of the paddock in Lon Lon Ranch.  The Gold
Skulltula will fall from the branches and land on the ground near you.

facts.subject: Lon Lon Ranch paddock awning
facts.text: Behind the paddock at Lon Lon Ranch, a Gold Skulltula crawls on the steel grating that makes up the back of the awning.

evidence.quote:
Run around to the back of the paddock, to where there is a steel grating which
makes up the back of the awning.  The Gold Skulltula crawls around it here.
You may need to backflip into the token to reach it.

facts.subject: Lon Lon Ranch mill wall
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is high on the wall to the east of the mill at Lon Lon Ranch.

evidence.quote:
The Gold Skulltula is high on the wall to the east of the mill.  Kill it and
take it's token with the Boomerang.

facts.subject: Kakariko Village entrance tree
facts.text: Rolling into the tree near the entrance to town causes a Gold Skulltula to fall from the branches above.

evidence.quote:
Roll into the tree near the entrance to town.  The Gold Skulltula falls from
the branches above and lands near you.

facts.subject: House of Skulltula window
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula hangs on a window on the backside of the House of Skulltula.

evidence.quote:
The Gold Skulltula hangs on a window on the backside of the House of Skulltula.
Run up to it and kill it to get it's token.

facts.subject: Unfinished House brick pile
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula rests on the second level of the pile of bricks in the Unfinished House.

evidence.quote:
The Gold Skulltula rests on the second level of the pile of bricks.  It's
easier if you kill it with the Slingshot instead of trying to climb up and kill
it with the sword.

facts.subject: Kakariko Village tower ladder
facts.text: High on the ladder leading to the top of the tower in the center of town, a Gold Skulltula can be killed with the Slingshot or Boomerang.

evidence.quote:
Look high on the ladder leading up to the top of the tower, and you'll see the
Gold Skulltula.  Kill it with the Slingshot or Boomerang before climbing up to
take it.

facts.subject: House near Death Mountain Trail Gate
facts.text: Behind a line of pots on the back of the house closest to Death Mountain Trail Gate lies a Gold Skulltula.

evidence.quote:
The Gold Skulltula lies on the back of the house closest to Death Mountain
Trail Gate, behind a line of pots.  Smash the pots to get at the Gold
Skulltula, then kill the spider to get it's token.

facts.subject: Impa's House south wall
facts.text: Using the Hookshot to pull onto Impa's House reveals a Gold Skulltula crawling around the south wall near the left corner.

evidence.quote:
Pull yourself on top of Impa's House using the Hookshot.  The Gold Skulltula
crawls around the south wall near the left corner of the house.

facts.subject: Kakariko Graveyard soft earth
facts.text: Dropping a Bottled Bug into the patch of soft earth in the northwest corner of the Graveyard reveals a Gold Skulltula.

evidence.quote:
Drop a Bottled Bug into the patch of soft earth in the northwest corner of the
Graveyard.  A Gold Skulltula will appear.  Kill it to get it's token.

facts.subject: Kakariko Graveyard southeast wall
facts.text: Using the Boomerang kills the Gold Skulltula on the southeast wall to the right of Composer Brothers' tombs.

evidence.quote:
Use the Boomerang to kill the Gold Skulltula on the southeast wall.  It's to
the right of Composer Brother's tombs.

facts.subject: Death Mountain Trail right wall alcove
facts.text: Using a bomb on the odd formation on the right wall around the first corner of Death Mountain Trail opens an alcove with a Gold Skulltula.

evidence.quote:
There is an odd formation on the wall to the right around the first corner.  Use a bomb to blow
it open.  On the inside is a Gold Skulltula.  Kill it with the Slingshot, then
climb up the inside wall (yes, it's climbable) to get the token.

facts.subject: Dodongo's Cavern entrance soft earth
facts.text: Dropping a Bottled Bug into the patch of soft earth outside Dodongo's Cavern reveals a Gold Skulltula.

evidence.quote:
Drop a Bottled Bug into the patch of soft earth outside Dodongo's Cavern.  Kill
the Gold Skulltula and take it's token after it appears.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #3 [GS064]
facts.text: Near the cliff above the entrance to Dodongo's Cavern on Death Mountain Trail, smash the red boulder with the Megaton Hammer to find a Gold Skulltula underneath.

evidence.quote:
Head for the red boulder, near the bomb flower that you used to blow open the
entrance to Dodongo's Cavern.  Smash the boulder with the Megaton Hammer.   The
Gold Skulltula is underneath it.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #4 [GS065]
facts.text: On the portion of Death Mountain Trail where burning rocks pelt Link, smash the last of the three boulders to reveal a Gold Skulltula underneath.

evidence.quote:
Smash the last of the three boulders on the way up the portion of Death
Mountain Trail where you are pelted with burning rocks.  The Gold Skulltula
lies underneath it.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #1 [GS023]
facts.text: Inside the Death Mountain Crater entrance at the top of Death Mountain Trail, smash into the two crates on the left to reveal a Gold Skulltula.

evidence.quote:
Use the entrance to Death Mountain Crater at the top of Death Mountain Trail.
As you enter, there are two crates to the left.  Smash into them.  One of them
contains the Gold Skulltula.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #2 [GS058]
facts.text: Warp to the lower half of Death Mountain Crater by playing the Bolero of Fire as Young Link, drop a Bottled Bug into the soft earth patch to the left, and defeat the Gold Skulltula that emerges.

evidence.quote:
As Young Link, play the Bolero of Fire to warp to the lower half of Death
Mountain Crater.  As you arrive, look to the left of the warp-in point to see a
patch of soft earth.  Drop a Bottled Bug into it, and kill the Gold Skulltula
that appears.

facts.subject: Boulder room
facts.text: From the entrance of Goron City, head left to a barrier of boulders, blow open a path with a bomb, and proceed through the tunnel behind and to the left.

evidence.quote:
Go to the left from the entrance until you reach a barrier of boulders.  Use a
bomb to blow open a path, and go through the tunnel behind and to the left of
the boulders.

facts.subject: Rock maze
facts.text: To navigate the rock maze in Goron City, destroy the brown rock on the right upon entering, destroy the brown rock behind it, walk through the gap, destroy the brown rock on the left, proceed right through the new opening, and destroy the brown stone directly ahead.

evidence.quote:
Destroy the brown rock to your right as
you enter the "rock maze," then the brown rock behind it.  Go through the gap
you have created, and destroy the brown rock on the left.  Go through the new
gap, and take a right.  Destroy the brown stone directly in front of you, and
