you will reach the end of the "maze."

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #1 [GS022]
facts.text: In the corner of the small enclosure at the end of the rock maze in Goron City, roll into the crate to reveal the Gold Skulltula.

evidence.quote: In the corner of this small enclosure,  there is a crate.  Roll into it to reveal the Gold Skulltula.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #2 [GS056]
facts.text: Stand on one of the ropes holding up the suspended central platform in Goron City to spot the Gold Skulltula on the back of the platform, then defeat it and retrieve its token with the Hookshot.

evidence.quote:
Head for one of the ropes that hold up the platform suspended above the middle
of the room.  Stand on the rope so that you can see the back of the platform,
where there is a Gold Skulltula visible.  Kill it and take it's token with the
Hookshot.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #1 [GS024]
facts.text: Roll into the tree located to the left of the stone wall near the entrance to Zora's River to knock down a Gold Skulltula.

evidence.quote:
Roll into the tree to the left of the stone wall near the entrance to Zora's
River.  A Gold Skulltula will fall from the tree and land near you.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #2 [GS025]
facts.text: Near the entrance to Zora's Domain, jump into the shallow river, shoot the Gold Skulltula on the ladder dipping into the water with the Slingshot, and climb the ladder to collect its token.

evidence.quote:
Head upstream to the entrance to Zora's Domain.  Near the bottom of the land
bridges, there is a ladder which dips down into the river.  The Gold Skulltula
sits on this ladder.  Jump down into the shallow part of the river, and shoot
the Skulltula with the Slingshot before climbing up the ladder to take it's
token.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #3 [GS066]
facts.text: Near where Link jumps across Zora's River for the second time, shoot the Gold Skulltula high on the south wall with the Longshot, or climb to the upper ledge if using the Hookshot.

evidence.quote:
Near the part of the river where you jump over it for the second time, there is
a Gold Skulltula high on the south wall.  You can shoot it from there with the
Longshot, but if you still have only the Hookshot then you'll have to climb up
to the upper ledge to reach it.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #4 [GS067]
facts.text: Just past the wooden bridge near the east side of Zora's River and around the corner, use the Hookshot to defeat the Gold Skulltula high on the northwest wall and collect its token.

evidence.quote:
Run to the end of the wooden bridge near the east side of Zora's River.  Just
past the wooden bridge and around the corner, the Gold Skulltula sits high on
the northwest wall.  Use the Hookshot to kill it and take it's token.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #1 [GS068]
facts.text: Climb to the top of the frozen waterfall using the tunnel on the left side of King Zora's throne room, walk to the edge, and use the Hookshot to defeat the Gold Skulltula on the left wall to get its token.

evidence.quote:
Climb up to the top of the frozen waterfall using the tunnel in the left side
of King Zora's throne room.  Edge to the edge of the waterfall, and look on the
wall on the left side to see the Gold Skulltula.  Use the Hookshot to kill it
and take it's token.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #1 [GS034]
facts.text: Climb onto the giant tree branch resting in the water in Zora's Fountain, defeat the Gold Skulltula on the wall to the west, and retrieve its token with the Boomerang.

evidence.quote:
Climb up onto the tree branch, and look on the wall to the west of the tree
branch to see the Gold Skulltula.  Kill it and use the Boomerang to get it's
token.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #2 [GS029]
facts.text: Roll into the single tree on the island in the southeast of Zora's Fountain to make a Gold Skulltula drop from its branches.

evidence.quote:
Roll into the single tree on the island in the southeast of the area.  The
Skulltula will fall from the branches, landing near you.

facts.subject: Gray Wolfos
facts.text: A Gray Wolfos can be killed in one shot by backflipping to dodge its attack when it moves close, then immediately landing and performing a Jump Attack while its back is turned.

evidence.quote: The easiest method to defeat the Gray Wolfos (or any Wolfos, for that matter) is to stand still, and wait for them to move in close.  Just as they attack, perform a back flip (Back + A while Z-Targeted) to dodge their attack, then immediately after you land perform a Jump Attack (press A while Z-targeted).  The Wolfos will briefly have his back turned to you, and the Jump Attack will kill it in one shot.

facts.subject: Sacred Forest Meadow Gate
facts.text: Defeating the Gray Wolfos causes the gate blocking the entrance to the Sacred Forest Meadow to disappear.

evidence.quote: When the Gray Wolfos dies, the gate blocking the entrance to the Sacred Forest Meadow will disappear, letting you in.

facts.subject: Saria's Song
facts.text: At the top of the stairs in a small overgrown courtyard, Saria teaches Link Saria's Song.

evidence.quote: At the top, you will find Saria sitting in a small, overgrown courtyard.  Saria will now teach you Saria's Song, which brings happiness to the depressed, and allows you to communicate telepathically with Saria at any time.

facts.subject: Fairy Fountain
facts.text: A Fairy Fountain is located in the pit in the middle of the upper cliffs area of the Sacred Forest Meadow.

evidence.quote: The pit in the middle of the upper cliffs area contains a Fairy Fountain if you need Life.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: Playing Saria's Song for the Skullkid standing on a small trunk in the Lost Woods rewards a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: Go left through the hollowed log, and jump onto the small trunk to interact with the Skullkid (and yes, this is the same Skullkid who unwittingly becomes the villain in Majora's Mask).  Play Saria's Song for the Scarecrow Kid, and he'll give you a Piece of Heart (which should get you another complete Heart Container).

facts.subject: Kakariko Village
facts.text: The entrance to Kakariko Village is in the northeast corner of Hyrule Field.

evidence.quote: We're now going to take Impa's advice and head for Kakariko Village, whose entrance is in the very northeast corner of Hyrule Field (1:00 on the  clock face).

facts.subject: Bottle
facts.text: Gathering all the Cuccos scattered around Kakariko Village and returning them to the Cucco Lady's pasture rewards a Bottle.

evidence.quote: The first order of business in Kakariko is to gather up all the Cuccos around town and deliver them to the Cucco Lady, who will give you a Bottle for your trouble.

facts.subject: Cucco #1
facts.text: A Cucco is found running near the archway at the front entrance of Kakariko Village.

evidence.quote: Run forward through the arch in front of the town, and immediately grab the Cucco (chicken) who is running around here.

facts.subject: Cucco #2
facts.text: A Cucco is located near the Cucco Lady's pasture, close to the arch leading to the Graveyard in the southeast corner of town.

evidence.quote: Grab the next Cucco very near the Cucco Lady's pasture, near the arch leading to the Graveyard in the southeast corner.

facts.subject: Cucco #3
facts.text: A Cucco is inside a crate near the center of town across from the stairs leading to the upper level.

evidence.quote: The next Cucco is in a crate near the center of town, across from the stairs leading to the upper level of Kakariko.

facts.subject: Cucco #4
facts.text: A Cucco is located on the north upper level of town near the gate leading to Death Mountain.

evidence.quote: The next Cucco is on the north side of town, on the upper level, near the gate that leads to Death Mountain.

facts.subject: Cucco #5
facts.text: To reach the Cucco trapped on a fenced ledge near the large tree, jump from the stairs of the partially constructed building toward the ledge while holding another Cucco to float over.

evidence.quote: To reach this Cucco, climb up the stairs to the partially constructed building, and jump off the edge towards the Cucco while holding another Cucco in your hands.  The Cucco will help you float out to the ledge.

facts.subject: Cucco #6
facts.text: A Cucco is found running in the small grotto behind the building reached by floating with a Cucco over the elevated fenced platform from the long stairset east of the pasture.

evidence.quote: Climb up the long stairset to the east of the Cucco Lady's pasture, and run straight to the edge, and aim yourself right at the elevated platform which is fenced off...grab another Cucco running around in the small grotto behind the building.

facts.subject: Cucco #7
facts.text: The final Cucco is found behind the Windmill at the top of the tall ladder in the small grotto.

evidence.quote: Drop back down into the grotto, then climb the tall ladder near where you found your most recent Cucco.  Climb it all the way to the top, and work your way around behind the Windmill.  Grab the last Cucco

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: Gliding with a Cucco from the narrow wooden beam onto the high balcony of Impa's House allows Link to enter a crack and collect a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: Run along the beam, and when you reach the corner where the beam bends to the right, leap off the edge and steer yourself right for the balcony...Throw aside the Cucco and enter the crack in the building...Take the Piece of Heart, then leave the way you came in.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula Token
facts.text: Releasing a bottled bug over the soft earth patch on the left side of Kakariko Graveyard causes a Gold Skulltula to emerge.

evidence.quote: Pass under the arch then follow the stone path to the left side of the graveyard, where there is a patch of soft earth.  Stand near the patch of soft earth, and release the bug you captured (which has magically become three separate bugs)...A few seconds later, a Gold Skulltula will appear.  Kill it and take it's token

facts.subject: Royal Family's Tomb
facts.text: Playing Zelda's Lullaby on the Triforce symbol in front of the largest tombstone in Kakariko Graveyard causes it to explode, revealing the pit to the Royal Family's Tomb.

evidence.quote: Stand on the large Triforce symbol burned into the grass in front of the tombstone, take out your Ocarina and play Zelda's Lullaby.  The tombstone will literally explode, revealing a pit.  Drop down the pit.

facts.subject: Bone Pit Door
facts.text: Killing all the Keese in the bone pit room unlocks the door at the top of the stairs in the Royal Family's Tomb.

evidence.quote: Run down the ramp and run in circles around the large bone pit to attract the attention of all the Keese in the room.  Pick them off with your Slingshot or with sword attacks.  Once they are all dead, the door at the top of the stairset will unlock.

facts.subject: Sun's Song
facts.text: Reading the inscription on the large tomb inside the Royal Family's Tomb teaches the Sun's Song, which turns day to night and night to day.

evidence.quote: Read the inscription on the tomb to discover the notes to the Sun's Song, which turns Night into Day and Day into Night.

facts.subject: Shield Grave
facts.text: Pulling back the front-row gravestone that has flowers behind it at nighttime reveals a pit leading to the Shield Grave.

evidence.quote: Head for the front row of gravestones, and stand behind the grave with the flowers behind it.  Grab a hold of it, and pull back to reveal a pit beneath the gravestone...Drop down the pit.

facts.subject: Poe
facts.text: Pulling aside other gravestones in Kakariko Graveyard reveals Poe enemies, who turn invisible when Z-targeted.

evidence.quote: Be careful pulling aside any other gravestones - they all contain Poe enemies, who become invisible when Z-Targeted.

facts.subject: Hylian Shield
facts.text: Opening the treasure chest inside the Shield Grave grants the Hylian Shield, which is impervious to flame attacks.

evidence.quote: Run forward and open the chest to find the Hylian Shield...switch the Hylian Shield, whose metal is impervious to flame attacks.

facts.subject: Sun's Song Rupee Trick
facts.text: Climbing the chains on the Hyrule Castle entrance gate in Hyrule Field and playing the Sun's Song causes the gate to retract, allowing Link to collect four invisible red rupees worth 80 rupees.

evidence.quote: Now that you have the Sun's Song, you also have access to a quick and easy 80 rupees.  If you return to the entrance to Hyrule Castle in Hyrule Field, then climb up the chains on the gate, then you can play the Sun's Song.  The gate will retract, letting you walk along the edge of the gate to claim four invisible red rupees.  This is known as the "Sun's Song Rupee Trick," and I will reference it a few times throughout the guide.

facts.subject: Secret pit near Great Fairy's Fountain
facts.text: Head for the silver rock near the entrance to the Great Fairy's Fountain, pick it up with the Silver Gauntlets, and destroy the boulder underneath with bombs to reveal a pit.

evidence.quote:
Head for the silver rock near the entrance to the Great Fairy's Fountain.  With
the Silver Gauntlets, pick up the rock and throw it aside.  There is another
boulder underneath.  Destroy it with bombs (sometimes this boulder is already
destroyed from when you open the Fairy Fountain) to reveal a pit.

facts.subject: Big Skulltula
facts.text: Inside the pit near the Great Fairy's Fountain, watch out for invisible Big Skulltulas on the ramp, and kill another Big Skulltula at the top of the ladder.

evidence.quote:
Drop down
the pit, and start heading up the ramp.  On the way, watch out for invisible
Big Skulltulas.  At the top of the ramp, climb up the ladder, and kill another
Big Skulltula at the top.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #3 [GS097]
facts.text: Gold Skulltula #3 [GS097] is on the wall to the left of the ladder at the top of the ramp inside the pit near the Great Fairy's Fountain.

evidence.quote:
Gold Skulltula #3 [GS097]...Drop down
the pit, and start heading up the ramp...The Gold Skulltula is on the wall to the left of the
ladder.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #1 [GS026]
facts.text: Dropping a Bottled Bug into the patch of soft earth behind the Observatory causes Gold Skulltula #1 [GS026] to emerge.

evidence.quote:
Gold Skulltula #1 [GS026]...Drop a Bottled Bug into the patch of soft earth behind the Observatory.  The
Gold Skulltula will emerge from the patch.  Kill it and take it's token.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #2 [GS035]
facts.text: Gold Skulltula #2 [GS035] is located on the wall behind the Observatory, where you can stand on the wooden plank bridge and use the Boomerang to kill it.

evidence.quote:
Gold Skulltula #2 [GS035]...Head around to the backside of the Observatory, where you are standing on the
wooden plank bridge suspended over the river from Gerudo Valley.  The Gold
Skulltula is on the wall on the back of the building.  Use the Boomerang to
kill it and take it's token.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #3 [GS027]
facts.text: Gold Skulltula #3 [GS027] appears on one of the two small posts on the small island in the southeast of Lake Hylia.

evidence.quote:
Gold Skulltula #3 [GS027]...Swim out to the small island in the southeast of the Lake.  It's to the east of
the large island.  The Gold Skulltula will appear on one of the two small posts
on the island.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #4 [GS078]
facts.text: Gold Skulltula #4 [GS078] is found on top of the trunk of the dead tree on the large island, reached by using the Longshot to pull yourself up.

evidence.quote:
Gold Skulltula #4 [GS078]...Use the Longshot to pull yourself up to the top of the tree.  Aim for the bit
of the trunk which sticks up over the large branch.  Once at the top, kill the
Gold Skulltula on top of the trunk, and use the Longshot to take it's token.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #5 [GS072]
facts.text: Equipping the Iron Boots to drop to the bottom of the pool in the Observatory and rolling into a crate reveals Gold Skulltula #5 [GS072].

evidence.quote:
Gold Skulltula #5 [GS072]...Equip the Iron Boots and drop to the bottom of the pool in the Observatory.  At
the bottom is a crate.  Roll into it, and it will shatter, revealing the game's
only underwater Gold Skulltula.  Kill it with the Longshot, then walk into the
token to take it.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #1 [GS037]
facts.text: Gold Skulltula #1 [GS037] can be seen above the waterfall to the right from halfway up the log bridge near the entrance from Hyrule Field.

evidence.quote:
Gold Skulltula #1 [GS037]...Head up the log bridge near the entrance from Hyrule Field.  Halfway up the
bridge, stop and look above the waterfall to the right to see the Gold
Skulltula.  Use the Boomerang to kill it and take it's token.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #2 [GS028]
facts.text: Dropping a Bottled Bug into the patch of soft earth on the west side of the narrow strip of earth near the river at the bottom of the canyon reveals Gold Skulltula #2 [GS028].

evidence.quote:
Gold Skulltula #2 [GS028]...Head for the narrow strip of earth near the river at the bottom of the canyon.
On the west side of the strip of earth, there is a patch of soft earth.  Drop a
Bottled Bug into it, and kill the Gold Skulltula that emerges to get it's
token.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #3 [GS087]
facts.text: Gold Skulltula #3 [GS087] is located on the wall behind the Carpenter's Tent and can be killed and collected with the Hookshot.

evidence.quote:
Gold Skulltula #3 [GS087]...Look on the wall behind the Carpenter's Tent to see the Gold Skulltula.  Kill
it and use the Hookshot to take the token.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #4 [GS088]
facts.text: Gold Skulltula #4 [GS088] is located on the inside of the stone arch across from the Carpenter's Tent to the left from the wooden bridge.

evidence.quote:
Gold Skulltula #4 [GS088]...Head for the stone arch across from the Carpenter's Tent, to the left from the
wooden bridge.  The Gold Skulltula is on the inside of the arch.  Kill it and
take it's token with the Hookshot.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #1 [GS089]
facts.text: Gold Skulltula #1 [GS089] is located on the wall between the gap of the two upper-most roofs on the top level of the Gerudo Fortress.

evidence.quote:
Gold Skulltula #1 [GS089]...Climb up to the top level of the Gerudo Fortress, to the gap between the two
upper-most roofs.  The Gold Skulltula is on the wall between this gap.  Kill it
and take it's token with the Hookshot.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #2 [GS090]
facts.text: Gold Skulltula #2 [GS090] is found on the lone target on the north side of the Horseback Archery Range.

evidence.quote:
Gold Skulltula #2 [GS090]...Head for the north end of the Horseback Archery Range.  Look on the lone target
on the north side to see the Gold Skulltula.  Kill it and take it's token with
the Hookshot.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #1 [GS091]
facts.text: Gold Skulltula #1 [GS091] rests on the opposite wall in the small room at the bottom of the pit inside the opening on the south side of the building.

evidence.quote:
Gold Skulltula #1 [GS091]...Enter the opening on the south side of the building, and drop down the pit
there.  In this small room, the Gold Skulltula rests on the opposite wall.
Kill it to get it's token.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #1 [GS092]
facts.text: Gold Skulltula #1 [GS092] is found halfway up the trunks of the Palm Trees near the dried-up Oasis.

evidence.quote:
Gold Skulltula #1 [GS092]...Look halfway up the trunks of the Palm Trees near the dried-up Oasis to find a
Gold Skulltula.  Kill it and take it's token with the Hookshot.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #2 [GS093]
facts.text: Dropping a Bottled Bug into the patch of soft earth near the entrance to the Spirit Temple reveals Gold Skulltula #2 [GS093].

evidence.quote:
Gold Skulltula #2 [GS093]...Drop a Bottled Bug into the patch of soft earth near the entrance to the Spirit
Temple, and then kill the Gold Skulltula that emerges.  Take it's token.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula at the Desert Colossus rests on the second rock passed while riding the Magic Leaf.

evidence.quote:
As Young Link, play the Requiem of Spirit to warp to the Desert Colossus.  Run
to the patch of soft earth near the entrance to the Spirit Temple, and plant
the Magic Bean.  Travel forward in time.  Back on Adult Link, return to the
Desert Colossus and ride the Magic Leaf.  The Magic Leaf will pass two rocks on
it's path; the Gold Skulltula rests on the second one.  Jump off as the Leaf
passes it.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula sits on the wall in the back of an alcove reached by jumping past the Big Skulltula from the second rising platform on the Deku Tree's top level.

evidence.quote:
Activate the three rising platforms, jump out to the second one, and then jump
to the left past the Big Skulltula.  The Gold Skulltula sits on the wall in the
back of the alcove.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula on the Deku Tree's first sub-level hangs on an ivy wall and can be killed with the Slingshot.

evidence.quote:
Drop down through the hole in the middle of the Deku Tree's main level.  When
you land, look on the ivy wall to see a Gold Skulltula.  Kill it with the
Slingshot, then climb up the Ivy Wall to get it.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula on the Deku Tree's first sub-level sits on the steel bars in the corner of the room.

evidence.quote:
Drop down through the hole in the middle of the Deku Tree's main level.  When
you land, look on the steel bars in the corner of the room to see a Gold
Skulltula.  Kill it with the Sling, then jump from the ledge to the steel bars.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is in a side room behind a bombable wall reached through a crawlspace from the upper area of the first sub-level, requiring the Boomerang to collect its token.

evidence.quote:
Drop down through the hole in the middle of the Deku Tree's main level, then
jump up to the upper area of the room.  Crawl through the small crawlspace,
then run to the bombable wall in the back of this room.  Go through the door on
the other side.  Kill the Gold Skulltula in this room, and take it's token with
the Boomerang.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula in Dodongo's Cavern is in a room behind a sealed wall in the first hallway from the main chamber, which can be opened by detonating a Baby Dodongo next to it.

evidence.quote:
In the first hallway that you reach from the Dodongo's Cavern main chamber, you
will be in a hall where Baby Dodongos erupt from the floor.  Run halfway down
the hall to find a sealed wall.  Kill a Baby Dodongo so that it dies near the
wall, and it will explode, opening the sealed wall.  Go through the door on the
other side.  The Gold Skulltula is in this room.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: In Dodongo's Cavern, a Gold Skulltula is found on the ivy at the top of the ramp on the second level of the collapsing staircase room.

evidence.quote:
In the room where you must use the ring of Bomb Flowers to lower the staircase,
head for the second level and kill the Gold Skulltula on the ivy at the top of
the ramp with the Slingshot.  Climb up the ivy to claim it's token.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: In Dodongo's Cavern, a Gold Skulltula rests behind an Armos Knight in a room behind a sealed wall on the other side of the Dodongo's Heads.

evidence.quote:
Head for the room with the multiple levels on the other side of the Dodongo's
Heads.  Near the back of the room, there is a sealed wall.  Blow open the wall
with a Bomb, and go through the door on the other side.  The Gold Skulltula
rests behind an Armos Knight.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: In Dodongo's Cavern, a Gold Skulltula is inside an alcove on the upper level of the collapsing stairwell room, reached by riding the main chamber elevator and backtracking through the dungeon.

evidence.quote:
To access this Gold Skulltula, you have to activate the elevator in the main
Dodongo's Chamber on a previous visit, then leave the dungeon and re-enter it.
Ride this elevator to the second level of Dodongo's Cavern, then go backwards
through the dungeon to the upper level of the collapsing stairwell room.  In
this fashion, you can reach the top of this room without making the stairs
collapse using the Bomb Flowers.

Climb up to the top of the stairs using the Ivy on the walls, and enter the
alcove.  Kill the Gold Skulltula and take it's token with the Boomerang.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: As Adult Link in Dodongo's Cavern, a Gold Skulltula is located in an alcove in the southeast hall, reached by summoning the Scarecrow and Hookshotting to it.

evidence.quote:
Head for the southeast hall where you first encountered the Baby Dodongos.
Head into the room until Navi flutters up towards the ceiling, then play the
Scarecrow's Song.  Pull yourself up to the Scarecrow with the Hookshot, and
kill the Gold Skulltula in the alcove.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: In Inside Jabu-Jabu's Belly, a Gold Skulltula hangs on an ivy wall in the lower-level room containing the water switch.

evidence.quote:
Head for the room in the lower level of Jabu-Jabu's Belly, which contains the
pit with the water level that can be raised with the switch.  Kill the Gold
Skulltula on the ivy wall in the middle of the room using the Slingshot, then
fill the water level in the room by stepping on the switch.  Climb up to the
ivy wall and take the Skulltula Token.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: In Inside Jabu-Jabu's Belly, a Gold Skulltula hangs on the wall to the right after dropping through the hole formerly blocked by a Green Tentacle.

evidence.quote:
Look on the wall to the right as you land from the room above.  The Gold
Skulltula hangs on the wall.  Kill it and take it's token with the Boomerang.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: In Inside Jabu-Jabu's Belly, a Gold Skulltula hangs on the wall to the left after dropping through the hole formerly blocked by a Green Tentacle.

evidence.quote:
Look on the wall to the left as you land from the room above.  The Gold
Skulltulla hangs on the wall.  Kill it and take it's token with the Boomerang.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: In Inside Jabu-Jabu's Belly, a Gold Skulltula hangs halfway up the left side of the tall ivy wall in the room immediately before Barinade.

evidence.quote:
Look on the left side of the tall ivy wall in the room immediately before the
Barinade boss fight.  The Gold Skulltula hangs halfway up the ivy wall.  Either
kill it with the Slingshot, then climb up and grab it's token, or else kill it
with the Boomerang and use the Boomerang to take it's token.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula token
facts.text: In the Forest Temple, a Gold Skulltula token is located on the top right of the ivy wall in the very first room and requires the Hookshot.

evidence.quote: Found: On the top and far-right of the ivy wall in very first room...Kill it and take it's token with the Hookshot.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula token
facts.text: In the Forest Temple, a Gold Skulltula token is located to the right of the northern door in the large chamber with four torches and requires the Hookshot.

evidence.quote: Found: To the right of the northern door in large chamber with four torches...Kill it and take the token with the Hookshot.

facts.subject: Poe Sisters
facts.text: In the Forest Temple, the Poe Sisters appear in the large torch chamber and steal the flames from the torches.

evidence.quote:
Enter the room where the Poe Sisters appear and steal the flames from the
torches.

facts.subject: Northeast courtyard
facts.text: In the Forest Temple northeast courtyard, a chest sits on the high ledge surrounded by a pool of water.

evidence.quote:
Head for the northeast courtyard; it's the courtyard with the Big Deku Baba,
two Octoroks and a high ledge surrounded by a pool of water.  Look on the high
ledge to see a chest.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula token
facts.text: In the Forest Temple, a Gold Skulltula token is located around the corner from the chest on the upper ledge in the northeast courtyard.

evidence.quote:
Found: On upper ledge in northeast courtyard...Pull yourself up to it with the Hookshot, then look on
the wall around the corner from the chest to see the Gold Skulltula.  Kill it
and take the token with the Hookshot.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula token
facts.text: In the Forest Temple, a Gold Skulltula token is located high on the wall past the broken pillars in the northwest courtyard, reached from the falling ceiling room.

evidence.quote:
Found: On wall in northwest courtyard...You have to use the upper entrance to the courtyard from the falling ceiling
room to reach this Skulltula....Jump out along these pillars, and at the other end of the pillars
look high on the wall to see a Gold Skulltula.  Kill it and take it's token
with the Hookshot.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula token
facts.text: In the Forest Temple, a Gold Skulltula token is located in a small room in the area with the spinning walls and requires the Hookshot.

evidence.quote:
Found: In a small room in the area with the spinning walls
Requires: Hookshot...Find the small room with the Gold Skulltula in it, and use the Hookshot to kill
it and take it's token.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula token
facts.text: In the Fire Temple, a Gold Skulltula token is located in a small room reached by playing the Song of Time to lower a Block of Time in the large fire cavern.

evidence.quote:
Found: In small room reached by the Block of Time in the large fire cavern
Requires: Song of Time...Head for the left side of the room, play the Song of Time to
make the Block of Time come down.  Climb onto the Block of Time and enter the
room.  Destroy the flying floor panels and the Like-Like, and then get the Gold
Skulltula from the rear wall.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula token
facts.text: In the Fire Temple, a Gold Skulltula token is located behind a bombable wall on the east side of the rolling boulder maze on the second level.

evidence.quote:
Found: In rolling boulder maze, behind bombable wall on east side of the room
Requires: Bombs...Head for the rolling boulder maze on the second level of the Fire Temple, and
go to the east side of the maze.  Find the bombable wall by attacking the walls
until they make an odd noise.  Destroy the wall with a bomb, and take the Gold
Skulltula from the other side.

facts.subject: Bombable wall
facts.text: In the Fire Temple rolling boulder maze, the bombable wall can be found by attacking walls until they make an odd noise.

evidence.quote:
Find the bombable wall by attacking the walls
until they make an odd noise.  Destroy the wall with a bomb, and take the Gold
Skulltula from the other side.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula token
facts.text: In the Fire Temple, a Gold Skulltula token sits on a wire wall on the second level of the room above the rolling boulder maze, accessible via Pierre and the Hookshot.

evidence.quote:
Found: In area above rolling boulder maze, accessible only with the
       Scarecrow's Song
Requires: Hookshot; Scarecrow's Song...The Gold Skulltula sits on a wire wall on the second level
of the next room.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula token
facts.text: In the Fire Temple, a Gold Skulltula token is found through the door at the top of the room past the upper level of the rolling boulder maze.

evidence.quote:
Found: In room past the upper level of the rolling boulder maze, accessible
       only with the Scarecrow's Song
Requires: Hookshot; Scarecrow's Song...Climb to the top of this room and through the door at the
top.  Kill the Gold Skulltula through the door on the other side.

facts.subject: Pierre
facts.text: Playing the Scarecrow's Song on the upper level of the Fire Temple rolling boulder maze makes Pierre appear on a small platform near the entrance.

evidence.quote:
Play the Scarecrow's Song to
make Pierre appear on that platform, and Hookshot yourself up to him.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula token
facts.text: In the Fire Temple, a Gold Skulltula token is located on the rear wall of a room with Like-Likes and flying tiles past the totem pole in the entrance room.

evidence.quote:
Found: In a room past the door behind the totem pole in the first room.
Requires: Megaton Hammer...Go through that door, to find another room with Like-Likes
and more flying tiles.  Kill them all, and then get the Gold Skulltula from the
rear wall.

facts.subject: Totem pole
facts.text: In the entrance to the Fire Temple, the Megaton Hammer must be used on the totem pole to access the door on the other side.

evidence.quote:
Use the Megaton Hammer on the totem pole in the entrance to the Fire Temple,
and go through the door on the other side.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula token
facts.text: In the Ice Cavern, a Gold Skulltula token is located on the left wall as Link enters from the southern door of the giant spinning scythe room.

evidence.quote:
Found: On the south wall in the room with giant spinning scythe.
Requires: Hookshot...The Gold Skulltula is on the
left wall as you enter from the southern door.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula token
facts.text: In the Ice Cavern, a Gold Skulltula token is located in the northern alcove of the small room east of the spinning scythe room, behind a red-colored wall.

evidence.quote:
Found: In small room to the east of the giant spinning scythe room
Requires: Hookshot; Blue Flame...Use a bottle of Blue Fire to melt the red-colored wall on the east side of the
spinning scythe room.  Run east into the next room, and look for the Gold
Skulltula in the northern alcove.  Use the Hookshot to kill it and take it's
token.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula token
facts.text: In the Ice Cavern, a Gold Skulltula token is located above the pit to the left upon entering the sliding block puzzle room west of the spinning scythe room.

evidence.quote:
Found: In sliding block puzzle room, above a pit
Requires: Hookshot; Blue Flame...Use a bottle of Blue Fire to melt the red-colored wall on the west side of the
spinning scythe room.  Run west into the sliding block puzzle room, and look
for the Gold Skulltula above the pit to the left as you enter the room.  Use
the Hookshot to kill it and take it's token.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #1 [GS073]
facts.text: Gold Skulltula #1 [GS073] is found in the southern tunnel from the bottom level of the central chamber with the tower, requiring Iron Boots.

evidence.quote:
Gold Skulltula #1 [GS073]
Found: In southern tunnel, from the bottom level of the central chamber with
the
       tower
Requires: Iron Boots

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #1 [GS073]
facts.text: Head down the southern tunnel on the bottom level of the central chamber to the grating, and use a Super Spin Attack to activate the crystal switch on the other side to reach the Gold Skulltula.

evidence.quote:
Head down the southern tunnel on the bottom level of the central chamber.  Head
towards the end of the tunnel, and when you reach the grating, use a Super Spin
Attack to activate the crystal switch on the other side.  The Gold Skulltula is
on the other side of the grating.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #2 [GS074]
facts.text: Gold Skulltula #2 [GS074] is found in the river rapids room on the wall after the second turn, requiring Iron Boots and Longshot.

evidence.quote:
Gold Skulltula #2 [GS074]
Found: In the river rapids room, on wall after second turn
Requires: Iron Boots; Longshot

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #2 [GS074]
facts.text: Head downstream, equip the Iron Boots after the second corner, and kill the Gold Skulltula on the wall near the corner to take the token with the Longshot.

evidence.quote:
Head down stream, and after the second corner equip the Iron Boots and use the
Longshot to kill the Gold Skulltula from the wall near the corner.  Take the
token with the Longshot.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #3 [GS075]
facts.text: Gold Skulltula #3 [GS075] is found at the very top of the central tower, requiring the Longshot.

evidence.quote:
Gold Skulltula #3 [GS075]
Found: In the central tower, at very top of the tower
Requires: Longshot

facts.subject: Central Tower Door
facts.text: Light the unlit torch on the second level of the tower using a Fire Arrow or by shooting an arrow through the nearby lit torch to unseal the door to the tower.

evidence.quote:
Light the unlit torch on the second level of the tower using either a Fire
Arrow, or by shooting an arrow through the nearby lit torch and into the unlit
torch.  The door to the tower will unseal itself.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #3 [GS075]
facts.text: Go through the unsealed door, look on the ceiling above to spot the Gold Skulltula, then kill it and take its token with the Longshot.

evidence.quote:
Go through it, and look on
the ceiling above to see the Gold Skulltula.  Kill it and take it's token with
the Longshot.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #4 [GS076]
facts.text: Gold Skulltula #4 [GS076] is found in the room with the waterfall and rising Longshot targets, requiring the Longshot.

evidence.quote:
Gold Skulltula #4 [GS076]
Found: In the room with the waterfall and rising Longshot targets
Requires: Longshot

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #4 [GS076]
facts.text: From the central room, go to the top level and through the west door, look on the right wall to find the Gold Skulltula, and use the Longshot to kill it and collect its token.

evidence.quote:
From the central room, go to the top level and go through the west door.  Look
on the right wall as you enter the room to see the Gold Skulltula.  Use the
Longshot to kill it and take it's token.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #5 [GS077]
facts.text: Gold Skulltula #5 [GS077] is located behind the waterfall in the tunnel immediately before the Boss Key, requiring the Longshot.

evidence.quote:
Gold Skulltula #5 [GS077]
Found: Behind waterfall in tunnel immediately before the Boss Key
Requires: Longshot

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #5 [GS077]
facts.text: Kill the Gold Skulltula behind the waterfall with the Longshot, then retrieve its token with the Longshot.

evidence.quote:
Kill the Gold Skulltula behind the waterfall using the Longshot, then take it's
token with the Longshot.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #1 [GS080]
facts.text: Gold Skulltula #1 [GS080] is found behind the locked door in the left side of the center area, requiring a Small Key and Boomerang.

evidence.quote:
Gold Skulltula #1 [GS080]
Found: Behind the locked door in the left side of the center area.
Requires: Small Key; Boomerang

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #1 [GS080]
facts.text: Use one of the dungeon's three keys to open the locked door, watch out for flying pots and Fire Keese, kill the Gold Skulltula in the room, and take its token with the Boomerang.

evidence.quote:
Use one of the three keys in the dungeon to open the locked door.  Kill the
Gold Skulltula in the room, and watch out for flying pots and fire keese.  Take
the token with the Boomerang.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #2 [GS079]
facts.text: Gold Skulltula #2 [GS079] is found behind the locked door in the right side of the center area, requiring a Small Key, Boomerang, and optionally the Lens of Truth.

evidence.quote:
Gold Skulltula #2 [GS079]
Found: Behind the locked door in the right side of the center area.
Requires: Small Key; Boomerang; Lens of Truth Optional

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #2 [GS079]
facts.text: Use one of the three dungeon keys to open the locked door, use the Lens of Truth to see the invisible platforms over the pit in the room's center, and kill the Gold Skulltula on the other side to take its token with the Boomerang.

evidence.quote:
Use one of the three keys in the dungeon to open the locked door.  Use the Lens
of Truth to see the invisible platforms that extend over the pit in the middle
of the room.  On the other side of the platforms, kill the Gold Skulltula and
take it's token with the Boomerang.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #3 [GS081]
facts.text: Gold Skulltula #3 [GS081] is located behind the locked door in the northwest corner of the dungeon, requiring a Small Key and Lens of Truth.

evidence.quote:
Gold Skulltula #3 [GS081]
Found: Behind the locked door in the northwest corner of the dungeon.
Requires: Small Key; Lens of Truth

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #3 [GS081]
facts.text: Go through the northwest crawlspace in the main area, unlock the door, use the Lens of Truth to avoid pits while watching for Fire Keese and the Beamos, then enter the next door to defeat the Like-Like, kill the Gold Skulltula, and retrieve its token.

evidence.quote:
Go through the crawlspace in the northwest corner of the main area of the
dungeon.  On the other side, go through the locked door on the other side, and
use the Lens of Truth to safely traverse the next room and avoid the pits.
Watch out for Fire Keese and the Beamos.  Go through the door on the other side
of the room, kill the Like-Like, then kill the Gold Skulltula and take it's
token.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #1 [GS082]
facts.text: Gold Skulltula #1 [GS082] is found in the first room with the invisible spinning scythes, requiring the Hookshot or Longshot and optionally the Lens of Truth.

evidence.quote:
Gold Skulltula #1 [GS082]
Found: In the first room with the invisible spinning scythes
Requires: Hookshot OR Longshot; Lens of Truth Optional

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #1 [GS082]
facts.text: Kill all enemies in the room while dodging the invisible scythes to retract the grating, then kill the Gold Skulltula on the wall behind it and take its token with the Hookshot or Longshot.

evidence.quote:
Kill all of the enemies in the room while dodging the invisible scythes, and
the grating in the room will retract.  Go behind the grating, and kill the Gold
Skulltula on the wall.  Take it's token with the Hookshot/Longshot.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #2 [GS083]
facts.text: Gold Skulltula #2 [GS083] is found in the room with the crushing ceilings and requires nothing.

evidence.quote:
Gold Skulltula #2 [GS083]
Found: In the room with the crushing ceilings
Requires: Nothing

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #2 [GS083]
facts.text: Use the hidden stone block to block the crushing ceilings, enter the cell hiding the Gold Skulltula, kill it, and collect its token.

evidence.quote:
Use the stone block hidden in the room to block the crushing ceilings.  The
Gold Skulltula is hidden in one of the cells in the room.  Enter the cell, kill
the Skulltula and take it's token.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #3 [GS084]
facts.text: Gold Skulltula #3 [GS084] is found behind the flaming skull in the room with the single flaming skull, requiring the Hookshot or Longshot.

evidence.quote:
Gold Skulltula #3 [GS084]
Found: Behind the flaming skull in the room with the single flaming skull
Requires: Hookshot OR Longshot

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #3 [GS084]
facts.text: In the room with the single flaming skull, kill the Gold Skulltula on the wall behind the skull and take its token using the Hookshot or Longshot.

evidence.quote:
Find the room with the SINGLE flaming skull.  The Gold Skulltula is on the wall
behind the flaming skull.  Use the Hookshot/Longshot to kill it and take it's
token.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #4 [GS085]
facts.text: Gold Skulltula #4 [GS085] is found in a high-up alcove in the room with the ship, requiring the Longshot and optionally Scarecrow's Song.

evidence.quote:
Gold Skulltula #4 [GS085]
Found: In a high-up alcove in the room with the ship
Requires: Longshot; Scarecrow's Song Optional

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #4 [GS085]
facts.text: Climb up to the front of the ship to shoot the Gold Skulltula in the high alcove with the Longshot to take its token, or play the Scarecrow's Song to pull over to the alcove.

evidence.quote:
Head for the room with the ship, and climb up to the front of the ship.  From
here, you can aim for the alcove high up in the room.  You can shoot the Gold
Skulltula from here with the Longshot, and take it's token.  If you like, you
can also use the Scarecrow's Song to pull yourself over to the alcove.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #5 [GS086]
facts.text: Gold Skulltula #5 [GS086] is found behind the trio of flaming skulls in the room with three flaming skulls, requiring the Hookshot or Longshot.

evidence.quote:
Gold Skulltula #5 [GS086]
Found: Behind the trio of flaming skulls in the room with the trio of flaming
skulls
Requires: Hookshot OR Longshot

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #5 [GS086]
facts.text: In the room near the end of the dungeon with three flaming skulls, kill the Gold Skulltula on the wall behind them and collect its token using the Hookshot or Longshot.

evidence.quote:
Find the room near the end of the dungeon with THREE flaming skulls.  The Gold
Skulltula is on the wall behind the trio of flaming skulls.  Use the
Hookshot/Longshot to kill it and take it's token.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #1 [GS094]
facts.text: As Young Link in the Spirit Temple, solve the Silver Rupee puzzle in the two-sided room, cross the fallen bridge, and use the Boomerang to kill the Gold Skulltula on the wire wall and collect its token.

evidence.quote: Solve the Silver Rupee Puzzle, and when the bridge in the middle of the room falls, cross it and use the Boomerang to kill the Gold Skulltula and take it's token.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #2 [GS095]
facts.text: As Young Link in the Spirit Temple room with two Lizalfos and a sun panel on the floor, climb to the top of the tiled wall, turn around, and use the Boomerang to kill the Gold Skulltula on the wall and retrieve its token.

evidence.quote: In the room with the pair of Lizalfos and the sun panel on the floor, climb to the top of the tiled wall and turn around at the top.  The Gold Skulltula is here, just behind you and on the wall.  Kill it and take it's token with the Boomerang.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #3 [GS096]
facts.text: As Young Link in the Spirit Temple, enter the stairwell immediately before the Iron Knuckle room to find a Gold Skulltula above the south door, then kill it and collect its token using the Boomerang.

evidence.quote: Enter the stairwell immediately before the room where Young Link fights the Iron Knuckle.  The Gold Skulltula is above the door on the south side of the room.  Kill it and use the Boomerang to take it's token.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #4 [GS099]
facts.text: As Adult Link in the Spirit Temple rolling boulder room with a Silver Rupee puzzle, play the Song of Time to move the Block of Time covering an alcove on the left side to reveal a Gold Skulltula.

evidence.quote: Find the room with the rolling boulders and a Silver Rupee puzzle.  On the left side of the room, there is an alcove covered up by a Block of Time.  Move the Block with the Song of Time, to find the Gold Skulltula behind it.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula #5 [GS100]
facts.text: As Adult Link on the top level of the west side of the Spirit Temple Colossus room, play the Scarecrow's Song to summon Pierre to the opposite ledge, pull yourself across using the Hookshot or Longshot, and find the Gold Skulltula behind him.

evidence.quote: Go to the top level of the west side of the room, and play the Scarecrow's Song to make Pierre appear on the opposite ledge.  Pull yourself over to the ledge with the Hookshot or Longshot.  The Gold Skulltula is behind Pierre on this ledge.

facts.subject: Shooting Gallery (Young Link)
facts.text: To win the Big Bullet Bag at the Young Link Shooting Gallery, you must shoot every rupee that appears without missing; missing two or less allows a free retry, while missing more requires paying to play again.

evidence.quote: To win the Big Bullet Bag, you have to shoot every rupee that appears without missing a single one.  If you miss two or less, then the clerk will let you try again for free.  If you miss more then two, you have to pay to play again.

facts.subject: Shooting Gallery (Young Link)
facts.text: During the first run through the Young Link Shooting Gallery, rupees appear in a preset order: in the middle, from the left then right, jumping from the middle, from both left and right, two from the right going left, and two from the left going right.

evidence.quote: For this first run through the Shooting Gallery, the rupees appear in a preset order.  The order is:...1.)  In the middle...2.)  From the left, then from the right...3.)  Jumps from the middle...4.)  From the left AND right...5.)  Two rupees coming from the right, going left...6.)  Two rupees coming from the left, going right

facts.subject: Shooting Gallery (Young Link)
facts.text: Successfully shooting all targets in the Young Link Shooting Gallery awards the Bullet Bag x40, which increases the ammo capacity of your Slingshot by 10.

evidence.quote: Keep playing the minigame until you successfully shoot all of the targets, and the clerk will award you with the Bullet Bag x40, which increases the ammo capacity of your Slingshot by 10.

facts.subject: Shooting Gallery (Young Link)
facts.text: If you run out of rupees while attempting the Shooting Gallery minigame, return to the Hyrule Castle Gatehouse and smash pots to replenish your supplies.

evidence.quote: If you run out of rupees trying to complete the game, then return to the Hyrule Castle Gatehouse and smash the pots to replenish your supplies.

facts.subject: Shooting Gallery (Adult Link)
facts.text: Hitting all targets in one attempt at the Adult Link Shooting Gallery rewards Link with his first Quiver upgrade.

evidence.quote: Keep playing the game until you nail all of the targets in one go, and the clerk will reward you with the first Quiver upgrade.

facts.subject: Shooting Gallery (Adult Link)
facts.text: In the Adult Link Shooting Gallery, if a single blue rupee appears from the left, the next one will always come from the right, and memorizing the target patterns allows you to predict subsequent targets.

evidence.quote: Note number 2: if a single blue rupee comes from the left, then the next one will ALWAYS come from the right, despite the randomness of the rest of it.  Keep this in mind.  Also, if you memorize the patterns that the targets appear in, then you can predict what will appear next, and you can always tell what the last pattern will be by simply looking at what has already appeared.

facts.subject: Horseback Archery Range
facts.text: At the Gerudo Archery Range, you receive twenty arrows to use and must score at least 1,000 points to win a Piece of Heart, with pots worth 100 points each and targets worth up to 100 points in the exact middle.

evidence.quote: You get twenty arrows to use, and in order to win the Piece of Heart from this game you must score at least 1,000 points.  There are huge wooden targets set up along the course as well pots that appear on the way.  Shoot the pots for 100 points each, and the targets are worth varying amounts depending upon how close to the center you are (the exact middle of the target is worth 100 points).

facts.subject: Horseback Archery Range
facts.text: Epona automatically runs up and down the course once in each direction, so focus on hitting the pots and the far north target on the first pass, then shoot the east targets and south target on the second pass.

evidence.quote: Epona will automatically run up and down the course (you get one pass in each direction before the game ends).  On your first pass, focus on hitting the pots as you pass by them.  Once you nail all the pots, focus on the target on the far north side of the course.  On your second pass, shoot for the targets on the east side of the course until you get near enough to accurately hit the target on the south side of the course.

facts.subject: Horseback Archery Range
facts.text: Scoring at least 1,500 points on a subsequent attempt at the Horseback Archery minigame awards the Quiver upgrade.

evidence.quote: Play the game again and score at least 1,500 to earn the Quiver.  If you score 1,500 or more on your first attempt, then you have to play again to earn the Quiver and repeat the feat.

facts.subject: Bombchu Bowling Alley
facts.text: In Bombchu Bowling, the goal is to send a Bombchu into the hole on the opposite end across three progressively difficult course goals to win the displayed prize.

evidence.quote: The object of Bombchu Bowling is to send the Bombchu (a mobile bomb) into the hole on the opposite end of the course.  The course has three different goals to obtain, each one becoming progressively more difficult.  Completing all three goals successfully will win you whatever prize the clerk showed you at the start.

facts.subject: Bombchu Bowling Alley
facts.text: The first Bombchu Bowling goal has a center target guarded by a Blade Trap, the second level target can be top, left, or right with a moving small Cucco, and the last goal is in the exact center guarded by a Fat Cucco.

evidence.quote: For the first goal, the target is always in the center of the field.  Simply stand in the exact middle of the field (slightly to the right of the center arrow is the exact middle of the field) and time it so your Bombchu avoids the Blade Trap.  The next level of the field can be on the top, left, or right, and adds a small Cucco to dodge...The last goal is always in the exact center, and adds a Fat Cucco who always stands roughly in the center of the field (but you can sneak a Bombchu by it if you're careful).

facts.subject: Bombchu Bowling Alley
facts.text: Always position yourself in the center of the field during Bombchu Bowling except when the second round target is on the right, and if the hole is on the left, angle the Bombchu along the floor then the wall into the hole.

evidence.quote: When you're playing Bombchu Bowling, always position yourself in the center of the field.  The one exception is when the target appears on the right in the second round; you have to minorly adjust your position to the left or right, otherwise it's impossible to angle yourself properly for the Bombchu to enter the target.  If the hole appears on the left side of the field, then adjust your angle so that the Bombchu goes along the floor, then the wall, then into the hole.

facts.subject: Diving Minigame
facts.text: In the Diving Minigame, position yourself above the rupees thrown off the waterfall and hold down A as you dive down to grab them.

evidence.quote: The Zora will throw a handful of rupees off the waterfall, which you need to dive down and grab.  Simply position yourself above the rupees, and hold down A as you dive down to grab them.

facts.subject: Zora
facts.text: Once you grab all the rupees from around the waterfall in the Diving Minigame, return to the Zora to receive the Silver Scale, which doubles diving depth.

evidence.quote: Once you have grabbed all of the rupees from around the waterfall, the Zora will call down for you to return to him and he'll give you a reward.  He'll give you the Silver Scale, which doubles how deep you can go in a single dive.

facts.subject: Fishing Pond
facts.text: At the Fishing Pond, Z-Target a fish, hit B to cast, use B, A, and the joystick to attract fish, then hold down A and pull back on the control stick to reel in.

evidence.quote: Z-Target a fish, then hit B to cast.  Use the B button, the A button and the joystick to play with the lure and attract fish to the fly.  The biggest fish are found near the submerged log on the left side of the pond and the reeds on the right.  Once a fish is on the line, hold down A and pull backwards on the control stick to reel the fish in.

facts.subject: Fishing Pond
facts.text: The biggest fish at the Fishing Pond are located near the submerged log on the left side of the pond and the reeds on the right.

evidence.quote: The biggest fish are found near the submerged log on the left side of the pond and the reeds on the right.

facts.subject: Bigocto
facts.text: Bigocto is vulnerable to the Boomerang, which stuns him and locks him in place, exposing his weakpoint green eye on his backside.

evidence.quote: His weakpoint is a large green "eye" on his backside.  The Bigocto is vulnerable to the Boomerang - it stuns him and locks him in place.

facts.subject: Bigocto
facts.text: Two Jump Attacks to Bigocto's green eye on his backside will defeat him.

evidence.quote: Once you have reached his backside, stun him with the Boomerang, and use a Jump Attack to damage his green eye.  Two Jump Attacks will defeat the Bigocto.

facts.subject: Bigocto
facts.text: Letting Bigocto run into you causes him to turn around, allowing you to stun and attack his backside quickly.

evidence.quote: Another alternative is to simply let him run into you.  He will then turn around, letting you stun him and attack him.  This is less glamorous and sloppier, but works much more quickly and easily.

facts.subject: Amy Poe
facts.text: The real Amy does a spin when splitting into four versions; shoot the spinning Amy with an arrow to force another split and repeat.

evidence.quote: The real Amy does a little spin when she first splits up.  Shoot this Amy with an arrow, and she will split into four new Amys.  Wait for the real Amy to spin, and shoot her again.

facts.subject: Flare Dancer
facts.text: Separate the Flare Dancer's heart from its flaming body using the Hookshot, then intercept the running heart and damage it with a jump attack.

evidence.quote: To damage the Flare Dancer, the first thing you must do is separate it's heart from it's flaming body using the Hookshot.  Once this is done, the heart will literally begin running around the room very quickly.  Begin circling the room in the opposite direction so that you intercept it halfway around the room, and use a jump attack to deal damage to it (use a regular strike if you have difficulty timing the jump attack).

facts.subject: Flare Dancer
facts.text: Using the Biggoron Sword on the Flare Dancer results in a faster victory.

evidence.quote: If you have the Biggoron Sword, then use it for a faster victory.

facts.subject: Shadow Link
facts.text: Shadow Link cannot deflect the Megaton Hammer, making smacking him with it an easy victory.

evidence.quote: This means using the Megaton Hammer.  He can't deflect the Megaton Hammer.  He won't even try.  Just smack him around with it until he dies.

facts.subject: Shadow Link
facts.text: Do not perform a stab attack against Shadow Link, and avoid Z-Targeting if using regular sword attacks.

evidence.quote: The first thing to know when fighting Shadow Link: do not perform a Stab attack (forward + attack while Z-targeted)... If you're a combat purist and refuse to use such an easy tactic, then the second-best way to beat him is to use regular sword attacks, but don't Z-Target him.

facts.subject: Deadhand
facts.text: Allow a hand to grab you to make Deadhand appear, struggle free by rotating the stick and pressing buttons, then hit his lowered head with a Jump Attack.

evidence.quote: Allow one of his hands to grab you, and Deadhand's body and head will appear and move slowly towards you.  Struggle free of the hand holding you by rotating the control stick and slamming buttons, then Z-Target Deadhand's head.  Stand still (out of the range of the hands), and wait for Deadhand to get near you, at which point his head will lower to attack.  Execute a Jump Attack before Deadhand can attack, and he will begin to run away, eventually sinking back into the ground.

facts.subject: Iron Knuckle
facts.text: Iron Knuckles can be defeated quickly by casting Nayru's Love and attacking while invulnerable.

evidence.quote: Or the easier, faster method is to just use Nayru's Love and go kamikaze while you are invulnerable.

facts.subject: Iron Knuckle
facts.text: As Adult Link, wait for the Iron Knuckle to attack, backflip out of range, land with a Jump Attack, and immediately backflip away again.

evidence.quote: First, wait for the Iron Knuckle to attack, then backflip out of the attack's range.  As soon as you land, use a Jump Attack, and then immediately backflip out of the range of the Knuckle's next attack.  Use another Jump Attack, backflip away, and repeat until the Knuckle is defeated.

facts.subject: Gohma
facts.text: Shoot Gohma in the eye with the Slingshot while her eye glows red to stun her and make her vulnerable to sword jump attacks.

evidence.quote: To stun Gohma and make her vulnerable to basic sword attacks, you must shoot her in the eye with the Slingshot while her eye glows red.

facts.subject: Gohma
facts.text: If you shoot Gohma in the eye before she can spawn Gohma Larva on the ceiling, she will fall and remain stunned for a long time.

evidence.quote: If you can shoot her in the eye before she is able spawn them, however, then she will fall to the floor and be stunned for a VERY long time.  You can easily get in three or four more Jump Attacks at this point, which are more then enough to shut down Gohma permanently.

facts.subject: King Dodongo
facts.text: When King Dodongo begins inhaling during his first phase, throw a Bomb into his mouth to stun him for a Jump Attack.

evidence.quote: In order to damage him, you must wait for him to begin inhaling in the first phase, and quickly throw a Bomb into his mouth.  The bomb will explode in his stomach, stunning the King Dodongo for a few seconds.  You are given only one sword swing when he is stunned, so make it a Jump Attack.

facts.subject: King Dodongo
facts.text: Avoid King Dodongo's rolling attack by standing on the edge of the lava or in a corner of the room; three Jump Attacks or six normal sword attacks will kill him.

evidence.quote: Stand on the edge of the lava or in one of the corners of the room to avoid his rolling attack... After three Jump Attacks or six normal sword attacks, Dodongo will die.

facts.subject: Barinade
facts.text: Circle Barinade continuously to avoid lightning bolts while using the Boomerang to destroy the tentacles attached to the ceiling.

evidence.quote: Z-Target the tentacles attached to the ceiling, and begin circling the boss.  It doesn't matter what direction you choose to circle in, but stick with it.  Changing course will result in you getting electrocuted.  Destroy the tentacles attached to the ceiling with the Boomerang.

facts.subject: Barinade
facts.text: In phase two, dodge through the circling Baris, strike Barinade's base with the Boomerang to stun the boss and release the Baris, then destroy them with the Boomerang.

evidence.quote: Dodge through the circling Biris, and stun the boss by striking it's base with the Boomerang.  The Baris will release from their bonding to Barinade, and become vulnerable.  Destroy them with your Boomerang.

facts.subject: Barinade
facts.text: Throwing the Boomerang at Barinade until it penetrates the ring of fast moving Baris will stun him so the Baris can be destroyed.

evidence.quote: Keep throwing your Boomerang at Barinade until it can penetrate the fast moving Baris, and it will stun him.  Destroy the Baris.

facts.subject: Barinade
facts.text: While destroying the Baris, be careful because the satellite dishes will resume their attacking.

evidence.quote: Be careful while destroying them, as the "satellite dishes" will resume their attacking.

facts.subject: Barinade
facts.text: In the final phase once all Baris are dead, stun Barinade with the Boomerang and strike its base with Jump Attacks while watching out for satellite dishes firing.

evidence.quote: Once all of the Baris are dead, then you enter the boss' final phase, in which you are finally able to damage him.  Stun him with your Boomerang, then run into strike it's base with Jump Attacks.  Watch out, however - the satellite dishes will keep on firing the whole time.

facts.subject: Barinade
facts.text: Barinade retreats into the ground briefly after two Jump Attacks and will be defeated after five Jump Attacks.

evidence.quote: After two Jump Attacks, Barinade will retreat into the ground briefly. ... After five Jump Attacks, Barinade will be defeated.

facts.subject: Phantom Ganon
facts.text: To damage Phantom Ganon in the first phase, shoot him with an arrow as he emerges from the painting that appears slightly brighter.

evidence.quote: To damage Phantom Ganon in this phase, you must shoot him with an arrow as he emerges from the painting.  The real Phantom Ganon will make the painting slightly brighter.

facts.subject: Phantom Ganon
facts.text: When Phantom Ganon charges down two paintings on a flying horse, the fake Ganon turns back at the last minute while the real one emerges and scatters the field with electricity.

evidence.quote: At the start of the fight, Phantom Ganon will be mounted on a flying horse, and will retreat into one of the paintings that encircle the room.  He will then appear in two of the paintings, charging towards you down the path; one of them is the real Phantom Ganon, the other is fake.  The fake one will turn back at the last minute, the real one will emerge from the painting and scatter the field with electricity.

facts.subject: Phantom Ganon
facts.text: After being shot three times in the first phase, Phantom Ganon enters his second phase where the Shield is worthless and switching to the Biggoron Sword provides a wider reach advantage.

evidence.quote: After you have shot Phantom Ganon three times in his first phase, then he will enter his second phase.  If you have the Biggoron Sword, then switch to it now.  The Shield is worthless in this phase, and the Biggoron Sword's wider reach is a significant advantage in this next part.

facts.subject: Phantom Ganon
facts.text: To damage Phantom Ganon in his second phase, stun him by reflecting his lightning balls back at him using sword strikes or Bottles as the ball accelerates with each successive hit.

evidence.quote: Phantom Ganon will now begin throwing balls of lightning at you.  To damage him now, you must stun him by reflecting these lightning balls back at him using sword strikes (if you're feeling silly, you can also use Bottles).  The ball moves faster with each successive hit.

facts.subject: Phantom Ganon
facts.text: Standing on the opposite end of the field to reflect lightning shots is easier and recommended for newer players, while standing closer makes reflection harder but finishes the fight faster.

evidence.quote: If you're feeling reckless, then you can stand closer to Phantom Ganon.  This makes it harder to reflect shots, but can get the fight over faster if you're good.  Conversely, you can stand on the opposite end of the field to reflect the shots.  This is easier, and recommended for newer or uncoordinated players.

facts.subject: Phantom Ganon
facts.text: When Phantom Ganon is stunned and falls to the ground, execute one Jump Attack with the Biggoron Sword or Master Sword followed by regular strikes.

evidence.quote: Once the ball strikes Phantom Ganon, then he will be stunned briefly and fall to the ground.  At this point, you should run in and begin pummeling him to death with the Biggoron Sword (or Master Sword if you don't have the Biggoron Sword yet).  Only do one Jump Attack, then proceed to regular strikes.

facts.subject: Volvagia
facts.text: To begin the fight against Volvagia, jump out to the large slab of rock in the middle of the cavern and run to the middle of the platform.

evidence.quote: Jump out to the large slab of rock in the middle of the cavern, and run to the middle of the platform to begin the fight.

facts.subject: Volvagia
facts.text: In Volvagia's first phase, he emerges from one of nine pits marked by smoke and cinders, where striking his head with a Megaton Hammer Jump Attack will stun him.

evidence.quote: In Volvagia's first phase, he appears randomly in one of the nine pits that dot the battlefield.  You'll know which pit he'll appear in, as a large amount of smoke and cinders will appear around the pit.  Run towards this pit, and Volvagia's head will emerge.  Smash his head with the Megaton Hammer (use a Jump Attack with the Megaton Hammer for best results), and it will briefly stun Volvagia.

facts.subject: Volvagia
facts.text: Once Volvagia is stunned in his first phase, follow up with a Jump Attack using the Biggoron Sword or Megaton Hammer.

evidence.quote: At this point, you can get one more attack in on him.  So make it a Jump Attack with the Biggoron Sword for best results (if you don't have the Biggoron Sword, then the Megaton Hammer is a decent substitute).

facts.subject: Volvagia
facts.text: In his second phase when Volvagia flies around breathing fire, avoid damage by running continuously in a small circle near the center of the battlefield.

evidence.quote: In his second phase, Volvagia will emerge from one of the pits (again, you can tell which ones by the smoke and cinders that appear around the pit) and fly around the room, chasing you and trying to breath fire on you.  The easiest way to avoid damage in this phase is to just run continuously to the left or right in a small circle, preferably near the center of the battlefield.

facts.subject: Volvagia
facts.text: When Volvagia flies toward the ceiling causing boulders to rain down, run to the edge of the battlefield and hang off the edge to avoid the attack.

evidence.quote: After you damage Volvagia again, then he will emerge from the pits once more and begin flying towards the ceiling.  The roof will begin to fall, raining the battlefield with boulders.  Easily the best way to avoid this form of attack is to just run to the edge of the battlefield and hang off the edge.

facts.subject: Morpha
facts.text: A single attack from Morpha deals four to six hearts of damage.

evidence.quote: The only thing "hard" about Morpha is it's ability to deal quite a large amount of damage in one attack (which deal four to six hearts of damage... but since you should have fourteen or fifteen heart containers by now, that's no big deal).

facts.subject: Morpha
facts.text: Avoid entering the water or standing on the four inner platforms; remain on the room's perimeter, using the middle platform ladders if you fall into the water.

evidence.quote: For the duration of this boss fight, it's very important that you avoid entering the water, since this will give the boss easy opportunity to attack you.  You should also avoid standing on the four platforms on the inside of the room, since this will allow Morpha to attack you from several sides ... If you fall in the water or somehow end up on one of the inner platforms, then get back to the perimeter of the room posthaste.  There are ladders on the platforms in the middle of the room you can climb up if you happen to fall in the water.

facts.subject: Morpha
facts.text: When Morpha spins rapidly in the water, it generates tentacle arms that grab and hurl you into the wall upon contact, but the Longshot outranges them.

evidence.quote: Morpha's "nucleus" (the large white brain/eye) will typically enter one of these arms, and the arm will stretch out towards you.  If you make contact with the arm, then it will grab you and hurl you into the wall. ... Thankfully, your Longshot outranges Morpha's arms by a considerable distance.  So stay a fair distance away to avoid Morpha's only attack - it's arms.  You'll know Morpha is generating another arm and is getting ready to attack when it spins around rapidly in the water below.

facts.subject: Morpha
facts.text: When Morpha's nucleus enters an arm, grab it with the Longshot to stun it and perform a Jump Attack with the Biggoron Sword or Megaton Hammer before it bounces back into the water.

evidence.quote: When Morpha enters one of it's arms, this is your opportunity to attack.  Grab it with the Longshot, and it will remained stunned long enough for you to attack it once, maybe twice.  Which is why you should make that attack a Jump Attack with the Biggoron Sword (which you can, and should, have by now, no excuses).  If you don't have the Biggoron's Sword, then a Jump Attack with the Megaton Hammer will do.  After Morpha is damaged, it will bounce randomly around the room for a little while, then return to the water and start spawning more arms.

facts.subject: Bongo Bongo
facts.text: Drop down the pit in the middle of the room to begin the boss fight against Bongo Bongo.

evidence.quote: Drop down the pit in the middle of the room to begin the fight.

facts.subject: Bongo Bongo
facts.text: Equip the Kokiri Boots to avoid making the fight unnecessarily difficult while dodging Bongo Bongo's hand attacks and drum pounds.

evidence.quote: The entire boss fight is fought on a giant drum.  A giant Bongo Drum.  Yep, that's right.  Bongo Bongo will attack you with his hands, or try to knock you off the drum by pounding it hard.  Just use basic dodging to avoid these attacks. ... Just make sure you're using the Kokiri Boots, otherwise this fight will be unnecessarily difficult.

facts.subject: Bongo Bongo
facts.text: Z-Target and shoot both hands with arrows to stun them, then use the Lens of Truth to spot Bongo Bongo's eye, shoot it with an arrow, and Jump Attack his fallen torso with the Biggoron Sword.

evidence.quote: To damage Bongo Bongo, you must make his eye appear.  To do this, shoot both of his hands with arrows to stun them.  They recover quickly, so shoot fast.  Use Z-Targeting; the hands move much too fast, and the constant movement of the drum makes manual aiming pretty much impossible.  Once you stun both hands, use the Lens of Truth to look at the space between the hands, and you'll see Bongo Bongo's eye.  Shoot it with an Arrow as well, and Bongo Bongo's torso will fall to the floor, letting you attack it.  As always, that attack should be a Jump Attack from the Biggoron Sword (which you can, and should, have by now).

facts.subject: Bongo Bongo
facts.text: Stunning Bongo Bongo's hands causes them to drop magic and arrows if you run low.

evidence.quote: If you run low on magic or arrows, Bongo Bongo's hands drop more when you stun them.

facts.subject: Twinrova
facts.text: The Sorceress Sisters have opposing elements: Kotake is Ice, and Koume is Fire.

evidence.quote: The Sisters each have their own element which opposes the other.  Kotake is Ice, and Koume is Fire.

facts.subject: Twinrova
facts.text: In the first phase, keep both sisters in view without Z-Targeting and use the Mirror Shield to reflect one sister's elemental magic beam into the opposing sister, as missing creates a damaging floor ring.

evidence.quote: You have to now use the Mirror Shield to reflect this beam into the other sister, much as you reflected the beams of light earlier in the dungeon. ... Don't even TRY to Z-Target to aim the beam; if you do, the beam will just fire off in some random direction and won't even get near the other sister. ... If you fail to reflect one of the beams, then it will impact on the floor, creating a ring that damages you (and in the case of Kotake's ice beam, freezes you... which sucks).

facts.subject: Twinrova
facts.text: To stun Twinrova and make her vulnerable to attack, you must absorb three spells of the same alignment in a row with your shield, as absorbing an opposing element negates prior charges.

evidence.quote: In order to stun Twinrova and make her vulnerable to attack, you have to absorb three spells of the same alignment IN A ROW.  This means that, if you absorb two fire spells, then an ice spell, then the two fires will be negated and you have to absorb two more ice spells.

facts.subject: Twinrova
facts.text: Twinrova indicates which beam she will use by waving her right wand for Ice and left wand for Fire, while the Mirror Shield flashes red for fire and white for ice, flashing faster as more beams are absorbed.

evidence.quote: You can tell which beam Twinrova is about to use by looking at which wand she waves - the right is Ice, the left is Fire.  You can also tell which beams your Mirror Shield has absorbed by looking at it - it flashes red for fire, and white for ice.  The faster it flashes, the more beams absorbed.

facts.subject: Twinrova
facts.text: After absorbing three consecutive beams, keep the Mirror Shield drawn to fire a beam that stuns Twinrova, then equip Hover Boots, Jump Attack across the gap, strike her with your sword, and switch back to Kokiri Boots on the main platform.

evidence.quote: After you absorb three beams of the same alignment in a row, then the Mirror Shield will unleash a massive beam back at Twinrova (keep the shield drawn to make sure the beam connects).  This will stun her momentarily, causing her to fall to the platform below her.  At this point, quickly equip the Hover Boots and draw your sword.  Run out to Twinrova.  When you're halfway across the gap, use a Jump Attack to go the rest of the way and damage Twinrova at the same time.  Then switch to basic sword strikes.  When Twinrova recovers, return to the main platform and switch back to the Kokiri Boots, where the second phase starts over.

facts.subject: Ganondorf
facts.text: Navi cannot Z-Target Ganondorf or provide C-Up advice until he is stunned with a Light Arrow, and she becomes unavailable again when he recovers.

evidence.quote: Navi is unavailable during this fight, meaning you can't Z-Target and she can't give you advice with C-Up.  Once Ganondorf is stunned with a Light Arrow, then Navi can Z-Target again, but Navi becomes unavailable once more when Ganondorf recovers.

facts.subject: Ganondorf
facts.text: Ganondorf remains stationary in the center of the room and performs a Shockwave attack that collapses floor pieces into pits leading down to Tower Floor Five if approached before he is stunned.

evidence.quote: For one, Ganondorf remains stationary in the center of the room.  He also has a Shockwave attack, which will collapse bits of the floor, creating pits that lead back down to the Tower Floor Five area.  For this reason, don't go near Ganondorf until he is stunned, or else he will use the Shockwave and make this fight more difficult then it needs to be.

facts.subject: Ganondorf
facts.text: Reflect Ganondorf's balls of lightning back at him with sword strikes or Empty Bottles, as any missed lightning ball will destroy the floor panel you are standing on.

evidence.quote: Ganondorf will throw balls of lightning at you, which you must reflect back at him with sword strikes (or you can use Empty Bottles if you're feeling creative).  If you miss a ball of lightning and it doesn't hit you, then it will destroy whatever floor panel you happen to be standing on, knocking you down to a lower floor.

facts.subject: Ganondorf
facts.text: If knocked down to the lower floor during the fight with Ganondorf, climb back up using the tiles on the pillar in the middle of the room.

evidence.quote: If you miss a ball of lightning and it doesn't hit you, then it will destroy whatever floor panel you happen to be standing on, knocking you down to a lower floor.  You'll have to climb back up using the tiles on the pillar in the middle of the room.

facts.subject: Twinrova
facts.text: When the sisters merge into Twinrova, players can Z-Target and use the Biggoron Sword, keeping it put away until ready to damage Twinrova, or use the Master Sword.

evidence.quote:
Now truly Twinrova, the Sorceress Sisters form one entity.  So you can now Z-
Target.  If you have the Biggoron Sword (which you can, and should, have by
now), then use it for this stage of the fight, but keep it "Put Away" until
you're ready to damage Twinrova. ... If all of this
is too much for you, just use the Master Sword

facts.subject: Ganondorf
