facts.text: Reflecting Ganondorf's energy balls back at him stuns him, after which shooting him with a Light Arrow stuns him further for Link to attack.

evidence.quote:
Ganondorf will reflect the balls back at you as well, so keeping reflecting
them until one strikes and stuns Ganondorf.  There is a new wrinkle to the
fight at this point; you must now shoot Ganondorf with a Light Arrow, whereupon
he will become stunned.

facts.subject: Ganondorf
facts.text: Link can equip Hover Boots to cross the central pit and perform a Jump Attack while crossing to hit the stunned Ganondorf.

evidence.quote:
Quickly equip the Hover Boots and use them to cross the pit in the middle of
the floor.  Just like in the Twinrova fight, use a Jump Attack when you're
halfway across the pit to deal extra damage to him, then switch to normal
attacks.

facts.subject: Ganondorf
facts.text: When Ganondorf charges up power with both arms raised, shooting him with a Light Arrow cancels the attack and stuns him instantly.

evidence.quote:
Ganondorf will occasionally use a new attack where he will charge up a lot of
power (you'll know when he's doing it, as he will hold up both arms to create
the spell instead of just one arm for the Lightning Ball).  To stop him from
using this attack, shoot him with a Light Arrow.  This will instantly stun him,
letting you get in more attacks.

facts.subject: Ganon
facts.text: Ganon's weak point is his tail, which can be reached during the first phase by Z-Targeting him and performing side dodges.

evidence.quote:
Like all evil demons of the underworld, Ganon's weakspot is his tail.  In his
first phase, you'll have to Z-Target Ganon and then begin performing side
dodges (hold right or left and press A) to speed around behind Ganon.

facts.subject: Ganon
facts.text: In the first phase of the Ganon fight without the Master Sword, Link can deal heavy damage to Ganon's tail using Jump Attacks with the Biggoron Sword or Megaton Hammer.

evidence.quote:
At the start of the fight you won't have access to the Master Sword.  Which
doesn't really matter, since Shields are useless against Ganon, and you should
have the Biggoron Sword by now.  If for whatever reason you don't have the
Biggoron Sword, then the Megaton Hammer will have to make due...When you
get behind him, do a Jump Attack with the Biggoron Sword or Megaton Hammer to
deal a hefty amount of damage to Ganon.

facts.subject: Master Sword
facts.text: When the surrounding ring of fire lowers during the Ganon battle, Link must run to Zelda to retrieve the Master Sword.

evidence.quote:
Repeat this method until a cutscene shows the flames around the perimeter of
the arena lowering.  Run over to Zelda and retake the Master Sword when this
happens.

facts.subject: Ganon
facts.text: Ganon can only be finished off with the Master Sword while held in place by Princess Zelda's magic.

evidence.quote:
Only the Master Sword can defeat Ganon.  After a
cutscene, you will be prompted to attack Ganondorf while he is being held in
place by Zelda's magic.  Do this, and the game is over.

facts.subject: Mido
facts.text: Mido will not let Link pass to the Great Deku Tree unless both the Kokiri Sword and Deku Shield are equipped in the Equipment subscreen.

evidence.quote:
Make sure you have them equipped in the Equipment subscreen.  If either the
Kokiri Sword or the Deku Shield is not equipped, then Mido will not let you
pass.

facts.subject: Game File Number
facts.text: The number displayed on the game file tracks how many times the player has reached the Game Over screen on that file, excluding deaths revived with a Fairy.

evidence.quote:
The real
answer is, this number records the number of times you have seen the Game Over
screen on that file (deaths that were recovered with a Fairy don't count).

facts.subject: Deku Nut Upgrade
facts.text: The Deku Nut upgrade from the Forest Stage cannot be obtained once Link has transformed into Adult Link.

evidence.quote:
Q: Why can't I get the Deku Nut Upgrade from the Forest Stage?

A: This upgrade cannot be gotten if you have already become Adult Link.

facts.subject: Triforce
facts.text: When young Link opens the Door of Time, the Sacred Realm is unsealed and the three Triforce pieces go to Ganondorf (Power), Link (Courage), and Zelda (Wisdom).

evidence.quote:
When Link opens the Door
of Time in his childhood, then the Sacred Realm was unsealed.  The three shards
of the Triforce (Power, Courage and Wisdom) each went to a different person in
the world: Ganondorf got the Triforce of Power, Link got the Triforce of
Courage, and Zelda got the Triforce of Wisdom.

facts.subject: Zora's Domain
facts.text: Zora's Domain cannot be manually thawed out during gameplay, but begins unfreezing after beating the Water Temple and is shown unfrozen during the credits.

evidence.quote:
Q: How do I unfreeze Zora's Domain?

A: Short answer: you can't.

Long answer: Zora's Domain begins to unfreeze after you beat the Water Temple...Zora's Domain unfreezes eventually.  We know this, as
Zoras appear in the party at Lon Lon Ranch during the credits.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Dropping a Bottled Bug into soft earth patches as Young Link reveals a Gold Skulltula in nine locations across Hyrule.

evidence.quote:
As Young Link, travel to the patches of
soft earth (Kokiri Forest, Lake Hylia, Gerudo Valley, Death Mountain Trail,
Death Mountain Crater, Kakariko Graveyard, Desert Colossus, and two in the Lost
Woods) and drop a Bottled Bug into the patch.  Each of the patches will produce
a Gold Skulltula.

facts.subject: Zora's River Soft Earth
facts.text: The soft earth patch located at Zora's River does not contain a Gold Skulltula.

evidence.quote:
For whatever reason, the patch of soft earth at Zora's River
does not contain a Gold Skulltula.

facts.subject: Skull Kid
facts.text: The Skull Kid in the Lost Woods will only buy the Skull Mask if Link has already played Saria's Song for him and earned the Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote:
Q: How come I can't sell the Skull Mask to the Skullkid?

A: He will only buy the mask from you if you've already played him Saria's Song
and earned the Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Kakariko Village Windmill
facts.text: Link can use the Longshot to access hidden openings inside the Kakariko Village Windmill, but they serve no purpose.

evidence.quote:
you can use the Longshot
to access hidden openings in the Kakariko Village Windmill.  These openings do
nothing.

facts.subject: East Lava Pit
facts.text: Crossing the lava pit on the east side of Goron City requires playing the Song of Time to summon a Block of Time, then using the Longshot to pull across to Business Scrubs.

evidence.quote:
You need both the Longshot and the Song of Time to get across the pit.  Play
the Song of Time to make a Block of Time appear, then stand on the block to use
the Longshot and pull yourself across the lava pit.  What's on the other side?
A pit containing Business Scrubs, selling rubbish.

facts.subject: Gerudo Valley Rupee Arrow
facts.text: The arrow formed of rupees in the pit in Gerudo Valley points only to a plain wall with nothing behind it.

evidence.quote:
Q: What does the arrow made of rupees point to in the pit in Gerudo Valley?

A: The wall.  There is nothing there.

facts.subject: Running Man
facts.text: As Adult Link, Link can challenge the Running Man to a footrace time trial from the Gerudo Valley Carpenter's Tent to the entrance to Kokiri Forest, though the Running Man always finishes one second faster.

evidence.quote:
As Adult Link, you can challenge the Running Man who bought your Bunny Hood
as a child to a footrace from the Gerudo Valley Carpenter's Tent to the
entrance to Kokiri Forest.  It doesn't matter how fast you go, he'll always
beat you by exactly one second...In the end, it seems that all the Running Man is a time trial to see how
quickly you can travel from Gerudo Valley to Kokiri Forest.  He does, after
all, keep track of your best time.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula Trick
facts.text: In the Hyrule Castle Garden pit opened with Song of Storms, Link can kill the Gold Skulltula, retrieve its token with the Boomerang, and backflip into the exit light before the token touches him to collect unlimited tokens.

evidence.quote:
This trick lets you get unlimited Gold Skulltula tokens, even past the 100
mark (the Quest Subscreen even shows the number going above 100).  To perform
this trick, head for the pit in Hyrule Castle Garden which can only be opened
with the Song of Storms.  It's near the tree in the area with Talon's Milk
Crates.  Drop down into the pit, and look for the Gold Skulltula.  Kill it, and
then Z-Target its token.  Use the Boomerang on the token, and then backflip
into the beam of light leading back to the surface just before the Token
touches you.

facts.subject: Fourth Gravestone from Right
facts.text: Pulling aside the fourth gravestone from the right in the rear row of Kakariko Graveyard reveals a pit leading to the Redead grave.

evidence.quote:
Go to the rear row of gravestones, and go to the far right.  Counting from the
right to the left, pull aside the fourth gravestone to reveal another pit.
Drop down the pit.

facts.subject: Redead
facts.text: Attacking the Redead repeatedly reduces its opportunity to attack, and tapping buttons and rotating the joystick frees Link if grabbed.

evidence.quote:
Just go ape crazy on this
Redead, attacking him repeatedly.  The faster you attack him, the less
opportunity he gets to attack you back.  If he does manage to grab hold of you,
tap buttons and rotate the joystick like mad to free yourself.

facts.subject: Sun's Song Chest
facts.text: After permanently defeating the Redead in the grave, playing the Sun's Song spawns a chest containing a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote:
Once the Redead
is permanently defeated (it will make an extra loud SWIPE noise when it is),
play the Sun's Song to make a chest appear that contains a Piece of Heart.
Open the chest, take the Piece of Heart, and return to Kakariko Graveyard.

facts.subject: Dampe's Heart-Pounding Gravedigging Tour
facts.text: Standing on a dirt patch in Dampe's path causes him to stop, allowing Link to pay him 10 rupees to dig.

evidence.quote:
Dampe takes a circular route around the graveyard, following
the path.  If you stand directly in his path, then he will stop....In order to find the Piece of Heart, stand directly on that dirt patch
so that way Dampe will stop directly in front of it, then speak to Dampe and
pay him 10 rupees to dig up that patch of dirt.

facts.subject: Dampe's Heart-Pounding Gravedigging Tour
facts.text: A Piece of Heart is hidden in one of twelve dirt patches in Kakariko Graveyard and randomly changes places whenever you leave the zone.

evidence.quote:
In one of the
twelve dirt patches dotted around the graveyard, there is hidden a Piece of
Heart....The Piece of Heart randomly changes places every time you
leave the zone, so if you have to leave to restock on Rupees, then just start
over from the beginning.

facts.subject: Dampe's Gravedigging Game
facts.text: Dampe's Gravedigging Game only runs during the first part of the night and cannot be accessed using the Sun's Song.

evidence.quote:
Dampe's Gravedigging Game
only runs for the first part of the night, so if Dampe isn't there then you'll
have to go hang around Hyrule Field until it becomes nighttime again, then
return to the Graveyard.  The Sun's Song won't work (it makes the time either
noon or midnight, and the Gravedigging Tour is open during neither time).

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: At night, a Gold Skulltula is found on the pile of bricks at the Unfinished House in Kakariko Village and should be shot with the Slingshot.

evidence.quote:
There are a ton of Golden Skulltulas to find and kill here in the dead of
night.  The first is at the Unfinished House, on the pile of bricks.  Kill it
with the Slingshot before trying to jump up and grab the token (the sword will
cause you to take damage because of the extreme close range).

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: At night, a Gold Skulltula is located directly beneath a window on the left side of the House of Skulltula.

evidence.quote:
The second
Skulltula can be found on the building directly to the west of the Unfinished
Building (the House of Skulltula).  It sits directly beneath a window on the
left side of the building.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula in Kakariko Village can be found by rolling into the tree near the center of town at night.

evidence.quote:
The third Skulltula can be found by rolling into the tree near the center of
Kakariko Village.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is perched on top of the tall observation tower on the upper level of Kakariko Village and can be shot down with the Slingshot.

evidence.quote:
The fourth can be found on top of the tall observation tower
on the upper level of Kakariko Village.  Shoot it with the slingshot before
climbing up the ladder to claim it.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is located on the north side of the building closest to the Death Mountain Gate at the northern edge of Kakariko Village.

evidence.quote:
The last of the Skulltulas can be found in
the northern edge of the village, on the north side of the building closest to
the Death Mountain Gate.

facts.subject: House of Skulltula
facts.text: Speaking to the man on the right inside the House of Skulltula rewards Link with the Adult's Wallet for collecting 10 Gold Skulltula tokens.

evidence.quote:
Enter the building, and turn to the right.  Speak to the man, and he will
reward you with the Adult's Wallet, the award for killing 10 Golden Skulltulas
and claiming their tokens.

facts.subject: Death Mountain Trail Gate Guard
facts.text: Showing Zelda's Letter to the guard by the northern gate allows Link through to Death Mountain Trail.

evidence.quote:
Go to the northern edge of the village and speak with the guard by the gate.
He will refuse to let you through to Death Mountain Trail.  Show him Zelda's
Letter, and he'll let you through, though he'll think it's all a big joke.

facts.subject: Death Mountain Trail Gate Guard
facts.text: The gate guard requests that Link bring him a Keaton Mask from the Hyrule Castle Market to begin the Happy Mask Trading Sequence.

evidence.quote:
He
will request, however, that you return to the Hyrule Castle Market and pick up
a Keaton mask for him.  This is the first step of the Happy Mask Trading
Sequence, the Young Link trading game.

facts.subject: Happy Mask Shop
facts.text: The Happy Mask Shop is located near the Temple of Time to the right of the entrance to the Hyrule Castle Garden.

evidence.quote:
The Happy Mask Shop is now open for business.  It's the small building near the
Temple of Time, to the right of the entrance to the Hyrule Castle Garden.
Enter the building.

facts.subject: Happy Mask Shop
facts.text: Link can borrow the Keaton Mask from the Happy Mask Shop window counter.

evidence.quote:
You will now be able to select masks from the
shop windows as though you were buying them from a regular shop.  Select the
only one available, the Keaton Mask, and return to Kakariko Village.

facts.subject: Death Mountain Trail Gate Guard
facts.text: Speaking to the Death Mountain gate guard while wearing the Keaton Mask prompts him to buy it for 15 rupees.

evidence.quote:
Return to the guard by the gate to Death Mountain, and speak to him while
wearing the Keaton Mask.  He'll pay you 15 rupees for the mask.

facts.subject: Happy Mask Shop
facts.text: After paying the 10-rupee fee for the Keaton Mask at the Happy Mask Shop, Link can borrow the Skull Mask.

evidence.quote: Pay the 10-rupee fee for the Keaton Mask, and then borrow the Skull Mask.

facts.subject: Northern Gate
facts.text: Passing through the northern gate of Kakariko Village leads to Death Mountain Trail.

evidence.quote: Head to the northern gate, and go through to Death Mountain Trail.

facts.subject: Tektite
facts.text: On Death Mountain Trail, hold R to execute Turtle Defense with the Hylian Shield if a Tektite tries to jump on Link.

evidence.quote:
Go forward a bit, and kill the Tektite.  If he tries to jump on you, do the
Turtle Defense with the Hylian Shield (hold R).

facts.subject: Tektite
facts.text: Two Tektites appear around the corner on the path, and another jumps down from above as you follow the trail upward.

evidence.quote:
Go around the corner and
defeat two more Tektites....Keep following the
path up and around, and defeat another Tektite who jumps down from on high.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula can be heard near the corner on Death Mountain Trail, but it cannot be reached until Link obtains Bombs.

evidence.quote:
You can vaguely hear a Gold Skulltula here, but you
won't be able to reach it until you get access to Bombs.

facts.subject: Giant Boulder
facts.text: A Piece of Heart is located high above the giant boulder along the path of Death Mountain Trail.

evidence.quote:
Note the Piece of Heart high above the giant boulder - we'll get to it in a few
minutes.

facts.subject: Wooden Post Intersection
facts.text: At the large wooden post with a red flag, taking the right path past the stone pedestal with a ring of rocks leads into Goron City through an archway.

evidence.quote:
Keep following the path
until you reach a large wooden post with a red flag tied to it.  From here, you
can go left to keep climbing the mountain, or go right to Goron City.  Go
right.  Keep following the path, past the large stone pedestal with the ring of
rocks, and enter the archway carved into the stone to enter Goron City.

facts.subject: Darunia's Room
facts.text: Playing Zelda's Lullaby while standing on the carpet in front of the sealed door on Goron City's lowest level opens the door.

evidence.quote: Jump down to Goron City's lowest level.  Look for the sealed door with the carpeting in front of it.  Stand on the carpet, and play Zelda's Lullaby to make the door open.

facts.subject: Darunia
facts.text: Playing Saria's Song while standing directly in front of Darunia cheers him up.

evidence.quote: Play Saria's Song while standing directly in front of him to cheer him up.

facts.subject: Darunia
facts.text: Darunia gives Link the Goron's Bracelet, which allows Link to pick up and use Bomb Flowers.

evidence.quote: He'll give you the Goron's Bracelet to help, which can be used to pick up and use Bomb Flowers that grow around Death Mountain.

facts.subject: Giant Pot
facts.text: Lighting all the braziers on the bottom level of Goron City with a flaming Deku Stick causes the giant pot in the middle of the room to begin spinning.

evidence.quote: Use the flame to light all of the braziers on the bottom level of Goron City.  Once all the braziers are lit, then the giant pot in the middle of the room will begin spinning.

facts.subject: Goron City Shop
facts.text: Igniting the Bomb Flowers near the sealed room with a lit Deku Stick blows open the wall to access the Goron City Shop.

evidence.quote: You can also use the lit Deku Stick to ignite the Bomb Flowers near the sealed up room, which will blow open the wall and let you access the Goron City Shop (not that it has anything of real value to buy... yet).

facts.subject: Goron City Second Level
facts.text: Climbing the stairs between the yellow-striped posts leads to the second level, where dropping a Bomb Flower near the boulders clears the tunnel path.

evidence.quote: Head up the stairs between the pair of yellow-striped posts to reach the second level of Goron City.  Run to the right, where you will find two unlit torched and a Goron sitting in front of a tunnel.  Run down this tunnel to see a long line of boulders surrounded by Bomb Flowers.  Pick up one of the Bomb Flowers, and drop it near the boulders to clear a path.

facts.subject: Lost Woods Clearing
facts.text: Going left through the tunnel, then left again, and left one final time leads to a dead-end clearing.

evidence.quote: Go left through the tunnel, then left again, then left one final time.  You'll be in a small clearing which is a dead end.

facts.subject: Soft Earth
facts.text: Releasing bottled bugs near the patch of soft earth by the right Business Scrub reveals a Gold Skulltula that yields a token.

evidence.quote: Release your Bottled Bugs near the patch of soft earth, and recapture one of the bugs before they all disappear.  Kill the Gold Skulltula who emerges from the patch, and take its token.

facts.subject: Invisible Pit
facts.text: Dropping into the invisible pit surrounded by butterflies near the large tree in the clearing leads to the Forest Stage.

evidence.quote: Now, run to the large tree in the back of the clearing, and look for a cluster of butterflies in the tall grass.  These butterflies are actually gathered around an invisible pit.  Drop down into the pit to reach the Forest Stage.

facts.subject: Deku Scrub Chief
facts.text: Wearing the Skull Mask in the Forest Stage prompts the Deku Scrub Chief to increase Link's Deku Stick capacity by 10.

evidence.quote: Put on the Skull Mask and take a few steps forward.  The Deku Scrubs in the stage will begin to cheer and mob you.  Run over to the right side of the room (facing from the entrance), and the Deku Scrub Chief will increase the number of Deku Sticks you can carry by 10.

facts.subject: Forest Stage Clearing
facts.text: Leaving the clearing through the log tunnel and going right, right, left, right, forward, and forward leads back to the Lone Skullkid.

evidence.quote: Leave the clearing through the log tunnel, then go right, right again, and then left.  Hang a right, then forward, and forward again.  You'll find yourself back by the Lone Skullkid.

facts.subject: Lone Skullkid
facts.text: Speaking to the Lone Skullkid while wearing the Skull Mask allows Link to sell the mask to him.

evidence.quote: Otherwise, speak to him while wearing the Skull Mask, and he'll buy it from you.  Unfortunately, he'll buy it from you for less then it's worth, so you're going to have to pay the difference next time you're in town.

facts.subject: Soft Earth
facts.text: Dropping a bottled bug into the soft earth patch at the cliff edge through the log tunnel behind the Skullkid reveals a Gold Skulltula that yields a token.

evidence.quote: Once you have sold the Skull Mask, enter the mouth of the log tunnel behind you.  At the edge of the cliff on the other side is another patch of soft earth.  Drop a Bottled Bug into the patch (remember to recapture one of the three bugs that pops out), and kill the Gold Skulltula who emerges from the earth.  Take it's token.

facts.subject: Goron City Top Floor
facts.text: Ascending the stairs between the red-striped posts on the second level and going right leads to the top floor, where taking two rights exits to Death Mountain Trail.

evidence.quote: Back on the second level of Goron City, go to the far left of the ledge and go up the stairs between the pair of red-striped posts.  When the stairs split left and right, go right.  At the top of the stairs, you'll find yourself on Goron City's top floor.  Go right from the stairwell exit, then right again the first chance you get to return to Death Mountain Trail.

facts.subject: Dodongo's Cavern Entrance
facts.text: Throwing a Bomb Flower from the alcove cliff so that it lands near the blocking boulder opens Dodongo's Cavern.

evidence.quote: Go around the corner to the right, where there is a small alcove with a Bomb Flower in it.  Pick up the Bomb Flower, and throw it off the cliff so that it lands on or near the boulder blocking Dodongo's Cavern.

facts.subject: Dodongo's Cavern Cliff
facts.text: Backflipping over the fence while running backward toward the cliff edge lands Link on the cliff above Dodongo's Cavern to collect a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: Run backwards towards the edge of the cliff, and when you reach the fence, hold back and press A to backflip over the fence.  If you do it just right, then you'll land on the cliff above Dodongo's Cavern and be able to get the Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Soft Earth
facts.text: Dropping a bug into the soft earth patch outside the entrance to Dodongo's Cavern reveals a Gold Skulltula that yields a token.

evidence.quote: Drop down from the cliff, and enter the mouth of Dodongo's Cavern.  Stop to drop a bug in the patch of soft earth (remember to recapture one of the three who comes out), and kill the Gold Skulltula who emerges.  Take the Token, then enter Dodongo's Cavern.

facts.subject: Cracked Wall
facts.text: Throwing a Bomb Flower near the cracked wall destroys the wall and reveals the main antechamber of Dodongo's Cavern.

evidence.quote: Grab one of the Bomb Flowers to your right, and throw it near the cracked wall.  The explosion will destroy the wall, revealing Dodongo's Cavern.

facts.subject: Beamos
facts.text: Throwing a Bomb Flower so that it strikes a Beamos on the head causes the Beamos to explode.

evidence.quote: Grab the bomb flower in front of the large window, and quickly Z-target the Beamos enemy to the right of the Bomb Flower.  Run at the Beamos, and throw the Bomb Flower at it.  If you do it right, then the Bomb Flower should strike the Beamos on the head and cause the whole apparatus to explode.

facts.subject: Sealed Wall
facts.text: Blowing open the sealed wall to the right of the Beamos with a Bomb Flower reveals a darkened tunnel leading to the next room.

evidence.quote: Grab another Bomb Flower and use it to blow open the sealed wall to the right of the Beamos.  Go through the darkened tunnel to the next room.

facts.subject: Sealed Barrier
facts.text: Killing a Baby Dodongo as it passes by the sealed wall destroys the barrier with its explosion, granting access to the door.

evidence.quote: You will come to a place where another Baby Dodongo appears, as well as a sealed up wall.  Stand next to the sealed up wall, and then kill the Baby Dodongo as it moves by it.  The explosion will destroy the barrier, letting you access the door on the other side.

facts.subject: Keese
facts.text: Keese that pass through torch flames catch fire, but their attacks can be blocked and their flames doused with the Hylian Shield.

evidence.quote: Watch out though; if they fly through the flame of the torch, they will catch on fire and deal additional damage (and also destroy your Deku Shield if you are still using it).  Use the Hylian Shield to absorb their attacks and douse the flame.

facts.subject: Torch Room Wall
facts.text: Killing the Gold Skulltula on the wall of the Torch Room yields a token that may require a backflip to reach.

evidence.quote: Kill the Gold Skulltula on the wall, take the token (you may need to use a backflip to reach it), and return to the Lower Southeast Hall.

facts.subject: Gray Switch
facts.text: Pushing an Armos statue onto the gray switch unlocks the door in the Lower Southeast Hall.

evidence.quote: Grab hold of one of the Armos Statues, and push it into place onto the gray switch.  This will unlock the door.

facts.subject: Keese
facts.text: Keese on either side of the Southeast Passage can be targeted and killed with the Slingshot.

evidence.quote: Z-target the Keese on either side of the room and kill them with the Slingshot.

facts.subject: Lizalfos
facts.text: Lizalfos attacks can be blocked using the shield, followed by an immediate sword counterattack.

evidence.quote: Luckily, all of their attacks are easily blocked using the Turtle Shield technique.  After they've attacked, quickly swing out with your sword.

facts.subject: Lizalfos Nest
facts.text: Defeating both Lizalfos in the nest unlocks the exit door on the west side of the room.

evidence.quote: After the Lizalfos are dead, the door on the west side of the room will unlock.  Go through it.

facts.subject: Dodongo
facts.text: Dodongos are defeated by running around behind them and attacking their tail, and they explode upon defeat.

evidence.quote:
Run to the end of the passage, and kill the pair of Dodongos in the long room
by running around behind them and attacking their tail.  Watch out - they blow
up just like the Baby Dodongos.

facts.subject: West door
facts.text: Lighting the three empty sconces along the room with a flaming Deku Stick opens the door at the west end of the hall.

evidence.quote:
Use the flaming Deku Stick to light the three
empty sconces along the room (each is very near to where one of the three
Dodongos was).  Once all three are lit, the door at the west end of the hall
will open.

facts.subject: Switch
facts.text: Stepping onto the switch inside the window in the Antechamber opens the door on the far side of the room.

evidence.quote:
Run forward and step onto the
switch, which will open the door on the far side of the room.

facts.subject: Chest
facts.text: A chest behind a sealed wall blasted open with a Bomb Flower contains the Dungeon Map.

evidence.quote:
Before you
go through the door you just unlocked, grab the Bomb Flower near the door and
use it to blast open the sealed wall to the left of the Bomb Flower.  Open the
chest on the other side to find the Dungeon Map.

facts.subject: Northwest door
facts.text: After unlocking the door and collecting the map, go through the door in the northwest corner of the Antechamber.

evidence.quote:
Go through the door you
unlocked, in the northwest corner of the room.

facts.subject: Oddly-colored wall
facts.text: At the south end of the Bomb Flower Room, using a Bomb Flower against the oddly-colored wall breaks open the sealed wall.

evidence.quote:
Go to the south end of the room, and use the
Bomb Flower against the oddly-colored wall to break open the sealed wall.  Go
through the opened wall and through the door.

facts.subject: Armos Knight
facts.text: To defeat the Armos Knight guarding the chest, drop a Bomb Flower near it and strike the knight with a sword to awaken it right before the bomb detonates.

evidence.quote:
To defeat it, grab a Bomb Flower, and drop
it near the Armos Knight (don't throw it - drop it).  Just before the Bomb
Flower explodes, strike the Armos Knight with your sword to bring it to life.
The explosion will kill the Knight, and he will begin spinning rapidly and
flashing.  After a few seconds, it will explode.

facts.subject: Chest
facts.text: Opening the chest guarded by the Armos Knight in the Armos Trap Room yields the Compass.

evidence.quote:
Open the chest to find the Compass, then
return to the previous room.

facts.subject: Iron pillar
facts.text: Throwing a Bomb Flower directly between the two long lines of Bomb Flowers surrounding the Iron Pillar ignites them simultaneously, lowering the pillar to form stairs.

evidence.quote:
Grab the Bomb Flower to your right as you come out of the door, and throw it
directly between the two long lines of Bomb Flowers surrounding the Iron
Pillar.  The Bomb Flowers will all ignite simultaneously, moving the pillar to
a lower level.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula Token
facts.text: Destroying the Gold Skulltula hanging from the ivy at the top of the Bomb Flower Room allows you to climb up and collect its token.

evidence.quote:
Destroy
the Skulltula and the Gold Skulltula hanging from the ivy, then climb up the
ivy to grab the token.

facts.subject: Fire Keese
facts.text: Take out the pair of flying Fire Keese in the Pillar Room using the Slingshot, and block them with the shield if they fly at you.

evidence.quote:
This room has a pair of Fire Keese flying around it.  Circle around the room,
taking them out with the Slingshot.  Use the Turtle Shield guard if a Keese
starts to fly at you.

facts.subject: Pillar switch
facts.text: Climbing up the ladder to the top of the pillar and stepping on the switch unlocks the door to the east.

evidence.quote:
Climb up the ladder to the top of the pillar, and step on the switch to unlock
the door in the east of the room.  Go east to the next room.

facts.subject: Upper Antechamber catwalk
facts.text: From high up in the Antechamber, leap over the gap in the rear upper catwalk and run through the tunnel to reach the room on the other side.

evidence.quote:
Run past or kill the Fire Keese,
and leap over the gap in the catwalk.  Run through the tunnel to the room on
the other side.

facts.subject: Chest
facts.text: In the Blade Trap Room, climbing the stone block and ladder and jumping to the small platform leads to a chest containing a red rupee.

evidence.quote:
Climb onto the stone block, then up the ladder.  Stand on the narrow
ledge at the top of the cliff, and carefully turn around so that you can see
the small platform.  Jump out to it; you'll just barely make it.

Open the chest for a red rupee.

facts.subject: Tunnel above ladder
facts.text: Throwing a nearly exploding Bomb Flower at the wall above the ladder blasts open a seal leading to a tunnel to the next room.

evidence.quote:
Grab the Bomb Flower, and hold onto it until
it is almost ready to explode.  Then, throw it at the wall above the ladder to
blast open the seal.  Once the seal is destroyed, jump out to the opened tunnel
and run through the tunnel to the next room.

facts.subject: Golden eye
facts.text: Shooting the golden eye above the circle of flames with the Slingshot extinguishes the ring of fire in the Solo Eye Room.

evidence.quote:
Shoot the golden eye above the circle of flames with your Slingshot, and the
ring of fire will disappear.  Jump across the now flame-free platform to the
other side, and through the tunnel.

facts.subject: Lizalfos
facts.text: Defeat the two Lizalfos in the upper level of the Lizalfos Nest by blocking attacks with the shield and using Jump Attacks to open the west door.

evidence.quote:
Kill the Lizalfos exactly how you did
before; wait for the Lizalfos to come to you, block their attacks with the
Turtle Shield technique, and attack with Jump Attacks.  Once both of the
Lizalfos are dead, the door to the west will open.

facts.subject: Golden eyes
facts.text: In the Double Eye Room, shoot the eye on the high wall with the Slingshot to extinguish the first flame, jump to the platform, and shoot the second eye in the alcove to extinguish the second flame.

evidence.quote:
Begin by shooting the eye on the high wall, above the flames.  The
first ring of flames will disappear.  Jump out to the platform, and look to the
left to see another golden eye in an alcove.  Shoot this with your Slingshot as
well, and the second ring of flames will disappear, leaving you free to jump
the rest of the way across.

facts.subject: Chest
facts.text: In the upper area of the Blade Trap Room, opening the chest on an upper ledge awards the Bomb Bag with 20 Bombs.

evidence.quote:
Jump across the gap, and
turn to the right to see a chest on an upper ledge.  Jump up to the ledge and
open the chest to find the Bomb Bag, which contains 20 Bombs.

facts.subject: Business Scrub
facts.text: Behind a sealed wall in the passage is a room containing a Business Scrub who sells Deku Sticks for fifteen rupees.

evidence.quote:
Behind it
is a door to a room which contains a lousy Business Scrub who sells Deku Sticks
for fifteen rupees a pop.

facts.subject: Armos Statue
facts.text: Pulling the Armos Statue on the south side of the pillar reveals a ladder behind it.

evidence.quote:
Go around to the south side of the pillar, and note the
ladder behind the Armos Statue.  Pull the Armos Statue away from the ladder,
and be careful not to touch any of the other statues - they are actually Armos
Knights in disguise.

facts.subject: floating pillar
facts.text: Stepping onto the switch directly in front of the upper level entrance causes a floating pillar below to rise to the top, providing access to the upper level of the dungeon.

evidence.quote: Step onto the switch directly in front of you, and one of the floating pillars below will rise to the top, giving you access to the upper level of the dungeon should you fall.

facts.subject: giant Dodongo's skull
facts.text: Dropping bombs through the catwalk gaps into both of the giant Dodongo skull's eye sockets causes the skull to open its mouth, granting access to the final area of the dungeon.

evidence.quote: Using your new bombs, drop bombs through the gaps in the catwalk so that they land in the giant Dodongo's skulls eye sockets (press the C-Button assigned to Bombs twice to drop bombs).  Igniting blasts in both eye sockets will cause the skull to open it's mouth, letting you access the last area of the dungeon.

facts.subject: chest
facts.text: A chest behind a sealed wall at the end of the catwalk contains a replacement Deku Shield, or a blue rupee if Link already has one.

evidence.quote: Before you drop down and enter the Dodongo's mouth, run to the end of the catwalk and blow open the sealed wall.  Open the chest for a replacement Deku Shield, or a blue rupee if you still have your old one.

facts.subject: Dodongo's mouth
facts.text: Entering the giant Dodongo's mouth on the central platform in the Antechamber leads inside to the next door.

evidence.quote: Drop down to the central platform in the Antechamber and enter the Dodongo's mouth.  Enter the door inside.

facts.subject: Fire Keese
facts.text: Fire Keese flap around the large pit area in the Back Room.

evidence.quote: Drop down into the large pit area.  Kill the Fire Keese flapping around the room, then climb up the ledge to the east.

facts.subject: darkened tunnel
facts.text: Climbing up the ledge to the east and running through the darkened tunnel leads to the Goron Graveyard.

evidence.quote: Drop down into the large pit area.  Kill the Fire Keese flapping around the room, then climb up the ledge to the east.  Run through the darkened tunnel to the next room.

facts.subject: Fire Keese
facts.text: Two Fire Keese swoop into the pit on the other side of the tunnel in Goron Graveyard.

evidence.quote: Jump down into the pit on the other side of the tunnel, and watch out for the two Fire Keese who will come swooping in.

facts.subject: sealed wall
facts.text: Dropping a bomb next to the sealed wall in the pit breaks it open to reveal a door.

evidence.quote: There is a sealed wall here.  Climb up next to it and drop a bomb next to the wall to break it open.  Go through the door on the other side.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is located behind an Armos Knight statue and can be killed with the Slingshot to collect its token.

evidence.quote: This room contains a single Gold Skulltula, behind an Armos Knight statue.  Normally, you'd have to kill the Armos Knight to reach the Gold Skulltula, but not so this time.  Kill the Gold Skulltula with your Slingshot, then carefully move forward to grab the token without touching the Knight.

facts.subject: Armos Knight
facts.text: If accidentally brushed against, the Armos Knight can be defeated using Bombs.

evidence.quote: If you do accidentally brush against the Armos Knight, use your Bombs to defeat him.

facts.subject: pots
facts.text: Breaking the pots in the pit at the end of the ledge yields recovery items and a Fairy.

evidence.quote: Run to the end of the ledge, and jump down into the pit.  Break the pots to find recovery items and a Fairy (put it in a bottle if you have a spare).

facts.subject: western door
facts.text: Pushing the brown stone block into the opening in the center of the floor unlocks the western door.

evidence.quote: Once it's far enough away that you can move around to it's other side, push the block into the opening in the floor in center of the room, and the western door will unlock.

facts.subject: chest
facts.text: A chest on the far end of the room contains Bombs.

evidence.quote: Open the chest on the other end of the room to get some Bombs, then drop a Bomb onto the iron plate in the middle of the room.

facts.subject: iron plate
facts.text: Dropping a Bomb onto the iron plate in the center of the room causes it to disintegrate, allowing access to the pit below.

evidence.quote: Open the chest on the other end of the room to get some Bombs, then drop a Bomb onto the iron plate in the middle of the room.  After the bomb explodes, the plate will disintegrate, letting you drop down the pit into the room below.

facts.subject: King Dodongo
facts.text: Throwing a Bomb into King Dodongo's mouth while he inhales stuns him, making him vulnerable to a sword Jump Attack.

evidence.quote: In order to damage him, you must wait for him to begin inhaling in the first phase, and quickly throw a Bomb into his mouth.  The bomb will explode in his stomach, stunning the King Dodongo for a few seconds.  You are given only one sword swing when he is stunned, so make it a Jump Attack.

facts.subject: King Dodongo
facts.text: Standing on the edge of the lava or in one of the room's corners avoids King Dodongo's rolling attack during his second phase.

evidence.quote: After you have hurt Dodongo, he will begin his second phase.  Stand on the edge of the lava or in one of the corners of the room to avoid his rolling attack.

facts.subject: King Dodongo
facts.text: King Dodongo will die after taking three Jump Attacks or six normal sword attacks.

evidence.quote: After three Jump Attacks or six normal sword attacks, King Dodongo will die.

facts.subject: King Dodongo
facts.text: King Dodongo leaves behind a Heart Container upon defeat.

evidence.quote: Grab the Heart Container he leaves behind, and enter the ring of light to warp back outside, where Darunia will give you the Goron's Ruby, and make you an official Blood Brother.

facts.subject: Darunia
facts.text: After defeating King Dodongo and entering the ring of light, Darunia rewards Link with the Goron's Ruby and makes him an official Blood Brother.

evidence.quote: Grab the Heart Container he leaves behind, and enter the ring of light to warp back outside, where Darunia will give you the Goron's Ruby, and make you an official Blood Brother.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Blasting open an oddly-colored section of wall with a Bomb reveals a Gold Skulltula that can be killed with the Slingshot to collect its token.

evidence.quote: Kill the Tektites, then look for the oddly-shaped and oddly-colored bit of wall.  Use a Bomb to blast open the wall, then use the Slingshot to kill the Gold Skulltula on the inside.  The wall is climbable; climb up it to grab the Token.

facts.subject: chest
facts.text: Blowing open another odd wall section past the Red Flag reveals a chest containing a 50 rupee piece.

evidence.quote: Turn right at the Red Flag, and keep heading for Goron City.  You'll find another odd part of wall identical to the one that hid the Gold Skulltula.  Blow it open if you like, but don't open the chest inside unless you need rupees - it contains a 50 rupee piece.

facts.subject: chests
facts.text: The chests at the end of the boulder maze contain two fifty rupee pieces.

evidence.quote: The chests contains two more fifty rupee pieces - save them for later if your Adult's Wallet is maxed.

facts.subject: crate
facts.text: Rolling into the crate at the end of the boulder maze exposes a Gold Skulltula that yields a token.

evidence.quote: Roll into the crate here to destroy it, and kill the Gold Skulltula that appears.  Take it's token, and return to the main part of Goron City.

facts.subject: Biggoron
facts.text: Stopping the rolling Biggoron with a bomb inside the northern tunnel on the third floor rewards the Bomb Bag x30.

evidence.quote: Drop down to the third level of the city (the level directly beneath the top floor), where there is a Biggoron rolling around the level in a giant loop.  You can stop him by placing a bomb in his path so that it explodes just as he passes over it.  If you do this while he is passing through the tunnel in the northern part of the third floor, then he will give you the Bomb Bag x30 as a reward for your daring.
blast the rolling Goron and...he will upgrade you to the big one

facts.subject: giant pot
facts.text: Throwing a bomb into the rotating giant pot so that it lands inside and stops on the happy face rewards a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: From the second level, you can throw bombs into the giant pot.  If you successfully land a bomb inside the pot, then it will begin to spin rapidly, finally coming to a stop.  If it stops on the side with the happy face, then you will get a Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: secret passage
facts.text: A secret passage on the second level of Goron City leads directly to the Lost Woods.

evidence.quote: Once you have the Piece of Heart, climb back up to the second level of Goron City and use the secret passage to go to the Lost Woods.

facts.subject: Cow
facts.text: A pit hidden beneath the boulder at the top of the ledges contains a Cow that replenishes Milk when Epona's Song is played.

evidence.quote: The last boulder at the top of the ledges hides a pit, which contains, among other things, a Cow which you can use to replenish your supply of Milk (play Epona's Song).

facts.subject: volcano eruptions
facts.text: Crouching under the Hylian Shield with R absorbs damage when shadows appear from falling volcanic lava.

evidence.quote: After a short distance, the volcano will begin erupting, spewing lava down onto you.  When you see the shadow beneath you, hide under the Hylian Shield with R to absorb the damage.

facts.subject: Kaepora Gaebora
facts.text: Kaepora Gaebora waits at the highest peak of Death Mountain and offers a ride back down to Kakariko Village if spoken to.

evidence.quote: Kaepora Gaebora waits for you here.  DO NOT SPEAK TO HIM.  If you do, he'll give you a ride back down the mountain to Kakariko Village, which you don't want to do just yet.

facts.subject: oddly-colored wall cave
facts.text: Bombing the oddly-colored wall to the left of Kaepora Gaebora opens an entrance to a cave.

evidence.quote: Bomb the oddly-colored wall to the left of KG, and enter the cave.

facts.subject: Business Scrub
facts.text: In a hidden pit beneath a boulder, a defeated Business Scrub will increase the number of Deku Nuts Link can carry for forty rupees.

evidence.quote: Use a Bomb to blow up the boulder in the corner of this crossroads.  Drop down the pit, and defeat both of the Business Scrubs inside with your Slingshot.  One of them will increase the number of Deku Nuts you can carry for forty rupees.

facts.subject: Great Fairy
facts.text: Playing Zelda's Lullaby on the Triforce emblem makes the Great Fairy appear to teach the Super Spin Attack and grant a Magic Meter.

evidence.quote:
Run forward to the fountain, and stand on the Triforce emblem.  Play Zelda's
Lullaby to make the Dominatrix er, uh... Great Fairy appear.  She will teach
you the Super Spin Attack, which adds extra damage and range to your basic Spin
Attack.  She'll also grant you a Magic Meter.

facts.subject: Death Mountain Trail
facts.text: A cave entrance to the right of Kaepora Gaebora leads into Death Mountain Crater.

evidence.quote: Enter the cave face to the right of KG.

facts.subject: Death Mountain Crater
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is found inside the crates to the left immediately upon entering Death Mountain Crater.

evidence.quote:
For the moment, smash both of the crates to your left as
soon as you enter to find a Gold Skulltula.  Kill it and take it's token, then
go back out to the Trail.

facts.subject: Kaepora Gaebora
facts.text: Speaking with Kaepora Gaebora gives Link a flight down to Kakariko Village, dropping him onto Impa's House.

evidence.quote:
Speak with Kaepora Gaebora, who will give you a lift down the mountain to
Kakariko Village.

Kaepora Gaebora not only brought you back to Kakariko Village... he even
dropped you on top of Impa's House!

facts.subject: Impa's House
facts.text: Dropping down from the roof of Impa's House onto the balcony above the Cucco Pasture leads to a Piece of Heart inside.

evidence.quote:
If you didn't get the Piece
of Heart from inside of Impa's House, then get it now by dropping down from the
roof onto the balcony above the Cucco Pasture.

facts.subject: Sun's Song
facts.text: Playing the Sun's Song warps Link back to the top of Impa's House roof if the balcony drop is missed.

evidence.quote:
If you miss it, then play the
Sun's Song and you'll warp back to the top of the roof.

facts.subject: House of Skulltula
facts.text: A decursed man on the left side of the House of Skulltula rewards Link with the Stone of Agony.

evidence.quote:
Go to the left side of the room, where a recently-decursed man will give you
the Stone of Agony.

facts.subject: Hyrule Castle
facts.text: Playing the Sun's Song at nighttime opens the gates of Hyrule Castle.

evidence.quote:
If it is nighttime,
play the Sun's Song to open the gates.

facts.subject: Hyrule Castle Garden
facts.text: Climbing ivy above the gate and bombing a boulder at the dead end reveals a crawl tunnel to a Great Fairy's Fountain.

evidence.quote:
Climb the ivy on the right to the cliff above the gate.  Run over to the marble
gate, and drop down on the other side.  Run over to the dead end (it's marked
with a sign which reads "Dead End").  Bomb the boulder to reveal a small
tunnel.  Crawl through the tunnel to find another Great Fairy's Fountain.

facts.subject: Great Fairy
facts.text: Playing Zelda's Lullaby on the Triforce emblem in the Hyrule Castle Great Fairy's Fountain grants Din's Fire.

evidence.quote:
Run to the Fountain, and stand on the Triforce Emblem.  Play Zelda's Lullaby on
the Ocarina to make another Dominatrix appear.  She'll give you Din's Fire, an
area of effect spell which burns all enemies in the room (and can also light
large numbers of braziers at the same time).

facts.subject: Hyrule Castle Garden
facts.text: Getting spotted by a guard in the Hyrule Castle Garden causes Link to be thrown back out to the gate.

evidence.quote:
Allow one of the guards to spot you, and you will be thrown back out to the
gate.

facts.subject: Bombchu Bowling Alley
facts.text: Playing a game at the Bombchu Bowling Alley costs 30 rupees.

evidence.quote: Pay the clerk 30 rupees to play the game.

facts.subject: Bombchu Bowling Alley
facts.text: The Bombchu Bowling Alley minigame offers a Piece of Heart, Bomb Bag upgrade, and Bombchus as winnable prizes.

evidence.quote:
This minigame has no less then three new things to win (Piece of Heart, Bomb
Bag and Bombchus), and isn't cheap to play.

facts.subject: Bombchu Bowling Alley
facts.text: Completing all three goals in Bombchu Bowling can award a Bomb Bag holding up to 40 bombs.

evidence.quote:
New Equipment: Bomb Bag x40...Completing all
three goals successfully will win you whatever prize the clerk showed you at
the start.

facts.subject: Bombchu Bowling Alley
facts.text: Completing all three rounds of Bombchu Bowling can reward Link with Bombchus.

evidence.quote:
New Item: Bombchus...Completing all
three goals successfully will win you whatever prize the clerk showed you at
the start.

facts.subject: Bombchu Bowling Alley
facts.text: In Bombchu Bowling, send a Bombchu straight from the middle for central targets, but adjust position to the left or right when the round 2 target appears on the right.

evidence.quote:
When you're playing Bombchu Bowling, always position yourself in the center of
the field.  The one exception is when the target appears on the right in the
second round; you have to minorly adjust your position to the left or right,  otherwise it's impossible to angle yourself properly for the Bombchu to enter
the target.

facts.subject: Happy Mask Shop
facts.text: Link must pay 20 rupees for the Skull Mask before borrowing the Spooky Mask from the Happy Mask Shop.

evidence.quote: Pay the 20 rupees for the Skull Mask, then borrow the Spooky Mask.

facts.subject: Dampe's Fanboy
facts.text: Speaking to the boy wandering Kakariko Graveyard during daytime while wearing the Spooky Mask prompts him to buy it for 30 rupees.

evidence.quote:
Speak with Dampe's
Fanboy (the little kid who walks around the graves during the day) while
wearing the Spooky Mask, and he'll buy it from you for 30 rupees.

facts.subject: Happy Mask Shop
facts.text: Paying 30 rupees for the Spooky Mask allows Link to borrow the Bunny Hood from the Happy Mask Shop.

evidence.quote: Pay the 30 rupees for the Spooky Mask, then borrow the Bunny Hood.

facts.subject: Forest Temple
facts.text: The Forest Temple is located in the Lost Woods.

evidence.quote: In the densely forested Lost Woods, there is the Forest Temple.

facts.subject: Fire Temple
facts.text: The Fire Temple is located in the midst of Death Mountain Crater.

evidence.quote: In the midst of the burning embers of Death Mountain Crater, there is the Fire Temple.

facts.subject: Water Temple
facts.text: The Water Temple is located underneath the surface of Lake Hylia.

evidence.quote: Underneath the surface of Lake Hylia is the Water Temple.

facts.subject: Shadow Temple
facts.text: The Shadow Temple is buried beneath the Kakariko Graveyard.

evidence.quote: Buried beneath the Kakariko Graveyard is the Shadow Temple.

facts.subject: Spirit Temple
facts.text: The Spirit Temple is located deep within the Gerudo Desert.

evidence.quote: Deep within the rugged Gerudo Desert is the Spirit Temple.

facts.subject: Inside the Deku Tree
facts.text: Inside the Deku Tree, players must climb down to the tree's roots to defeat the parasite sapping its strength.

evidence.quote: In the game's first dungeon, Inside the Deku Tree, players must open up passages in the Deku Tree's main chamber, climbing from the Tree's top to it's bottom, finally reaching the Tree's roots and defeating the parasite that is sapping it's strength.

facts.subject: Dodongo's Cavern
facts.text: In Dodongo's Cavern, players must reach the top of a giant Dodongo skull and open its mouth to reach King Dodongo.

evidence.quote: In Dodongo's Cavern, players must climb to the top of a massive Dodongo's skull and force it's mouth open, opening a passage to the King Dodongo.

facts.subject: Jabu-Jabu's Belly
facts.text: In Jabu-Jabu's Belly, players must destroy parasitic tentacles to reveal a path to the parasite in the brain.

evidence.quote: In Jabu-Jabu's Belly, players must destroy parasitic tentacles that sap Jabu-Jabu's strength, finally revealing a path to the parasite in Jabu-Jabu's brain.

facts.subject: Forest Temple
facts.text: In the Forest Temple, defeating four Poes that stole magic flames opens the passage to the boss chamber.

evidence.quote: In the Forest Temple, players must track down and kill four elusive Poes who have stolen magic flames, which open the passage to the boss chamber.

facts.subject: Fire Temple
facts.text: In the Fire Temple, players must climb to the top of the structure to create a bridge leading to the boss.

evidence.quote: In the Fire Temple, players must climb clear to the top of the massive structure, in order to create a bridge to the boss at the bottom of the Temple.

facts.subject: Water Temple
facts.text: In the Water Temple, players must raise and lower the water level to access different areas of the dungeon.

evidence.quote: In the Water Temple, players must proactively raise and lower the water level in the Temple in order to reach the different areas of the dungeon (a Temple which, may I add, has irked Ocarina players for over a decade).

facts.subject: Shadow Temple
facts.text: In the Shadow Temple, players must navigate through wide expanses filled with deadly traps.

evidence.quote: In the Shadow Temple, players must cross great expanses of deadly traps in an almost Indiana Jones-esque environment.

facts.subject: Spirit Temple
facts.text: Completing both wings of the Spirit Temple requires traveling through time.

evidence.quote: In the Spirit Temple, players have to travel through time in order to complete both wings of the dungeon.

facts.subject: Ganon's Castle
facts.text: In Ganon's Castle, players must break the six seals located in the Keep.

evidence.quote: And lastly, in Ganon's Castle, players must destroy the six Seals in the Keep.

facts.subject: Link
facts.text: Opening the Door of Time and pulling the Master Sword transforms Young Link into Adult Link seven years in the future.

evidence.quote: After opening the Door of Time and drawing the Master Sword from it's pedestal, Young Link immediately finds himself awakening seven years in the future, and he has become a full-grown Adult.

facts.subject: Temple of Time
facts.text: Link can travel between childhood and adulthood by visiting the Temple of Time with the Master Sword and Ocarina of Time.

evidence.quote: What's more, thanks to the magic of the Master Sword and the Ocarina of Time, Link gains the ability to travel back and forth between his childhood and his adulthood, simply by visiting the Temple of Time.

facts.subject: Magic Bean
facts.text: Actions taken as child Link, such as planting magic beans, directly influence the future.

evidence.quote: Actions that Link performs as a child, be it planting a magic bean, uncovering a new item, or forging a special bond with a denizen of Hyrule directly affect the future.

facts.subject: Bombchus
facts.text: Bombchus crawl along walls and ceilings in a straight line before exploding.

evidence.quote: New items in the series include the unorthodox and under-utilized Bombchus (which crawl along walls and ceilings in a straight line before finally exploding)...

facts.subject: Lens of Truth
facts.text: The Lens of Truth reveals invisible objects and causes illusory surfaces to disappear.

evidence.quote: ...and the Lens of Truth (which reveals things for what they truly are, making the invisible visible, and the fake disappear).

facts.subject: Tunics
facts.text: Different tunics allow Link to breathe underwater or endure intense heat, and can be swapped at any time.

evidence.quote: In Ocarina, new tunics grant Link the ability to breath underwater or withstand tremendous heat, and the player can change between available tunics at will.

facts.subject: Kokiri Sword
facts.text: The Kokiri Sword is the only sword small enough for Young Link to equip.

evidence.quote: The Kokiri Sword, which is little more then a large knife, is the only weapon small enough for Young Link to brandish.

facts.subject: Biggoron's Sword
facts.text: The Biggoron's Sword is a two-handed blade that prevents Adult Link from using a shield and cannot be swung in narrow halls.

evidence.quote: The Biggoron's Sword, on the other hand, is so massive that Adult Link can't use a shield while wielding it, and has such a wide reach that the blade is impossible to use in narrow corridors.

facts.subject: Hylian Shield
facts.text: Young Link cannot wield the Hylian Shield normally and instead crouches beneath it like a shell.

evidence.quote: Even the way Young Link and Adult Link use the Hylian Shield is markedly different. Though both can equip the shield, it is too big for Young Link to actually use, and he instead has to resort to hiding under it like a shell.

facts.subject: Zelda's Lullaby
facts.text: Zelda's Lullaby proves Link's royal allegiance to the Gorons and Zoras, and activates secrets in adult dungeons.

evidence.quote: One of the first songs you learn, Zelda's Lullaby, is used by Young Link to show his allegiance to the Hyrule Royal Family to the Gorons and Zoras, and is later used by Adult Link in the dungeons and other hidden locations of Hyrule.

facts.subject: Epona's Song
facts.text: Playing Epona's Song is the only method to acquire Link's horse, Epona.

evidence.quote: Epona's Song is the only way to obtain Epona, Link's legendary horse.

facts.subject: Sun's Song
facts.text: The Sun's Song changes day into night and night into day.

evidence.quote: The Sun's Song possesses the power to turn day into night, and night into day.

facts.subject: Song of Storms
facts.text: The Song of Storms calls down a rainstorm at Link's current position.

evidence.quote: The Song of Storm's can summon storms to Link's location.

facts.subject: Ocarina
facts.text: Playing songs on the Ocarina allows Link to warp instantly across different destinations in Hyrule.

evidence.quote: But the Ocarina is used more then to just play music; later, he can use it to travel instantaneously between different locations in Hyrule.

facts.subject: Z-Targeting
facts.text: Navi enables Z-Targeting to lock Link's view onto a single foe and swap his controls for battle.

evidence.quote: Navi nevertheless performs a pivotal action in the game: Z-Targeting....Z-Targeting allows Link to focus his attention on a single target, and radically alters his moveset to focus on combat.

facts.subject: Z-Targeting Jump Attacks
facts.text: While Z-Targeted, the A button strafes left or right, executes a backflip when moving backward, or unleashes a Jump Attack when tilting forward.

evidence.quote: While Z-Targeted, however, it causes Link to perform different jumping actions. Jumping to the left or right will strafe in a circle around the enemy, while a backwards jump will make Link do a backflip. A jump while holding forward causes Link to perform the Jump Attack, the most powerful attack in his repertoire.

facts.subject: Shield Mobility
facts.text: Holding the R button while Z-Targeted allows Link to keep moving while guarding with his shield.

evidence.quote: While in free-form camera mode, the R Button activates Link's shield. However, it also makes him completely stationary. While Z-Targeted, however, holding the R button will tell Link to raise his shield, but he still maintains his mobility.

facts.subject: Z-Targeting Sword Strikes
facts.text: While Z-Targeted, tapping the B Button causes Link to perform a downward plunge attack, while holding forward and B causes him to stab.

evidence.quote:
While in free-
form mode, tapping the B Button will cause Link to perform a sideways, sweeping
attack.  While Z-Targeted, however, this attack becomes a downward plunge.
Holding forward and B will cause Link to stab, or a whole new assortment of
cool attacks.

facts.subject: Zora's River
facts.text: The entrance to Zora's River is a small passage located at the 2:00 position in Hyrule Field, upstream from Kakariko Village.

evidence.quote: We're now headed for Zora's River. It's a small passage at the 2:00 position in Hyrule Field, a short ways upstream from Kakariko Village.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Rolling into the tree near the entrance of Zora's River makes a Gold Skulltula appear, which drops a token when killed.

evidence.quote: After he's gone, roll into the tree to make a Gold Skulltula appear. Kill it and take it's Token, then bomb the stones blocking the path.

facts.subject: Stones
facts.text: Bombs are required to clear the stones blocking the path upstream in Zora's River.

evidence.quote: Kill it and take it's Token, then bomb the stones blocking the path.

facts.subject: Bean Man
facts.text: The Bean Man near the iron gate in Zora's River sells Magic Beans that become progressively more expensive.

evidence.quote: Speak to the fat slob-like guy, and buy as many Magic Beans from him as you can. They become progressively more expensive as you buy more; just keep buying them until you go broke.

facts.subject: Magic Beans
facts.text: A Magic Bean can be planted in the patch of soft earth next to the Bean Man in Zora's River.

evidence.quote: Plant one of the Magic Beans in the patch of soft earth next to the Bean Man.

facts.subject: Musical Frogs
facts.text: Playing Zelda's Lullaby, Epona's Song, The Sun's Song, or Saria's Song while standing on the white circle of the log awards fifty rupees per song from the frogs.

evidence.quote: Play the Frogs each of the four songs that you have learned so far (Zelda's Lullaby, Epona's Song, The Sun's Song and Saria's Song). The frogs will award you with fifty rupees for each song.

facts.subject: Tall Pillar
facts.text: A Piece of Heart rests on a tall pillar in Zora's River, reached by gliding with a Cucco from the cliff with the Gossip Stone.

evidence.quote: Jump over to the cliff with the Gossip Stone on it, then turn to the west to see the tall pillar with the Piece of Heart on it. You'll have to jump out with the Cucco, and land on the pillar to get the Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Waterfall Path
facts.text: A Piece of Heart is reached near the large waterfall in Zora's River by gliding out with a Cucco.

evidence.quote: Look to the left, and you will see another Piece of Heart. Leap off with the Cucco over your head, and you will glide out to the Piece of Heart (which should complete your eighth Heart Container).

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: At night, a Gold Skulltula climbs on a ladder rising from the river bed to the zigzagging path in Zora's River and can be killed with the Slingshot for a token.

evidence.quote: If it's daytime, play the Sun's Song to make it night (time passes normally in this zone, so you won't warp back to the entrance). From the platform that you picked the Piece of Heart from, drop straight down, where you will see a ladder rising from the river bed to the zigzagging path. A Gold Skulltula climbs on it. Kill the Skulltula with the Slingshot, and climb up the ladder to take it's Token.

facts.subject: Waterfall
facts.text: Playing Zelda's Lullaby on the plaque before the waterfall retracts the water and opens the entrance to Zora's Domain.

evidence.quote: From the top of the ladder, go around the zigzagging path, and stand on the plaque before the waterfall. Play Zelda's Lullaby, and the waterfall will retract, letting you access the doorway behind it. Jump over to the doorway and go through to enter Zora's Domain.

facts.subject: Waterfall Alcove
facts.text: Lighting all the torches and braziers in Zora's Domain before any burn out reveals a chest behind the waterfall containing a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: Put away your Deku Stick, and run to the left to a small alcove behind the waterfall, where there are two more braziers. Use Din's Fire to light them both. If you did it fast enough so that you lit all the braziers without any of them burning out, then a chest will appear behind the Waterfall which contains a Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Diving Minigame
facts.text: Completing the Diving Minigame for 20 rupees by collecting all the rupees thrown off the waterfall rewards the Silver Scale, doubling Link's dive depth.

evidence.quote: Play the Diving Minigame with him for 20 rupees (you need it's reward, the Silver Scale, to progress)... Once you have grabbed all of the rupees from around the waterfall, the Zora will call down for you to return to him and he'll give you a reward. He'll give you the Silver Scale, which doubles how deep you can go in a single dive.

facts.subject: Underwater Tunnel
facts.text: Diving into the underwater tunnel south of the waterfall in Zora's Domain warps Link to Lake Hylia.

evidence.quote: There is a tunnel under the water here. Dive down and enter this tunnel to warp to Lake Hylia.

facts.subject: Lake Floor
facts.text: A Bottle containing Princess Ruto's Letter rests on the floor of Lake Hylia near a ruined pillar south of the tunnel exit.

evidence.quote: On the floor of the lake, near a ruined pillar, there is a Bottle. Dive down and grab it. You'll find that the Bottle already contains a Letter! This is actually the SOS sent by the Princess Ruto, who is trapped inside Lord Jabu Jabu, the Zora demigod.

facts.subject: Scarecrow
facts.text: Playing an eight-note song with at least two different notes on the Ocarina for the Scarecrow in the lower garden teaches it a custom tune.

evidence.quote: Show the Scarecrow in the lower garden your Ocarina, and he'll ask you to play a song for him. Play the easiest eight-note song you can come up with, and don't play any of the songs you have learned or will learn later. Make sure the song has at least two different notes. Write this song down somewhere; you're going to need it later.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Releasing a Bug onto the patch of soft earth near the tall building in Lake Hylia reveals a Gold Skulltula that drops a token.

evidence.quote: Head west to the tall building, and look for a patch of soft earth near it. Release a Bug from your Bottle near the patch of earth (remember to recapture one), and kill the Gold Skulltula that appears. Take it's token, then plant one of your Magic Beans.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula appears at night on the small island with two pillars east of the dead tree in Lake Hylia.

evidence.quote: Look east from the tree, and you'll see a small island with two pillars on it. Swim out to this island, and change the time to nighttime. A Gold Skulltulla will appear. Kill it and take it's Token.

facts.subject: Island Door
facts.text: A door built into the wall on the small island to the north in Lake Hylia leads to the Fishing Pond.

evidence.quote: Look to the north, where you will see a small island. Swim to the island, and enter the door built into the wall.

facts.subject: Fishing Minigame
facts.text: Catching a fish of at least nine pounds in the Fishing Pond and showing it to the Clerk awards a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: In order to win the Piece of Heart, you have to capture a record breaking fish: nine pounds... Once you have captured a nine-pound fish (minimum), return to the Clerk and show him your fish. He'll give you a Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Fenced-in Corral
facts.text: Dropping a bomb in the center of the fenced-in corral near Lake Hylia in Hyrule Field reveals a hidden pit.

evidence.quote: After Kaepora Gaebora is done telling you what a Lake is, move to the exact center of the corral and drop a bomb to reveal a pit.

facts.subject: Business Scrub
facts.text: A defeated Business Scrub inside the secret pit in the Hyrule Field corral sells a Piece of Heart for ten rupees.

evidence.quote: Drop down into the pit that appears, and defeat the Business Scrub inside. The Scrub will offer to sell you a Piece of Heart for ten rupees. That's not a typo. Ten rupees. Buy the Heart Piece, then return to Hyrule Field.

facts.subject: Rocky Canyon
facts.text: Heading west through the canyon road from Hyrule Field leads to Gerudo Valley.

evidence.quote: After another meeting with Kaepora Gaebora, go west into a rocky, canyon-like area. Keep going west through the canyon until you reach the zone break to Gerudo Valley.

facts.subject: Wooden Crate
facts.text: A Piece of Heart is hidden inside a wooden crate on a platform across the canyon in Gerudo Valley, reached by gliding across with a Cucco.

evidence.quote: Look to the opposite side of the canyon, and try to spot a small platform with a wooden crate on it. Once you have found it, jump out to it with the Cucco... Grab the Piece of Heart that was in the crate, which will cause you to drop the Cucco again.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Releasing bugs near the patch of soft earth by the Cow at the bottom of the canyon in Gerudo Valley spawns a Gold Skulltula that yields a token.

evidence.quote: Head for the southern edge of this strip of land, look for the patch of soft earth near the Cow. Release some Bugs near the patch of soft earth. Remember to recapture one of the three bugs that comes out. Kill the Gold Skulltula that appears, and take it's Token.

facts.subject: Waterfall Ladder
facts.text: A Piece of Heart sits at the top of a ladder behind the waterfall at the bottom of Gerudo Valley, accessed using a Cucco.

evidence.quote: Look behind the waterfall, and you will see a ladder. Jump out to the ladder, and don't drop the Cucco until you're pressing your face right up next to it... Climb to the top of the ladder, where you will find another Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Submerged Ruins
facts.text: An underwater tunnel located in the submerged ruins in Lake Hylia leads back to Zora's Domain.

evidence.quote: Swim to the submerged ruins near the shore, to the east of the Observatory and the west of the Scarecrows. Dive into the water and swim into the tunnel to return to Zora's Domain.

facts.subject: King Zora
facts.text: Presenting the Bottled Letter to King Zora causes him to move aside, revealing the passage to Zora's Fountain.

evidence.quote: Return to King Zora's Throne Room, and show him the Bottled Letter. He'll then, uh... "move" aside, and beg Link to save his daughter from Jabu Jabu's Belly.

facts.subject: Shallow Water
facts.text: Fish swimming in the shallow water near the waterfall in Zora's Domain can be caught in an empty Bottle.

evidence.quote: For now, return to the bottom level of Zora's Domain, and go to the area of shallow water near the waterfall. Catch one of the fish who swim around here in an empty Bottle.

facts.subject: Throne Room Tunnel
facts.text: The tunnel behind King Zora's throne leads directly to Zora's Fountain.

evidence.quote: Go through the tunnel behind his throne to reach Zora's Fountain.

facts.subject: Super Cucco Catching
facts.text: The Super Cucco Catching minigame costs ten Rupees and requires finding all three Super Cuccos within thirty seconds.

evidence.quote: Speak with Talon and for ten Rupees you can challenge yourself to try to find all three Super Cuccos in thirty seconds.

facts.subject: Super Cucco Catching
facts.text: Finding all three Super Cuccos in the minigame rewards Link with Lon Lon Milk in an Empty Bottle.

evidence.quote: After you have located all three of the Super Cuccos, Talon will reward your with some LON LON MILK.
worth it but rather the EMPTY BOTTLE that you have after the milk is gone.

facts.subject: Treasure Chest
facts.text: Dropping into the hole behind the small fence leads to a small treasure chest containing a Red Rupee.

evidence.quote: Jump down behind you and you'll land beside a hole, drop down into the hole and open the small treasure chest to acquire a RED RUPEE.

facts.subject: Cucco Catching
facts.text: Returning all seven Cuccos to the pen for the woman in Kakariko Village rewards an Empty Bottle.

evidence.quote: Now all you have to do is find those two which you threw over the fence for later and that takes care of all seven.
Speak to the girl and she will reward you nicely with another EMPTY BOTTLE.

facts.subject: Bombchu Bowling Alley
facts.text: The Bombchu Bowling Alley opens in Hyrule Market after completing Dodongo's Cavern and costs 30 Rupees per game.

evidence.quote: After you have completed the Dodongo's Cavern the Bombchu Bowling Alley in Hyrule Market is open for business.  Each game costs 30 Rupees and you'll likely be playing a lot so be sure to bring a lot of money with you.

facts.subject: Bombchu Bowling Alley
facts.text: Randomized prizes available at the Bombchu Bowling Alley include Bombs, Purple Rupee, Bombchus, Piece of Heart, and the Biggest Bomb Bag.

evidence.quote: The prizes are Bombs, Purple Rupee, Bombchus, PIECE OF HEART [010] and BIGGEST BOMB BAG, the final two are obviously the ones you'll really be working toward.

facts.subject: Diving Game
facts.text: The Diving Game in Zora's Domain costs 20 Rupees and requires jumping down to collect all five Blue Rupees.

evidence.quote: You will have the option of playing the Diving Game for 20 Rupees.  The Diving Game is one of the easiest minigames ever, your goal is to jump down into the water and collect all five of the Blue Rupees.

facts.subject: Diving Game
facts.text: Successfully collecting all five Blue Rupees in the Diving Game rewards the Silver Scale, allowing Link to dive for six seconds.

evidence.quote: After successfully collecting all five Blue Rupees, head back up to where you started the game and speak to the Zora there once again.  The Zora will reward you with a SILVER SCALE which allows you to dive for six seconds rather than a mere three seconds, this means of course that you can go deeper as well.

facts.subject: Fishing Pond
facts.text: Catching a ten-pound fish as Young Link in the Lake Hylia Fishing Pond awards a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: Once you eventually catch this fish go back and talk to the guy at the counter, as a reward for the ten pound fish you get PIECE OF HEART [014].

facts.subject: Fishing Pond
facts.text: Catching a fish of at least fifteen pounds as Adult Link at the Fishing Pond rewards the Golden Scale, extending dive time to nine seconds.

evidence.quote: This fish should be at least fifteen pounds or more, which will net you the reward GOLDEN SCALE
and allow you to dive underwater for nine seconds as opposed to six.

facts.subject: Deku Scrub
facts.text: Wearing the Skull Mask in the hidden hole past the right, left, right, left, left path in the Lost Woods prompts the Deku Scrub to grant a Deku Stick upgrade.

evidence.quote: Make a right at the beginning, then a left, then a right, then a left and then a left... Speak with the Deku Scrub on your right in order to get the next DEKU STICK UPGRADE.

facts.subject: Happy Mask Shop
facts.text: Selling the Bunny Hood to the running man at Lon Lon Ranch and returning to the shop unlocks the Mask of Truth, allowing Link to hear rumors from Gossip Stones.

evidence.quote: There is also a special bonus, you are now free to borrow the MASK OF TRUTH whenever you want to.  The Mask of Truth allows you to listen to all those Gossip Stones placed conveniently around the world, before they really didn't do anything.

facts.subject: Ingo Horse Race
facts.text: Challenging Ingo to a horse race costs a bet of 50 Rupees.

evidence.quote:
Speak to Ingo and he will ask if you want to bet 
50 Rupees on a race, you certainly do.

facts.subject: Obstacle Course
facts.text: Beating the Lon Lon Ranch obstacle course with a time of 0:49 or better rewards Link with a cow delivered to his house in Kokiri Forest.

evidence.quote:
speak to Malon two times, she will offer to let you race 
and obstacle course.  The time to beat is 50 Seconds...Assuming you 
get a time of 0:49 or better then Malon will give you a present...The present 
is in fact a whole cow that now lives in your house in Kokiri Forest.

facts.subject: Dampe's Race
facts.text: Finishing the race against Dampe's ghost under the grave next to the magic bean sprout in Kakariko Village Graveyard awards the Hookshot.

evidence.quote:
Head to the Kakariko Village Graveyard as Adult Link and move the tombstone 
next to the magic bean sprout.  You will reveal a hole that you can drop down 
and find Dampe's ghost there.  Agree to race him and you have two goals, 
finish the race to get the HOOKSHOT and finish the race in under one minute to 
get the PIECE OF HEART [019].

facts.subject: Dampe's Race
facts.text: Finishing Dampe's race in under one minute awards a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote:
finish the race in under one minute to 
get the PIECE OF HEART [019].

facts.subject: Big Poe
facts.text: Catching Big Poes requires riding Epona and using the Fairy Bow.

evidence.quote:
First of all, in order to catch the Big Poes you must be riding Epona and you 
must have the Fairy Bow.

facts.subject: Ghost Shop
facts.text: The ghost shop owner at the entrance to Hyrule Castle Town awards 100 points per Big Poe and requires 1000 points from ten Big Poes for his special prize.

evidence.quote:
He says that you'll 
get a special prize once you reach 1000 points, and since each Poe nets you 
100 points, that means you must collect a total of ten.

facts.subject: Big Poe
facts.text: The tenth Big Poe appears when riding past a lone tree located north of the path fork southeast of Gerudo Valley.

evidence.quote:
north of that fork there 
is a lone tree and when you ride past this tree, the tenth BIG POE will appear 
and allow you to capture it.

facts.subject: Ghost Shop
