facts.text: Playing a game at the Bombchu Bowling Alley costs 30 Rupees and gives 10 Bombchus to aim at the target holes.

evidence.quote: It takes 30 Rupees to play a game, and you have 10 Bombchus to play with. Basically Bombchus are mobile bombs that scurry along the ground until they blow up. You have to place a Bombchu appropriately so that they run over the hole in the wall (they blow up on contact with the hole).

facts.subject: Biri
facts.text: Biri should only be attacked from a distance, because touching it with a sword electrocutes Link.

evidence.quote: Only attack it from a distance. Even touching it with your sword electrocutes you.

facts.subject: Blue Tektite
facts.text: A Blue Tektite is capable of standing on the surface of water.

evidence.quote: This is a Tektite that's able to stand on the surface of water.

facts.subject: Dark Link
facts.text: Dark Link serves as the mini-boss of the Water Temple and can eventually be defeated by slashing him without targeting.

evidence.quote: Dark Link: MINI-BOSS OF THE WATER TEMPLE...Just slash him without targeting him and he'll eventually go down.

facts.subject: Dead Hand
facts.text: Dead Hand is lured to the surface by getting caught in one of its hands, allowing Link to slash its head when lowered.

evidence.quote: Dead Hand: BOSS OF THE BOTTOM OF THE WELL, MINI-BOSS OF THE SHADOW TEMPLE...Get caught in one of its hands to lure it to the surface, then slash its head when it lowers it.

facts.subject: Deku Baba
facts.text: Killing a Deku Baba by slashing its head always drops Deku Nuts.

evidence.quote: If the Deku Baba is killed by slashes to the head, it always drops Deku Nuts.

facts.subject: Deku Baba
facts.text: Cutting a Deku Baba by its stalk during its non-aggressive state causes it to always drop Deku Sticks.

evidence.quote: If it's cut by the stalk during its non-aggressive state, it will always drop Deku Sticks.

facts.subject: Deku Scrub
facts.text: Deku Scrubs are vulnerable to being slashed after deflecting the Deku Nuts they fire back at them with a shield.

evidence.quote: They can't be sword-slashed up close, so you have to deflect the Nuts it fires by shielding. After getting hit with its own Nut, it runs around, allowing you to slash it to kill it. Some Deku Scrubs tell you important information in an attempt for you to spare them.

facts.subject: Dodongo
facts.text: Dodongos are vulnerable at the tail when hopped behind after their fire breath attack.

evidence.quote: Their weakness is the tail. Wait until they use their fire breath attack, then hop around behind them and slash like crazy.

facts.subject: Dodongo
facts.text: A Dodongo's tail swipe turn-around attack can be blocked using the Deku Shield as Young Link or avoided with a backflip.

evidence.quote: They might swipe their tail to turn around quickly. If so, either use the Deku Shield to block this attack as Young Link, or simply backflip out of the way.

facts.subject: Fire Keese
facts.text: Equipping the Deku Shield should be avoided when Fire Keese ram into Link.

evidence.quote: Don't have the Deku Shield out when they ram into you....

facts.subject: Flare Dancer
facts.text: The Flare Dancer in the Fire Temple must be pulled out of its flaming clothes with the Hookshot before sword slashes can harm it.

evidence.quote: Flare Dancer: MINI-BOSS OF THE FIRE TEMPLE...In order to be able to hit this dude, you have to Hookshot it right out of its flaming clothes. Once it's out, sword slashes will harm it.

facts.subject: Floormaster
facts.text: When hit, a Floormaster splits into three smaller hands that will reassemble if not eliminated quickly.

evidence.quote: If hit, it splits up into three smaller hands. Get rid of the smaller hands quick, or else they'll reassemble.

facts.subject: Freezard
facts.text: Freezards freeze Link upon contact and regenerate body parts unless completely cut down with sword slashes.

evidence.quote: It blows ice cold air at you and if you touch them, you freeze. Slash it with the sword to cut it down until it's completely gone. If you don't get rid of it, it'll regenerate its body parts.

facts.subject: Gerudo Thief
facts.text: Defeating a Gerudo Thief in Gerudo's Fortress always yields a small key to free a carpenter.

evidence.quote: You encounter this kind of enemy frequently in Gerudo's Fortress, mostly when trying to rescue a carpenter...She always drops a small key to free the carpenter from his cell.

facts.subject: Gerudo Thief
facts.text: Being hit by a Gerudo Thief's jumping attack stuns Link and sends him back to his cell.

evidence.quote: If you get hit by her jumping attack, you'll be stunned and be taken back to your cell.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: There are exactly 100 Gold Skulltulas distinguished by the gold skull-like shell on their back.

evidence.quote: You can tell the difference between them and a normal Skullwalltula by the gold skull-like shell on its back. There are exactly 100 of these critters, and they supposedly hold curses.

facts.subject: Green Bubble
facts.text: Green Bubbles can be killed by waiting until their flames subside before slashing them.

evidence.quote: In order to kill it, wait until its flames subside before slashing it.

facts.subject: Ice Keese
facts.text: Ice Keese freeze Link on contact and can be sniped from afar using the Slingshot or Bow.

evidence.quote: A bat enemy that freezes you on contact. Avoid at all costs. It's easy to just snipe it from afar with the Slingshot or Bow.

facts.subject: Iron Knuckle
facts.text: When fighting an Iron Knuckle as Young Link in the Spirit Temple, using Nayru's Love or throwing bombs helps overcome its tough defense.

evidence.quote: Iron Knuckle: MINI-BOSS OF THE SPIRIT TEMPLE...He's tough when you face him as Young Link, so use either Nayru's Love to protect you, or just throw as many bombs as you have at him.

facts.subject: Keese
facts.text: A Keese transforms into a Fire Keese when exposed to fire, or into an Ice Keese when exposed to blue flame or ice.

evidence.quote: It is highly adaptive to its surroundings, and turns into a Fire Keese when exposed to fire, and an Ice Keese when exposed to blue flame/ice.

facts.subject: Like Like
facts.text: If a Like Like swallows Link and steals equipment, defeating it quickly recovers the stolen items.

evidence.quote: If you let it attack, it will swallow you and possibly steal some of your equipment. Get any stolen equipment back by beating it quickly.

facts.subject: Lizalfos
facts.text: The recommended strategy against Lizalfos is to keep shielded, wait until they strike first, and then execute a jump strike.

evidence.quote: The best strategy for these is to wait until they strike first, then jump striking them. Keep shielded throughout the whole fight and follow this strategy, and they won't stand a chance.

facts.subject: Blue Bubble
facts.text: Blue Bubble: shield so that when they hit you, their flames will go away, and then you can slash 'em.

evidence.quote: Blue Bubble...Just shield so that when they hit you, their flames will go away, and then you can just slash 'em.

facts.subject: Meg
facts.text: The real Meg among the clones can be identified because she spins around after cloning herself.

evidence.quote: The real one is pretty obvious, she spins around after cloning herself.

facts.subject: Moblin
facts.text: A Hookshot shot to the back will instantly kill a Moblin.

evidence.quote: A Hookshot to the back will kill them instantly.

facts.subject: Moblin
facts.text: The club-wielding Moblin must be slashed three times before he clubs Link.

evidence.quote: The last Moblin has a club and must be slashed three times before he clubs you.

facts.subject: Parasitic Tentacle
facts.text: Parasitic Tentacles in Jabu-Jabu's Belly can be killed by Z-targeting them and using the Boomerang.

evidence.quote: Just simply Z-target it and use the Boomerang to kill it. These are only found in Jabu- Jabu's Belly.

facts.subject: Peahat
facts.text: A Peahat's weak point is its root.

evidence.quote: Peahat's weak point is its root.

facts.subject: Peahat Larva
facts.text: Peahat Larvae are killed when they hit Link's shield.

evidence.quote: (Yep, strangely they die if they hit your shield.)

facts.subject: Poe
facts.text: Drinking a bottled Poe soul causes Link to lose one heart of health.

evidence.quote: Don't drink it though, as you'll lose a heart from your health if you do.

facts.subject: Poe Shop
facts.text: As Adult Link, a Poe shop in the former guard's shack in Hyrule Market buys Poe souls.

evidence.quote: as Adult Link, there's a Poe shop where the guard's shack used to be in Hyrule Market. He buys Poe souls from you.

facts.subject: ReDead
facts.text: ReDeads can be stunned by playing the Sun's Song near them.

evidence.quote: It can also be stunned by playing the Sun's Song near it, making it easy to kill.

facts.subject: Shell Blade
facts.text: A Shell Blade's weakness is its heart, which is vulnerable to sword stabs or the Hookshot when opened.

evidence.quote: Its weakness is the heart, so wait for it to open up, then stab or use the Hookshot.

facts.subject: Stalchild
facts.text: Defeating a giant Stalchild on Hyrule Field awards a Red Rupee worth 20 normal Rupees.

evidence.quote: If enough are killed, a giant Stalchild will appear; killing him will give you a Red Rupee worth 20 normal ones.

facts.subject: Tailpasaran
facts.text: Tailpasaran are found inside Jabu-Jabu's Belly and can be killed with an Advanced Spin Slash.

evidence.quote: Killed with an Advanced Spin Slash, these rare creatures are only found inside Jabu-Jabu's Belly.

facts.subject: Wolfos
facts.text: If Link backs away from a Wolfos attack and it misses, jump slashing its exposed back will kill it instantly.

evidence.quote: If he doesn't hit you, he'll turn his back to you. Jump slash him quickly to kill him instantly.

facts.subject: Queen Gohma
facts.text: Hitting Queen Gohma's eye with the Fairy Slingshot stuns her, allowing Link to slash her eye repeatedly.

evidence.quote: Hit the eye with the Fairy Slingshot to stun her, then get up to her eye and slash at the eye repeatedly.

facts.subject: Queen Gohma
facts.text: Queen Gohma can be defeated in one sequence by stunning her with the Fairy Slingshot, jump slashing with a Deku Stick, and repeatedly pressing B while holding R to stab her to death.

evidence.quote: Stun her with the Fairy Slingshot, then jump slash with a Deku Stick to do a lot of damage. Afterwards, hold R while facing her(without locking on) and press B repeatedly to stab her to death. This method should only require one sequence.

facts.subject: Queen Gohma
facts.text: When Queen Gohma is on the ceiling laying eggs, shooting her red eye with the Fairy Slingshot causes her to fall to the ground.

evidence.quote: when she's at the ceiling laying eggs, shoot her in the eye while it's red with the Fairy Slingshot, and she'll fall to the ground, open for another attack.

facts.subject: King Dodongo
facts.text: Throwing a Bomb down King Dodongo's gullet when he inhales stuns him, allowing Link to slash his head with the sword.

evidence.quote: Basically avoid this boss until he starts to inhale. When he does, whip out a Bomb and throw it straight down his gullet. This'll stun him, so run up and slash his head with your sword.

facts.subject: King Dodongo
facts.text: King Dodongo's rolling attack can be avoided by standing on the edge of the platform where it meets the lava.

evidence.quote: After a few slashes, he'll then roll into a ball and roll around the room. He can be easily avoided here by standing on the very edge of the platform where it meets the lava.

facts.subject: King Dodongo
facts.text: King Dodongo can be defeated more quickly by jump striking with Deku Sticks and shield stabbing while he is stunned.

evidence.quote: SPEEDY STRATEGY: Just jump strike with Deku Sticks and shield stab (hold R and press B repeatedly while not locked on) after he's stunned to defeat him more quickly.

facts.subject: Barinade
facts.text: Z-targeting Barinade's 3 tentacles and cutting them loose with the Boomerang makes the surrounding jellyfish spin.

evidence.quote: Z-target one of its tentacles and use the Boomerang to cut it loose. Do this for all 3 tentacles, and the jellyfish surrounding it will spin around.

facts.subject: Barinade
facts.text: Hitting Barinade's center with the Boomerang loosens its grip on its protective jellyfish, and stunning it reveals another layer of jellyfish around its weak spot.

evidence.quote: Boomerang its center to make it loose its grip on the jellyfish. Destroy all these jelly fish, and doing so makes it rise to reveal some more jellyfish, this time surrounding its weak spot. Keep on using the Boomerang until you stun it, then kill all these other jellyfish.

facts.subject: Barinade
facts.text: Once Barinade's jellyfish defenses are gone, stun its center with the Boomerang to slash it, being mindful that it fires electric beams faster as it takes damage.

evidence.quote: Stun its center with the Boomerang, then move in and slash it. It'll take a few tries, and it unleashes electric beams more rapidly as it's damaged. Keep stunning and slashing until it's dead.

facts.subject: Barinade
facts.text: Stunning Barinade after eliminating all jellyfish and performing shield stabs kills it more quickly.

evidence.quote: SPEEDY STRATEGY: After getting rid of all its protective jellyfish, stun it and simply use the shield stab attack to kill it more quickly.

facts.subject: Phantom Ganon
facts.text: Shoot an arrow at Phantom Ganon when purple magic surrounds him as he escapes from a painting.

evidence.quote: Basically what you have to do, is aim your arrow at the Phantom when he escapes from the painting. (purple magic surrounds him when he's about to exit)

facts.subject: Phantom Ganon
facts.text: Failing to shoot the real Phantom Ganon when he emerges from a painting results in a lightning attack that takes away at least five hearts.

evidence.quote: The fake one turns around, so if you encounter that one, hurry up and find the real one and fire that arrow. If you don't, you'll be struck with a lightning attack that takes away at least five hearts.

facts.subject: Phantom Ganon
facts.text: Swinging the Master Sword reflects Phantom Ganon's magic spell back at him, stunning him on the floor so he can be slashed.

evidence.quote: Use the Master Sword and swing it at the right time to reflect the magic spell back at Phantom Ganon. He'll usually reflect it back, so continue this tennis game until it hits either one of you. If it hits Phantom Ganon he'll go to the floor, stunned. So go up to him and slash him.

facts.subject: Phantom Ganon
facts.text: Deflecting Phantom Ganon's magic point-blank immediately hits him, allowing Link to shield stab him while he is grounded.

evidence.quote: SPEEDY STRATEGY: After getting rid of its stallion, get really close to Phantom Ganon, and time your slash right so that it's deflected as soon as it fires its magic ball attack...Once it reaches the ground, shield stab the phantom until it's dead.

facts.subject: Volvagia
facts.text: Avoiding Volvagia's fiery hair attack and pounding her head with the Hammer causes her to retreat.

evidence.quote: Wait for Volvagia to reveal its head, and when it does, it will throw its fiery hair to try to attack you...Stay away from her(?) hair attack, and go up to her and pound her head down with the Hammer.

facts.subject: Volvagia
facts.text: As Volvagia takes damage, fire erupts from one hole as a trick before she emerges from a different hole.

evidence.quote: As you damage her, she'll try to trick you by having fire come up where she should appear, but then she appears in another hole.

facts.subject: Volvagia
facts.text: Hanging from the edge of the platform when Volvagia flies causes her to immediately retreat underground.

evidence.quote: SPEEDY STRATEGY: When she starts flying around, drop down the sides slowly and you'll grab onto the sides as if its a grate or vine, or something. Doing this will make her lose her interest in attacking you and will go back underground immediately.

facts.subject: Morpha
facts.text: Getting grabbed by Morpha inflicts three hearts of damage.

evidence.quote: It'll throw itself towards you, and if it grabs you, you'll suffer three hearts of damage.

facts.subject: Morpha
facts.text: Morpha can form bodies even while its brain is exposed and will eventually spawn two bodies simultaneously.

evidence.quote: As you damage it, it'll form its body even when the brain is outside of it...It'll even still form two bodies at once.

facts.subject: Morpha
facts.text: Using the Longshot between slashes prevents Morpha's brain from escaping.

evidence.quote: SPEEDY STRATEGY: To keep the brain from escaping while you're attacking it, Longshot between slashes and you should take care of it more quickly.

facts.subject: Bongo Bongo
facts.text: Shooting Bongo Bongo's hands with arrows prompts a ramming attack, allowing Link to see him with the Lens of Truth and stun his eye with an arrow.

evidence.quote: First of all, you have to arrow its hands. Do so, and the boss will try to ram you. Use the Lens of Truth to see him, and put an arrow into his eye. This'll stun him, so go up to him and slash him until he's dead.

facts.subject: Bongo Bongo
facts.text: The Biggoron's Sword works best for slashing Bongo Bongo when he is stunned.

evidence.quote: The Biggoron's Sword works best.

facts.subject: Bongo Bongo
facts.text: Using the Biggoron's Sword with the shield stab technique is optimal when Bongo Bongo is stunned.

evidence.quote: SPEEDY STRATEGY: The Biggoron's Sword with the shield stab technique is your best friend when he's stunned.

facts.subject: Twinrova
facts.text: Reflecting an elemental beam with the Mirror Shield toward the witch of the opposite element damages her.

evidence.quote: One fires a powerful ice beam, the other fires a powerful fire beam. In order to damage these witches, you must reflect their spells with the Mirror Shield and point it toward the other witch.

facts.subject: Twinrova
facts.text: Locking on with Z or L and then releasing targeting aligns Link directly with the witch firing the beam.

evidence.quote: If you're having trouble facing the boss that fires the beam, Z (or L) target the boss then break out of lock-on. That way you'll be perfectly facing the boss. Each witch needs to take a few hits before the next phase begins.

facts.subject: Twinrova
facts.text: Absorbing three projectiles of the same element with the Mirror Shield fires a beam that stuns merged Twinrova.

evidence.quote: You must absorb three projectiles OF THE SAME ELEMENT. If you absorb two fires and one ice, it'll cancel out and you'll have to try again...Once you do, you'll fire a beam of that element, stunning her. Now's your chance. Rush to her and start slashing her repeatedly.

facts.subject: Twinrova
facts.text: Running toward Twinrova while absorbing the third projectile enables an immediate Biggoron's Sword shield stab upon stunning her.

evidence.quote: SPEEDY STRATEGY: Since reflecting the beams and absorbing the projectiles are random or hard to speed up, when you absorb the last projectile needed to stun her, run toward her as you absorb the projectile, and as soon as she's stunned, break your lock, get out the Biggoron's Sword as you jump over, and shield stab her.

facts.subject: Ganondorf
facts.text: Rolling to the outer rim when Ganondorf pounds the ground prevents Link from falling down.

evidence.quote: The boss starts out by pounding the ground. Quickly roll away to the outer rim so you won't fall down.

facts.subject: Ganondorf
facts.text: Ganondorf's magic spells can be reflected back at him using sword swipes or Empty Bottles.

evidence.quote: Just like Phantom Ganon, Ganondorf throws magic spells that you have to reflect back at him with sword swipes. (Or oddly enough, Empty Bottles)

facts.subject: Ganondorf
facts.text: Using an Advanced Spin Slash deflects Ganondorf's simultaneous multi-magic projectile barrage.

evidence.quote: When you see both his arms raised and energy gathers toward him, he'll fire multiple magic spells at you simultaneously. In order to deflect those, use the Advanced Spin Slash.

facts.subject: Ganondorf
facts.text: Shooting Ganondorf with a Light Arrow in the face while he charges his multiple magic attack interrupts him and saves magic.

evidence.quote: Another thing to do is that, when he's charging up for that multiple magic spell attack, he's open for a Light Arrow to the face. Saves magic, actually, so thanks, WiiKyle!

facts.subject: Ganondorf
facts.text: Striking Ganondorf with a Light Arrow after he is hit by a reflected spell lowers him to the ground where he can be slashed.

evidence.quote: Once he finally gets hit by a spell, quickly get the Light Arrows out and hit him with one before he recovers. Once he's hit, he'll lower to the ground. Quickly get to him and slash him before he gets back up.

facts.subject: Morpha
facts.text: To damage the boss, dodge its attack and Longshot the brain to snatch it away and start slashing it before it retreats back into its body.

evidence.quote: To damage the boss, dodge its attack and its brain will move around its body. Longshot the brain to snatch it away, and start slashing it. It'll then retreat back into its body.

facts.subject: Ganondorf
facts.text: Getting right on the central platform Ganondorf is hovering above leaves him no time to react once you reflect his spells, allowing shield stabs with the Biggoron's Sword or quick spin slashes once he's down.

evidence.quote: you can get right on the central platform Ganondorf is hovering above, leaving the 'dorf no time to react once you reflect his spells. Once he's down, either shield stab with the Biggoron's Sword or do quick spin slashes. (Rotate stick then immediately press B)

facts.subject: Ganon
facts.text: Ganon slashes with his huge swords, causing Link to lose his Master Sword.

evidence.quote:
Ganon slashes with his huge swords, making Link lose
his Master Sword.

facts.subject: Ganon
facts.text: Link can stun Ganon with Light Arrows or roll between his legs to get behind him, then slash his tail with the Biggoron's Sword.

evidence.quote:
The way to defeat this monster is to either stun it
by shooting Light Arrows then going behind it, or rolling between its legs.
Either way, slash his tail with the Biggoron's Sword.

facts.subject: Master Sword
facts.text: Link is able to get the Master Sword back after dealing some damage to Ganon.

evidence.quote:
After dealing some
damage, you're able to get your Master Sword back.

facts.subject: Ganon
facts.text: When Ganon falls, Zelda holds him down while the sages power Link's sword to deliver the final slash to his head.

evidence.quote:
After some more damage, Ganon will fall, and Zelda will keep him down,
telling you to deal the final blow. The sages will power your sword for the
final hit. Just head up to his head, and slash.

facts.subject: Bombchu Bowling Alley
facts.text: For the first hole at the Bombchu Bowling Alley, stand at the center and release a Bombchu so it avoids the spike trap.

evidence.quote:
The first one is very easy. Just stand at the center and release a Bombchu 
so it won't hit the spike trap.

facts.subject: Bombchu Bowling Alley
facts.text: For the second hole at the Bombchu Bowling Alley, wait until the Cucco is clear if the hole is near the ceiling, or aim diagonally from the opposite side if it is on the side.

evidence.quote:
The second hole is always at a random spot. If it's at the center near the
ceiling, just use the same strategy as hole 1, but this time wait until the
Cucco is out of the way. ... If 
it's on the side, simply stand at the complete opposite side and plant a 
Bombchu at a diagonal angle towards the hole and it'll almost always hit it.

facts.subject: Bombchu Bowling Alley
facts.text: For the third hole at the Bombchu Bowling Alley, stand on the third black mark from the left of the middle blue arrow and drop a Bombchu straight ahead so a ledge redirects it toward the hole.

evidence.quote:
stand right on the third black mark from the left of 
the middle blue arrow, wait until you're all clear, including the Huge Cucco, 
and drop a Bombchu straight ahead, not at the hole. ... there's actually a ledge after the 
indentation with the Huge Cucco in it that makes the Bombchu turn towards the 
hole.

facts.subject: Bombchu Bowling Alley
facts.text: Bombchus can be won as an inventory item prize at the Bombchu Bowling Alley.

evidence.quote:
You might want to get BOMBCHUS
as a prize while you're here, so you can have an item in your Inventory screen.

facts.subject: Great Fairy Fountain
facts.text: Blasting the boulder at the Castle Grounds reveals a Great Fairy Fountain where playing Zelda's Lullaby grants the Din's Fire magic power.

evidence.quote:
Blast the 
boulder to reveal another Great Fairy Fountain. Head in here. Summon her with 
Zelda's Lullaby and she'll give you Din's Fire, a special magic power.

facts.subject: Death Mountain Trail guard
facts.text: The guard at the entrance to Death Mountain Trail buys the Keaton Mask for 15 Rupees, after which 10 Rupees must be paid to the Happy Mask Shop owner.

evidence.quote:
Talk to him with the mask on and he'll buy it for 15 Rupees. ... Head back to the Happy Mask Shop and give the owner the 10 
Rupees that the mask is worth.

facts.subject: Deku Scrub leader
facts.text: Speaking to the Deku Scrub leader while wearing the Skull Mask inside the Secret Cave in the Lost Woods rewards an upgrade allowing Link to carry 30 Deku Sticks.

evidence.quote:
head right, left, right, left, then left again to get to a grassy 
area. Find the butterflies flying around, and walk around there to find a 
Secret Cave. Put on your Skull Mask, and head forward. A bunch of Deku Scrubs 
will pop up. We're looking for the leader of this pack. Talk to the leader 
and he'll give you a DEKU STICK UPGRADE which allows you to carry 30 Deku 
Sticks.

facts.subject: Skull Kid
facts.text: The Skull Kid in the Lost Woods buys the Skull Mask for 10 Rupees, requiring a 20 Rupee payment to the shop owner.

evidence.quote:
Now head back to that Skull Kid and he'll buy it for 10 Rupees. It's 
worth 20 Rupees, so you lost some money. Head back to the shop and pay the 
owner 20 Rupees.

facts.subject: Spooky Mask
facts.text: The kid in Kakariko Graveyard buys the Spooky Mask during the day for its full price of 30 Rupees, which is paid back to the shop owner.

evidence.quote:
Head over to Kakariko Graveyard, 
making sure it's day. You should see a very small kid. He wants to imitate 
Dampe, so give him the Spooky Mask and he'll pay the full price for it. (30 
Rupees) Well, head back to the owner and pay 30 Rupees.

facts.subject: Bunny Hood
facts.text: Wearing the Bunny Hood at night in Hyrule Field prevents Stalchilds from attacking.

evidence.quote:
A bonus for the Bunny Hood is that while you're wearing it at night in Hyrule
Field, the Stalchilds won't attack you.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Rolling into the tree near the entrance to Zora's River knocks down a Gold Skulltula.

evidence.quote:
Roll into the tree to knock down a Gold Skulltula, (GOLD 
SKULLTULA: 025 out of 100) then bomb the rocks.

facts.subject: Magic Bean salesman
facts.text: The salesman at Zora's River sells the first Magic Bean for 10 Rupees, increasing the price on each purchase up to 10 total beans.

evidence.quote:
Talk to him and he'll sell a Magic Bean for 10 
Rupees. Now you see, this guy is a real scammer. Every time you buy a Magic 
Bean from him, he raises the price of it. ... (There should be 10 total, I think.)

facts.subject: Secret Cave
facts.text: Entering the Secret Cave in Kakariko Village and defeating the Redeads yields a Huge Rupee from a chest.

evidence.quote:
Remember that Secret Cave I told you about? Open it up, then 
head inside, kill the Redeads, and grab the Huge Rupee from the chest.

facts.subject: Drawbridge
facts.text: Standing on the drawbridge chains as it raises at night provides access to three hidden Red Rupees along the narrow edge.

evidence.quote:
During the day, head to the 
drawbridge and stand on one of the chains. Either wait for night or have it 
come immediately by playing Sun's Song and the drawbridge will go up, taking 
you with it. Now, walk along the narrow drawbridge edge and you'll find three 
hidden Red Rupees.

facts.subject: Secret Cave
facts.text: Climbing the ladder on the strip of land at Zora's River leads to a Secret Cave containing a small chest with a Red Rupee.

evidence.quote:
Climb up the ladder and 
you'll find a Secret Cave, a boulder surrounded by smaller rocks, and another 
Cucco. The Secret Cave contains a small chest with a Red Rupee

facts.subject: Fairy Fountain
facts.text: Blasting the boulder surrounded by smaller rocks at Zora's River reveals a Fairy Fountain.

evidence.quote:
Blasting the boulder reveals another Secret Cave which is a regular 
Fairy Fountain.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: Gliding from an elevated platform with a Cucco allows Link to reach a Piece of Heart sitting on a pillar in Zora's River.

evidence.quote:
Now see the Piece of Heart on the pillar? First get 
up to the other platform then use the Cucco to glide over to the Piece. (HEART 
PIECES: 12 out of 36)

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: Using a Cucco at the top bridge in Zora's River allows Link to glide to the west ledge to obtain a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote:
At the top bridge, use the Cucco to get to the west ledge which 
contains another Piece of Heart. (HEART PIECES: 13 out of 36)

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Dropping below the ladder near the waterfall at night reveals a Gold Skulltula that can be killed with the slingshot.

evidence.quote:
Now if it's 
night, drop below where the ladder is and you'll see a Gold Skulltula. Kill it 
with the slingshot then collect its token. (GOLD SKULLTULAS: 026 out of 100)

facts.subject: Frogs
facts.text: Playing Zelda's Lullaby, Epona's Song, Saria's Song, and Sun's Song on the log at Zora's River causes four frogs to enlarge, each giving a Purple Rupee.

evidence.quote:
Play Zelda's Lullaby and a frog will grow large and give you 
a Purple Rupee in return. ... Play Epona's Song. 
Another frog will grow large and give you another Purple Rupee. Play Saria's 
Song and yet another frog will grow large and give you another Purple Rupee. 
Play the Sun's Song last and another frog will grow large and give you a Purple 
Rupee.

facts.subject: Waterfall
facts.text: Playing Zelda's Lullaby on the mark in front of the waterfall at Zora's River causes the water to part, opening the entrance to Zora's Domain.

evidence.quote:
Head back to the waterfall and stand on the special mark in front. Play
Zelda's Lullaby and the waterfall will recede, allowing you to enter.

facts.subject: Diving Game
facts.text: Collecting all the Rupees thrown during the Diving Game in Zora's Domain within the time limit awards the Silver Scale, allowing dives of up to 6 seconds.

evidence.quote:
Talk to him to play this game. He'll throw a bunch of Rupees down 
below, and you have to dive to get them in a limited time. ... If you get them all, he'll ask you to come back up to 
receive a prize. Do so, and he'll give you a Silver Scale, which allows you to 
dive down for 6 seconds.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: Lighting the torches along the stairs, down the spiral ramp, and behind the waterfall reveals a treasure chest containing a Piece of Heart in Zora's Domain.

evidence.quote:
Light another Deku Stick from this torch, and head left down the spiral path, 
lighting all these torches (they don't stay lit for long), the final two 
torches are behind the waterfall. ... If you lit 
them all, a treasure chest with the Piece will appear. (HEART PIECES: 14 out of 
36)

facts.subject: Bottle
facts.text: Diving through the underwater cave from Zora's Domain into Lake Hylia leads to Princess Ruto's letter in a bottle.

evidence.quote:
find the cave 
entrance underwater. Get near it and use the Silver Scale to enter. Now you're 
in Lake Hylia. Below the Zora here is a letter in a BOTTLE. Grab it. Now you 
have the third bottle in the game.

facts.subject: Scarecrow
facts.text: Playing any 8 notes on the Ocarina to the scarecrow closer to shore at Lake Hylia causes him to memorize the song.

evidence.quote:
head to the two scarecrows and pull out your 
Ocarina in front of the one closer to shore. Play any 8 notes of your choice 
(write down the notes you play) and the scarecrow will remember the song you 
played.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: At night, a Gold Skulltula is found on the platform with pillars near the island with the large tree in Lake Hylia.

evidence.quote:
Head toward the island 
with a large tree.  Ahead is a platform with pillars on it. Head over there at 
night to find a Gold Skulltula. (GOLD SKULLTULAS: 027 out of 100)

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Releasing bugs from a bottle into the dirt plot beside the Lakeside Laboratory causes a Gold Skulltula to appear.

evidence.quote:
head 
over to the building (it's the Lakeside Laboratory) and drop some bugs from 
your Bottle to make another Gold Skulltula appear. (GOLD SKULLTULAS: 028 out of 
100)

facts.subject: Fishing Pond
facts.text: Catching a fish weighing 10 lb. or more at the Fishing Pond for 20 Rupees awards a Piece of Heart from the fisherman.

evidence.quote:
This is the Fishing Pond. ... At the cost of 20 Rupees, you can fish for as long as you want. We're 
looking at getting a 10 lb. fish. ... when you eventually get that 10 lb. (or 
more) fish, bring it to the fisherman and he'll give you a Piece of Heart. 
(HEART PIECES: 15 out of 36)

facts.subject: Lord Jabu Jabu
facts.text: Releasing a bottled fish directly in front of Lord Jabu Jabu makes him inhale the fish along with Link.

evidence.quote:
drop that bottled fish right in front of him. He'll open his mouth and 
inhale the fish, along with you in it.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Rolling into the tree on the island at the far end of Zora's Fountain knocks down a Gold Skulltula.

evidence.quote:
head to the far end where the island is. Roll into the 
tree to knock down a Gold Skulltula. (GOLD SKULLTULAS: 029 out of 100)

facts.subject: Great Fairy Fountain
facts.text: Blowing up the wall behind the white rock in Zora's Fountain opens a Great Fairy Fountain where summoning the Great Fairy grants Farore's Wind.

evidence.quote:
Plant a 
bomb near the white rock to blow up the wall behind it. Head through it to 
enter a Great Fairy Fountain. Summoning this Great Fairy will get you Farore's 
Wind, another C item.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is located on the vines above a switch that raises the water level.

evidence.quote: Now, use the Fairy Slingshot to kill the Gold Skulltula on the vines, then raise the water level by hitting the switch to collect the token. (GOLD SKULLTULAS: 030 out of 100)

facts.subject: Boomerang
facts.text: A large chest containing the Boomerang appears after defeating all the Stingers in the room.

evidence.quote: Inside are more of those Stingers. Once you kill them all, a large chest containing the BOOMERANG appears.

facts.subject: Dungeon Map
facts.text: Defeating the large tentacle by striking its narrow part with the Boomerang reveals a large chest containing the Dungeon Map.

evidence.quote: Get close to it and keep moving while hitting the narrow part with the Boomerang (Z-targeting is excellent here) until it's dead. A large chest will appear. Open it to get the DUNGEON MAP for this dungeon.

facts.subject: Compass
facts.text: Popping all the Shaboms within 40 seconds makes a large chest appear containing the Compass.

evidence.quote: Head inside with Ruto and you'll be in a room filled with Shaboms. You have to pop them all in 40 seconds. If successful, a large chest will appear. Opening this will get you the COMPASS for this dungeon.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Two Gold Skulltulas are found along the wall in the large room where Ruto was first encountered.

evidence.quote: Look along the wall and you'll see two, yes two, Gold Skulltulas. Kill them and retrieve their tokens with the Boomerang. (GOLD SKULLTULAS: 32 out of 100)

facts.subject: Bigocto
facts.text: Bigocto can be stunned with the Boomerang while circling to its backside to attack the green spot behind it.

evidence.quote: Instead of using my impossible "Boomerang it then hurry to its back", just Boomerang it as you're heading to its behind (Z-Target is your friend here) and you will have an easier time attacking the green spot behind it.

facts.subject: Recovery Heart
facts.text: One of the pots behind Link contains a fairy.

evidence.quote: (There's some pots behind you. One of them has a fairy.)

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is located on some vines in the room with Biri before the boss room.

evidence.quote: In this next room, kill all the Biri, then find a Gold Skulltula on some vines. Use the Boomerang to kill it and retrieve the token. (GOLD SKULLTULAS: 33 out of 100)

facts.subject: Switch
facts.text: Standing to the left of the glass wall and throwing a curved Boomerang hits the switch that unlocks the boss room door.

evidence.quote: Head to the left of the glass wall, Z-Target it, and throw the Boomerang. If you got it right, it should just clear the wall and curve to hit the switch. Enter the door it just opened to enter the boss's room.

facts.subject: Barinade
facts.text: Barinade requires cutting loose its 3 tentacles with the Boomerang, stunning its center, destroying the protective jellyfish, and then stunning and slashing its exposed core.

evidence.quote: Z-target one of its tentacles and use the Boomerang to cut it loose. Do this for all 3 tentacles, and the jellyfish surrounding it will spin around. Boomerang its center to make it loose its grip on the jellyfish...Stun its center with the Boomerang, then move in and slash it.

facts.subject: Barinade
facts.text: Barinade can be killed more quickly by stunning it and using the shield stab attack after removing its protective jellyfish.

evidence.quote: SPEEDY STRATEGY: After getting rid of all its protective jellyfish, stun it and
simply use the shield stab attack to kill it more quickly.

facts.subject: Heart Container
facts.text: Defeating Barinade awards a Heart Container, bringing the total health to 9 hearts.

evidence.quote: When it's dead, collect the Heart Container, (9 hearts now!) and head over to the light where Princess Ruto is floating.

facts.subject: Zora's Sapphire
facts.text: Princess Ruto gives Link the Zora's Sapphire, the Spiritual Stone of Water, after exiting Jabu-Jabu's Belly.

evidence.quote: After exiting, say you want the Spiritual Stone and she'll give it to you. This Zora's Sapphire, is the last of the Spiritual Stones.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: At night, a Gold Skulltula is found on the wall across from the log sticking out of the water in Zora's Fountain.

evidence.quote: First, make sure it's night here in Zora's Fountain, then head on top of the log sticking out of the water. You should find a Gold Skulltula on the wall across from the log. Remember to use the Boomerang for far away Gold Skulltulas. (GOLD SKULLTULAS: 34 out of 100)

facts.subject: Zora's River
facts.text: Diving down to the bottom of the pool of water outside Zora's Domain connects through an underwater entrance to the Lost Woods.

evidence.quote: Once you exit, see the pool of water to the left? Head to it and dive down to the bottom, going through the entrance here. This is a warp over to Lost Woods.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Inside the Great Deku Tree, bombing a wall behind a Deku Baba past the upper crawlspace reveals a Gold Skulltula.

evidence.quote: On the other side, find the bombable wall behind a Deku Baba, bomb it, and you'll find a Gold Skulltula behind it. Kill it and use the Boomerang to retrieve the token. (GOLD SKULLTULAS: 35 out of 100)

facts.subject: Magic Bean
facts.text: A Magic Bean can be planted in the soft dirt plot by the shop in Kokiri Forest.

evidence.quote: Plant a Magic Bean on the plot of dirt by the Shop, then head back to Lost Woods.

facts.subject: Magic Bean
facts.text: A Magic Bean can be planted in the soft dirt plot found by heading left from the Lost Woods entrance.

evidence.quote: Once you enter, head left until you find another plot of dirt. Plant a Magic Bean here.

facts.subject: Magic Bean
facts.text: A Magic Bean can be planted in the plot of dirt behind the Business Scrub in the Lost Woods.

evidence.quote: Now, head back to the Lost Woods entrance, then head right, left, right, left, then left again and plant a Magic Bean on this plot of dirt behind the Business Scrub.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Planting a bomb near the tree by the castle walls opens a Secret Cave containing a Gold Skulltula.

evidence.quote: Head to Kakariko Village, but before you enter, notice the tree near the castle walls. Plant a bomb there to make a Secret Cave appear. Drop down, kill the Skulltula, and kill the Gold Skulltula here with the Boomerang. (GOLD SKULLTULAS: 36 out of 100)

facts.subject: Giant's Wallet
facts.text: The Skulltula House gives the Giant's Wallet, which increases rupee carrying capacity to 500 Rupees, after collecting enough tokens.

evidence.quote: Head inside the Skulltula House and get the next prize, the Giant's Wallet, which can carry 500 Rupees.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is perched high up on the south wall at the far end of the Graveyard.

evidence.quote: Next, head to the Graveyard. Head to the far end and look on the south wall. There's another Gold Skulltula here. It's high up, so you know what item you need. (GOLD SKULLTULAS: 37 out of 100)

facts.subject: Magic Bean
facts.text: A Magic Bean can be planted in the soft dirt plot located in the Graveyard.

evidence.quote: Before exiting, plant a Magic Bean on the plot of dirt here.

facts.subject: Magic Bean
facts.text: A Magic Bean can be planted in the plot of dirt located near the entrance to Dodongo's Cavern.

evidence.quote: Next head to Death Mountain Trail and deposit a Magic Bean on the plot of dirt near the entrance to Dodongo's Cavern.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Climbing up the left side of the raised staircase room on the second floor leads to an alcove with a Gold Skulltula.

evidence.quote: Get to the second floor using the high-rise platform. From there, head over to the staircase room. Once you are there, you'll notice the staircase is back up. Climb up the left side and you'll reach an alcove with a Gold Skulltula. (GOLD SKULLTULAS: 38 out of 100)

facts.subject: Ocarina of Time
facts.text: After Zelda throws the Ocarina of Time into the moat during her escape, retrieving it triggers a scene where Zelda teaches Link the Song of Time.

evidence.quote: After the scene is over, get into the moat and you'll see the Ocarina of Time Zelda threw. After grabbing it, a scene will show Zelda telepathically teaching Link the Song of Time to open up the Temple of Time.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: At night, a Gold Skulltula is found up high on the left building of Lon Lon Ranch.

evidence.quote: Once in the ranch, (make sure it's night) look up at the left building. There's a Gold Skulltula up high. Use the Boomerang. (GOLD SKULLTULAS: 39 out of 100)

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is located on the wall to the right of the silo at Lon Lon Ranch.

evidence.quote: Now head toward the silo. The wall to the right has another Gold Skulltula. (GOLD SKULLTULAS: 40 out of 100)

facts.subject: Running Man
facts.text: The Running Man running around Lon Lon Ranch will buy the Bunny Hood for as much money as Link can carry.

evidence.quote: Remember the Bunny Hood? This guy wants it, and he'll pay as much money to you as you can carry to get it.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Bombing the center of the stone circle outside Gerudo Valley reveals a Secret Cave with a Gold Skulltula behind cobwebs.

evidence.quote: Before entering, plant a bomb in the middle of the circle of stones near the entrance. Drop inside after opening this Secret Cave. Now use Din's Fire to burn all the cobwebs off, and head into the corridor with a cow. There's another Gold Skulltula here. (GOLD SKULLTULAS: 41 out of 100)

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: At night, a Gold Skulltula is found on the wall to the right of the wooden plank in Gerudo Valley.

evidence.quote: Exit the cave, and enter Gerudo Valley during the night...For now, head forward to the wooden plank. To the right, on the wall, is another Gold Skulltula. (GOLD SKULLTULAS: 42 out of 100)

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: Gliding down to the ledge to the left of the bridge with a Cucco and breaking the crate reveals a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: Now grab the Cucco, and drop down to the left of the bridge. You see the ledge with the crate? Float down there and break it to reveal a Piece of Heart. (HEART PIECES: 16 out of 36)

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Dropping bugs into the plot of dirt on the lower ledge in Gerudo Valley causes a Gold Skulltula to appear.

evidence.quote: Now drop some bugs onto the plot of dirt (grabbing another if possible) and another Gold Skulltula will pop out. (GOLD SKULLTULAS: 43 out of 100)

facts.subject: Magic Bean
facts.text: A Magic Bean can be planted in the soft dirt plot on the lower ledge of Gerudo Valley.

evidence.quote: Plant a Magic Bean on the same plot of dirt.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: Behind the waterfall in Zora's River, a ladder leads from the water to a hidden alcove containing a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: If you look behind it, you'll see a ladder extending from the water. Use the Cucco you used to get down here in the first place to get to this ladder. Climb the ladder and you'll find a hidden alcove with another Piece of Heart inside.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: At night, a Gold Skulltula is located on the wall of the Laboratory at Lake Hylia.

evidence.quote: Once you do, head to shore, make sure it's night, and you'll see yet another Gold Skulltula on the wall of the Laboratory.

facts.subject: Mask of Truth
facts.text: The Mask of Truth allows Link to read minds and speak with Gossip Stones.

evidence.quote: - Mask of Truth: Allows you to read people's minds, and you are also able to talk to Gossip Stones.

facts.subject: Deku Nut Upgrade
facts.text: Wearing the Mask of Truth in the Forest Stage allows Link to receive a Deku Nut Upgrade that increases carrying capacity to 40 Deku Nuts, but this upgrade cannot be obtained after pulling the Master Sword.

evidence.quote: Wear the Mask of Truth and find the leader and he'll give you a Deku Nut Upgrade. You can now carry 40 Deku Nuts...NOTE: You can NOT get this upgrade after pulling out the Master Sword for the first time.

facts.subject: Master Sword
facts.text: Pulling the Master Sword from its pedestal in the Temple of Time seals Link away in the Chamber of Sages for 7 years until he grows into a teen.

evidence.quote: Head through and you'll find the Master Sword on a pedestal. Go pull it out...Link pulled the Master Sword, his soul was sealed away in the Chamber of Sages for 7 years because he was not old enough to be the Hero of Time and to wield the Master Sword yet.

facts.subject: Advanced Spin Slash
facts.text: The Advanced Spin Slash is performed by holding B until the sword glows yellow, then releasing.

evidence.quote: Advanced Spin Slash (Hold B until the sword is yellow, then release)

facts.subject: Adult Link
facts.text: Adult Link can only use Deku Nuts, Ocarina of Time, Bombchus, Bombs, magic powers, and Bottles among items obtained as Young Link.

evidence.quote: The only items Adult Link can use are the Deku Nuts, Ocarina of Time, Bombchus, and Bombs. Of course, you can use Bottles and the magic powers with either Link.

facts.subject: Epona
facts.text: After paying 50 Rupees to race Ingo twice and winning both races, Link can jump the ranch boundary fences with Epona to keep her and ride her across Hyrule Field.

evidence.quote: talk to Ingo, and he'll ask if you want to race him for 50 Rupees...After beating him, he'll want you to race him again, and if you win you get to keep Epona...You see the fences acting as the ranch's boundary? Build up a lot of speed and you'll be able to jump clean over them. Now you're free to use Epona!

facts.subject: Pocket Egg
facts.text: The lady who owns the chicken pen in Kakariko Village gives Link a Pocket Egg that hatches overnight.

evidence.quote: In the town, head over to that lady who owns the chicken pen. She'll give you a Pocket Egg. This'll hatch over night.

facts.subject: Song of Storms
facts.text: Showing the Ocarina of Time to the man inside the Kakariko Village windmill teaches Link the Song of Storms.

evidence.quote: Show him the Ocarina of Time and he'll play the song that the young boy played. You now have learned the SONG OF STORMS!

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: Riding the grown Magic Bean plant in the Graveyard brings Link to a ledge where breaking a crate reveals a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: Get on the plant, and it'll take you to a ledge with a crate on it. Break the crate to reveal a Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Hookshot
facts.text: Following Dampe's ghost through his grave race to the end awards Link the Hookshot.

evidence.quote: Down below is Dampe's grave...Once you reach the end, he'll give you the HOOKSHOT, a useful weapon and item that lets you stun enemies and cling onto wooden surfaces and drag you toward it.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: Moving the Time blocks inside Dampe's grave leads to a high ledge inside the windmill where Link can reach a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: Head through the opening here and you'll find some blocks with the same design as the Door of Time. Use the Song of Time to move these blocks. Head through and you'll be inside the windmill on a high ledge. Use one of the ledges on the machine to reach yet another Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: Finishing Dampe's grave race a second time in under 1 minute awards a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: Race him again, but this time you have to finish in under one minute...If you finish under a minute, you'll get another Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: Hookshotting from the windmill fence onto the house with the gray roof in Kakariko Village allows Link to speak to a person on the roof for a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: hop on the fence near the windmill here, equip the Hookshot (keep it equipped as you're gonna use it a lot), and use it to hook onto the house with the gray roof. On top of here is a person here. Talk to him and he'll give you another Piece of Heart for your trouble.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: At night, Link can Hookshot from the Skulltula House onto the roof of Impa's house to retrieve a Gold Skulltula token.

evidence.quote: Now, make it night and head to Impa's house. It's the southernmost house in the village. Before entering the door though, face the Skulltula House and Hookshot on top of it. From there, Hookshot on top of Impa's House. Up here is a Gold Skulltula. Use the Hookshot to retrieve the token.

facts.subject: Cojiro
facts.text: Waking Talon with the hatched Pocket Cucco and returning it to the Cucco lady rewards Link with the blue Cucco Cojiro.

evidence.quote: Use the Pocket Cucco that just hatched to wake him up and he'll get up and take back the ranch...Send the Pocket Cucco to the Cucco lady and she'll be so pleased that she'll give you a blue Cucco named Cojiro.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: Riding the grown Magic Bean plant at the entrance of Dodongo's Cavern allows Link to jump to a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: Right at the entrance of Dodongo's Cavern, the Magic Bean you planted there while you were young has grown now. Ride it to reach another Piece of Heart you can jump to.

facts.subject: Huge Rupee
facts.text: Playing the Song of Storms on the platform outside Goron City opens a Secret Cave with a treasure chest containing a Huge Rupee.

evidence.quote: On the platform in front of the entrance, play the Song of Storms to open a Secret Cave. Inside is a treasure chest with a Huge Rupee.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: In Goron City, a Gold Skulltula is located on the back of the suspended platform accessible via the ropes behind it.

evidence.quote: Now you see the platform in the middle suspended by ropes? Walk on one of the ropes behind it to see a Gold Skulltula on the back of that platform.

facts.subject: Business Scrubs
facts.text: Playing the Song of Storms near the rock circle at the start of Zora's River reveals a Secret Cave with Business Scrubs selling Green Potion and Red Potion for 40 Rupees each.

evidence.quote: At the start, play the Song of Storms near the circle of rocks where the Cucco is to reveal a Secret Cave. Inside are two Business Scrubs. One sells a Green Potion for 40 Rupees, another sells a Red Potion for the same price.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: At night, riding the grown Magic Bean plant to the high platform in Zora's River reveals a Gold Skulltula on the southern wall.

evidence.quote: Exit, and use the grown Magic Bean plant to get to the high platform with the two Secret Caves, making sure it's night. Up here, look around the southern wall to see another Gold Skulltula.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Past the wooden bridge in Zora's River, a Gold Skulltula hangs high on the wall and can be reached by Hookshot from the fence.

evidence.quote: Next, continue on in Zora's River, and past the wooden bridge, you'll see a Gold Skulltula high up on the wall. It may seem too far for your Hookshot, but hop onto the fence facing the Skulltula, and the Hookshot will be able to reach the enemy.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: In Zora's Fountain, jumping across the floating ice platforms leads Link to a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: You'll notice here that Lord Jabu-Jabu is gone, and in its place is a bunch of ice platforms. You see the Piece of Heart in the distance? Jump across the ice carefully to reach it.

facts.subject: Piece of Heart
facts.text: Riding the grown Magic Bean plant by the Laboratory in Lake Hylia and climbing the roof ladder yields a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: Here, use the now grown Magic Bean by the Laboratory to get up on the roof. Be careful of the Guays, and climb up the ladder to get yet another Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Pierre the Scarecrow
facts.text: Playing the custom song to the scarecrow at Lake Hylia makes his brother appear at specific locations across Hyrule to act as a Hookshot target.

evidence.quote: Now, head over to the scarecrow by the now-dry shore and play the song you played to it while as Young Link, and he'll remember the song...Now when you play this song at certain spots, the scarecrow's brother will pop up and you'll be able to Hookshot onto him to reach hidden areas.

facts.subject: Gold Scale
facts.text: Catching a fish of 15 lb. or greater at the Lake Hylia Fishing Hole rewards Link with the Gold Scale, which allows diving for 9 seconds.

evidence.quote: Inside, again play for 20 Rupees, and attempt to catch a 15 pound or more fish...If you're patient enough and get the 15 lb. or greater fish, then the Fishing Hole owner will give you the Gold Scale, which allows you to dive for a whopping 9 seconds.

facts.subject: Bombchus
facts.text: The prize obtained at the Skulltula House in Kakariko Village is a bunch of Bombchus.

evidence.quote: Head over to Kakariko Village and gain your next prize at the Skulltula House, which is a measly bunch of Bombchus.

facts.subject: Lakeside Laboratory
facts.text: Diving 9 meters to the bottom of the Lakeside Laboratory pool by holding A earns a Piece of Heart from the old man.

evidence.quote:
9 meters in the pool is the goal, and each 
second amounts to a meter. Once you do a full dive, talk to the old man again 
and he should give you another Piece of Heart.

facts.subject: Gerudo Valley
facts.text: At night, a Gold Skulltula is located behind the stone pillar across the broken bridge in Gerudo Valley.

evidence.quote:
While riding Epona, 
jump across the broken bridge in an awesome-looking cutscene to cross to the 
other side. While here, make sure it's night, and look behind the stone pillar 
for another Gold Skulltula.

facts.subject: Gerudo Valley
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is located behind the tent across the broken bridge in Gerudo Valley.

evidence.quote:
Now look behind 
the tent for another. (GOLD SKULLTULAS: 050 out of 100)

facts.subject: Dodongo's Cavern
facts.text: In the southeastern entrance of Dodongo's Cavern, playing the Scarecrow's Song allows Link to Hookshot up to a Gold Skulltula.

evidence.quote:
Once inside, head to the southeastern entrance (with the Baby Dodongos) 
and at one point, Navi will fly up to somewhere high. While she's up there, 
play the Scarecrow's Song to summon a scarecrow up where Navi was. Hookshot to 
it and you'll find the last Gold Skulltula of this dungeon.

facts.subject: Lon Lon Ranch
facts.text: Beating Malon's obstacle course by finishing two laps around Lon Lon Ranch in under 50 seconds rewards a cow sent to Link's house.

evidence.quote:
Talk to Malon twice over at the 
horse stable and agree to try to beat her horse riding record....This is an obstacle course around the track. You 
have to finish two laps in under 50 seconds....If you succeed, Malon will give you a present so 
big that you can't carry it, so she'll send it to your house in Kokiri Forest. 
It's actually a cow, so you can get Lon Lon Milk right at your house.

facts.subject: Advanced Spin Slash
facts.text: The Advanced Spin Slash is performed by holding B until the sword glows yellow, then releasing.

evidence.quote: Advanced Spin Slash (Hold B until the sword is yellow, then release)

facts.subject: House of Twins
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is found on the back of the House of Twins in Kokiri Forest.

evidence.quote:
Anyway, kill them, and head to where the 
House of Twins is at, and you'll notice a Gold Skulltula on the back of the 
house.

facts.subject: Secret Cave
facts.text: Playing the Song of Storms near the Gossip Stone outside the Lost Woods entrance reveals a Secret Cave with a treasure chest containing a Red Rupee.

evidence.quote:
Before entering, play the Song of Storms near the Gossip Stone up here to 
reveal a Secret Cave. This contains a treasure chest with a Red Rupee inside, 
if you're bothered enough to get it.

facts.subject: Odd Mushroom
facts.text: Waking the sleeping bum in the Lost Woods with Cojiro rewards the Odd Mushroom, which spoils in 3 minutes.

evidence.quote:
Head left to find a bum who 
thinks everyone but him is disgusting. Well, wake him up with Cojiro, his 
chicken. So that's where Cojiro's owner went! He'll give you an Odd Mushroom 
in return. This item will spoil in 3 minutes, and you're supposed to give him 
a potion made with this.

facts.subject: Odd Potion
facts.text: Giving the Odd Mushroom before it spoils to the witch in the hidden Potion Shop behind the red house in Kakariko Village yields the Odd Potion.

evidence.quote:
From this shop, 
head through the back door, then enter the red house to find a hidden witch's 
Potion Shop. Give her the Odd Mushroom (if it hasn't spoiled) and she'll make 
an Odd Potion with it.

facts.subject: Poacher's Saw
facts.text: Giving the Odd Potion to the Kokiri girl in the Lost Woods rewards the saw left behind by the bum.

evidence.quote:
Head all the way back to where the bum was in Lost Woods, and you'll see a 
Kokiri girl in his place....In return for 
giving the girl the potion, she'll give you the saw he left behind.

facts.subject: Mido
facts.text: From the Lost Woods entrance, going right, left, and right leads to Mido, who allows passage once Saria's Song is played for him.

evidence.quote:
Now, head 
back to the entrance to Lost Woods, then head right, left, right, and you'll 
find Mido blocking the correct entrance here. Play Saria's Song for him and 
he'll let you through.

facts.subject: Lost Woods
facts.text: At night, riding the Magic Bean plant in the grassy area past Mido leads to a Gold Skulltula reachable with a sword slash.

evidence.quote:
Anyway, after going through the entrance Mido was blocking, head left once more
to get back to the grassy area. Making sure it's night, ride the Magic Bean 
plant and it'll take you to a Golden Skulltula. It's just reachable for a 
sword slash.

facts.subject: Secret Cave
facts.text: Bombing a Secret Cave in the Sacred Forest Meadow and defeating two Wolfos reveals a small chest containing a Purple Rupee.

evidence.quote:
First, place a bomb somewhere around here to open a Secret Cave which contains 
two Wolfos. Kill them both to reveal a small chest containing a Purple Rupee.

facts.subject: Large Moblin
facts.text: Large Moblins in the Sacred Forest Meadow maze charge when Link enters their sight, allowing Link to sneak behind them and slash them.

evidence.quote:
Large Moblins are now invading this place. 
What you have to do is be in their sight so that they'll charge, and you have 
to sneak up behind them. Once you are behind them, slash them to kill them.

facts.subject: Sacred Forest Meadow
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is located on a wall reached by climbing the ladder at the end of the Sacred Forest Meadow maze hedges.

evidence.quote:
Once you get past here, climb the ladder at the end to get on top of the 
hedges. Look around on one of the walls to find another Gold Skulltula.

facts.subject: Club Moblin
facts.text: The club Moblin smashes shockwaves that must be dodged to reach and slash him three times to defeat him.

evidence.quote:
With this 
one, it has a club, and wherever you are, it'll smash its club, creating a wave 
that'll move toward you. You have to keep dodging these until you reach him, 
then slash him to damage him. After that, you'll have to do it over again. Do 
it twice more after the first time to kill him, then continue to the Forest 
Temple's entrance.

facts.subject: Minuet of Forest
facts.text: Sheik teaches the Minuet of Forest at the Sacred Forest Meadow, which warps Link back to the Forest Temple entrance when played.

evidence.quote:
You'll encounter Sheik. He'll tell you about a few things, then teach you the
MINUET OF FOREST, which will warp you here whenever you play it.

facts.subject: Tree
facts.text: In the entrance area of the Forest Temple, climbing vines on the wall and jumping to the tree reveals a small chest with a Small Key.

evidence.quote:
Walk a few steps forward and two Wolfos will pop out. Use the tactic in the 
Enemy list section to defeat them, then find some vines on a wall. Climb up 
them, and you'll find a small chest on the tree on the other side. Jump over to 
it and open the chest to get a SMALL KEY.

facts.subject: Forest Temple
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is located around the vines near the entrance of the Forest Temple.

evidence.quote:
Around the vines you climbed 
is a Gold Skulltula. (GOLD SKULLTULAS: 055 out of 100)

facts.subject: Main Room
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is located on the right wall across from the entrance before the opposite door in the Forest Temple main room.

evidence.quote:
First, head 
straight across to the door on the opposite side. Before entering, take a look 
over at the right wall. You'll see another Gold Skulltula. (GOLD SKULLTULAS: 
056 out of 100)

facts.subject: Blue Bubble
facts.text: Shielding against an attacking Blue Bubble extinguishes its flames, leaving it vulnerable to sword slashes.

evidence.quote:
As soon as you enter, shield, as a Blue Bubble (a flaming skull) will try to 
hit you. If you shield successfully, its flames will go out and all you have 
to do is slash it until it's dead.

facts.subject: Stalfos Room
facts.text: Defeating two Stalfos by jump striking when their shields are lowered reveals a chest containing a Small Key.

evidence.quote:
Continue onward and you'll encounter two 
Stalfos, like the young Kokiri girl mentioned....What you have to do is jump strike them when they 
don't have their shield out....If you manage to defeat 
them both, a chest containing another SMALL KEY will appear.

facts.subject: Time Block
facts.text: Playing the Song of Time in front of the block in the right hallway makes the block disappear.

evidence.quote:
Head to the right hallway, and while standing in front of the block there, play
the Song of Time to make it disappear.

facts.subject: Dungeon Map Room
facts.text: Defeating the Blue Bubble in the upper room past the vines unseals the doors and spawns a large chest containing the Dungeon Map.

evidence.quote:
Inside, another Blue 
Bubble will immediately attack. Kill it and the doors will open back up and a 
large chest will appear. Open it to get, you guessed it, the DUNGEON MAP.

facts.subject: Well
facts.text: Stepping on the red switch drains the river and well, where a small chest with a Small Key can be found at the bottom.

evidence.quote:
Step on the red 
switch to lower the water level of the river. Drop down to the bottom.  You'll 
notice that the well is now completely drained. Drop down it and follow the 
hall to a small chest with a SMALL KEY.

facts.subject: Courtyard Ledge
facts.text: Hookshotting to the back of the small chest on the high ledge reaches the chest containing a Recovery Heart.

evidence.quote:
Hookshot to its 
backside (the side facing the wall) and you'll successfully climb up there....Inside this chest is a RECOVERY HEART

facts.subject: Courtyard Ledge
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula is located on the wall above the ledge reached by Hookshotting to the chest's backside.

evidence.quote:
Hookshot to its 
backside (the side facing the wall) and you'll successfully climb up there....Inside this chest is a RECOVERY HEART, but the real reason why we're up 
here is for a Gold Skulltula. It's on one of the walls up here. (GOLD
SKULLTULAS: 057 out of 100)

facts.subject: Block Puzzle
facts.text: In the west room, pull the block out into the corridor, push it along the ground arrow until it hits the wall, then push it from the upper hallway into the crevice.

evidence.quote:
Shortly thereafter, Navi will interrupt you. After she's done, look 
left and you'll see a block. Grab this and pull it to where you were, then 
follow the arrow on the ground and push the block that way until it reaches a 
wall. Now head back to the hallway where the block was...blocking...and 
continue up here and push the block until it falls into a little crevice.

facts.subject: House of Skulltula
facts.text: Visiting the Skulltula house in Kakariko Village rewards another Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote:
Now get back clear to 
Kakariko Village. Visit the Skulltula house and you'll get another Piece of 
Heart for your troubles!

facts.subject: Stalfos
facts.text: In the Forest Temple, if one Stalfos in the pair is defeated and the second is not defeated quickly, the first one will re-assemble.

evidence.quote: The thing here is, these two depend on each other. If you kill one, if you don't kill the other quickly, the first one will re-assemble, so be quick with these guys.

facts.subject: large treasure chest
facts.text: Defeating the pair of Stalfos makes a large treasure chest appear containing the FAIRY BOW.

evidence.quote: Killing them will finally make a large treasure chest appear. Open it to get the FAIRY BOW, which is a very useful projectile attack for Adult Link.

facts.subject: Poe sister
facts.text: Staying at a distance to keep the Poe picture visible and shooting all three pictures with arrows causes the Poe sister to appear at the bottom.

evidence.quote: What you have to do is be at a certain distance to keep the picture there, and fire an arrow with your new Bow at the picture. Do this with all three pictures and the Poe sister from the pictures will appear and will wait at the bottom.

facts.subject: small chest
facts.text: Defeating the first Poe sister causes a small chest containing a SMALL KEY to appear.

evidence.quote: A small chest will appear, and you'll get a SMALL KEY.

facts.subject: large chest
facts.text: Defeating the Poe sister in the second staircase room reveals a large chest containing the COMPASS.

evidence.quote: Here's another staircase room with three pictures of a Poe sister. Get rid of them all, then get rid of the actual Poe the same way you did the first one, and a large chest will appear. Open it for the COMPASS for this dungeon.

facts.subject: silver eye switch
facts.text: Shooting an arrow at the silver eye switch untwists the hallway.

evidence.quote: Now get back past the twisted hall, then turn around and fire an arrow at the silver eye switch. This will untwist the hallway.

facts.subject: small chest
facts.text: Hitting the gold eye switch with an arrow makes a small chest containing a bundle of Arrows appear.

evidence.quote: Now, in this huge room, you might have seen a gold eye switch. If you hit it with an arrow, a small chest containing a bundle of Arrows.

facts.subject: colorful chest
facts.text: Falling down after passing the untwisted hallway leads to a colorful chest containing the BOSS KEY.

evidence.quote: Go back through the now-untwisted hallway, then fall down and open the colorful chest for the BOSS KEY, which lets you access the door leading to the boss room.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Looking up at the end of the thin walkway with Recovery Hearts allows Link to Hookshot a Gold Skulltula (058 out of 100).

evidence.quote: Get to the end, look up, and Hookshot the Gold Skulltula. (GOLD SKULLTULAS: 058 out of 100).

facts.subject: treasure chest
facts.text: Fully defeating the Floormaster causes a treasure chest containing a SMALL KEY to appear.

evidence.quote: If you get rid of the Floormaster fully, a treasure chest will appear. Open it to get a SMALL KEY, then head through the other door outside this room.

facts.subject: Green Bubbles
facts.text: Green Bubbles are killed by slashing them when their fires subside.

evidence.quote: There's Green Bubbles here. In order to kill these, slash them when their fires subside.

facts.subject: eyeball switch
facts.text: Firing an arrow across a torch on the rotating platform lights the arrow in flames, melting the ice and triggering the eyeball switch.

evidence.quote: In here, you have to hit an eyeball switch with an arrow, but it's covered in ice, and there's a torch in the middle of rotating platforms. Get on one of the platforms, aim at the switch, and fire an arrow when you pass the torch. This will light the arrow on flames and will melt the ice AND hit the switch.

facts.subject: treasure chest
facts.text: In the falling ceiling room of the Forest Temple, a treasure chest contains a bundle of arrows.

evidence.quote: Hit the switch when you can to unlock the door ahead, and continue to the treasure chest. Open it to get a bundle of arrows, then head through the door to reach a room.

facts.subject: colored blocks
facts.text: Assembling the tops of the colored blocks to match the picture causes the Poe sister to emerge.

evidence.quote: What you have to do here is assemble the blocks by pushing them. You have to assemble the top side of the blocks so that they match the picture.

facts.subject: last Poe sister
facts.text: The real fourth Poe sister can be distinguished from her copies because she spins around when appearing.

evidence.quote: The same Poe will make copies of herself and surround you. They look virtually the same but the one way to tell the difference is that the real one spins around when she and her copies appear.

facts.subject: outward walls
facts.text: Pushing the outward walls in Basement 2 rotates the entire room to allow tripping three switches.

evidence.quote: You have to trip three switches, and in order to do so, you have to push the outward walls, which rotates the WHOLE room.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: A Gold Skulltula (059 out of 100) is hidden in the treasure chest section of Basement 2.

evidence.quote: Also there's a Gold Skulltula hidden here. Make sure to get it before leaving this room. (GOLD SKULLTULAS: 059 out of 100) It's in the treasure chest section of the room.

facts.subject: Phantom Ganon
facts.text: When Phantom Ganon emerges from a painting surrounded by purple magic, Link must shoot an arrow at the real phantom, as failing to do so triggers a lightning attack that inflicts at least five hearts of damage.

evidence.quote: Basically what you have to do, is aim your arrow at the Phantom when he escapes from the painting. (purple magic surrounds him when he's about to exit) The thing is, there's TWO of these phantoms. The fake one turns around, so if you encounter that one, hurry up and find the real one and fire that arrow. If you don't, you'll be struck with a lightning attack that takes away at least five hearts.

facts.subject: Phantom Ganon
facts.text: Swinging the Master Sword to reflect Phantom Ganon's magic spell back and forth stuns him when it connects, leaving him vulnerable to sword slashes on the floor.

evidence.quote: Use the Master Sword and swing it at the right time to reflect the magic spell back at Phantom Ganon. He'll usually reflect it back, so continue this tennis game until it hits either one of you. If it hits Phantom Ganon he'll go to the floor, stunned. So go up to him and slash him.

facts.subject: Phantom Ganon
facts.text: Standing very close to Phantom Ganon after his stallion disappears allows Link to deflect the magic ball attack immediately without giving him time to react.

evidence.quote: SPEEDY STRATEGY: After getting rid of its stallion, get really close to Phantom Ganon, and time your slash right so that it's deflected as soon as it fires its magic ball attack. Doing this won't give it enough time to react, and will immediately get hit.

facts.subject: HEART CONTAINER
facts.text: Defeating Phantom Ganon causes a HEART CONTAINER and a warp light to appear.

evidence.quote: When it is dead, a HEART CONTAINER (pick it up) and a light will appear.

facts.subject: Saria
facts.text: In the Chamber of Sages, Saria reveals herself as the Sage of the Forest Temple and gives Link the Forest Medallion.

evidence.quote: After grabbing the Container, step into the light and you'll be at the Chamber of Sages again. Saria will appear, tell you that she's the Sage of the Forest Temple, and give you the Forest Medallion.

facts.subject: PRELUDE OF LIGHT
facts.text: Sheik teaches Link the PRELUDE OF LIGHT, an ocarina song that warps him to the Temple of Time.

evidence.quote: Also with this info, he'll teach you the PRELUDE OF LIGHT, a song which warps you to the Temple of Time.

facts.subject: Master Sword
facts.text: Placing the Master Sword back into its pedestal returns Link to the past as Young Link.

evidence.quote: He'll tell you that whenever you want to return to the past, simply place the Master Sword back on its pedestal.

facts.subject: Gold Skulltula
facts.text: Playing the Song of Storms near the tree at Castle Grounds reveals a hole where blowing open walls yields a Gold Skulltula (060 out of 100) collectible via Boomerang.

evidence.quote: Surface, then play the Song of Storms near the tree to open a hole. Drop in. Inside, blow open the walls until you find a Gold Skulltula. Remember that you can't use the Hookshot as Young Link, so use your Bommerang. (GOLD SKULLTULAS: 060 out of 100)

facts.subject: windmill
facts.text: Playing the Song of Storms inside the windmill drives the mechanism out of control and drains the well.

evidence.quote: Once inside, play the Song of Storms to make the windmill mechanism go out of control, and thus draining the well.

facts.subject: skeleton wall
facts.text: In the Bottom of the Well, Link can walk straight through the fake wall where the skeleton is positioned.

evidence.quote: Navi will tell you that spirits are whispering a message that you must find the eye of truth. Well, this seems to be a dead-end. Wrong. Head right through the wall where the skeleton is to walk through it.

facts.subject: large chest
facts.text: Hugging the right wall past the water fork in the Bottom of the Well leads through a fake wall to a large chest containing the COMPASS.

evidence.quote: Turn the corner, and hug the right wall while going forward and you'll go through another fake section of wall. Open the large chest there to get the COMPASS.

facts.subject: large treasure chest
facts.text: Bombing the boulders past the hall with lit torches in the Bottom of the Well reveals a large treasure chest containing the DUNGEON MAP.

evidence.quote: Bomb the boulders past the hall showcased with lit torches. Kill the Redead walking around here, and open the large treasure chest to get the DUNGEON MAP.

facts.subject: Triforce symbol
facts.text: Playing Zelda's Lullaby while standing on the Triforce symbol lowers the water level.

evidence.quote:
Turn right until you find a Triforce symbol on the ground. Stand on 
it and play Zelda's Lullaby to lower the water level.

facts.subject: small chest
facts.text: A small chest in the drained pool area contains Bombs.

evidence.quote:
Head back to the section 
of the room where you first entered, and the pool of water will be drained. 
Head down, open the small chest for some BOMBS, and head through the
crawlspace, kill the Skulltula, climb the wall and enter the door to face a 
sub-boss.

facts.subject: large chest
facts.text: Defeating the Dead Hand sub-boss by slashing its reachable head causes a large chest with the Lens of Truth to appear.

evidence.quote:
You have to slash its 
head when it's reachable. Keep doing this and it will lower again. Get caught 
in a hand again to lure it back up, and repeat this process until it's dead, 
and a large chest will appear. Open it to get the LENS OF TRUTH.

facts.subject: small chest
facts.text: A small chest revealed behind the large chest with the Lens of Truth contains a Huge Rupee.

evidence.quote:
Use this to reveal a small chest behind the large one. This contains a 
HUGE RUPEE.

facts.subject: small chest
facts.text: Bombing the brown pile of dirt on the second basement floor reveals a hole leading to a small chest with Bombchus.

evidence.quote:
Facing forward from the first fake wall, bomb the brown pile 
of dirt to the left to reveal a hole. Fall down it and open the small chest 
for some BOMBCHUS.

facts.subject: small chest
facts.text: A small chest reached through the first left off the west hallway contains a Recovery Heart.

evidence.quote:
Head down the west hallway, and head 
through the first left. Drop down and open the small chest for a RECOVERY 
HEART.

facts.subject: coffin
facts.text: Lighting each unlit torch with a Deku Stick opens adjacent coffins, one of which contains a Small Key.

evidence.quote:
Alright, now use a Deku Stick (haven't used one of those in a 
while, eh?) to light all the unlit torches. Each torch opens the coffin next 
to it, so make sure to put away the stick after lighting each torch so you 
don't waste one. Pretty much all the coffins have enemies inside, but one of 
them has a SMALL KEY.
